But consider, if someone has changed their residence, can you compel the person to make a false declaration by submitting that pre-filled enumeration? Why can't that person simply give a Form 8 because anyway, his name is there in the existing list he just wants to get his address changed.. Why compel enumeration form?" Justice Menezes observed.
items.response: LiveLaw reported that the Commission's counsel argued that a voter had to submit the enumeration form along with Form 8 to have an address changed, and that a voter who did not submit it had to file Form 6.

items.case: Petition on the implementation of the SIR in Maharashtra, Bombay High Court
items.headline: Maharashtra SIR: Bombay High Court Declines Oral Plea To Restrain ECI From Deleting Voters' Names, Says SC Seized Of Issue
items.claim: The Chief Justice's bench refused an oral request to order that no names be deleted from the roll in Maharashtra for the time being. It said it would follow the Supreme Court, which it was told had restrained High Courts in November 2025 from hearing petitions on the revision, and adjourned the case by four weeks, LiveLaw reported. The petition asks for the order and reasons behind the revision in the state and for safeguards against wrongful exclusion.
items.quote: "There are restraining orders already... No purpose will be served by a parallel litigation. Let the SC hear the matter first and we will consider it later," Chief Justice said. ... The judges turned down the said oral prayer, by observing, "No no no...we are not going to pass any such orders... We will follow judicial propriety." The bench accordingly, adjourned the hearing for four weeks.

items.case: WP 32975 of 2026, a petition by two electors, Telangana High Court
items.headline: Telangana SIR | Plea Challenges 'AI-Based' SIR Process; High Court Asks ECI Why Voter Was Excluded Without Notice
items.claim: The Telangana High Court asked the Commission why one petitioner was left off the roll without a notice and what happened to the other after his hearing, LiveLaw reported. The petition challenges notices over minor discrepancies and the automated matching used in the revision. The case was listed again for 13 October. At the hearing of 13 October, senior counsel for the Commission said one petitioner's name had been deleted and he would have to file Form 6, and that the other's petition was premature because the final roll had not been published, Telangana Today reported. He assured the bench that reasoned orders, open to appeal, would be passed where electors on the draft were left off the final roll, provided they attended the hearings on their notices and gave documents. He said that where no order was passed, the elector's name could be taken as included. The case was adjourned to 15 October.
items.quote: If he has satisfied and explained on the mismatch, you must have taken a decision on that,
items.response: The Commission's counsel sought time for instructions. She said the second petitioner was sent a notice over a mismatch in his father's name and heard on 15 September, and that the first could file Form 6.

items.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
items.headline: Goa HC adjourns hearing on plea challenging voter deletion as ECI points out SC cases
items.claim: The Bombay High Court at Goa adjourned the St Cruz family's petition by a week at the Commission's request, after the Commission said orders the Supreme Court might pass could bear on it. The judges took the view that the Supreme Court's orders may not have a direct bearing, PTI reported, and the Commission's advocate told reporters the Supreme Court had asked High Courts to defer such hearings.
items.quote: The orders the Supreme Court may pass can have a bearing on the matter before the HC,
items.response: The Commission's counsel also said "what is under challenge is the rejection of Form 8" and that it "cannot be looked at in isolation."

items.case: Application by five deleted electors in the West Bengal SIR matter, Supreme Court
items.headline: SIR-Deleted Voters Move Supreme Court For Expeditious Disposal Of Appeals Before Kolkata, Howrah Municipal Elections
items.claim: Five electors deleted from West Bengal's roll after adjudication applied to the Supreme Court for their appeals to be decided before the Kolkata and Howrah municipal elections, LiveLaw reported. They also asked for a Special Investigation Team to examine how the revision's decisions were made. The application cites the Commission's affidavits as showing 1.7 lakh appeals pending from Kolkata and Howrah.
items.quote: the applicants claim that their names were deleted without any notice to them.
items.response: None was reported. The applicants say the Chief Electoral Officer has not published the criteria for logical discrepancies.

items.case: MA Baby v. Union of India and others, WP(c) 63560/2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: Don't Completely Stop Trains/Metro In Delhi To Handle October 10 Protests : Supreme Court To Centre
items.claim: The Supreme Court told the Centre not to stop all trains and Metro services in Delhi before the 10 October protests against the Chief Election Commissioner, and to run them in a regulated way, LiveLaw reported. The petition was brought by CPI(M) General Secretary MA Baby and others against the closure of 57 Metro stations and the cancellation of trains due at New Delhi and Nizamuddin. The order said the notifications appeared to be overreaching, and ETV Bharat reported that the bench also asked the Centre to reconsider Jantar Mantar as the designated protest site.
items.quote: there shall be no outright prohibition on the movement of Metro trains
items.response: The order records that the Solicitor General "has fairly agreed to impress upon the authorities to reassess such prohibitions." He said the impression that the whole city had been shut "is far from the truth."

items.case: Application by five deleted electors in the West Bengal SIR matter, Supreme Court
items.headline: 'We Are Conscious' : Supreme Court To Consider Plea To Prioritise SIR-Deleted Voters' Appeals Ahead Of Kolkata, Howrah Municipal Elections
items.claim: Counsel for electors deleted from West Bengal's roll after adjudication asked the Supreme Court to hear their plea before the Kolkata and Howrah municipal elections and to let appellants vote, LiveLaw reported. The Chief Justice said the Court would try to list it on 16 October, or else on 29 October, and suggested the tribunals take up appeals for inclusion first and appeals seeking deletion last. Counsel told the Court that nearly 1.70 lakh appeals from the two municipal areas were pending.
items.quote: We will find out if we can list on 16th (Friday) ...otherwise 29th is best way.
items.response: No submission by the Commission was reported. The figures put to the Court were counsel's, partly drawn from the Commission's affidavits.

items.case: Paka Suresh v. Union of India, SLP(C) No. 35786/2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: Andhra Pradesh Local Body Elections | Conduct Polls As Per Old Rolls If SIR Not Complete Before Notification: Supreme Court
items.claim: The Supreme Court, hearing a challenge to the Andhra Pradesh High Court's order for local body elections within six weeks, said the elections should use the revised roll if it is published before the polls are notified, and the existing roll if it is not. It said the roll in force applies until the Commission publishes the revised list and that the revision cannot be a reason to delay the polls.
items.quote: However, if the final SIR rolls were not published before the notification, the elections would be conducted using the existing electoral rolls in accordance with the applicable State laws.
items.response: The bench noted that the Election Commission had proposed to publish the final roll on 16 October 2026. Senior counsel for the State Election Commission said the rolls in force continue until the Commission publishes a fresh list. Deccan Chronicle reported on 15 October that the Commission had moved the final publication in Andhra Pradesh to 30 October and the last date for disposing of claims and objections to 22 October. The Wire reported that the YSRCP moved the Supreme Court on 20 October, alleging that violence during the filing of nominations for the state's urban local body elections kept its candidates from taking part.

items.case: Contempt petition against the Union Home Secretary, the Delhi Police Commissioner and the DMRC chairperson, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court Contempt Plea Alleges Delhi Authorities Defied Order On Metro, Train Curbs
items.claim: A contempt plea filed in the Supreme Court on 10 October alleged that the Centre and Delhi authorities defied the Court's order of 9 October, keeping 57 Metro stations shut and cancelling Delhi-bound trains before the protest against the Chief Election Commissioner, Outlook reported. The plea also said no traffic advisory had been published in newspapers. A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana listed it to be heard with a petition against the detention of opposition leaders at a special sitting on Sunday 11 October, Bar and Bench reported. On 15 October, before the Chief Justice and Justice Bagchi, the Delhi Police Commissioner filed two affidavits that tendered an unconditional apology for any perceived non-compliance and said there had been no non-compliance with the Court's orders of 9 and 11 October. Justice Bagchi observed that on the Solicitor General's account the apology appeared qualified.
items.quote: "Notwithstanding the solemn judicial mandate and the assurance recorded before the bench of the Chief Justice of India (CJI), the contemnors have consciously maintained a blanket shutdown across transit corridors, persisted with unwarranted train cancellations, and failed to issue or publicize transparent traffic and transit advisories."
items.response: The Solicitor General said the apology was included as standard practice in answering a contempt notice and that the government was defending its actions on facts. The Commissioner asked for the contempt notice to be discharged.

items.case: Rahul Gandhi v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026 (Diary No. 64196 of 2026), Supreme Court
items.headline: SC registry points out 10 defects in Rahul Gandhi's plea in SIR case
items.claim: Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and other INDIA bloc leaders filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court on 12 October against the Election Commission, the Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners. Delhi Police stopped their march to the Court on Bhagwant Das Road, and counsel filed the petition shortly before the filing counter closed. LiveLaw reported that the leaders then went to the Registry, and that a large crowd gathered inside the Court's precincts. The petition asks for the SIR to be suspended in every state while the case is heard, for a committee under a retired Supreme Court judge to audit the names left off or deleted, and for the Commission's files on its decision to hold the revision. PTI reported that the Registry flagged more than ten defects in it, among them illegible or missing pages, an unclear copy of Kharge's identity card and a court fee short by over Rs 200. LawBeat reported that the Registry registered it on 13 October once the defects were cured.
items.quote: Besides, the registry also pointed out a shortfall of over Rs 200 in court fee.
items.response: No response from the Commission was reported.

items.case: A fresh writ petition on the modified Form 6, Supreme Court (petitioner not reported)
items.headline: We have neither approved nor disapproved ECI's Form 6 modification: Supreme Court clarifies
items.claim: On a fresh writ petition, the bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said its remarks of 5 October meant only that the modified Form 6 did not exist when the Bihar case was heard, and that the Court had neither approved nor disapproved it, Bar and Bench reported. Counsel for the petitioner had said the Commission was presenting the altered form as approved by the Court. The Hindustan Times reported that the bench said it would examine the issue and listed the petition with the batch of SIR petitions on 27 October, when it would also take up the wider challenge to how the Commission's decisions on the revision were taken.
items.quote: What was said was that when the Bihar SIR matter was before us, the new Form 6 was not there. That does not mean it was either approved or disapproved by the Supreme Court
items.response: The Commission's press note of 26 September said the Supreme Court had upheld the additional declaration attached to Form 6 for the revision. The Hindustan Times reported that the Commission maintains the statutory form itself was not altered and that the declaration is an addendum for the revision only. In its affidavit of 26 October in the Supreme Court, the Commission said Form 6 had not been amended and that the SIR declaration is a separate document, Bar and Bench reported (court-52).

items.case: Application by two transparency activists in their pending petition on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: Delhi SIR: Supreme Court Advances Hearing After Plea Flags Deleted Voters Being Asked To Fill Form 6
items.claim: Two transparency activists who had petitioned the Court on the Delhi revision filed an application against the requirement that electors left off Delhi's draft apply again on Form 6, whose declaration says the applicant is applying for inclusion for the first time, LiveLaw reported. The application says 47,56,722 electors, 32.78% of those on the roll before the revision, were left off the draft, and that a false declaration can be punished under section 31 of the 1950 Act. It asks for a way to restore these electors without that declaration, and for the additional declaration form added to Forms 6 and 8 through the SIR guidelines to be declared without the force of law because it was not made under section 28 of the Act. Counsel asked the Court to let them use Form 8 or another form. On 14 October the bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi moved the hearing of the main petition from 30 to 28 October.
items.quote: we are thinking of passing an order that will take care of [all this]
items.response: No submission by the Commission was reported. Counsel told the Court that 30 October was the last date in Delhi for correcting deletions.

items.case: Rahul Gandhi v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026 (Diary No. 64196 of 2026), Supreme Court
items.headline: 'One Petitioner Has To Explain His Conduct': Supreme Court Issues Notice On INDIA Bloc Leaders' Petition Against ECI Over SIR
items.claim: A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notice on the INDIA bloc leaders' petition to the Election Commission, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, LiveLaw reported. Bar and Bench reported that the bench tagged it with the SIR cases already pending. The Chief Justice said that issuing notice did not mean the Court was condemning anything, and that the Court would ask one of the petitioners about his conduct at the next hearing. He said the petition would be entertained on that petitioner's behalf on a provisional basis, subject to his explaining his conduct. The bench did not name him in court. LiveLaw reported that the written order, uploaded later that day, names him as petitioner no. 6, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut. Notice was also issued on separate petitions by AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi and Congress leader Digvijaya Singh. No interim order was reported. The Hindustan Times had reported on 12 October that the batch of SIR petitions was listed for 27 October. LiveLaw reported on the morning of 27 October that the joint petition was listed that day with two other petitions on the Commission's functioning, before the bench of the Chief Justice, Justice Bagchi and Justice Mohana.
items.quote: "We would also ask one of the petitioners about his conduct."
items.response: No counsel for the Commission was reported. The Court said "Somebody will accept notice on behalf of the Election Commission of India," Bar and Bench reported.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1360 of 2026 (Diary No. 64394 of 2026), a petition by four advocates on the march of 12 October, Supreme Court
items.headline: 'Nobody Can Browbeat Us' : Supreme Court In Plea Against October 12 March By Opposition Leaders; Issues Notice
items.claim: The same bench issued notice on a petition by four advocates about the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court on 12 October, and on a second plea seeking similar relief, LiveLaw reported. The petition asks for rules on demonstrations near the Supreme Court and the High Courts and for criminal contempt proceedings against Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav and Mahua Moitra. Senior counsel for the petitioners said about 200 lawyers had signed a memorandum calling the march browbeating. The Chief Justice said nobody could browbeat the Court and that the judges knew what was said outside it. The Court directed all law enforcement agencies to preserve the CCTV footage and other digital material they had collected, and LiveLaw reported that it also directed footage of the Court's premises to be preserved. Bar and Bench reported that notice went to the Congress, Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders, and that the Court declined to begin contempt proceedings that day.
items.quote: "Nobody can browbeat us," the CJI responded. ... "We are not sitting in ivory towers." "We know what statements they make outside and what they say in Court."
items.response: No reply from the leaders named was reported.

items.case: Plea on voter deletions in Maharashtra's SIR, Supreme Court (petitioner and case number not reported)
items.headline: Supreme Court Lists Maharashtra SIR Voter Deletions Plea For October 26, Says Matters Cannot Be Generalised
items.claim: The Supreme Court declined to issue notice on 15 October on a plea about deletions in Maharashtra's revision and listed it for 26 October, LawChakra reported. The Chief Justice refused to hear it with the other petitions on the revision and said the Court would take the states one at a time, Maharashtra first and then Delhi. The petition says about 1.2 crore of Maharashtra's 9.79 crore electors were flagged for logical discrepancies, and the Commission had not yet replied. Bar and Bench reported that senior counsel for the petitioner, Arvind Datar, told the Court that 1.2 crore of Maharashtra's 9.79 crore electors had been flagged for logical discrepancies and that 40.6% of electors had been left off the roll in Pune and some other areas. He asked for notice to be issued that day so that the authorities could reply before 26 October, and the Chief Justice said "Not today. Not today."
items.quote: This cannot be generalised. We have to look at it state-wise.
items.response: LawChakra reported that the Election Commission's response was not yet on record. Maharashtra's period for claims and objections ran to 26 October, the day of the hearing.

items.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals
items.headline: Election Commission Seeks to Remove Half the Bengal Voters Judges Have Cleared For Inclusion
items.claim: The Election Commission had filed appeals before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals against the inclusion of at least 14,75,887 voters by 17 October, 49.2% of the 30,00,545 voters in the records whom judicial officers had examined and found eligible, The Wire reported from appeal records collected by the Civic Research Group. Malda, Murshidabad and Uttar Dinajpur hold 44.6% of these appeals. In the 41 seats where minorities are more than half the population the appeals equal 5.9% of the draft roll, and in the 89 seats where they are under 10% they equal 0.6%. The tribunals had decided 80,091 appeals, or 5.4%, and the report says no tribunal has been able to upload an order since 21 September. In a follow-up on 24 October, The Wire reported that the Civic Research Group's fuller records show 16,08,175 appeals by the Commission against 32,53,401 voters found eligible, 49.4%, close to the 16,10,311 appeals against inclusion that the Commission reported to the Supreme Court in September. It reported that the appeal numbers carry a filing date, a structure that activists found and The Wire says it verified, and that 13,85,374 of the 13,95,794 appeal IDs in an earlier extract of 17 October, or 99.3%, carry one of three dates, 5, 6 or 8 April 2026, with more than 12 lakh on 5 April. The roll was frozen for the Assembly election at midnight on 7 April.
items.quote: The Commission has not disclosed on what grounds it is challenging these voters, and who exactly decided to file the appeals.
items.response: The report says the Commission has not said on what grounds it filed the appeals, who decided to file them, or whether each case was reviewed before an appeal was filed. The follow-up says only the Commission can confirm the dates read from the appeal numbers, and that a single date on more than 12 lakh appeals does not by itself show who authorised them.

items.case: PIL by an advocate for an expert committee on the Election Commission, Supreme Court
items.headline: Plea before Supreme Court seeks expert committee headed by former CJI to examine ECI's functioning
items.claim: An advocate filed a PIL in the Supreme Court asking for an independent expert committee, chaired by a former Chief Justice or judge of the Court, to examine shortcomings in the functioning of the Election Commission, Bar and Bench reported. It relies on The Indian Express report of 23 September that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi recorded written objections at least 14 times over ten months to decisions taken by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar alone. Citing reports of a Commission affidavit, it says about 38.20 lakh appeals had been filed in West Bengal by people excluded from the roll and about 1.02 lakh decided. It also asks the Commission to bar campaigning on religious tags, religious symbols and communal appeals. No hearing date was reported.
items.quote: The petition states that it is intended to be non-partisan and prospective and that the petitioner is not seeking a finding against any political party or office-holder, nor does it challenge the result of any election.
items.response: The plea says the Commission acknowledged the dissenting notes and described them as routine suggestions. The plea describes all the West Bengal appeals as filed by people excluded from the roll. The Commission's own count splits them into 22,21,118 appeals by people found not eligible and 16,10,311 appeals against inclusion.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1330 of 2026, a petition on voter deletions in Maharashtra's SIR, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court assures no deleted voters will be prosecuted for submitting Form 6
items.claim: The Supreme Court issued notice to the Election Commission on 26 October on a petition against deletions in Maharashtra's revision and listed it for 5 November, and the Chief Justice orally assured that no elector deleted in the revision would be prosecuted for applying again through Form 6, The Hindu and LawChakra reported. The Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana declined to extend the period for claims and objections, which closed that day, or to stop the final roll before hearing the Commission. Senior advocate Arvind Datar, for the petitioner, said thousands of electors in Mumbai and Pune were marked absent and then deleted because their old buildings were being redeveloped and they had moved out, and he put the redevelopment projects at 3,500 in Mumbai and 1,500 in Pune. He said electors who had been deleted were being made to file Form 6 as new voters, which he said is an offence, and asked for a new form to be notified for electors deleted in the revision. LawChakra reported that he also said about 3 crore of the state's roughly 9 crore electors had been deleted after the draft, 1.22 crore of them for a logical discrepancy, and that about 40% were missing from the rolls in Pune and Mumbai. ANI reported the Chief Justice as saying the Court could extend the date later if it found people who had yet to file their documents.
items.quote: “Do not worry. Nobody will be prosecuted,” Chief Justice Kant responded orally.
items.response: The Commission's reply is awaited. LawChakra says the Court recorded no finding on the petitioner's figures. The assurance on Form 6 was given orally in court.

items.case: A petition seeking a writ of quo warranto against the Chief Election Commissioner, on which notice was issued on 5 October 2026, heard with W.P.(Crl.) No. 401 of 2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: No change to Form 6; members' approval obtained electronically in urgent matters: ECI to Supreme Court
items.claim: The Election Commission filed a short affidavit in the Supreme Court on 26 October in reply to a petition seeking a writ of quo warranto against the Chief Election Commissioner over how the Commission's decisions are taken, and said the affidavit was approved by a unanimous decision of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, Bar and Bench reported. The affidavit says files go to one Election Commissioner, then to the other and then to the Chief Election Commissioner, and that a suggestion, observation or query by a member during this process is not a decision of the Commission under Section 18 of the 2023 Act. It says that in urgent cases members approve electronically and the approval is recorded on the file later. It says the three SIR orders of 24 June 2025, 27 October 2025 and 14 May 2026 were unanimous decisions of the Commission. It says Form 6 has not been amended, because only the Central Government can amend it, and that the SIR declaration is a separate document. It accepts that the way the declaration was shown online could be read as an amendment, and says this was done so that an applicant needs a single OTP and e-sign. By a decision of the Commission's ER Division of 21 October 2026 the online application is to be in two parts, as the paper forms are. It says the appeals in West Bengal against the inclusion of electors were filed by officers of the state Chief Electoral Officer under the Court's orders and were not placed before the Commission. It says the Commission decided on 26 September 2026 that Booth Level Officers will collect documents from the homes of unmapped electors, who need not be called to a hearing, and that hearings will be held only in exceptional cases, preferably online. Item iii of the Commission's press note ECI/PN/120/2026 of 26 September 2026 reads "The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon’ble Supreme Court." The affidavit, as Bar and Bench reported it, says the SIR declaration is a separate document. LiveLaw reported that the petitions were listed before the bench of the Chief Justice, Justice Bagchi and Justice Mohana on 27 October. The Indian Express, which reported the affidavit on 27 October, said it was approved for filing by a unanimous decision of all three members and reported further points. The affidavit accepts that the way the declaration appeared online "could be construed as though an amendment of Form 6 had been made" and that "certain steps taken by the officers" needed "to be corrected". It says the Electoral Registration Officer remains the statutory authority for the roll and that "no entry is added or deleted or modified except by order of the Electoral Registration Officer". It sets out a committee that includes experts from IIT Mumbai and IISc Bengaluru to review whether ECINet complies with the law, as decided by the Commission on 26 and 30 September, and the scrutiny of new IT modules before they are approved. It says 88 of the 97 Goa electors left off the final roll have since applied through Form 6. It says the West Bengal appeals were filed by officers in the state Chief Electoral Officer's office, citing a letter from that office of 22 October. It says an order by which a senior officer redistributed work among the Commission's officers was never implemented after the two Election Commissioners' joint direction, and that the letters the two Commissioners wrote were about that order.
items.quote: "In the eyes of law, a newspaper report is not treated as evidence of the facts it narrates. The Commission has neither released nor authorized the release of any internal note / file to any news agency," the affidavit said.
items.response: This is the Commission's own account, given on oath. The Commission filed a short reply because of the Dussehra vacation and asked for liberty to file a detailed reply paragraph by paragraph. The affidavit does not say how many West Bengal appeals were filed, who in the Chief Electoral Officer's office approved them, or on what grounds, Bar and Bench reported. The Indian Express's analysis says the affidavit does not say who approved the online change to Form 6 in July, two months after two of the three members had recorded in writing that it should not be made. It says the affidavit presents the ECINet committee as the Commission's decision of September without mentioning Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi's proposal of 29 May, does not explain why Goa's registration officers could not act on their decisions in the software in February, and does not reconcile its West Bengal account with Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu's note that the state's Chief Electoral Officer told him she had no information about the appeals. On the July order, the paper says the affidavit does not say why it was issued without the Commission, why the file was withheld from a member of the Commission, or what has happened to the officer, who is not named.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026, the petition seeking a writ of quo warranto against the Chief Election Commissioner, heard with the connected petitions on the Commission's functioning, among them W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: 'We Will Examine': Supreme Court Adjourns Pleas Alleging Unilateral ECI Decisions
items.claim: The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana adjourned the batch of petitions on the Election Commission's functioning on 27 October and gave the petitioners 10 days to file rejoinders to the Commission's affidavit of 26 October (court-52), LiveLaw reported. LiveLaw reported that the bench tentatively listed the matter on 17 November. Senior Advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, for Rahul Gandhi and the INDIA bloc leaders (court-43), asked the Court to order that file notings and internal communications be preserved. The Chief Justice replied that the Court knew everything and would examine it. No order to preserve the records was reported. Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy, for Trinamool Congress MP Dola Sen, said the affidavit accepted many of the charges in Sen's petition about the online Form 6, and that the Commission had issued a press note saying the Court had authorised the change. Bar and Bench reported that she told the Court it had done no such thing. LiveLaw's live page records the Chief Justice saying that the Court was issuing notice on her petition. No interim order was reported.
items.quote: "We know everything, we will examine," CJI replied.
items.response: Senior Advocate Maninder Singh, for the Commission, objected to Guruswamy's submissions. Bar and Bench reported that he said "I represent the Election Commission. They are following rhetoric for some other purpose," and that Solicitor General Tushar Mehta called the request to preserve the file notings an unfair request.

items.case: The petition of two transparency activists on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, and their application on Form 6 (court-30, court-48), Supreme Court
items.headline: Delhi SIR : Why Deleted Voters Asked To File Form 6 When They Were On 2026 Rolls? Supreme Court Asks ECI
items.claim: The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana asked the Election Commission on 28 October why electors left off Delhi's draft for not returning enumeration forms are asked to apply on Form 6, which is meant for first-time voters, when they were on the roll of 2026, LiveLaw reported. Justice Bagchi said the Commission's four categories leave no place for electors who were never served a form, such as someone away from Delhi for a month, and that if the roll of 2026 is the base an elector who has shifted should be allowed Form 8. The bench suggested a residual category for those temporarily away, asked the Commission to reach out to electors given Delhi's floating population, and, as Bar and Bench reported, said the excluded names must be easily accessible in simple Hindi and local languages. Bar and Bench also reported Justice Bagchi saying the Court had not finally decided whether the logical discrepancy exercise is lawful, and had allowed it in West Bengal only as an interim arrangement. Counsel for the petitioners, Prashant Bhushan, said 43 of the 47 lakh left off are shown as permanently shifted or absent. The Indian Express reported that the bench said electors left off the draft who had only been away for a time should be allowed to submit the enumeration form, and those who had moved to another address in Delhi should be allowed Form 8. The Chief Justice suggested a statement or circular saying that Form 6 is to be filled only by those registering as voters in Delhi for the first time, LiveLaw and The Indian Express reported, and The Indian Express reported him adding that it was not for those on the roll of 2026 who could not fill the enumeration form because they had moved or were away. Hindustan Times reported the Court asking for a public notice saying that Form 6 is for first-time enrolment and that those who had moved could use Form 8 or the enumeration form. The Chief Justice also told the Commission not to go by any cut-off date while no election is due in Delhi, to keep inviting Form 6 and Form 8 and verify the documents attached, and to issue a public notice in newspapers and online that the process is continuing, The Indian Express reported. The Times of India reported the bench's suggestion that the Commission publish the list of electors left off with the reason against each name, ask them to contact the nearest booth level officer and fill Form 8, give them enumeration forms and tell them they may fill either Form 6 or Form 8. The bench listed the matter after two weeks. The Indian Express reported that the bench said it was not issuing an order to extend the deadline of 30 October and expected the Commission to act on its own, and The Times of India reported that the bench spoke without passing any order. No written order was reported. Anjali Bhardwaj, one of the two petitioners, wrote on X on 30 October that the Court had said electors on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors should be allowed to fill the enumeration form or Form 8 in place of Form 6, which she wrote requires them to make a false declaration that they are first-time voters. She wrote that 32 lakh of the 47 lakh on that list in Delhi were marked permanently shifted and 12 lakh untraceable or absent.
items.quote: In Bihar, the Election Commission had not initially undertaken logical discrepancy as a category. We permitted it as an interim arrangement in West Bengal. We have not finally adjudicated upon the legality of the logical discrepancy exercise,
items.response: Senior Advocate Dama Seshadri Naidu, for the Commission, said the authorities would examine the concerns, take remedial steps and consider extending the deadline, LiveLaw reported. He said the roll of 2026 before the revision is the base. Bar and Bench reported that the Commission would consider accepting late enumeration forms and would extend the deadline of 30 October if needed. The Indian Express reported Naidu telling the bench that the Commission would report its steps in two weeks and that the time would be extended in the meanwhile. The Times of India reported him saying that the Commission had held more than one lakh camps in Delhi, that not a single person had come to fill Form 8, and that no one had been prosecuted for using Form 6 to restore a name.

items.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals in Samserganj and Sujapur (court-47)
items.headline: Two Bengal Seats, 72,000 ECI Appeals, One Timestamp: 99% of Target Voters Are Muslim
items.claim: In Sujapur, in Malda district, the Election Commission has filed appeals against the inclusion of 61,066 of the 1,07,690 electors whom judicial officers examined and found eligible, 56.7%, The Wire reported. It said that is more appeals than in any other seat in West Bengal. The figures come from appeal records collected by the Civic Research Group. In Samserganj, in Murshidabad district, judicial officers found 74,775 electors not eligible, the most of any seat, and the Commission has appealed against 15,195 of the 33,152 they cleared, 47.6%. The Wire reported that 72,838 of the 76,156 pending appeals in the two seats, 96%, carry one timestamp of 5 April 2026, two days before the roll was frozen for the Assembly election, and that their numbers run in sequence one roll part at a time, which it reads as appeals generated in batches. It reported that 99.9% of the electors appealed against in Samserganj and 99.6% in Sujapur have names it describes as recognisably Muslim, a classification it says it estimated from Bengali names and not from official records. It said the Commission did not single them out from among those cleared, because almost everyone the judges cleared in both seats has such a name. The tribunals had decided 105 of the 76,261 appeals in the two seats. In Sujapur the appeals equal almost a quarter of the draft roll of 2,56,276 and slightly exceed the winning margin of 60,287 in April, and in Samserganj they are about twice the margin of 7,587.
items.quote: Of these 76,156 appeals in total, 72,838, or 96%, share a single timestamp on April 5, 2026.
items.response: The report says the Commission has not said on what grounds it is challenging these electors, whether each case was reviewed before an appeal was filed, why so many appeals share one timestamp, or why it has appealed against about half or more of those cleared. No reply from the Commission is reported.

items.case: Petitions on the Kerala SIR, heard with the SIR matters concerning Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh (up-26), Supreme Court
items.headline: केरल में SIR की समयसीमा बढ़ाने से सुप्रीम कोर्ट का इनकार, कहा- सुधार और नाम जोड़ने की प्रक्रिया जारी रहेगी
items.claim: The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant declined on 30 October to extend the time for the revision in Kerala and said that corrections and inclusions in the roll are a continuing process, Times Now Navbharat reported. Counsel for the petitioners said many people could not submit their enumeration forms for want of time. The Chief Justice asked them to identify the people who should still be given a chance and bring them to the Election Commission's notice by representation, and said the Court would ask the Commission to examine them and keep the matter pending. The Commission agreed to consider such representations and to file a report in the Court. Senior Advocate Datar gave the Court a note for the petitioners, saying they had raised the exclusion of names at a large scale, that the Commission should file a detailed affidavit, and that the matter cannot be treated as infructuous only because the revision is over. The bench gave the Commission four weeks to file its counter affidavit in the main matter and to answer the points in the note.
items.quote: Find out wherever you feel there are persons who should still be given a chance or opportunity. Bring it to their notice by way of representation. We will tell them to examine it, and we will keep it pending,
items.response: Counsel for the Commission said the revision was complete and that electors can still apply for corrections because the process is continuous, Times Now Navbharat reported.

items.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals against electors cleared by judicial officers (court-47, court-55)
items.headline: Bengal SIR Observer Says He Knew Nothing About CEO Office's 16 Lakh Appeals Against Cleared Voters
items.claim: Subrata Gupta, the Election Commission's special roll observer for West Bengal's revision, told The Wire that the observers had no information that the Chief Electoral Officer's office had filed appeals against electors whom judicial officers had examined and found eligible. He said the observers' role ended with the supplementary rolls, which listed about 33 lakh electors the judicial officers retained and 27 lakh they deleted, that he had heard that many of the 27 lakh deleted had appealed for inclusion and that the observers had no access to those records, and that they had heard of the appeals against inclusion only informally, with no official communication. The Commission told the Supreme Court in September that 16,10,311 such appeals had been filed. Its counter affidavit of 26 October (court-52) said a letter of 22 October from the Chief Electoral Officer's office stated that the office's officers had filed them as authorities under the Representation of the People Act. The Wire reported that Gupta, a retired IAS officer of the 1990 batch, now advises Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari.
items.quote: So, when you say that such a large number of appeals have been filed, that is information we are now receiving. We had no information about these appeals being filed or having been filed.
items.response: The Wire says it has written to the Chief Electoral Officer and the Additional Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal asking which officers filed the appeals, on whose decision and on what grounds. No reply is reported.

items.case: Revision petition by the Banbhoolpura police against the Haldwani magistrate's order of 6 October to register an FIR over 28 Form 7s (form7-36), court of the First Additional Sessions Judge
items.headline: 28 मतदाताओं के नाम कटवाने के मामले में उत्तराखंड पुलिस की किरकिरी, अदालत ने ठुकराई अर्जी
items.claim: The First Additional Sessions Judge, Sujit Kumar, on 30 October rejected the Banbhoolpura police's application to stay a Haldwani magistrate's order of 6 October to register an FIR over Form 7s seeking the deletion of 28 electors (form7-36), Dainik Jagran and Live Hindustan reported on 11 November. The station house officer of Banbhoolpura had filed a revision petition against the order and asked for it to be stayed. The court held that the police are not a victim or an aggrieved party in the matter and that registering an FIR and investigating on information of a cognisable offence is their legal duty, Dainik Jagran reported. By the account of the complainant's advocate, Manish Kumar Pandey, the court also questioned why no FIR had been registered for about 24 days. The revision petition is listed for 7 December 2026, and with the stay refused the magistrate's order stands. The complainant, a resident of Indiranagar who says he is the BJP's booth level agent, alleges that an unknown person misused his identity and login to file the Form 7s online on 12 August 2026 against electors of part 134, that he learnt of it on 20 August, and that he neither filed them nor authorised anyone to. Live Hindustan reports that the order of 6 October was passed by the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Shubhangi Gupta. It also reports the complainant's account that he went to Delhi on 30 October and raised the case with more than 20 MPs and senior leaders of the INDIA bloc, among them Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, P. Chidambaram, Mahua Moitra and Mehbooba Mufti.
items.quote: 30 अक्टूबर को न्यायाधीश सुजीत कुमार की अदालत में सुनवाई में कोर्ट ने स्पष्ट किया कि पुलिस इस मामले में पीड़ित या व्यथित पक्ष नहीं है। संज्ञेय अपराध की सूचना मिलने पर एफआईआर दर्ज कर विवेचना करना पुलिस का कानूनी दायित्व है।
items.response: The Nainital Senior Superintendent of Police, Manjunath T.C., told Live Hindustan that the police were examining the legal aspects of the case. The complainant's advocate told Dainik Jagran that no FIR had yet been registered and called that a serious matter. Neither report gives the police's grounds for the revision petition. Live Hindustan says the allegations have not been confirmed and that the investigation of the forms, user IDs and login records on the Commission's portal could show who filed them. The police had told the magistrate that the complaint concerned SIR Form 7s and that the complainant could object before the assistant returning officer (form7-36).

items.case: The petitioners' interim application on Form 7 in the SIR matters concerning Uttar Pradesh, Kerala and Chhattisgarh, Supreme Court
items.headline: UP SIR: Supreme Court asks ECI to take steps against filing Form 7 applications in bulk for voter deletion
items.claim: The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana directed on 30 October that the petitioners give the Election Commission's senior counsel a note of the irregularities in Form 7 applications in Uttar Pradesh that they say remain unresolved, and that the Commission then examine the facts, take corrective steps and file a compliance report, Bar and Bench reported. Counsel for the petitioners said the Court had asked the Commission on 5 August to respond to their interim application on Form 7 applications submitted before booth level officers in Chhattisgarh, Kerala and Uttar Pradesh, and that the issues in the first two states had since been addressed. He said 32 forms had been filed in one constituency against members of one community, that two forms on record were signed by the booth level officer, and that the Commission's affidavit carried material inconsistencies. He said FIRs had been directed in Telangana and Karnataka over similar filings and that nothing was done in Uttar Pradesh. Senior Advocate D.S. Naidu, for the Commission, said bulk Form 7 applications had been submitted and that officers checked them, found them false and did not act on them.
items.quote: The irregularities which have been brought to the notice of the Court shall be submitted to learned senior counsel appearing for the Election Commission of India by way of a note. On receipt thereof, let the Election Commission examine the factual aspects, thereafter take necessary corrective steps and file a compliance report,
items.response: Naidu said the Commission can examine further claims once a formal complaint is filed. LawChakra notes that the Court made no finding on the petitioners' allegations.

items.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals in Hemtabad (court-47, court-55)
items.headline: In One Bengal Seat, EC Appealed Against 599 Voters Even Before Their Adjudication Result Was Published
items.claim: In Hemtabad, a seat reserved for Scheduled Castes in Uttar Dinajpur district, the Election Commission has filed appeals against 15,381 of the 34,327 electors whom judicial officers examined and found eligible, 44.8%, The Wire reported. The appeal records were collected and verified by the Civic Research Group and given to The Wire, which says it analysed and verified them again. Of the 13,776 pending appeals, 12,758 carry the code that activists read, and The Wire says it verified, as the batch lodged on the evening of 5 April 2026, 978 carry the code for 6 April, and 40 were filed online. The paper reported that 599 of the appeals with the 5 April code concern electors cleared in the constituency's twelfth and last supplementary list, which was published on 6 April, so the appeals were on record before the list that cleared those electors was made public. The 599 come from nine polling stations, and 162 of them from part 237. Of the 2,65,162 electors on Hemtabad's draft roll, 52,542 were placed under adjudication, and judicial officers struck 18,215 off the roll and found 34,327 eligible. By The Wire's classification of names, which counts the elector's own name or a relative's, at least 97.7% of the electors appealed against have Muslim names, as do all 599, and at least 97% of all those the judges cleared do, so the appeals largely mirror who was cleared. The report says the Commission's appeal rate in the seat is close to its statewide rate of 49.4%. The tribunals have marked the other 1,605 of the seat's appeals disposed of.
items.quote: For 599 of those voters, the appeal came before their clearance had even been made public.
items.response: The report says the records cannot show whether the judicial officers' decisions were already on the Commission's portal before the list was published. The Commission told the Supreme Court on 26 October that officers of the office of the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer filed the appeals (court-52), and the report says it has not said which officers or on what grounds. No reply from the Commission is reported.

items.case: A petition by a group of advocates for guidelines on processions and protests near the Supreme Court, after the march of 12 October against the Chief Election Commissioner (court-44)
items.headline: SC seeks Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge’s replies on plea over Opposition march against CEC to top court
items.claim: A bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, on 3 November sought replies from the Congress president, Mallikarjun Kharge, and Rahul Gandhi, and from the Centre, on a petition by a group of advocates about the Opposition's march to the Supreme Court on 12 October against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and listed it for 23 November, Hindustan Times reported. The petition seeks guidelines regulating processions, protests, demonstrations and assemblies near the Court. The senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia, for the petitioners, told the Court that the march drew a large gathering of lawyers and supporters into the court precincts. He alleged in court that Gandhi pushed a woman journalist who was three months pregnant and that she had to be taken to hospital, and he moved an application for an FIR against Gandhi. These are allegations made for the petitioners, and the report gives no order of the Court on that application. The Solicitor General, Tushar Mehta, said the Centre would reply by the next date and asked that the matter be heard with a petition by the Network of Women in Media, India on alleged sexual harassment of women journalists covering protests in Delhi. The petition also names Akhilesh Yadav, the Delhi Commissioner of Police, the Supreme Court registry and the Congress as respondents.
items.quote: The plea is seeking guidelines regulating processions, protests, demonstrations and assemblies in the vicinity of the top court.
items.response: The senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, for Gandhi and Kharge, said their replies would be filed soon and asked that "irresponsible statements should not be made before the court takes up the matter".

items.case: The petition of Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, Supreme Court (court-54, court-60)
items.headline: SIR: Don’t fear, Supreme Court tells Delhi voters struck off draft electoral roll
items.claim: Prashant Bhushan, counsel for the petitioners in the Delhi case, mentioned the matter before a bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, on 4 November and said electors left off the draft feared prosecution if they filed Form 6 with its declaration that they were enrolling for the first time, although the Commission's letter of 3 November says no action will be taken on that ground alone (court-60), Hindustan Times and The Hindu reported. He said the letter went against what the Court had said at the hearing of 28 October (court-54), and that the Commission had extended the time for claims and objections in Delhi to 25 November. The Chief Justice asked how electors could be afraid when the Court was hearing the matter, told the petitioners to file an application, and said the Court would hear it on 19 November, the date the matter is already listed for. The Court passed no urgent order. The Hindu reports that the Chief Justice said the case would be heard after the Deepavali holidays, and that the bench said the Commission could be asked to extend the date further if required.
items.quote: How can they feel afraid like this when we are hearing the matter? You can file your application. The matter is already listed on November 19. We will hear it that day.
items.response: The Commission's letter No. 23/2026-ERS (Vol.-II) of 3 November 2026 says no action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 is to be started against an elector only because the elector was on an earlier roll and filed Form 6, provided the elector is not enrolled in another constituency (court-60). Neither report gives anything said for the Commission at the mentioning.

items.case: Petitions by Manoj Jha and an advocate challenging section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, Supreme Court
items.headline: SC seeks Centre, EC response on law giving blanket, lifelong immunity to CEC, Election Commissioners
items.claim: A bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission on 4 November on petitions challenging section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, and listed them for 18 December, The Hindu and The Indian Express reported. Section 16 bars every court from entertaining or continuing any civil or criminal proceedings against a serving or former Chief Election Commissioner or Election Commissioner for any act, thing or word in the discharge of official duty. The Hindu reports that the petitions were filed by the RJD Member of Parliament Manoj Jha and by an advocate. The petitions argue that the section bars the jurisdiction of the constitutional courts and interferes with judicial review, which has been held to be part of the basic structure of the Constitution. The advocate's plea, as The Hindu quotes it, says the section bars all kinds of prosecution, gives immunity for life and covers acts that may be outside lawful authority. The petitions point out that the President and the Governors are protected from criminal proceedings only while in office. The advocate's plea, as The Indian Express quotes it, says a voter whose name is wrongly deleted from the roll is left without a remedy, and it cites the paper's reports of alleged differences between the Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners over the SIR. The Indian Express reports that the Court is already hearing a petition by the NGO Lok Prahari against the same section, in which it issued notice in January and declined to stay the section.
items.quote: A voter whose name is wrongly deleted from the electoral roll, a candidate prejudiced by a mala fide act, and any citizen aggrieved by corruption in the functioning of the Commission are left without a remedy.
items.response: Neither report gives anything said for the Centre or the Commission at the hearing. The advocate's plea says the section was added to the Bill by an amendment that gave no reasons for it, and that the Minister's justification in Parliament did not show it was needed.

items.case: West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals of retired judges (court-18)
items.headline: Bengal SIR tribunal sees another exit as retired judge Biswajit Basu resigns
items.claim: The retired Calcutta High Court judge Biswajit Basu resigned on 7 November as head of one of West Bengal's 19 SIR appellate tribunals, citing personal reasons, and sent his resignation to the High Court's Chief Justice, Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge, The Indian Express, The Hindu, the Hindustan Times and The New Indian Express reported. He was one of the two tribunal heads hearing appeals from Murshidabad district, and The New Indian Express reports that he and Indrajit Chatterjee each had 11 of its 22 constituencies. The Times of India reports that Murshidabad had over 7.4 lakh appeals pending when the Commission reported to the Supreme Court in September. The reports count the resignations differently. The Hindu, the Hindustan Times, The New Indian Express and PTI, as The Times of India carried it, call him the fourth to resign, after the former Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court T.S. Sivagnanam and the retired judges Ranjit Kumar Bag and Indrajit Chatterjee, and The Hindu says Sivagnanam was the first, in May 2026. The Telegraph also calls him the fourth and does not name the others. The Indian Express calls him the second within a month in one report and the third in another, and The Times of India's Kolkata edition calls him the third in seven months. Those three reports and The Telegraph say Chatterjee stayed on after the Commission promised to deal with his complaints about the commute and its portal. The Indian Express reports, from sources, that Basu was unhappy with the tribunal's infrastructure and its login procedures, and its second report says the requirement of Aadhaar to log in to the Commission's portal was the last straw. The Times of India's Kolkata edition reports that the tribunals have not been examining appeals since 21 September, because the judges refused to log in to a new portal the Commission introduced. The Telegraph reports that no order has been uploaded to the portal since then, because the judges refused to share their Aadhaar details. Basu also chairs the state government's Commission on Institutional Corruption.
items.quote: “I have resigned from my duties of SIR tribunals. The resignation is for personal reasons,” Basu said on Saturday.
items.response: An official of the Commission told PTI that with both judges hearing Murshidabad's appeals stepping down within a month, the disposal of appeals from Murshidabad had effectively come to a standstill, as The Times of India carried it. The Trinamool Congress leader and lawyer Baiswanor Chatterjee asked what use the tribunal was when its judges had heard very few appeals, and the state BJP spokesperson Sayantan Basu said there was no reason to read anything into the resignation, since Justice Basu heads the inquiry commission probing corruption cases and was probably unable to spare the time, the Hindustan Times reported. No report says who will hear the appeals he was hearing.

items.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals against electors cleared by judicial officers (court-47, court-55, court-58)
items.headline: 9 in 10 Voters the Election Commission Wants Removed From Bengal’s Rolls Have Muslim Names
items.claim: The Wire's classification of the names in appeal records compiled by the Civic Research Group finds that at least 14,39,797 of the 16,08,175 electors against whose inclusion the Election Commission has appealed, after judicial officers examined them and found them eligible, have Muslim names, 89.5%. The report gives Muslims as 27% of West Bengal's population in the 2011 Census and about 29% of its electorate. Grouping seats by the minority share of their population, The Wire finds Muslim names among 61.7% of the electors appealed against in the 89 seats where that share is under 10%, 83.8% in the 71 seats at 10% to 20%, 90.3% in the 51 seats at 20% to 30%, 93.8% in the 39 seats at 30% to 50% and 96.6% in the 41 seats over 50%. In every group the Commission appealed against between 46.5% and 51.2% of the electors the judges cleared, and the report says that across seats there is almost no relationship between a seat's Muslim share and the share of its cleared electors appealed against. It counts 137 constituencies where at least 90% of the electors appealed against have Muslim names, and 2,62,416 electors with Muslim names facing appeals in the 160 seats where Muslims are under a fifth of the population. In Purba Medinipur district, where it gives the Muslim share of the population as 12.0%, 92.9% of the 27,091 electors appealed against have Muslim names, and in Purba Bardhaman, at 23.3%, 95.9% of 90,637 do. In Murshidabad the figure is 98.2%. In Krishnaganj in Nadia, a seat reserved for Scheduled Castes, Muslim names are 157 of the 2,412 electors appealed against, 6.5%, against a population share of 5.7%, and in Jadavpur they are 125 of 881, 14.2%, against 1.2%. The report also uses a second set of records, of appeals by electors whom judicial officers deleted, and does not say who compiled them. It counts 22,17,619 such appellants among the 27,06,057 deleted, 82%, and finds Muslim names among 79.3% of them. The two sets of records cover 38,25,794 of the 59,59,458 electors sent to judicial officers in these constituencies, and The Wire counts 31,99,122 of them with Muslim names, which it says means that at least 53.7% of all those sent to adjudication had Muslim names even if none of the others did. In the seats under 10%, it finds Muslim names among about a third of the deleted electors who appealed and among 61.7% of the cleared electors the Commission appealed against.
items.quote: Nine in every ten West Bengal voters whom the Election Commission of India (ECI) is seeking to remove from the electoral rolls, even after judicial officers have found them eligible, have Muslim names.
items.response: The Wire says it has written to the office of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer and two Additional Chief Electoral Officers asking which officers filed the appeals, under what provision officers of that office can appeal against electors in constituencies they do not administer, whether registration officers were consulted, on what grounds and by what criteria electors were chosen, and whether each case was reviewed. It has also asked for the letter of 22 October that the Commission cites in its affidavit. It says the report will be updated when the office replies. The Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October (court-52), as the report quotes it, says officers of the Chief Electoral Officer's office filed the appeals as authorities under the Representation of the People Act and that the matters were not brought to the Commission. No reply from the Commission is reported.

items.case: The petition of Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, Supreme Court (court-54, court-60)
items.headline: ECI Urged to Restore Old Voter IDs for All Excluded During SIR, Not Just In 7 States
items.claim: Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, the petitioners in the Supreme Court case on Delhi's revision, wrote on 10 November 2026 to the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and the Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, asking that the remedies in the Commission's letter of 6 November to seven states be given to every elector in the country who was left off a draft roll and placed on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors, The Wire reported. The letter of 6 November lets such electors in Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland seek inclusion on an enumeration form in place of Form 6. The petitioners write that these "vital remedies" must be extended to all voters in a similar legal standing. Citing 13.30 crore electors on the rolls before the revision who were left off the drafts across the country, they say the new safeguards help only the 4.52 crore in the seven states. They say the new procedure treats unequally the electors who filed Form 6 under the Commission's earlier instructions and were issued new EPIC numbers, because Form 6 carries a declaration that the applicant is a first-time voter, which the Supreme Court called a "structural incongruity" in the hearings on Delhi's revision (court-54). They ask that every elector on these lists be allowed to file an enumeration form, that the Form 6 applications such electors have already filed be cancelled and their original EPIC numbers restored, and that the Commission publish regular updates on a dashboard or in daily bulletins of how many electors on the lists have filed enumeration forms and how many have been approved.
items.quote: People who took remedial action as per ECI’s instructions prior to November 6, 2026, should not be misclassified by being processed as new voters and prejudiced by the erasure of their prior presence on the electoral rolls,
items.response: No reply from the Commission was reported by 11 November. The Commission's letter of 6 November says an elector in the seven states who has already filed Form 6 during the revision need not submit the enumeration form, and that the application is to be decided under its letter of 3 November (court-60), which says such a Form 6 is not false merely because the elector was enrolled before.

items.case: Appeals against inclusion before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals (court-47)
items.headline: In 7k WB booths, all cleared voters face EC exclusion plea
items.claim: In 7,335 polling booths across 23 districts of West Bengal, every elector whom judicial officers examined and found eligible in the adjudication of logical discrepancies faces an appeal against inclusion before the SIR appellate tribunals, the Hindustan Times reported on 11 November from a report on the tribunals by the Civic Research Group, which it describes as a research collective based in Kolkata. The paper reports that these booths held 27,277 such electors, that by the group's analysis the appeals against 21,615 of them, 79%, were pending and those against 5,662 had been disposed of, and that every one of the state's 294 constituencies has at least one such booth. It reports from the group's report that the share of cleared electors facing an appeal is highest in Kalimpong at 71.4%, Purba Bardhaman at 59.7% and Darjeeling at 59.3%, and lowest in Dakshin Dinajpur at 39.3%, Cooch Behar at 39.4% and Nadia at 39.5%. The group compiled its statewide figures from the tribunals' appeal portal, the paper reports, and its published count is 16,08,175 appeals against inclusion, 15,26,933 of them pending and 81,242 disposed of. The group says the portal does not show the outcome of a disposed appeal.
items.quote: These 7,335 booths held 27,277 voters who judicial officers cleared. Of these, 21,615 (79%) were pending and 5,662 were disposed of, according to the CRG analysis.
items.response: The Commission declined to comment, the paper reported. A senior official of the Commission told it, on condition of anonymity, that the appeals were filed by officials of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer who had the authority to do so as per the Supreme Court, that this was a technicality, that an appeal against an elector does not mean the elector was ineligible to vote, and that the electors' names appeared in the supplementary lists, which meant they were eligible to vote in the Assembly election. The Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October cited a letter from the Chief Electoral Officer's office saying the office's officers had filed the appeals as authorities under the Representation of the People Act (court-57).

items.case: Writ petition over an EWS certificate withheld from a son because a parent was deleted in the revision, Calcutta High Court
items.headline: Calcutta High Court Issues Notice On Plea Challenging Denial Of EWS Certificate To Son Over Parent's Deletion From SIR Rolls
items.claim: Justice Krishna Rao of the Calcutta High Court issued notice on a petition challenging the withholding of an Economically Weaker Section certificate from a candidate solely because his parent's name was deleted from the roll in the revision, and permitted an early hearing, LiveLaw reported on 12 November. The petitioner contends that the authorities are withholding the certificate on that ground alone, and the petitioner's counsel told the court that the son is eligible for it. The son had taken part in a government recruitment process and could go no further without the certificate, which is why the matter was urgent. The petition questions the link between a parent's deletion from the roll and the son's entitlement to the certificate.
items.quote: The petitioner approached the High Court contending that the authorities were withholding the certificate only on the ground of the deletion of the parent's name from the SIR rolls.
items.response: LiveLaw gives no response from the State or from the authority that issues the certificate, and no date for the next hearing.

items.case: Writ petition by a student refused a passport because his mother was deleted in the revision, Calcutta High Court
items.headline: Calcutta High Court Seeks State Response On Plea Against Passport Denial Over Mother's Name Being Deleted From SIR
items.claim: Justice Krishna Rao of the Calcutta High Court directed the West Bengal government to file a report on a petition by a student who says he cannot obtain a passport because his mother's name was deleted from the roll in the revision, LiveLaw reported on 12 November. The student told the court that he had secured admission to a medical college in Bangladesh, that his own name is still on the roll and that he has voted. The court said the State had to be made a party and cautioned the petitioner against making the SIR tribunal a respondent, and he was directed to remove the tribunal from the respondents and add the State of West Bengal. The State is to file its report on the next date of hearing.
items.quote: They explained that the mother's name had to be mentioned while printing the passport and questioned how the passport could be printed when her name no longer figured in the SIR electoral rolls.
items.response: The passport authorities opposed the petition and said a police report should be obtained, LiveLaw reported. They said the mother's name had to be printed on the passport and asked how it could be printed when her name was no longer on the roll.

items.case: Application by Karnataka's State Election Commission on the elections to the five city corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority, Supreme Court
items.headline: GBA polls: Karnataka SEC seeks Supreme Court nod to use pre-SIR rolls
items.claim: Karnataka's State Election Commission applied to the Supreme Court on 12 November for leave to hold the elections to the five city corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority on the final rolls published on 18 April 2026, and for time until 31 January 2027 to complete them on those earlier ward-wise rolls, Deccan Herald reported on 13 November. It also asked for leave to hold the elections to all panchayats and urban local bodies in the state on the Assembly rolls as they stood on 1 October 2025. The Supreme Court had directed on 17 July that the five corporation elections be completed by 31 December 2026. The State Election Commission told the Court that unforeseen delays in the final publication of the Assembly rolls on 27 October, and the Election Commission's not supplying complete and authenticated roll data since then, had disrupted its schedule. It said it needs the full data, with the additions, deletions, transpositions and corrections, to divide the rolls by ward and to map, verify and publish them. Deccan Herald reports that the data had still not been supplied when the application was filed. It estimated that if it had to wait for the new rolls it would need at least two months after receiving the data to prepare the ward rolls and another month to hold the elections. It said it had already prepared and published rolls for the five corporations from the data of 1 October 2025 that the Election Commission had supplied, and had printed and distributed state voter identity cards on that basis. On 5 November it had told the five corporations to prepare ward rolls from the final rolls of 27 October (protest-66).
items.quote: As of the filing of the application, this data had still not been supplied. If forced to wait for the fresh rolls, the SEC estimated it would need at least two months after receiving the data to prepare ward-wise lists, followed by another month to conduct the elections.
items.response: Deccan Herald gives no response from the Election Commission or from the state government, and no date on which the Court will hear the application.

items.case: Writ petition by an Army aspirant refused a domicile certificate because his mother was deleted in the revision, Calcutta High Court
items.headline: Indian Army Aspirant Moves Calcutta High Court After Denial Of Domicile Certificate Over Deletion Of Mother's Name In SIR
items.claim: Justice Krishna Rao of the Calcutta High Court agreed to hear a petition by an Indian Army aspirant who asks for a domicile certificate so that he can take part in the second phase of the Army's recruitment process, LiveLaw reported on 13 November. The petitioner says the authorities refused him the certificate because his mother's name was deleted from the roll in the revision. He told the court that his father's name is still on the roll after the revision, and that he has only just turned 21 and his own name has not yet been registered in the revision. Without the certificate he cannot go further in the recruitment process. The court listed the matter for hearing.
items.quote: The petitioner approached the court after the authorities allegedly refused to issue him a domicile certificate on the ground that his mother's name had been deleted from the electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.
items.response: LiveLaw gives no response from the State or from the authority that issues domicile certificates, and no date for the hearing.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026, the petition on the Commission's functioning (court-52, court-53), in which LiveLaw reports the affidavit was filed, and the petition on Delhi's revision, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026 (court-54, court-60, court-61), with which The Hindu reports it, Supreme Court
items.headline: ‘Alive’ to voters’ need to find their names on the electoral roll, ECI assures Supreme Court
items.claim: The Election Commission filed a supplementary affidavit in the Supreme Court on 14 November 2026, The Hindu reported. LiveLaw reports that Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu filed it on behalf of the Commission in the writ petition that leads the batch on the Commission's functioning, W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026 (court-52, court-53). The interrogatories that INDIA bloc leaders asked the Court on 16 November for leave to serve also describe it as sworn by Yeturu (court-78). The Indian Express describes it as a joint affidavit of the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and the Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. The Hindu gives no case number and reports the affidavit together with the concerns about Form 6 raised by the petitioners in the case on Delhi's revision, in which Anjali Bhardwaj is a petitioner (court-54, court-60, court-61). The affidavit says the Commission took note of the Court's suggestion at the hearing of 28 October that it reach out to electors left off as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, and that by a communication of 6 November it directed the Chief Electoral Officers of the states and union territories where the revision is under way, which LiveLaw lists as Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland, to let electors left off the draft roll submit the enumeration form (Annexure A) to the Electoral Registration Officer or Assistant Electoral Registration Officer for their current ordinary residence. An elector who has not shifted may submit the signed form with an Annexure B statement giving the reason it was not submitted earlier, in person or through family members, to the Electoral Registration Officer, the Assistant Electoral Registration Officer or the booth level officer, and that an option to submit it online with e-sign will be available on ECINET. An elector who has shifted within the state does not need Form 8 and may submit the enumeration form with an Annexure C statement giving the new address and Assembly constituency, and proof of address, to the Electoral Registration Officer or Assistant Electoral Registration Officer of the new constituency. The affidavit says booth-wise lists of electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate are to be displayed afresh with the probable reasons why they were not included, and that Electoral Registration Officers are to process the enumeration forms of these electors under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 and re-assign the same EPIC number to them. It says a previously enrolled elector who has already filed Form 6 need not submit the enumeration form again, and that such applications will be processed under the clarification of 3 November (court-60). It repeats that clarification, that no prosecution will be launched against anyone for filing Form 6 merely because the applicant was enrolled before the revision and was not in the draft roll, provided the applicant is not enrolled in any other Parliamentary or Assembly constituency and the declaration is otherwise in accordance with law. ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, also reported the affidavit and says the Chief Electoral Officers have been asked to give the clarification wide publicity, in local languages as well. The affidavit says a mechanism has been directed to ensure that no eligible elector is deprived of the chance to be included in the final roll, with due care to avoid duplicate enrolment. It also says that after a new Deputy Election Commissioner joined on 2 November, a work order of 4 November gave oversight of the Commission's IT division to a Senior Deputy Election Commissioner, that the Director General (IT) puts the division's files to the Commission through that officer, and that the IT division has always been under the supervision of a Deputy Election Commissioner. The Times of India also reported the affidavit, from PTI. The batch on the Commission's functioning was tentatively listed for 17 November (court-53), and the Delhi case is listed for 19 November (court-61).
items.quote: Electors who have not shifted may submit the signed Enumeration Form (Annexure A) with the Annexure-B statement giving the reason for the earlier non-submission of the Enumeration Form.
items.response: The affidavit is the Commission's own account of what it has done since the hearing of 28 October (court-54). The Indian Express and ThePrint quote it as saying it 'remains committed to its constitutional duty of ensuring the purity of the election process' and that problems 'have been and will be' arising from time to time. None of the five reports gives a response from the petitioners or a hearing on the affidavit.
