items.response: Neither report gives a statement from the Chief Electoral Officer's office or from the tribunals' judges on the order, or says how many judges it covers.

items.headline: Jharkhand Assembly passes resolution against SIR
items.claim: The Week, carrying a PTI report, said the Jharkhand Assembly passed a resolution opposing the SIR, moved by Parliamentary Affairs Minister Radhakrishna Kishore on behalf of the INDIA bloc. The BJP opposed it. When a Congress member asked for a vote, the Speaker ruled that it stood passed because the ruling coalition had a majority.
items.quote: Ranchi, Aug 26 (PTI) A resolution opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was passed in the Jharkhand assembly on Tuesday. ... Replying to him, the speaker said, "The resolution stands automatically passed as the ruling coalition has a majority in the House."

items.headline: Kerala Assembly passes unanimous resolution against SIR
items.claim: The Siasat Daily, carrying a PTI report, said the Kerala Assembly unanimously passed a resolution moved by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan against the SIR in the state, with the Congress-led opposition backing it.
items.quote: Kerala Assembly on Monday unanimously passed a resolution against the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s move to carry out the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voters’ list in the state and urged the poll body to conduct the revision of voters’ list in a transparent manner.

items.headline: Punjab House resolution seeks probe into electoral ‘irregularities’ under CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.claim: The Punjab Vidhan Sabha passed a resolution by voice vote on 23 October asking for an independent and impartial inquiry into alleged irregularities in voter lists, the electoral process and the functioning of the Election Commission under the Chief Election Commissioner, The Indian Express reported. The paper calls it the first resolution of its kind by an Assembly against the Chief Election Commissioner. Members of the Congress, the Shiromani Akali Dal and the BJP were not in the House when it passed. These are the resolution's and the speakers' allegations.
items.quote: This House demands establishment of an independent, impartial, and credible investigative mechanism to inquire into alleged irregularities concerning the electoral process and voter lists under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, so that the truth can come to light and accountability can be fixed,
items.response: The report carries no response from the Commission or the BJP.

items.headline: Jharkhand Assembly passes resolution seeking immediate halt to SIR
items.claim: The Jharkhand Assembly passed a government resolution on 25 November, the first day of a two-day special session, asking for the SIR in the state to be halted, PTI, The New Indian Express and The Times of India reported. PTI and The Times of India report that it was passed by voice vote. It was moved by the minister Radha Krishna Kishore. PTI reports that it will be sent to the Centre and other competent authorities, seeking a fresh standard operating procedure framed in consultation with political parties to make the process transparent. The Times of India reports that it asks for the exercise to be suspended until a simpler and inclusive framework is drawn up in consultation with states and political parties, and that it says the state had given its consent in principle to the SIR. By the resolution, as The New Indian Express and The Times of India give it, Jharkhand had about 2.64 crore electors and 2.21 crore were on the draft roll, so that the names of about 16% were left off the draft. About 27% of the electors on the draft were sent notices as doubtful, more than 75% of those notices were over logical discrepancies such as differences in the spelling of a parent's name, in age or in the number of dependants, and more than 38% of the electorate were either left off or sent notices. The New Indian Express reports that the resolution also sets out the difficulties of tribal electors who lack old documents, of migrant workers who cannot return home to fill in forms, of electors born before 1987 in producing their parents' documents and of married women whose names differ after they move, and objects that Aadhaar, ration cards and khatiyan land records are not accepted as documents. Kishore told the House that the Election Commission was working as the Centre's puppet and that the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, was necessary to protect the Constitution, PTI reported. When the JD(U) member Saryu Roy said that the written resolution does not mention the removal, Kishore agreed and asked the Speaker to make his statement on it part of the proceedings, PTI and Dainik Jagran reported. The Leader of the Opposition, Babulal Marandi of the BJP, opposed the resolution, said the session was politically motivated and told the Speaker that the Assembly was no place to pass and forward a resolution for the Chief Election Commissioner's removal. He said the government had hidden the break-up of the deleted names, which he gave, by PTI's report, as 7.63 lakh dead, 15.53 lakh shifted, 4.38 lakh duplicate and 14.50 lakh untraceable out of 43 lakh, and he urged the government to cooperate with the Commission in including those left out.
items.quote: There is an urgent need to halt the SIR exercise immediately and to issue a fresh standard operating procedure to ensure transparency in the process,
items.response: The reports carry no reply from the Election Commission or the Chief Electoral Officer. Marandi's answer for the BJP is in the claim. The figures in the resolution are the state government's and the break-up is Marandi's, and neither report gives the resolution's full text.

items.headline: Bandh Against SIR By INDIA Alliance Throws Life Out Of Gear In Bihar
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that a Bihar bandh called by the INDIA bloc parties against the SIR disrupted life across much of the state, with Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav taking part.
items.quote: Patna: The Bihar Bandh called by parties of INDIA Alliance to protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) before the Assembly elections, threw life out of gear in most parts of the state.

items.headline: Assembly Protest Bihar: Anti-SIR Demonstrations Disrupt Monsoon Session Opening Day
items.claim: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said opposition members protested against the SIR inside the Bihar Assembly on the first day of its monsoon session, with CPI(ML) Liberation legislators wearing black.
items.quote: Patna: Protests against special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar rocked the state assembly on the inaugural day of the monsoon session on Monday.

items.headline: Sonia, Kharge, Rahul, Akhilesh Join Opposition Leaders In Protest Against SIR
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that INDIA bloc MPs protested at the Makar Dwar of Parliament against the Bihar SIR for a fifth day running and demanded that it be rolled back.
items.quote: Several MPs of the INDIA bloc parties, including Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge and Congress parliamentary party chairperson Sonia Gandhi, protested in the Parliament House complex on Monday against the Election Commission's voter roll revision in Bihar, and demanded its rollback.

items.headline: Police Stop March of 300 Opposition MPs Against Bihar SIR, Detain Lawmakers
items.claim: The Wire reported that Delhi Police detained opposition MPs, among them Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, when their march from Parliament to the Election Commission against the Bihar SIR was stopped, and that they were released in the afternoon.
items.quote: Opposition MPs including leaders of opposition in the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha – Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi – were detained by Delhi Police today (August 11) after they were stopped during their protest march against the ‘special intensive revision’ of the voter rolls in Bihar.
items.response: The Wire reported that the Commission had written to Jairam Ramesh the day before asking for the names of 30 members for a meeting “due to limitation of space”.

items.headline: Rahul Gandhi Kicks Off 'Vote Adhikar Yatra' In Bihar To 'Protect' Electoral Rights
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that Rahul Gandhi began a 16-day Vote Adhikar Yatra from Sasaram against the SIR in Bihar, due to end with a rally in Patna on 1 September. The Congress leader alleged that the SIR was being done to steal votes.
items.quote: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi began his ‘Vote Adhikar Yatra’ from Sasaram on Sunday, protesting against the irregularities in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls by the Election Commission (EC) in Bihar, and with a vow to prevent anyone from stealing anyone's votes.

items.headline: Tamil Nadu all-party meeting opposes Election Commission’s voter roll revision, to move Supreme Court
items.claim: The News Minute reported that an all-party meeting chaired by Chief Minister M.K. Stalin, attended by nearly 50 parties, resolved to approach the Supreme Court against the SIR in Tamil Nadu. The AIADMK and the BJP were not invited and several other parties stayed away.
items.quote: In Tamil Nadu, an all-party meeting on November 2 by the ruling Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and chaired by Chief Minister MK Stalin resolved to approach the Supreme Court of India against the Election Commission’s controversial Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in the state ahead of the 2026 Assembly elections.

items.headline: Mamata Leads Massive Kolkata Rally Against SIR, Vows To ‘Topple Delhi’ Over Voter List Purge
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee led a procession in Kolkata against the SIR. She called the SIR an assault on people's existence and democratic rights.
items.quote: Kolkata: Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee led a huge procession from Dr B.R. Ambedkar’s statue to Thakurbari, Constitution in hand, joined by lakhs, including Matua and other communities, to protest the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

items.headline: DMK, Allies Protest Against SIR Revision in Tamil Nadu
items.claim: Akashvani News reported that the DMK and its alliance partners held protest demonstrations across Tamil Nadu against the SIR, with MPs, MLAs and district functionaries taking part.
items.quote: The ruling DMK and its alliance partners are holding protest demonstrations across the State against SIR exercise.

items.headline: Mamata leads anti-SIR march; EC to meet TMC leaders on Nov 28
items.claim: The Tribune reported that Mamata Banerjee led a three-km march from Bongaon to Thakurnagar in North 24 Parganas against the SIR, after addressing a rally at Bangaon.
items.quote: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Tuesday led a three-km march from Bongaon's Chandpara to Matua- heartland Thakurnagar in North 24 Parganas district to protest the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in the state.
items.response: The Tribune reported that the Commission granted a five-member TMC delegation a meeting on 28 November.

items.headline: Opposition in Assam protests 'vote theft' through SR; slams Himanta, BJP
items.claim: The Siasat Daily, carrying a PTI report, said the united opposition held a protest at Chachal in Guwahati against alleged irregularities in the draft rolls of Assam's Special Revision. Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi accused Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma of misusing the Election Commission.
items.quote: Guwahati : The united opposition on Friday held a protest against alleged irregularities in the draft electoral rolls and “vote theft” through the Special Revision (SR) ahead of assembly elections in Assam.
items.response: The report said the Commission stated that the flagged names had not yet been deleted and would only be processed after formal applications in the claims and objections period.

items.headline: सपा ने फॉर्म-7 में धांधली का आरोप लगाया:सुल्तानपुर में मतदाता सूची से नाम हटाने के खिलाफ प्रदर्शन
items.claim: The Samajwadi Party demonstrated at the Sultanpur Collectorate on 3 February 2026 and gave the District Magistrate a memorandum for the Chief Election Commissioner, Dainik Bhaskar reported. The party alleged that pre-printed Form 7s in one handwriting were being submitted in bulk against voters from backward, Dalit and minority communities, and asked for them to be cancelled and for FIRs under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
items.quote: पार्टी के अनुसार, गाँवों और नगरों में 'प्री-प्रिंटेड' फॉर्म-7 थोक में जमा किए जा रहे हैं। इन फॉर्मों में एक ही लिखावट और छपे-छपाए विवरण पाए गए हैं, जो बूथ लेवल ऑफिसर (बीएलओ) के पास बड़ी संख्या में पहुँच रहे हैं।

items.headline: Citizens Protest Special Intensive Revision In Bengaluru's Freedom Park
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that trade unions, women's groups, student bodies and Dalit and minority rights groups protested against the SIR at Freedom Park in Bengaluru under the banner My Vote, My Right, and urged the state government to take a stand.
items.quote: Bengaluru: Citizens gathered at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on Saturday to protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

items.headline: Mamata Ends Dharna Against 'Flaws' In SIR
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that Mamata Banerjee ended her sit-in against the SIR on its fifth day after the Supreme Court ordered appellate tribunals to hear appeals against exclusions in West Bengal. She said the protest was suspended temporarily.
items.quote: Kolkata: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Tuesday lifted her dharna against the "flawed SIR" on the fifth day, saying the protest was being suspended temporarily after the Supreme Court ordered the setting up of an appellate mechanism regarding the voter list revision.

items.headline: Congress Alleges Irregularities In SIR In Uttarakhand, Seeks Election Commission's Intervention
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that a Congress delegation led by Kumari Selja staged a sit-in outside the Election Commission headquarters in Delhi over the SIR in Uttarakhand after saying it was not allowed into the premises.
items.quote: The delegation staged a sit-in outside the ECI headquarters. Later, they submitted a representation to a poll panel official, highlighting alleged discrepancies in the ongoing SIR of electoral roll in the Himalayan state.

items.headline: Congress protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar spread across India; Gaurav Gogoi detained in Guwahati
items.claim: Business Today reported that Congress workers protested in several states demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the handling of the SIR, after The Indian Express reported objections recorded by two Election Commissioners.
items.quote: Congress workers staged protests across several parts of India on Friday, demanding the resignation and removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the Election Commission’s handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
items.response: Business Today reported that the Commission rejected the characterisation of these exchanges as institutional dissent and said final decisions on the SIR were unanimous.

items.headline: Congress protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar spread across India; Gaurav Gogoi detained in Guwahati
items.claim: Business Today reported that police detained Assam Congress president and MP Gaurav Gogoi during a protest in Guwahati demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.
items.quote: In Guwahati, Assam Congress president and MP Gaurav Gogoi was detained by police while participating in a protest against Gyanesh Kumar.

items.headline: Jantar Mantar Protest Demanding Gyanesh Kumar’s Resignation Sees Mass Detentions Amid Delhi Police Crackdown
items.claim: The Quint reported that police detained protesters from civil society groups and student organisations at Jantar Mantar, among them CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, as they demanded the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation and a rollback of the SIR.
items.quote: Several civil society groups, the All India Students’ Association ... Swaraj Party leader Yogendra Yadav, and activist Prashant Bhushan held a protest at Jantar Mantar to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and a rollback of the SIR exercise.

items.headline: Congress workers protest against CEC in Lucknow, clash with police
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said police detained Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai and hundreds of party workers in Lucknow after they were stopped while marching to demand the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.
items.quote: Lucknow, Sep 25 (PTI) Congress workers, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, clashed with police here on Friday after they were stopped from marching towards the Uttar Pradesh Assembly.

items.headline: 'Gyanesh, it's done bro!': Youth Congress marches to Jantar Mantar; water cannons in Bihar, Punjab
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying an ANI report, said police used water cannons on Congress workers in Patna who were protesting against the Chief Election Commissioner as part of the party's nationwide programme over the SIR.
items.quote: In Patna, Bihar, police used water cannons to disperse Congress workers protesting against Gyanesh Kumar and demanding his resignation.
items.response: The report said the Commission described operational queries and internal feedback as part of the normal functioning of a multi-member body and said all final SIR decisions were unanimous.

items.headline: 'Gyanesh, it's done bro!': Youth Congress marches to Jantar Mantar; water cannons in Bihar, Punjab
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying an ANI report, said police used water cannons on Punjab Congress workers demonstrating in Chandigarh as part of the party's protests over the SIR.
items.quote: Similar scenes were witnessed in Punjab, where police deployed water cannons as Congress workers staged a demonstration in Chandigarh.

items.headline: HP Congress protests in Shimla; demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal, arrest
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said the Himachal Pradesh Congress protested outside the Election Commission office in Shimla, burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner and raised slogans against the SIR.
items.quote: The Congress workers burned an effigy of Kumar, blackened the Commission’s board, and wrote “Chor Aayog” on it. They also raised slogans against the CEC and the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: Meghalaya Cong burns Gyanesh Kumar effigy, demands his removal and arrest
items.claim: UNI reported that Congress workers in Shillong, led by state Congress president Vincent H. Pala, burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner and demanded his removal amid the row over the SIR.
items.quote: Congress workers in Meghalaya burnt an effigy of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar here on Friday, demanding his immediate arrest and removal amid an ongoing row over the functioning of the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: Uttarakhand Congress gheraos EC office, demands CEC's resignation
items.claim: Asianet Newsable reported that the Uttarakhand Congress marched in Dehradun, surrounded the Election Commission office and burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner. The party raised concerns over how names were added and deleted and how objections were disposed of.
items.quote: The protesters marched from the Pradesh Congress office to the Secretariat, raising slogans, and later "gheraoed the Election Commission office". They also burnt an effigy of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

items.headline: Karnataka Cong protests against SIR, demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said the Karnataka Congress, with Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, protested at Freedom Park in Bengaluru against the SIR and demanded the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.
items.quote: Bengaluru, Sep 26 (PTI) Karnataka Congress on Saturday staged a protest at Freedom Park here against the Election Commission’s SIR exercise, demanding the resignation and arrest of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
items.response: The Election Commission, however, has asserted that its official orders, decisions and administrative directions have full legal sanction, and that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberations within any institution.

items.headline: Gehlot, Dotasra detained during Cong protest in Jaipur over SIR row
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said police used water cannons and detained former Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot and state Congress chief Govind Singh Dotasra during a march to the State Election Commission office in Jaipur over alleged SIR irregularities.
items.quote: Jaipur, Sep 28 (PTI) Former chief minister Ashok Gehlot and Rajasthan Congress chief Govind Singh Dotasra were among senior party leaders detained by police during a protest march to the State Election Commission office here on Monday over alleged vote theft and irregularities in SIR.

items.headline: ‘EC Played Like a Puppet’: INDIA Bloc Seals Roadmap to Ramp Up Anti-SIR Agitation
items.claim: Leaders of the INDIA bloc, 33 of them from 19 parties, agreed a plan of district marches from 2 to 8 October, a march of opposition MPs to the Commission on 6 October, a meeting with the President in the second week of October and five rallies including one in Delhi on 1 November, The Wire reported. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the Commission was being used as a puppet by the Prime Minister and the Home Minister.
items.quote: The leaders' six-point action plan included "Save Democracy" marches at the district level from October 2-8, opposition MPs march to the Election Commission on October 6, a meeting with the President in the second week of October, five major rallies by the opposition including a major rally in New Delhi on November 1 as well as an appeal for the early resolution of all cases relating to the SIR and electoral matters pending before the Supreme Court.

items.headline: ‘Attempt to kill democracy’: Hyderabad civil society protests SIR, demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation
items.claim: The South First reported that more than a dozen civil society groups held a day-long protest at Dharna Chowk in Hyderabad, demanding that the SIR be scrapped and the Chief Election Commissioner resign.
items.quote: Citizens in Hyderabad gathered at Dharna Chowk on Saturday, 3 October, for a day-long protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: Garjana Morcha: Uddhav, Raj Thackeray Lead Protest Seeking Gyanesh Kumar’s Resignation, Scrapping Of Maharashtra SIR
items.claim: The Free Press Journal reported that Uddhav Thackeray of the Shiv Sena (UBT) and Raj Thackeray of the MNS led the Virat Garjana Morcha in Mumbai seeking the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation. Raj Thackeray demanded that the SIR in Maharashtra be cancelled.
items.quote: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray on Sunday led a protest seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of irregularities in the special intensive revision process.

items.headline: Delhi Police Detain Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi During INDIA Bloc Protest Seeking CEC's Resignation
items.claim: The Wire reported that police stopped an INDIA bloc march from Parliament to the Election Commission, and that opposition MPs held a sit-in at the All India Radio building until police detained Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra that night.
items.quote: As night fell on Tuesday, October 6, opposition parties had refused to vacate the protest site until they were allowed to meet Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and hand over their demand for his resignation.

items.headline: CEC row | EC refuses Opposition's demand for meeting
items.claim: Opposition MPs of the INDIA bloc marched from Parliament to the Commission's headquarters to press for the Chief Election Commissioner's removal, and asked for 240 MPs to meet the three Commissioners at Parliament House Annexe, Deccan Herald reported.
items.quote: "After 4.00 PM today, when the Election Commission was considering the above proposal for the...meeting with the...MPs, it was informed by the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Delhi Police, that the meeting being sought was to be held with a group of 240 MPs and that the proposed venue was the Parliament House Annexe," the EC said in a statement. The EC considered this request as "unusual and therefore, could not be accepted," as, in accordance with the protocol, such meetings are held only on the premises of the poll body. It then proposed that its "senior-most officer on duty could be sent to the meeting venue to receive the memorandum", which in itself would have been an "unprecedented step". The statement added, "however, this offer was also declined by the MPs."
items.response: The Commission said no party had sought an appointment until 4 pm, that a meeting of 240 MPs away from its premises was unusual and could not be accepted, and that the MPs declined its offer to send its senior-most officer on duty to receive their memorandum, Deccan Herald reported.

items.headline: AAP Protest: Delhi CEO office gheraoed over SIR, CEC resignation demanded
items.claim: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said AAP workers and members of other parties protested outside the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation over alleged SIR irregularities. It said AAP had earlier protested at Jantar Mantar and India Gate.
items.quote: New Delhi: Scores of AAP and other parties' workers protested outside the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office at Kashmere Gate on Wednesday for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: INDIA bloc leaders march to EC office in Delhi, seek rollback of SIR
items.claim: The Tribune reported that Delhi leaders of the INDIA bloc marched to the Election Commission office and gave the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer a memorandum demanding that the SIR be cancelled and excluded eligible voters be restored. It said police detained Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav at a separate protest at Jantar Mantar.
items.quote: Delhi leaders of the INDIA bloc on Wednesday staged a protest march from Kashmiri Gate to the Election Commission (EC) office and submitted a memorandum to the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer, demanding immediate cancellation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and restoration of names of eligible voters excluded from the draft rolls.

items.headline: INDIA bloc hands over memorandum on 'vote chori' to President Murmu, says she didn't deny charge
items.claim: An INDIA bloc delegation including Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi gave President Droupadi Murmu a memorandum after opposition MPs marched from Parliament House and were stopped by police at Vijay Chowk, PTI reported. Kharge said the President had asked for evidence, which the bloc would provide, and Rahul Gandhi said she had not denied what they told her and that the leaders would meet the Chief Justice on Monday. The News Mill reported that the memorandum asked for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation, repeal of the 2023 law on the Commissioners, suspension of the SIR with the names the bloc says were left off or deleted illegally put back, a return to paper ballots, and annulment of Assembly elections of the past two years where it said evidence of vote theft had been presented. These are the INDIA bloc's demands and allegations.
items.quote: "President in no way denied what we said, she did not question what we said... she accepted our statement and sought proof of 'election chori',"
items.response: No response from Rashtrapati Bhavan or the Commission to the memorandum was reported.

items.headline: Cockroach Janta Party protest: New Delhi sealed even before the first slogan
items.claim: The South First reported on the morning of 10 October that police sealed central Delhi before the Cockroach Janta Party's protest at Jantar Mantar demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation over the SIR. It said more than 1,000 people had been detained overnight and 45 Metro stations were shut, and that police detained CPI(M) leaders including Pinarayi Vijayan and John Brittas when they tried to march from Kerala House.
items.quote: "A gathering of more than four people is not allowed," a Delhi Police officer told CPM's Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas, when he tried to argue that there were only three of them. ... "This is a murder of democracy," Pinarayi told reporters.
items.response: No statement from the Commission was reported. Police told the protesters that a gathering of more than four people was not allowed.

items.case: Uday Bhanu Chib v. Union of India and Ors, Delhi High Court
items.headline: Decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as protest site taken after Supreme Court order: Delhi police to High Court
items.claim: The Delhi Police told the Delhi High Court on 13 October that it de-notified Jantar Mantar as the designated protest site, and identified three other sites, on the basis of the Supreme Court's order of 9 October, Bar and Bench reported. That order had said suitable sites where basic amenities could be provided to protesters should be identified, and left the decision to the competent authority. The submission came on Indian Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib's petition against the refusal of permission to protest at Jantar Mantar against the Chief Election Commissioner. Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice on three of its prayers, which challenge the police's reliance on its 2022 standing order and the 10-day advance notice for protests.
items.quote: The Court said appropriate sites need to be identified and designated and we have precisely done that,
items.response: The police said the petition had become infructuous because Jantar Mantar had been de-notified. On 15 October the Solicitor General told the Supreme Court that the decision followed the recommendations of a committee set up by the Union Home Ministry well before the Court's oral observations, Bar and Bench reported.

items.case: Petition by the Delhi Kirana Committee and the Delhi Iron and Hardware Merchant Association, Supreme Court
items.headline: 'If NDMC Order Disproportionate, We'll Act': Supreme Court Lists Petition Against CJP Protest After Vacation
items.claim: Counsel for two traders' associations raised in the Supreme Court on 16 October their petition against the Cockroach Janta Party's call to unfurl the tricolour in Connaught Place's Central Park that evening, saying it would obstruct trade worth Rs 200 crore a day, The Wire reported. The party had called the protest after two of its leaders were arrested for waving the flag at Jantar Mantar. The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said it would act on compensation if the NDMC's restrictions were found disproportionate, noted that the Delhi High Court was hearing a similar matter, and listed the petition for 26 and 27 October, after the Dussehra break.
items.quote: If we feel that the NDMC’s order is a disproportionate restriction, we told you, there is ample jurisdiction evolved by this court under compensation and public law. We will act
items.response: The Wire says the petitions appear to be concerned with the protest itself, though counsel told the Court the NDMC had shut the place by a notice the night before, as LiveLaw reported. It carries the party founder's post on X that businesses suffer when the government shuts down a city and restricts its citizens' movement.

items.headline: Students, youth activists arrested for protesting against SIR in Chennai
items.claim: Chennai police arrested students and youth activists who began a 24-hour sit-in against the revision near Rajarathinam Stadium in Egmore at 4 pm on 22 October in defiance of a police ban, The Hindu reported. Nine organisations, among them Left student and youth groups and the Cockroach Janta Party, had formed a platform called Chennai's Jantar Mantar 2.0 and asked for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation. They were held overnight at a community hall and released the next morning at the stadium, where they resumed the protest.
items.quote: The city police on Thursday arrested students and youth activists who launched a 24-hour protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in defiance of a police ban.
items.response: The report carries no statement from the police beyond the ban.

items.headline: Over 150 detained in Delhi during protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.claim: Delhi Police detained more than 150 people on 23 October at a march in central Delhi against the revision and the Chief Election Commissioner, called by the Delhi Coordination Committee of People Against SIR, The Indian Express reported. About 300 people gathered near Gole Dak Khana around 2 pm and marched towards Gurdwara Bangla Sahib. When they could not reach the Commission's office they held a sit-in near the roundabout, and security forces began detaining them by 3 pm. The paper also reported that over 57 cases registered during the protests of 2 to 15 October had been moved to the Crime Branch.
items.quote: Delhi Police Friday detained more than 150 protesters during a march in Central Delhi against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
items.response: A senior police officer said the cases were moved because they needed close technical investigation and thorough questioning.

items.headline: Keralam SIR: LDF representatives walk out of all-party meet convened by Chief Electoral Officer
items.claim: Representatives of the Left Democratic Front walked out of an all-party meeting called by Kerala's Chief Electoral Officer on 23 October for the Special Summary Revision, The Hindu reported, and asked that the names of 24.08 lakh voters left off the draft roll of the state's earlier revision be put back. The paper reports that 24.08 lakh is the fall at the draft stage and that the final roll of 21 February 2026 was 8.97 lakh below the roll of October 2025.
items.quote: The CEO expressed his helplessness. We have asked the CEO to convey the demand to the Election Commission of India (ECI),
items.response: The Chief Electoral Officer, D. Sajith Babu, said he had told the leaders he would convey to the Commission their demand that the 2 November deadline for rationalising polling stations be extended.

items.headline: 'Hold Civic Polls Only After Deleted Voters Return to Rolls': Mamata TMC, Left, Congress, Rights Groups Urge EC
items.claim: The Congress, the Trinamool Congress, the CPI(M), the CPI(ML) Liberation, civil rights organisations and public figures gave West Bengal's State Election Commissioner a memorandum on 26 October asking that elections to the Kolkata and Howrah municipal corporations be held only after electors deleted in the revision have been heard, The Wire reported. They asked the State Election Commission to use its powers under Section 5 of the West Bengal State Election Commission Act, 1994 to add to the civic rolls everyone whose appeal is pending before the SIR appellate tribunals. Citing the Election Commission's affidavit of 16 September in the Supreme Court, the memorandum puts the pending appeals at about 1.2 lakh in the Kolkata Municipal Corporation area and about 39,000 in the Howrah Municipal Corporation area. It asks that the polls wait until the re-enrolment drive and the Special Summary Revision, whose final roll is due on 4 January 2027, are complete.
items.quote: Excluding around 1.6 lakh appellants in the two corporations from the civic rolls “would disenfranchise them for the second time, after the assembly polls,” the memorandum said.
items.response: The State Election Commissioner's office said he would meet a delegation of the signatories on 28 October, according to their press release as The Wire reports it. No reply from the State Election Commission on the substance was reported.

items.headline: Anti-SIR coalition urges Karnataka government to reject final SIR voter list, calls for social audit and public hearings
items.claim: SIR-Virodhi Karnataka, a coalition opposed to the revision, asked the State government on 28 October to reject the final roll prepared through the revision and to hold a social audit, public hearings and public scrutiny of the exercise, The Hindu reported. A leader of the coalition told the press, a day after Karnataka's final roll was published, that the State should use the previous roll for the coming local body elections, and called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The coalition said official projections put Karnataka's population aged 18 and above at 5.19 crore in 2026, against about 4.5 crore electors on the final roll, and questioned the fall in Bengaluru's electors, reports of alleged attempts by BJP members to file Form 7 applications in bulk, and the pressure on booth level officers. It said it would protest during the Assembly session that begins on 26 November, after the INDIA bloc's protest against the revision on 1 November.
items.quote: For the upcoming local body elections in the State, the previous voters’ list should be used as the basis instead of the list prepared through SIR,
items.response: The report gives no reply from the State government, the Chief Electoral Officer or the Election Commission.

items.case: Petition against a Leave India Notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office, Bombay High Court
items.headline: Bombay HC extends stay on [the actor's] ‘Leave India Notice’, seeks unconditional apology over SIR protest
items.claim: A division bench of the Bombay High Court, Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna, on 2 November kept in abeyance until 7 December the Leave India Notice that the Foreigners Regional Registration Office issued on 14 October to an actor who is a United States citizen holding an Overseas Citizen of India card, The Hindu and The Indian Express reported. Police had detained him near August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai on 10 October at a protest demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner over the SIR. The actor filed an unconditional apology and an undertaking that he would not take part in any protest or influence others to take part. The bench said Overseas Citizen of India cardholders could not claim the same rights as citizens, and The Indian Express reports that it said he was not remotely affected by the SIR. It allowed him to stay in India until the registration office decides the notice after hearing his response, and listed the matter for 7 December.
items.quote: law-abiding person, not associating/indulging in any activities/protests, rights which are available to the citizens of this country, under the Constitution
items.response: Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh, for the Union, argued that the actor had been involved in the protest from the start and had no legally enforceable right to remain in India. Senior advocate Venkatesh Dhond, for the actor, said he had gone to the site out of curiosity, had no link with the organisers and had not been heard before the notice was issued.

items.headline: Delhi police files FIR against 22 people from INDIA bloc rally who went near Jantar Mantar
items.claim: Delhi Police registered an FIR against 22 protesters detained at Minto Road on 1 November as they marched from the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan towards Jantar Mantar, Hindustan Times reported on 3 November. Police said members of the Disha Students' Organisation and the Revolutionary Workers' Party of India took out the march at about 5 pm, that Jantar Mantar is no longer a protest site, and that the protesters were taken in two buses to the Dwarka Sector 23 and Jafarpur Kalan police stations and released by 2 am the next day. The FIR is under Sections 223(a), 132, 221, 121(1), 3(5) and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. An artist affiliated with the party was placed in preventive detention at the Connaught Place police station under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita. Before the Special Executive Magistrate at Mandir Marg he refused to sign a peace bond, and he was released after furnishing sureties and a personal bond. A member of the party said the march demanded that Jantar Mantar be reclaimed as a protest site and that the SIR be scrapped. Hindustan Times had reported on 2 November that police said over 50 protesters were briefly detained near Minto Road after the rally, and the later report does not say whether the 22 are among them.
items.quote: Officials said while the Ramlila Maidan event had permission, students started going towards Jantar Mantar, which is no longer a protest area
items.response: Members of the two organisations alleged that police dragged protesters, women among them, into the buses and that one woman fainted, and the party said the artist was held for 23 hours and denied medication. The report carries no reply from the police to these allegations.

items.headline: Kochi Corporation Council passes SIR resolution amid protests; BJP councillors walk out
items.claim: The Kochi Corporation Council passed a resolution on 3 November moved by the United Democratic Front councillor Deepthy Mary Varghese, a general secretary of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee, expressing solidarity with the nationwide protests by political, youth and student groups against alleged irregularities in the SIR, The Hindu reported. The resolution, backed by the Left Democratic Front's leader in the council, V.A. Sreejith, criticised the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, for bringing disrepute to a constitutional office by, as it alleged, stripping more than 13 crore voters of their votes. All six BJP councillors walked out during the discussion. A BJP councillor had said that more than 2.50 crore of the names taken off the rolls were those of dead people, and UDF councillors rose to protest. The Mayor, V.K. Minimol, declared the resolution passed in the absence of the BJP councillors.
items.quote: The resolution expressed solidarity with the nationwide protests by political, youth and student outfits against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
items.response: The BJP's leader in the council, Sudha Dilipkumar, said UDF councillors had ridiculed BJP councillors and denied them the right to respond, and later accused the Mayor of behaving like a Mahila Congress leader. The Mayor said that holding a discussion before approving the resolution was in keeping with the democratic spirit.

items.headline: Opposition parties demand re-enrolment for 27 lakh deleted voters in Bengal
items.claim: Leaders of the Trinamool Congress, the Left Front and the Congress asked at an all-party meeting with West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer, Neelam Meena, on 3 November that the 27 lakh electors whose names judicial officers deleted in the revision be allowed to apply again on Form 6, The Times of India reported. They alleged that the Commission was acting at the BJP's behest to have lakhs of names deleted through Form 7, and questioned the 16 lakh appeals filed before the tribunals, which they alleged officials of the Chief Electoral Officer's office had filed to seek the deletion of electors whom judicial officers had cleared. The Trinamool Congress's Kunal Ghosh alleged that the Commission was imposing the special summary revision while appeals from the revision were pending. He said the special roll observer, Subrata Gupta, had said he had no information about the 16 lakh appeals, and that the Chief Electoral Officer had told the parties the appeals were filed before she took charge. The CPI(M)'s Palash Das asked whether Form 7 was a project for the mass deletion of electors in the BJP's interest. The Congress's Ashutosh Chatterjee said the tribunals had been unable to upload their orders since 21 September and that the tribunal for Kolkata had no judge.
items.quote: The voters whose names were deleted on the grounds of logical discrepancies should be allowed to fill Form 6 for re-enrolment.
items.response: The BJP's Sisir Bajoria told the meeting that one elector in the Barabani constituency was linked as father to 389 electors and one in Bally to 310, the paper reported. The report gives no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer to the demand.

items.headline: Police detain rail roko protesters demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's arrest in Tamil Nadu
items.claim: Members of the Jananayaka Meetpu Kuzhu staged a rail roko near the old railway station in Kanchipuram on 4 November, demanding the arrest of the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, Hindustan Times reported from ANI. The protesters alleged that he had acted in favour of the Prime Minister by "disqualifying 13 crore voters". More than 350 protesters marched from near Hotel Tamil Nadu towards the East Railway Station, where a scuffle broke out when police tried to stop them, and more than 50 sat on the tracks. Police detained all the protesters and held them in a private marriage hall. Members of Makkal Mandram, the Communist Party of India and the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi and independent activists took part, and the report says the protest caused tension in the area for about an hour.
items.quote: Defying police barricades, more than 50 protesters sat on the railway tracks and raised slogans against the Prime Minister and the Election Commission, repeating their demand for the arrest of the CEC.
items.response: The report carries no statement from the police or the railways and does not say whether a case was registered or when the protesters were released.

items.headline: [The actor] apologised for SIR protest. Now his cousin faces OCI scrutiny
items.claim: Mumbai Police asked the Foreigners Regional Registration Office to verify the Overseas Citizen of India status of a second actor detained at the protest of 10 October in Mumbai against the Chief Election Commissioner, The Indian Express reported on 4 November. She is a cousin of the actor whose Leave India Notice the Bombay High Court kept in abeyance on 2 November (protest-51). The paper reports that an FIR was registered against her for taking part in the protest, and a police officer told it that she was born in Mumbai and holds an OCI card. A police officer told the paper that the police had written to the registration office after the two were detained, asking that both actors' OCI status be checked, and that on 16 October, two days after the notice to her cousin, they wrote again to say she held an OCI card and that an FIR had been registered against her. The paper reports that the registration office then examined the status of both. The protest was organised by Tushar Gandhi's Hum Bharat Ke Log.
items.quote: The regional office wrote to the FRRO stating that an FIR had been registered against her and that her OCI status must be checked,
items.response: Her cousin's lawyer told The Indian Express that she had not been served a notice by the registration office. The report gives no statement from the registration office.

items.headline: Karnataka INDIA Bloc Stages Massive Protest Over Electoral Roll Audit
items.claim: The INDIA bloc's Karnataka unit held a protest against the SIR at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on 5 November, demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, ANI reported. The Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee president, B.K. Hariprasad, said the protest continued the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on 1 November and would go on until the Chief Election Commissioner resigned. He said District Congress Committee presidents were holding rallies at every district headquarters the same day and that the protest would reach the taluks and blocks from the next day. The Chief Minister, D.K. Shivakumar, said every elector whose name had been deleted, other than those who had died, should get justice. The Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge alleged that the Commission had made five U-turns over its stand on Form 6 and Form 7 and over the software, which he said had been manipulated for deletions. The report names the Congress, the CPI(M), the CPI, the CPI(ML) Liberation, the Forward Bloc and the Samajwadi Party among the organisers, with student, youth and other groups, and gives the protest as running from 11 am to 2 pm.
items.quote: In continuation of this, the INDIA bloc has assembled today at Freedom Park, and we are going to start our protest today.
items.response: The report carries no statement from the Election Commission. It says police were deployed at Freedom Park and reports no arrests.

items.headline: INDIA bloc demands scrapping of SIR, seeks use of pre-SIR 2025 electoral rolls for next local polls
items.claim: The INDIA bloc adopted a five-point resolution at its protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on 5 November (protest-55), The Hindu reported. The resolution demands that the SIR be scrapped, that the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, resign and that the revised rolls in Karnataka be rejected. It asks the state government to hold the coming local body, taluk panchayat and zilla panchayat elections on the rolls of 2025, from before the revision, and calls for the repeal of the law on the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner. It puts the fall in Karnataka's roll at 99.32 lakh names, from 5.54 crore to about 4.5 crore in the final roll of 27 October, It says about 23 lakh of these were dead or duplicate electors and alleges that nearly 76 lakh were eligible electors, including migrants and people who had moved house. It alleges that BJP workers misused Form 7 to seek the deletion of names. The Chief Minister, D.K. Shivakumar, announced at the protest that the state government would start a police investigation into the alleged misuse of Form 7, and he alleged that Form 7 applications had been printed at the BJP office and handed to constituency leaders with electors' names and identity details. The state Cabinet discussed the SIR the same day. The Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister, Eshwar Khandre, said afterwards that no decision had been taken on whether the rolls after the revision would be used for the zilla and taluk panchayat elections, and that the State Election Commission would decide and would seek the government's opinion, The Hindu reported.
items.quote: There is CCTV footage showing who instigated vote theft and who brought the applications. Cases will be registered in this regard, and justice will be delivered,
items.response: The reports carry no statement from the Election Commission. The BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra, at a press conference in Bengaluru that The Hindu reported the same evening, denied the Congress's claims and its figures on eligible electors who had lost their votes. Neither report gives an answer from the BJP to the allegation about Form 7.

items.headline: Karnataka CM favours committee to review final electoral rolls amid SIR controversy
items.claim: Karnataka's Chief Minister, D.K. Shivakumar, favours a committee to study the final rolls prepared through the revision, Deccan Herald reported, and the Public Works Minister, Satish Jarkiholi, said the Chief Minister was forming one to see whether eligible electors were left out. Some ministers told the Cabinet on 5 November that the revision had not had much effect on deletions in their constituencies. Jarkiholi said the government must decide whether the coming local body elections use the roll prepared through the revision or the one from before it. The Deputy Chief Minister, G. Parameshwara, said the government's stand must agree with the Congress's. He said that in some ministers' constituencies only about 2,000 electors had been left out, and that across the state 1.08 crore electors were left off, 16 lakh of them marked dead, some of whom were apparently alive, and 65 lakh shown as shifted.
items.quote: The CM has said that a committee should be formed. He’s forming the committee. It will study the final electoral rolls to see if eligible voters were left out,
items.response: The report does not give the committee's members, its terms or a date for it, and carries no statement from the Election Commission or the State Election Commission.

items.headline: Karnataka: State Election Commission asks Bengaluru corporations to prepare ward-wise poll rolls
items.claim: Karnataka's State Election Commission directed the commissioners of the five city corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority to speed up the preparation of ward-wise electoral rolls for the elections to the five corporations, Deccan Herald reported on 12 November. In a communication dated 5 November, the State Election Commission told officials to base the rolls on the final Assembly rolls published on 27 October after the revision. Officials are to map electors' details to the notified ward boundaries and prepare the rolls in Excel format, with no more than 1,200 electors in a polling part, and are to send the ward rolls and related details to the State Election Commission by 12 November. The State Election Commission said the work was begun in accordance with the Supreme Court's directions, which set the end of December as the deadline for completing the elections.
items.quote: In a communication dated November 5, the commission instructed officials to base the rolls on the final Assembly-wise electoral rolls published on October 27, following the special intensive revision (SIR).
items.response: The direction is the State Election Commission's own. The report does not name the Supreme Court case or date its order, and it carries no statement from the state government or from the parties that asked for the local body elections to be held on the rolls from before the revision.

items.headline: Delhi SIR: Days After EC Order, Delegation Meets CEO, Seeks Restoration of Wrongly Deleted Voters
items.claim: A delegation of opposition parties and civil society groups met Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer at his office at Kashmiri Gate on 9 November to discuss carrying out the Commission's letter of 6 November on electors left off the draft roll as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, The Wire and Hindustan Times reported. The Wire names Amit Mishra of the Aam Aadmi Party, Dinesh Varshney of the CPI, Anurag Saxena of the CPI(M), Shamsher Singh of the CPI(ML), R.S. Dagar of the Revolutionary Socialist Party, Hari Shankar of the All India Forward Bloc, Anjali Bhardwaj of Voter Adhikar Manch and Amrita Johri of Satark Nagrik Sangathan, with members of Voter Adhikar Manch, Jan Sarokar and the Centre for Financial Accountability. By the delegation's statement after the meeting, the Chief Electoral Officer accepted several of its suggestions and issued directions, and a standard operating procedure is to be released shortly. The delegation says he accepted that electors left off the draft and placed on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors published on 31 August can be restored by an enumeration form and keep their earlier serial and EPIC numbers, and that he assured it he would consider giving their earlier EPIC numbers to electors who applied again on Form 6 after 31 August. On Form 7 it asked for verification with the booth level agent who filed each form, publication of every application, notices to affected electors and no decision without a fair hearing. It raised Form 7s it says were wrongly filed in Mustafabad, and it says it was agreed that Form 7s filed by registration officers or assistant registration officers would be examined again. It also asked for enrolment camps in unauthorised colonies, JJ clusters and slum settlements from 7 am and from 7 pm to 10 pm, for the publication of the names deleted before the revision with the reasons, for a fixed time to decide Form 6 applications, for surprise inspections of the booth level officers' work, and for more time for the 47,56,722 electors left off the draft roll to be included. The delegation says it was asked to submit the names of electors its own surveys found wrongly deleted.
items.quote: The CEO accepted several suggestions and issued directions, with a Standard Operating Procedure (SoP) expected to be released shortly, the delegation announced shortly after the visit.
items.response: Everything the claim says the Chief Electoral Officer accepted, assured or agreed rests on the delegation's own account, and neither report carries a statement from him. A senior official of his office told Hindustan Times that the meeting went well and that the office would work on the suggestion, and said "Several suggestions were already in the pipeline. We will consider all demands which help make the process easier for ordinary voters." Neither report says when the standard operating procedure will be released, and no reply from the Commission was reported.

items.headline: SIR: KRMO flags higher voter deletions in Muslim-dominated constituencies
items.claim: The Karnataka Rajya Muslim Okkoota, an umbrella body of Muslim community groups, said in a statement on 9 November that an analysis of the Commission's booth level data by the political research consultancy Sankalp found that 27.59% of the electors in the 10 Assembly constituencies represented by Muslim MLAs were left off the roll, against a state average of 19.45%, The Hindu and The Indian Express reported. The statement calls these names deleted. By the body's estimate, those 10 constituencies held 9,62,359 Muslim electors on the 2025 roll, of whom 2,46,759 (25.64%) were left off, and more than 8.80 lakh Muslim electors were left off in 64 constituencies where Muslims are a large share of the population. By the same estimate, 2,58,770 of the 15,15,088 electors left off as absent across the state, and 1,43,940 of the 7,08,666 left off as already enrolled elsewhere, were Muslims. The Indian Express gives the body's shares as 17.1% and 20.3%, against a Muslim share of 12.9% of the state's population and 12.2% of the electors left off as dead. The body argues that a finding of absent or enrolled elsewhere rests on the judgement of booth level officers and other field officials, where a death can be checked against official records. It gives Chamarajpet 1,07,722 names left off, Kalaburagi North 1,05,257, Narasimharaja 99,367 and Shivajinagar 81,230. It asked the Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission to explain, and demanded that the revision be scrapped, that the previous rolls be used for future elections, that a judicial inquiry be held and that legal action be taken against officials found responsible for irregularities.
items.quote: In a statement issued on Monday, the organisation said an analysis of booth-level data released by the ECI, carried out by political research consultancy Sankalp, showed that 27.59% of voters had been deleted across the 10 Assembly constituencies represented by Muslim MLAs in Karnataka.
items.response: Neither report carries a reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission.

items.headline: After SIR deletions, Karnataka plans police-led household survey in Bengaluru
items.claim: Karnataka's Chief Minister, D.K. Shivakumar, announced on 15 November that the government would collect household-level records of residents door to door across Bengaluru through the police department, The Indian Express reported. Speaking at the Bharathinagar Habba festival in Bengaluru, he said the data was needed for residents' safety. He said Bengaluru's electoral roll had shrunk from 51 lakh to 45 lakh voters, and that instructions would therefore be issued for the police to keep accurate records of who lives where in the city. The paper reports that the final roll of 27 October deleted over 43 lakh voters in Bengaluru. A home department official told the paper that the department had not yet discussed how the exercise would be carried out, and that local police officers and wardens under the beat system would be assigned to collect the data.
items.quote: It has also come to our notice that Bengaluru's electoral roll has shrunk from 51 lakh to 45 lakh voters. Given this, instructions will be issued to ensure the police department maintains accurate records of who resides where in the city.
items.response: The report does not say when the exercise will begin, what data will be collected or how it will be kept, and carries no statement from the Election Commission or the Chief Electoral Officer.

items.headline: CPI (M) Demands Re-enrolment of 54000 Excluded Voters into Electoral Rolls – Walks out of CEO’s Meeting
items.claim: The CPI(M)'s state secretary in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, D. Ayyappan, and a member of its state secretariat, P. Sathyapal, walked out of a meeting of national parties called by the Chief Electoral Officer at Sri Vijaya Puram on 17 November, after the Chief Electoral Officer refused their demand that all the electors they say were excluded in the intensive revision of 2025-26 be put back on the roll before any further revision, Andaman Chronicle and Andaman Sheekha reported. Andaman Sheekha says its account follows the party's press release. The meeting was called to brief the parties on the proposed schedule for revising the roll of the Andaman and Nicobar Parliamentary Constituency. The two leaders said a revision of the roll prepared in the intensive revision would be of no use unless the excluded electors were enrolled again first, and Ayyappan gave the Chief Electoral Officer a letter repeating the party's opposition. He said the party had opposed the intensive revision since its letter to the Chief Electoral Officer of 25 September 2025, and that its fears were borne out when the Commission announced that 64,014 electors, including 9,191 who had died, were excluded from the roll. He put the electors to be enrolled again at 54,000. He said the Commission had assured the Supreme Court that excluded electors could enrol again on Form 6 and would not be prosecuted, but that it might not be possible for all of them to come forward and file the form. He also said the Commission has no power to remove citizens from the roll without following the procedure established by law.
items.quote: When the Chief Electoral Officer refused to accept the demand, CPI (M) delegation walked out of the meeting to register its protest.
items.response: Andaman Sheekha's report rests on the party's press release, and Andaman Chronicle's follows it closely without saying so. Neither carries a statement from the Chief Electoral Officer on the meeting or on the demand, and neither gives a figure for the draft roll of the summary revision.
actors: Chief Electoral Officer, Andaman and Nicobar Islands

items.headline: Karnataka poll chief urged not to use SIR voter lists for local elections
items.claim: The Federation of Anti-SIR Secular Parties and Pro-People Organisations asked Karnataka's State Election Commissioner, G.N. Sangreshi, in a memorandum to leave the rolls of the SIR unused for the coming Greater Bengaluru Authority elections and other local elections and to use the electoral roll of 2025 after a public review, The Indian Express reported on 24 November. The memorandum says the SIR is under judicial scrutiny and has become controversial over alleged errors in the revised roll. Citing official population figures, it says Karnataka has an estimated 5.2 crore residents aged 18 or above against about 4.5 crore names on the rolls after the revision, and asks why the remaining 70 lakh are missing. It cites a verification by the Mata Kavalu Samiti across 73 polling booths that it says found many eligible electors wrongly deleted, alleges that around 20 lakh entries in the final roll lack proper addresses, and asks that the 2025 roll be revised through gram sabhas and ward sabhas under the Election Commission's Manual of 2023. It says election authorities in Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh chose the 2025 rolls for their local elections. The paper reports that the number of electors fell by around 18% across the state and by around 40% in the four electoral districts under the Greater Bengaluru Authority.
items.quote: Why are the remaining 70 lakh people missing from the voters’ list? When Bengaluru is growing rapidly, how can such a large number of voters disappear from the electoral roll? The Election Commission has no answers to these questions,
items.response: The report carries no reply from the State Election Commission, the Chief Electoral Officer or the Election Commission. The memorandum's figures and its account of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh are its own and are not checked.
actors: Federation of Anti-SIR Secular Parties and Pro-People Organisations

items.headline: Delhi Congress protests against SIR 'irregularities', demands protection of voting rights
items.claim: The Delhi Congress marched on Constitution Day, 26 November, against what it calls irregularities in Delhi's SIR, PTI reported in Hindustan Times. The march began at about 12.15 pm from Chandgi Ram Akhara, opposite the Trauma Centre in Civil Lines, led by the party's Delhi president, Devender Yadav, and was to end at the Dr Ambedkar National Memorial. PTI names the AICC general secretary K.C. Venugopal, the treasurer Ajay Maken and the party's Delhi in-charge Qazi Nizamuddin among those who took part. Yadav said that 47.56 lakh names were missing from Delhi's draft roll and sought details of how many were left off because they had died, had moved or for other reasons. The protesters asked for an impartial inquiry, special hearings for the electors affected and action against officials responsible for wrong deletions. The day before, on 25 November, Yadav asked for the deadline of 30 November to be extended, The Times of India reported, and The Hindu reported the same request from the Delhi Congress. The Hindu says the deadline is the one for voters left off the draft roll to submit reprinted enumeration forms and supporting documents to be included in the final roll. Yadav told The Times of India that against 47.5 lakh names deleted from the draft only 5.41 lakh applications for restoration had been received, and that the Commission had processed only 2.81 lakh of them. The chairman of the party's booth management committee, Rajesh Garg, also wrote to the Commission asking for the deadline to be extended and for a break-up of the 47.5 lakh by reason.
items.quote: Deleting the names of living voters by showing them as dead is anti-democratic and a direct assault on the voting rights of the people,
items.response: The Times of India says no comment from the Election Commission was available, and neither report carries a reply from the Chief Electoral Officer. The counts of applications are Yadav's own. Delhi's final roll is due on 22 December.

items.headline: Congress leaders briefly detained as they try to march in Lucknow defying restrictions
items.claim: Police in Lucknow detained leaders and workers of the Uttar Pradesh Congress on Constitution Day, 26 November, when they tried to take out a Samvidhan Raksha march after the administration refused permission for it, PTI and Hindustan Times reported. The party had moved its programme to its state office after permission was refused, PTI reported, and Dainik Jagran reports that the district administration declared Hazratganj and Mall Avenue sensitive areas. The Congress president, Mallikarjun Kharge, spoke at a Samvidhan Raksha Sammelan at the party office and left for Delhi before the march. Workers then marched from the office towards the Ambedkar Crossing in Hazratganj. Police stopped them about 150 metres from the office at three layers of barricades, and after about 40 minutes detained the party's state in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, its state president Aradhana Mishra, its working president Imran Masood and other leaders and workers, PTI reported. They were taken to the Eco Garden, the designated protest site in Lucknow, and released. Mishra said that every other state had been given permission for the march and that the party would go on until all 13 crore votes deleted under the SIR were brought back on the roll, Hindustan Times reported. Gautam asked why the administration gave permission for every BJP event and not for theirs. Kharge said at the meeting that the Prime Minister, Narendra Modi, and the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, were taking away people's right to vote through the SIR and EVMs, and that elections would not be free and fair until both were removed from office, Dainik Jagran and The South First reported.
items.quote: We have been detained but the Congress will continue the struggle until all 13 crore votes deleted under SIR are brought back on the electoral roll,
items.response: PTI and Hindustan Times carry no statement from the police or the district administration beyond the refusal of permission. The 13 crore is Mishra's own figure, and she does not say where the votes were deleted. The draft rolls published in 31 states and union territories left off 13,39,03,307 names, 2,88,74,067 of them in Uttar Pradesh.

items.headline: Farmers, student groups hold marches in Delhi on Constitution Day over SIR
items.claim: Delhi Police stopped a march against the SIR at Mandir Marg on Constitution Day, 26 November, PTI and The Hindu reported. The Hindu reports that hundreds of protesters under the banner of People Against SIR gathered at Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg, asking for the SIR to be scrapped, for the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, to be removed and for Jantar Mantar to be restored as a designated protest site, and that police barricades kept them from marching to Jantar Mantar. PTI reports that the Samyukt Kisan Morcha marched in Delhi as part of demonstrations across the country on the sixth anniversary of the farmers' agitation, and that its demands included scrapping the SIR and removing and prosecuting Kumar. After the police stopped the farmers' march at Mandir Marg, the farmer leaders Yudhvir Singh and Revula Venkaiah handed a memorandum addressed to the President to an Additional DCP, the Morcha said in a statement. The Students' Federation of India held a separate march at Mandir Marg against Kumar over the SIR and asked for Jantar Mantar to be notified as an official protest site, PTI reported. The night before, the New Delhi Deputy Commissioner of Police posted on X that no application had been received and no permission granted for a march by the Morcha and others from Kali Bari to Jantar Mantar, and that the order under section 163 of the BNSS was in force in New Delhi district, The Wire reported.
items.quote: After the Delhi Police stopped the farmers’ march at Mandir Marg, senior farmer leaders Yudhvir Singh and Revula Venkaiah handed a memorandum addressed to the President of India to Additional DCP Jagdev Singh, the SKM said in a statement.
items.response: The police's position is the Deputy Commissioner's post as The Wire gives it. The reports carry no statement from the Election Commission. The Hindu's count of the protesters is its own, and its standfirst puts them at over 200.

items.headline: Constitution Day: Telangana CM leads march against ‘vote chori’ in Hyderabad
items.claim: Telangana's Chief Minister, A. Revanth Reddy, led the Congress's Samvidhan Raksha march in Hyderabad on Constitution Day, 26 November, Siasat reported. It started at 10.30 am from the B.R. Ambedkar statue on Tank Bund and ended at the Indira Gandhi statue on Necklace Road. The Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee president B. Mahesh Kumar Goud, ministers and legislators took part. The state committee organised it on a call from the All India Congress Committee and set up a committee covering 37 Assembly constituencies in and around Greater Hyderabad to bring out workers. Leaders at the march accused the BJP of undermining the Constitution and the right to vote through the SIR, and the Congress MP Anil Kumar Yadav alleged that votes were being stolen in the name of the SIR. Siasat reports that the march was one of several held by the party's state units as part of its Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao campaign. K.C. Venugopal's circular of 15 November had postponed the Dilli Chalo programmes planned for 25 and 26 November and asked every state committee to march on Constitution Day instead, and party workers were asked beforehand to visit every booth and check names deleted from the rolls in a Vote Rakshak drive.
items.quote: The Constitution that the Congress party gave, the BJP is trying to destroy that Constitution,
items.response: The report carries no statement from the Election Commission or Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer. The allegations are the Congress leaders' own. Telangana's final roll is due on 22 December, under the Commission's letter of 17 November.

items.headline: NPCC urges comprehensive SIR
items.claim: The Nagaland Pradesh Congress Committee and the Kohima District Congress Committee marched under the slogans Samvidhan Bachao, Desh Bachao and Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao on 26 November, The Morung Express reported from the party's press statement. After the march the party's president, the Lok Sabha MP Supongmeren Jamir, and its working president, Khrieti, met Nagaland's Chief Electoral Officer, Bhagyashree Banayat, about the SIR, and the party asked the Election Department to carry out a more detailed and comprehensive revision so that electors whose names had been deleted or not yet covered get an adequate chance to be included.
items.quote: Every genuine voter must be protected and no eligible citizen should be deprived of their fundamental democratic right to vote,
items.response: The account is the party's own press statement. The report carries no statement from the Chief Electoral Officer, and the party's statement thanks her and the Election Department for their efforts.

items.case: Petition by Saurav Das, Delhi High Court
items.headline: Not just Saurav Das: CJP’s Dipke, Ranka also face Mumbai Police lookout circulars
items.claim: Mumbai Police has issued lookout circulars against the Cockroach Janta Party's founder Abhijeet Dipke and its co-convenors Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das over the FIR on the party's protest at Shivaji Park in Dadar on 2 October (protest-27), a senior officer said on 26 November, The Indian Express reported. The FIR was registered on 3 October and names party leaders and more than 400 supporters for gathering illegally and raising slogans, under sections 189 and 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and sections 37 and 135 of the Maharashtra Police Act, the paper reports. The paper says the 2 October protest began the party's campaign for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation over alleged irregularities in the SIR, that Mumbai Police had refused permission for it, and that police said no one was detained and the protest ended peacefully. The circular against Das came to light the same day, when the Centre told the Delhi High Court that it had been issued at Mumbai Police's request early on 23 November, hours before immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him from flying to London, The Times of India reported. Das has asked the court for leave to travel to the United Kingdom. His counsel, Akhil Sibal, told the court that Das had never been told of a circular and asked for its contents. The Additional Solicitor General, Chetan Sharma, said a copy could not be given yet because Das had still to answer a show-cause notice of 23 November from the passport authorities. The court did not allow the request and will hear the matter next on 9 December, The Indian Express reported.
items.quote: Since there was apprehension that they would leave the country, an LOC was issued against them,
items.response: The reason for the circulars is the senior officer's, as The Indian Express gives it. Das said in a statement that the circular was clearly an afterthought, The Times of India reported. The government also relies on the passport notice, whose contents are the government's allegations and are not carried here.

items.headline: Civil society groups urge Karnataka Chief Minister to scrutinise SIR deletions ahead of local polls
items.claim: Members of civil society groups under the banner of the Anti-SIR alliance submitted a memorandum to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Friday, 27 November, asking the State government to reject the final roll published after the revision and to take a clear stand against the exercise, with local body elections approaching, The Hindu reported. The paper's standfirst says the alliance called the final roll riddled with errors and demanded that the 2025 roll be restored, put to public scrutiny and revised in a voter-friendly manner before it is used for the local body elections. The description published with the report adds demands that the lists be published and a social audit be held.
items.quote: The alliance said the final electoral roll was riddled with errors and demanded that the 2025 electoral roll be restored, subjected to public scrutiny and revised in a voter-friendly manner before being used for local body elections.
items.response: The part of the report The Hindu shows free carries no reply from the Chief Minister or the State government.

items.headline: Kerala BLO death sparks boycott; BLOs strike over SIR deadline stress
items.claim: The News Minute reported that hundreds of booth level officers across Kerala stayed away from SIR work on a strike call after the death of a BLO in Kannur, and that employee and teacher action councils marched to collectorates.
items.quote: A day after the death of a Booth Level Officer in Kerala’s Kannur, allegedly due Special Intensive Revision (SIR) workpressure, hundreds of Booth Level Officers (BLOs) across the state skipped work following a strike call on Monday, November 17.
items.response: The News Minute reported that Kerala's Chief Electoral Officer said he had not received any complaints regarding work pressure from BLOs.

items.headline: Tamil Nadu revenue employees association begin boycott of SIR work
items.claim: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said the Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu began a statewide boycott of SIR work over workload, staff shortages, deadline pressure and poor training.
items.quote: Chennai: The members of the Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu commenced their boycott of the SIR work from Tuesday, protesting against excessive workload, insufficient manpower, deadline pressure, and inadequate training.
actors: Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu

items.headline: BLOs protest outside Bengal CEO's office over excessive work pressure, EC calls them 'real heroes'
items.claim: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said booth level officers marching under the BLO Adhikar Raksha Committee clashed with police outside the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer's office in Kolkata over SIR workload.
