items.quote: Kolkata: Alleging "excessive work pressure" and "unmanageable workload", Booth-level officers (BLOs) engaged in the ongoing SIR process in West Bengal clashed with the police on Monday while attempting to enter the Chief Electoral Officer's (CEO) office here during a demonstration, a senior officer said.
items.response: Deccan Herald reported that Chief Electoral Officer Manoj Agarwal described the BLOs as the "real heroes" of the exercise.

items.headline: ‘BLOs facing harassment in Gautam Buddha Nagar amid SIR Phase-2’: UP teachers’ body submits memorandum to DM
items.claim: The Gautam Buddh Nagar unit of the Uttar Pradesh Primary Teachers' Association wrote to the District Magistrate on 24 November 2025 alleging mental harassment of the about 1,800 teachers deployed as booth officers, two days after FIRs were registered against more than 60 booth officers and seven supervisors under section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, The Indian Express reported. The association asked for the FIRs to be withdrawn and said the Commission's app did not work in rural areas.
items.quote: However, you or officials under your direction have been registering FIRs and adverse entries which is leading to the mental harassment of the teachers
items.response: The Indian Express reported that the FIRs were lodged on the orders of the District Magistrate and District Election Officer, Medha Rupam, against booth officers alleged to have shown a lack of compliance.

items.headline: Four BLOs die amid mounting pressure during electoral revision drive in UP
items.claim: After a lekhpal supervising the revision died by suicide in Bindki, Fatehpur, the Lekhpal Association protested, would not let the body be taken for post-mortem until a case was registered, and announced a boycott of SIR work unless action was taken, The New Indian Express reported.
items.quote: It also announced a boycott of SIR work from Thursday unless action was taken against those responsible for the death.

items.headline: Ahmedabad: 250 BLOs Stage Protest, Citing Threats, Pressure, Abuse and Late Night Calls
items.claim: The Wire reported that nearly 250 primary school teachers working as booth level officers stopped work and held a sit-in at a data uploading centre in Ahmedabad, alleging threats and pressure during the SIR.
items.quote: Nearly 250 primary school teachers assigned as Booth Level Officers (BLOs) halted work and held a sit-in protest on Thursday (November 27) at the data uploading centre in Khokhra, Ahmedabad, alleging “threat and pressure” during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: ‘Denied medical leave’, booked for ‘not signing attendance’: BLOs say UP SIR is inhumane
items.claim: Newslaundry reported that Ghaziabad registered an FIR against 21 employees for negligence in booth officer duties on 27 November 2025, after Gautam Buddh Nagar's FIRs, and that glitches in the Commission's mobile application were a main reason for slow digitisation. The Ghaziabad complainant, a deputy tehsildar, admitted the app sometimes hung. The teachers' association letter cited app glitches and repeated OTP failures.
items.quote: A key reason for lagging in the digitisation effort has been the technical glitches in the EC’s national mobile application.
items.response: Officials told Newslaundry the FIRs were for negligence. An electoral registration officer said "Those who do not work will face action." Newslaundry said it sent questions to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's office.

items.headline: Up:blo की मौतों से नाराज शिक्षकों संगठनों ने खोला मोर्चा
items.claim: Amar Ujala reported that teachers' organisations in Uttar Pradesh, among them the Uttar Pradeshiya Prathmik Shikshak Sangh, objected to the deaths of teachers and staff on SIR duty and demanded jobs and compensation for their families.
items.quote: प्रदेश में विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण अभियान में लगे शिक्षामित्रों व कर्मचारियों की मौत से शिक्षक संगठनों में काफी नाराजगी है। उनका कहना है कि उनका काम शिक्षण कार्य है, उसके बावजूद प्रशासन जबरन उनसे निर्वाचन से जुड़े कार्य कराता है।

items.case: A teacher's petition against his suspension from booth level officer duty, Punjab and Haryana High Court
items.headline: Punjab & Haryana High Court grants relief to teacher suspended for not joining SIR duty after wife's death
items.claim: The Punjab and Haryana High Court quashed the suspension of a teacher in Hisar district who had asked to be relieved of booth level officer duty after his wife died, and imposed costs of Rs 50,000 on the District Elementary Education Officer, Hisar and the Electoral Registration Officer for the Barwala constituency, Bar and Bench reported. Justice Harpreet Singh Brar found that the authorities appointed three substitutes for his booth without making sure any of them joined, and then suspended him for a duty he no longer held. The Court directed the Chief Electoral Officer, Haryana to make sure that a booth level officer who is replaced is told in writing whether he stands relieved.
items.quote: Instead of deciding his application, the respondents appointed one substitute after another without ensuring that any of them actually joined. They then held the petitioner responsible for the default of others, replaced him, and thereafter suspended him for a duty he no longer held, on an allegation of missing a training whose date they themselves cannot state
items.response: The authorities said he had never been relieved of the duty and had missed the SIR training. The Court found they could not state the date of the training, and noted that none of the three substitutes attended it either.

items.headline: Boards near but endless free periods in schools as most teachers away as BLOs
items.claim: Most teachers at two government inter colleges in Ghaziabad were away on booth level officer duty for the special summary revision, leaving students with free periods weeks before their pre-board and board examinations, The Times of India reported on 17 November. At Shambhu Dayal Inter College, which the paper calls one of the largest government schools in Ghaziabad and which has 2,548 students, 38 of 42 teachers were absent on the duty on Monday, 16 November, and the campus is also a training centre for booth level officers. At Seth Mukund Lal Inter College 34 of 36 teachers were on the duty, and 1,300 students were affected. By the paper's count the intensive revision deployed 1,868 booth level officers in Gautam Budh Nagar and 3,224 in Ghaziabad for 85 days in three phases. These were 32 days of house-to-house enumeration from 4 November to 5 December 2025, 38 days of special camps and hearings from 21 January to 27 February 2026 and 15 days of claims and objections from 27 March to 10 April 2026. A similar number have been given duties for nearly 80 days of the summary revision, from 17 October to 4 January, when the final roll is due. The house listing for Census 2027, from 22 May to 20 June, took 9,000 officials in Gautam Budh Nagar and 10,025 in Ghaziabad. Data the district administrations shared show 1,089 teachers in Noida and 2,025 in Ghaziabad deployed as booth level officers for the three rounds, and the paper reckons that over 3,000 teachers spent about 102 of the 221 days of the school year from April 2026 to March 2027 on duties other than teaching. A secondary school teacher told the paper that only teachers on medical leave or with physical disabilities had been exempted, that teachers who protested were warned of action, and that a request to spread the work so that classes could go on was met with an instruction to put Census duties first.
items.quote: With voter enrolment drives beginning again in UP after controversial exclusions from the rolls during special intensive revision (SIR) earlier this year, 38 of its 42 teachers are absent because they have been assigned booth-level officer (BLO) duty.
items.response: A senior official of the district administration said Census and booth level officer duties need many people and teachers have traditionally done them, that academic work must not suffer, that at least a few teachers remain in each school to manage classes and that schools have been asked to make internal arrangements. The report carries no statement from the Chief Electoral Officer or the District Election Officers.

items.headline: Karnataka’s education department asks Election Commission not to deploy teachers for roll revision
items.claim: The Additional Chief Secretary of Karnataka's Department of School Education and Literacy, V. Rashmi Mahesh, asked the state's Chief Electoral Officer, V. Anbukumar, in a letter dated 17 November, not to assign teachers of government schools and lecturers of government pre-university colleges to the special summary revision of the roll, and to instruct the District Election Officers to the same effect, The Times of India and Deccan Herald reported on 22 November. The letter says that many of them were deployed as booth level officers and supervisors in the intensive revision, which ran from June to October 2026 after its deadline was extended several times, and that this disrupted teaching. It cites the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, which The Times of India says prescribes at least 45 working hours a week for teachers, including preparation time, and says that deploying teachers for the summary revision would violate the Act, affect the completion of the curriculum and the conduct of examinations, and harm children from the most vulnerable sections of society. The Times of India reports that the department had earlier said about 30 per cent of the state's teachers were drafted for the intensive revision, with Bengaluru among the worst affected. Both papers give the preparatory examinations of the second year of pre-university college as running from 2 to 29 January 2027. The claims and objections of Karnataka's summary revision begin on 1 December.
items.quote: Deploying teachers for SSR will be tantamount to violation of the RTE Act, and affect the completion of curriculum, besides impacting the conduct of examinations. It will be particularly detrimental to children from the vulnerable sections of society,
items.response: Neither report carries a reply from the Chief Electoral Officer. The Times of India reports that the department plans to bring a bill to protect teachers from being drafted for these duties, and that until then teachers are likely to be deployed for a range of duties, among them the Census from January.

items.headline: Ludhiana: Salary of 33 teachers withheld over BLO duty, union objects
items.claim: The office of the electoral registration officer for Sahnewal, who is also the sub-divisional magistrate of Ludhiana East, told the district education officers for secondary and elementary education in a letter of 17 November not to pay the November salaries of 33 government school teachers who had not done booth level officer duty unless they obtained a no-objection certificate from the sub-divisional magistrate's office, Hindustan Times reported on 22 November. The 33 are 18 teachers of secondary and middle schools and 15 teachers and head teachers of primary schools. The teachers say they have already been given appointment letters, identity cards and material for census duty by the same office, and they cite instructions of the additional deputy commissioner (rural development) that staff assigned to census work must not be deployed elsewhere. The Lecturer Cadre Union Punjab says a warning of disciplinary action under section 134 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, has added to the teachers' anxiety. The union's state finance secretary, who is also its Ludhiana district president, called the directive unnecessary mental and financial harassment, and asked for the order to be withdrawn and for staff on census duty to be exempted from booth level officer duty.
items.quote: We will certainly hear out employees who are already assigned census duties and take action accordingly.
items.response: The sub-divisional magistrate of Ludhiana East, Baljinder Singh, told the paper that his office would hear out employees already assigned to census duty and act accordingly. The headline says the salaries were withheld. The text reports the directive not to pay them and does not say whether any salary has been held back.

items.headline: 60,000 Chhattisgarh teachers to miss classrooms for 81 days amid SIR, Census duties
items.claim: Around 60,000 teachers of government schools in Chhattisgarh will be away from their classrooms for nearly 81 days in this academic session for phased duties of the SIR and work for the coming Census, The New Indian Express reported on 24 November. The paper says more than 40,000 teachers have been assigned as booth level officers and designated officers under the SIR, and that more than 50,000 are to be deployed for the Census. It says schools usually get about 220 teaching days in a year, that this session began on 1 April instead of the usual 16 June, and that teachers have been told to finish the syllabus by 30 March. The School Education Minister, Gajendra Yadav, told officials at a review meeting to ensure the syllabus is completed on time and to arrange teachers for schools that have none or only one. The state president of the School Teachers Union said that continuous field duties for the SIR and the Census put immense pressure on the teachers left in schools, and asked the administration to consider this before setting rigid deadlines for the syllabus.
items.quote: It seems proper planning is missing, and many teachers are upset owing to excessive non-academic workload.
items.response: The report carries no statement from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission. It does not say whether the SIR duties it counts belong to the intensive revision or to the summary revision now under way in the state.

items.headline: आगरा में 500 से ज्यादा BLO ने दिखाई सुस्ती, 10 वोटर भी नहीं जोड़ पाए; रुकेगी सैलरी
items.claim: The district administration in Agra has ordered the salaries of 500 booth level officers to be withheld because each added fewer than ten new electors in the summary revision, Dainik Jagran reported on 25 November. The deputy district election officer, Yamunadhar Chauhan, told the paper that the assistant election officers, whom the paper calls AROs, had been directed to withhold the salaries of the 500 for negligence, and that booth level officers who add more than 150 electors would be honoured. The paper says the administration has for the first time sorted the booth level officers into six groups by the number of Form 6 applications each has had filled in, with groups at 10, 25, 50, 100 and 150, and that lists of the other groups are being prepared. Agra district has 30 lakh electors in 3,849 polling booths across nine Assembly constituencies. By the paper's figures, the district received 10,138 applications on Form 6, 577 on Form 7 and 759 on Form 8 on 21 November, and 16,504 on Form 6, 617 on Form 7 and 1,137 on Form 8 on 22 November. In Ghaziabad, private schools have been asked to send parents the links to Forms 4, 6 and 8 through the schools' WhatsApp groups, collect the filled in forms and submit them to the administration through the offices of the district inspector of schools or the basic shiksha adhikari, and to hold parent-teacher meetings to explain the forms, The Times of India reported on 26 November. Over 500 government and private schools in the district have been told to set up electoral literacy clubs, whose teachers are now helping parents with the forms. The Additional District Magistrate, Ajeet Kumar, told the paper that schools give an established channel to a large number of families and that their help will also be sought for the Census from 1 December. A representative of a private school in Sahibabad told the paper that the work adds to the load on teachers, and the paper reports that schools are unhappy with the task in the examination season.
items.quote: Schools have been directed to share links to the three forms through WhatsApp groups. Parents are required to download the forms, take printouts, fill in the requisite details and submit them to the schools,
items.response: The figures and orders are the district administrations'. Neither report carries a statement from the Chief Electoral Officer or from the booth level officers whose salaries are withheld. Jagran does not say how many booth level officers Agra has or over what period the count of fewer than ten was taken.

items.place: Dadri; Gautam Buddh Nagar; Ghaziabad; Mainpuri; Karhal
items.headline: Dadri ERO orders salary cut for 13 BLOs over SSR duty lapses
items.claim: The electoral registration officer for Dadri, Sub-Divisional Magistrate Ashutosh Gupta, ordered on Friday, 27 November, that the November salaries of 13 booth level officers be withheld until further orders and released only with his written approval, Hindustan Times reported on 28 November. His order says the supervisors reported in writing that the 13 did not receive and digitise forms on 21 and 22 November, the summary revision's first special campaign days, when they were to be at their polling stations to take claims and objections, and the officers have been asked to explain in writing through the heads of their institutions. The Times of India reported the same day that booth level officers who have collected few enrolment forms in Ghaziabad and Gautam Budh Nagar will have their areas checked on the ground, on directions the Meerut divisional commissioner and roll observer, Bhanu Chandra Goswami, gave at review meetings in both districts on Thursday, 26 November. Electoral registration officers, assistant electoral registration officers and supervisors are to make random checks of households. Ghaziabad has been told to identify at least 75 booth level officers with the fewest forms in each Assembly constituency, and in Gautam Budh Nagar the work of around 100 is to be verified after the special camps of 28 and 29 November. Goswami also directed that the figures on the ERO-Net portal be matched with those the booth level officers submit, that suspected duplicate entries be verified by field visits and no eligible elector's name be deleted, that recognised parties be given lists of booth level officers with their contact numbers, and that control rooms watch the officers' attendance, location and progress every two hours on the camp days. In Mainpuri, District Magistrate Indramani Tripathi told a press conference on 27 November that three booth level officers in the Karhal area who did not take up the duty they were given had been suspended and penalised, ETV Bharat reported. He said the district had received 37,000 Form 6 applications, 2,051 Form 7 applications and about 3,900 Form 8 applications in the 11 days to 27 November, and that it had a target of about 2.27 lakh new electors set by the ratio of electors to population.
items.quote: The progress of the concerned BLOs is being displayed as zero on the ECINET portal,
items.response: The orders and figures are the officials' own. None of the three reports carries a statement from the booth level officers concerned or their associations. Hindustan Times does not say how many booth level officers Dadri has, and The Times of India does not say how few forms puts an officer on the list for checks.

items.outlet: Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi, daily bulletin dated 19.11.2026, posted on the office's account on X
items.headline: SIR 2026 daily bulletin Claims & Objections status on 19/11/2026
items.claim: The daily bulletin of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer dated 19 November gives 3,18,409 Form 6 applications for inclusion, 584 Form 6A applications, 33,018 Form 7 objections seeking deletion and 1,18,222 Form 8 applications received from the draft of 31 August to 18 November. Up to 30 August the office had received 2,12,400 Form 6, 1,351 Form 6A, 51,471 Form 7 and 2,60,768 Form 8. The bulletin gives the counts for each of Delhi's 13 districts. Since the draft West district received the most Form 6 applications, 38,790, and New Delhi the fewest, 5,615, and South West received the most Form 7 objections, 4,692, and Outer North the fewest, 615. Before the draft, South East and North districts received 14,659 and 11,626 of the 51,471 Form 7 objections. The bulletin says claims and objections received till 25 November will be disposed of by 15 December, and that the final roll is to be published on 22 December.
items.quote: Claims & Objections received till 25.11.2026 will be disposed by 15.12.2026.
items.response: The bulletin counts applications received. It gives no count of applications decided, accepted or rejected, and no count of the enumeration forms of electors left off the draft.

items.outlet: Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi, press note and daily bulletin dated 23.11.2026, posted on the office's account on X
items.headline: Special Drive to Enroll Left Out Electors from Draft Electoral Roll on being marked as ASDD
items.claim: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer said in a press note dated 23 November that 2,81,360 Form 6 applications, 34,204 Form 7 objections and 2,64,688 Form 8 applications had been disposed of so far in the period for disposing of claims and objections, and that 32,95,950 of the 33,14,032 electors issued notices for no mapping or logical discrepancies had been parked for inclusion in the final roll. The office's daily bulletin of the same date gives 3,26,163 Form 6 applications, 604 Form 6A, 34,602 Form 7 objections and 1,22,268 Form 8 applications received from the draft of 31 August to 22 November, and 2,12,400 Form 6, 1,351 Form 6A, 51,471 Form 7 and 2,60,768 Form 8 received up to 30 August. Since the draft West district received the most Form 6 applications, 39,473, and New Delhi the fewest, 5,737, and South West received the most Form 7 objections, 4,781, and Outer North the fewest, 642. The press note says booth level officers have begun handing out enumeration forms to electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, visiting their registered addresses, and that all efforts will be made to trace these electors in coordination with resident welfare associations and the agents of recognised parties, and that the forms are to be handed out and collected by 30 November and disposed of by 10 December. Claims and objections close on 25 November, and the final roll is due on 22 December.
items.quote: As on date, 2,81,360 Forms-6, 34,204 Forms-7 and 2,64,688 Forms-8 have also been disposed during the ongoing period of disposal of claims & objections.
items.response: The press note does not say how many of the applications disposed of were accepted and how many rejected, or whether the counts disposed of include applications received before the draft. It gives no count of enumeration forms handed out to or returned by electors left off the draft.

items.outlet: Election Commission of India, letter No. 23/2026-ERS dated 25 November 2026 to the Chief Electoral Officers of 25 states and union territories
items.headline: Special Summary Revision of Electoral Rolls w.r.t. 01.01.2027 as qualifying date
items.claim: The Election Commission directed the Chief Electoral Officers of 25 states and union territories in a letter of 25 November 2026, No. 23/2026-ERS, to identify and rectify probable incorrect or erroneous entries in the particulars of electors during the special summary revision now under way. The existing particulars on the rolls, such as the name, the relation's name or type, the date of birth, the mobile number and the photograph, are to be compared with the information collected during the Special Intensive Revision, and every mismatch is to be flagged for verification and corrective action. For each flagged entry the booth level officer is to visit the elector to verify the particulars and obtain a filled-in Form 8 signed by the elector where one is required, and the assistant registration officer or the registration officer is to decide the application under the prescribed procedure. The letter says that every correction is to be made only through Form 8 signed by the elector and after the prescribed verification and approval, that no change is to be made solely on the basis of automated identification, and that the work is to be done through the booth level officer, assistant registration officer and registration officer modules of ECINet. The 25 are the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha, Sikkim, Karnataka and Meghalaya. The letter refers to the Commission's letters of 15 October, 4 November and 16 November 2026 on the summary revision in these states and union territories.
items.quote: Since this exercise involves updation of the demographic particulars of electors, all corrections shall be effected only through Form-8, duly signed by the concerned elector and subject to the prescribed verification and approval by the competent authority. No changes shall be made solely on the basis of automated identification.
items.response: The letter gives no count of entries flagged or expected, does not say how such entries arose and sets no date by which the comparison is to be finished. Senior Commission officials told Hindustan Times that the move followed irregularities flagged in the rolls after the revision, and one of them gave as examples one person appearing on the rolls several times and duplicate EPIC numbers. The standfirst of The Hindu's report says it follows complaints of incorrect entries in several cases in the final rolls published after the revision.

items.outlet: Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi, daily bulletin dated 25.11.2026, posted on the office's account on X
items.headline: SIR 2026 daily bulletin Claims & Objections status on 25/11/2026
items.claim: The daily bulletin of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer dated 25 November, the last day for claims and objections, gives 3,31,540 Form 6 applications for inclusion, 618 Form 6A applications, 35,592 Form 7 objections seeking deletion and 1,24,554 Form 8 applications received from the draft of 31 August to 24 November. Up to 30 August the office had received 2,12,400 Form 6, 1,351 Form 6A, 51,471 Form 7 and 2,60,768 Form 8, so 87,063 Form 7 objections had been received in all. Since the draft West district received the most Form 6 applications, 40,029, and New Delhi the fewest, 5,798, and South West received the most Form 7 objections, 4,816, and Outer North the fewest, 645. Counting the objections received before the draft as well, South East received the most Form 7 objections, 18,396, and New Delhi the fewest, 1,249. The bulletin says claims and objections received until 25 November will be disposed of by 15 December, and that the final roll is to be published on 22 December. Election officials told The Times of India that the counts for 24 and 25 November were being compiled across the districts on the evening of 25 November and that the counts up to 25 November would be released on 26 November.
items.quote: Claims & Objections received till 25.11.2026 will be disposed by 15.12.2026.
items.response: The bulletin counts applications received and gives no count of applications decided, accepted or rejected. The Times of India reports that 34,204 Form 7 applications had been disposed of by 23 November, the figure of the press note of 23 November (form7-96), and that officials did not say how many were rejected or how many names were deleted. An official told the paper that filing Form 7 does not mean a name will be deleted, and that of 37 Form 7 applications examined recently 36 were rejected after being found false, one was found to be valid and an FIR was registered.

items.outlet: Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi, press note dated 26.11.2026, posted on the office's account on X
items.headline: Special Drive to Enroll Left Out Electors from Draft Electoral Roll on being marked as ASDD
items.claim: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer said in a press note dated 26 November that the period for claims and objections, which opened on 31 August, closed on 25 November, and that 3,37,970 Form 6 applications for inclusion, 631 Form 6A applications, 37,038 Form 7 objections seeking deletion and 1,26,241 Form 8 applications, 5,01,880 in all, were received in that period. Before 31 August the office had received 2,12,400 Form 6, 1,351 Form 6A, 51,471 Form 7 and 2,60,768 Form 8, 5,25,990 in all. Together the two periods make 88,509 Form 7 objections. As on 26 November, the note says, 3,03,353 Form 6 applications, 36,373 Form 7 objections and 2,76,498 Form 8 applications had been disposed of in the period for disposing of claims and objections, and 33,00,164 of the 33,14,032 electors issued notices for no mapping or logical discrepancies had been parked for inclusion in the final roll, which leaves 13,868. Forms received up to 25 November are to be disposed of by 15 December and the final roll published on 22 December. The note says electors can still file Form 6, and that forms received after 25 November will be disposed of only after the final roll is published. It repeats the schedule for electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, whose enumeration forms are handed out and collected from 18 to 30 November and disposed of by 10 December. It says such an elector will be given back the same EPIC number once the enumeration form is accepted, and that for homeless electors without documents the booth level officer's field verification report will serve as proof of residence.
items.quote: As on date, i.e. 26.11.2026, out of 33,14,032 electors to whom notices have been issued under no-mapping and logical discrepancies, 33,00,164 electors have been parked for inclusion in final electoral roll.
items.response: The press note does not say how many of the applications disposed of were accepted and how many rejected, how many names have been deleted on Form 7 objections, or how many notices were decided against electors. It gives no count of enumeration forms handed out to or returned by electors left off the draft, and The Times of India reports that the number already contacted was not immediately available.

items.headline: Bihar Voter Roll Revision: Semi-Filled Forms Distributed to 87% Voters
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported the Commission saying that about 87 per cent of Bihar's 7.96 crore voters had been given semi-filled enumeration forms on the first booth officer visit.
items.quote: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Friday said that nearly 87 per cent of the 7.96 crore voters in Bihar had been provided with semi-filled enumeration forms for the ongoing special intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: Bihar SIR | BLOs Mass-Uploading Enumeration Forms Without Voters' Knowledge Or Consent : ADR Tells Supreme Court
items.claim: LiveLaw reported that the Association for Democratic Reforms told the Supreme Court that enumeration forms in Bihar were being uploaded by officials without voters' knowledge or consent. This is ADR's allegation in a court filing.
items.quote: "...enumeration forms are being mass-uploaded by BLOs without the knowledge or consent of the voters, in order to achieve the unrealistic target set by the ECI. Many voters have reported that their forms have been submitted online, despite never having met with any BLOs or signed any documents.
items.response: LiveLaw reported that ADR filed the rejoinder in reply to the Commission's counter-affidavit.

items.headline: Form-7 flashpoint: Bengal sees clashes, rival claims of voter roll sabotage
items.claim: National Herald reported that Trinamool workers stopped a vehicle in Khatra, Bankura said to carry thousands of pre-filled Form 7s, that police seized it and began an inquiry, and that both parties traded allegations over bulk Form 7s on the last day for filing.
items.quote: The latest confrontations follow a flashpoint last week in Bankura’s Khatra subdivision, where TMC workers intercepted a vehicle said to be carrying thousands of pre-filled Form-7s. Police seized the vehicle and began an inquiry after TMC alleged the forms were intended to erase “legitimate voters” under cover of the SIR.
items.response: National Herald reported that the BJP alleged its workers were attacked and prevented from filing forms inside government offices.

items.headline: Rajasthan SIR: BJP fraudulently removing Opposition supporters from voter lists, alleges Congress
items.claim: Scroll reported that Rajasthan Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra alleged that computer-printed Form 7s were distributed in every constituency and that booth agents' signatures were forged, and demanded a forensic inquiry. These are the Congress's allegations.
items.quote: “In every Assembly constituency, 10 thousand to 15 thousand fake computerised forms are printed,” he claimed. ... He added that several booth-level agents had given statements to the media that they had not signed these forms, and that the signatures were forged and the applications were incomplete.
items.response: Scroll reported that BJP minister Gautam Dak said a voter proposed for deletion gets time to be heard and that the Congress wanted to create a dispute.

items.headline: In Assam, ‘forged’ forms aimed at deleting thousands of Muslim voters ring alarm bells
items.claim: Scroll reported that during Assam's Special Revision a booth officer in Karimganj North was handed objections against 133 voters on forms she described as half printed and half handwritten, all in the name of one elector who told Scroll he had not filed them, and that hearings were suspended in three Nagaon constituencies after complaints of fake Form 7s.
items.quote: In several Muslim-majority districts and areas of Assam, bulk objections have been filed against voters, seeking to strike their names off the electoral roll. ... In Nagaon district, the hearing process has been suspended in three Assembly constituencies after complaints of fake Form 7 applications.
items.response: Scroll quoted a senior Commission official in Guwahati saying a voter can file any number of objections but that an ERO reviews them individually when one person files more than five.

items.headline: BJP workers in Assam say their names used to seek mass voter deletion – without their knowledge
items.claim: Scroll reported that at least seven people named as objectors on Form 7s in Assam, some of them BJP booth agents and members, said they had not filed the objections.
items.quote: Scroll found at least seven people who denied having filed the complaints, even when their names, voter identity cards and phone numbers had been used in the objection forms.
items.response: Scroll quoted BJP MP Kamakhya Prasad Tasa as saying anyone can file objections and that it is for the Election Commission to take a final call.

items.headline: ‘Nothing to hide’: Assam CM says he has told BJP members to file complaints against ‘Miya’ voters
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma told reporters he had told BJP members to keep filing complaints against people he called 'Miyas' and to fill Form 7s wherever possible during the Special Revision.
items.quote: I myself have told the BJP people that they should keep giving complaints against Miyas. There is nothing to hide about this. I have held meetings, I have done video conferences, and I have told people that, wherever possible, they should fill Form 7s.

items.headline: Fake Objections Filed To Delete Voter Names In Bhopal, Probe Ordered
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that Bhopal's Collector ordered a probe after a man named as objector on Form 7s in Bhopal South-West denied filing them, and that officials found incorrect or fake objector details in several of the district's 9,037 Form 7s.
items.quote: District officials said that across seven Assembly constituencies, a total of 9,037 objections have been filed through Form 7 under the SIR process. While the number is relatively small compared to the total electorate, several cases have been found to involve incorrect or fake complainant details, prompting further scrutiny.
items.response: ETV Bharat quoted District Election Officer Kaushlendra Vikram Singh saying no one's name would be deleted without verification.

items.headline: Akhilesh Yadav flags "massive conspiracy" in SIR, questions use of pre-printed form 7 in UP villages
items.claim: The Samajwadi Party president alleged on X that pre-printed Form 7s were being distributed in villages to strike off opposition voters, that the objectors listed on them could not be traced and that signatures were forged, The Economic Times reported from ANI. He said voters from backward, Dalit and minority communities were most affected.
items.quote: Under SIR, who is distributing the pre-printed Form 7 in villages (through which someone can conspire to get another's name struck off by raising an objection)?

items.headline: Form-7’s journey from a civic chore to a political weapon
items.claim: Frontline reported that Congress general secretary K. C. Venugopal wrote to the Commission on 29 January alleging misuse of Form 7 in several states, and that the Commission said there was no limit on forms per voter but that an ERO must verify when one person files more than five.
items.quote: In the wake of the swirling controversy over Form-7, the Election Commission has clarified that there is no limit on the number of forms a voter can submit in a constituency. However, in order to prevent misuse of the facility, if more than five objections are filed by an individual, the ERO will mandatorily verify the claims.
items.response: Scroll reported on 23 January 2026 that a senior Commission official in Guwahati gave the same rule.

items.headline: सोनभद्र में मतदाता सूची से नाम हटाने की साजिश:फॉर्म 7 में झूठी आपत्तियां दर्ज कर कटवाए जा रहे नाम, जांच शुरू
items.claim: Form 7 objections were filed against 14 voters of one community in part 14 of the Sadar constituency in Sonbhadra, Dainik Bhaskar reported. The booth officer inspected on the spot and found the objections false. Two of the 14 had died and the rest were present. The booth officer told the Samajwadi Party's district secretary that one person had complained and filled in the forms, and the secretary said he would take the case to the District Magistrate.
items.quote: स्थलीय निरीक्षण में इनमें से दो की मृत्यु की पुष्टि हुई, जबकि अन्य सभी मौके पर उपस्थित पाए गए।

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: Residents of a village in Siddharthnagar went to the Mishrauliya police station to complain that about 86 villagers were being objected to by Form 7, BBC News Hindi reported. The booth officer told local media that one person had handed him all 86 forms, that every voter named in them was Muslim and that all of them were present.
items.quote: सभी 86 फ़ॉर्मों में जिनके नाम काटने के लिए आवेदन किया गया है वे सभी मुसलमान हैं. सभी मौजूद भी हैं. इसलिए जैसा जो भी है, मैं अपनी रिपोर्ट लगा दूंगा.
items.response: The Chief Electoral Officer told BBC News Hindi "जिन लोगों के नाम कटवाने के लिए फ़ॉर्म 7 मिला है, उन्हें नोटिस दिए बिना और सुनवाई के बगैर नाम नहीं काटे जाएंगे."

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: A Samajwadi Party former minister from Gonda said more than 6,000 deletions were being sought in the Karnalganj constituency and showed BBC News Hindi printed Form 7s, one of which carried the district, polling station and constituency already filled in but no objector's name. BBC News Hindi reported that every form had 'already enrolled' ticked as the reason.
items.quote: इसके अलावा जिस कॉलम पर आपत्ति का कारण दर्ज करना होता है, सभी फ़ॉर्मों में उनमें 'पहले से नामांकित' पर टिक किया गया है.
items.response: At a press conference on 6 February the Chief Electoral Officer said "कोई भी राजनीतिक दल का कार्यकर्ता एक दिन में 10 फ़ॉर्म से ज़्यादा नहीं जमा कर सकता है. जो फ़ॉर्म 7 जमा किए गए हैं, उनकी जांच होगी. अभी कोई नाम नहीं काटे जा रहे हैं." The BJP called the Samajwadi Party's allegations baseless.

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: The Samajwadi Party MP for Badaun gave the District Magistrate a list alleging that objections were being filed to a plan, BBC News Hindi reported, including a Form 7 against an elected ward member of Kakrala who said he had been a voter since 2012. In Datganj, a BJP Assembly convener whose name was on an objection told BBC News Hindi he had signed forms the party gave him and did not personally know the voter.
items.quote: मैं बीजेपी का विधानसभा संयोजक हूं. मुझे पार्टी की तरफ़ से कुछ फ़ॉर्म मिले थे, हमने इसे साइन कर दिया
items.response: The BJP called the allegations baseless, BBC News Hindi reported, and the Commission said complaints would be examined.

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: The Congress said its workers in Sant Kabir Nagar caught Form 7s being submitted to delete villagers and that the man whose signature was on them denied signing, BBC News Hindi reported. BBC News Hindi said it could not verify the video of the incident.
items.quote: इसमें जिस व्यक्ति के हस्ताक्षर थे, वह इनकार कर रहा है कि ये हस्ताक्षर उसके हैं.
items.response: The Chief Electoral Officer said "इस पर उस व्यक्ति को एफ़आईआर दर्ज करानी चाहिए जिनका हस्ताक्षर फर्ज़ी है." He said officers had been told to make sure each Form 7 was submitted by the person whose signature it carried.

items.headline: Lakhs of ‘doubtful voters’ deleted in Assam based on BJP complaints, says Himanta Sarma
items.claim: Scroll reported, citing PTI, that after Assam's final roll the Chief Minister said several deletions had been made on complaints filed by BJP workers.
items.quote: “As far as possible, our party members filed complaints,” the BJP leader said. “Names have been struck off based on these.”

items.headline: Inside the ‘organised’ attempt to delete 15,000 voters in Gujarat’s Somnath
items.claim: Newslaundry reported that the 15,663 Form 7s in Somnath were filed by 269 people, each filing 50 or more, that copies it reviewed had the voter's details printed in English and the objector's details handwritten in Gujarati, and that six of the objectors filed affidavits saying they had not filed them.
items.quote: Of the 15,663 Form-7 applications, a staggering number appeared to be pre-filled and then submitted by just 269 people. ... Newslaundry has reviewed copies of Form-7s where voter details – such as name, mobile number, constituency, EPIC number, and booth number – are printed in English, while the objectors' details are handwritten in Gujarati.
items.response: Newslaundry reported that the District Election Officer, V. N. Upadhyay, said he had deployed six AEROs to verify the objections and assured that no name would be deleted arbitrarily.

items.headline: Muslim Voter Deletion Attempts in Alwar: EC's Silence Raises Questions
items.claim: The Quint reported that thousands of Form 7s in Alwar were filed in the names of BJP booth agents, several of whom said their signatures were forged, and that no FIR or inquiry had been announced a month later.
items.quote: As per copies of forms, seen by The Quint, they were overwhelmingly filed under the names of Booth Level Agents (BLAs) working for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and predominantly targeted Muslim voters in Rural Alwar. ... Yet no FIR, no administrative inquiry, no forensic audit of handwriting or digital origin has been announced in Alwar.
items.response: The Quint reported that calls to the District Magistrate and Sub-Divisional Magistrate for comment went unanswered.

items.headline: Form 7 controversy deepens strain on SIR 2.0
items.claim: National Herald reported that the Commission wrote to West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer to send all Form 7 objections to EROs by 16 February and dispose of them by statutory procedure, and that it had taken cognisance of reports of Form 7 records being burnt.
items.quote: The ECI's latest communication also cited reports alleging the burning of records related to Form 7 objections in parts of West Bengal — an issue it said it had taken cognisance of.

items.headline: SIR: 544 Muslim voters marked for deletion in UP village leads to one man
items.claim: Siasat reported, citing The Indian Express, that Form 7s against 544 voters of a Shamli village were found with a booth officer, said to have been already printed with the voters' EPIC numbers. All of them named one applicant, whom officials could not find, and the District Magistrate said the forms were fake and the probe found nothing.
items.quote: The forms were allegedly already printed with Electors’ Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers and other personal details. In the forms, the applicant cited relocation from the village as the reason for seeking their deletion from the electoral rolls.
items.response: DM Arvind Kumar Chauhan ordered a probe and later said that the case “didn’t have any substance.” “We got an investigation done and found nothing,” he added.

items.headline: Gujarat HC notice: Probe sought into fake voter deletion pleas in SIR row
items.claim: Deccan Herald reported that the Gujarat High Court issued notice to the Commission and the state on two petitions seeking a Special Investigation Team inquiry into Form 7 objections filed during the SIR. The Kodinar petition says about 47 people filed 6,722 applications, and the Sidhpur petitioners say one person filed about 140.
items.quote: The petitions have sought investigation by the Special Investigation Team. They have claimed that as part of a "larger conspiracy" thousands of illegal objection applications under form-7 were filed seeking deletion of voters' names during the recently concluded Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in the state.
items.response: Deccan Herald reported that the matter was posted for further hearing on 7 July.

items.headline: Enumeration Form 'Must' For Draft Electoral Roll
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported Hyderabad's District Election Officer R. V. Karnan explaining that booth officers would hand out enumeration forms already printed with each elector's details and photograph, which the elector completes and signs.
items.quote: The BLOs will carry forms already containing the elector’s photograph. Electors must paste a recent photograph, fill details and sign a declaration. BLOs will distribute forms with pre‑printed details of existing electors and guide households in filling them.

items.headline: BJP Lodges Complaint Against Officials Allegedly Favouring AIMIM
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Telangana BJP alleged to the Chief Electoral Officer that booth officers in Hyderabad were handing enumeration forms in bulk to AIMIM leaders at party camps and letting them upload filled forms. This is the BJP's allegation.
items.quote: The BJP on Tuesday alleged that booth level officers (BLOs) were avoiding mandatory house-to-house visits in the city. Instead, they were found to be distributing enumeration forms related to ongoing SIR exercise ‘in bulk’ to AIMIM leaders at party organised camps set up in several constituencies of the Hyderabad district, the BJP alleged.

items.headline: SIR: BJP Urges CEO To Conduct Probe Into Allegations
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that the BJP alleged that some booth officers in Serilingampally uploaded the blank back of enumeration forms to the Commission's app without the voter's details, and asked the Chief Electoral Officer for a probe. This is the BJP's allegation.
items.quote: Party’s State Election Commission Affairs committee chairman Marri Shashidhar Reddy alleged some BLOs have uploaded the reverse side of the Enumeration Form to the official BLO mobile application without filling in any mandatory voter details on the front side in Vivekananda Nagar division’s 575 to 580 booths.

items.headline: Form-7 misuse: Supreme Court to consider Congress MP’s plea alleging targeted deletions in U.P.
items.claim: The Hindu reported that the Supreme Court agreed to consider an application by Congress MP Tanuj Punia alleging that Form 7 objections in the Uttar Pradesh SIR were filed with false particulars, forged signatures and in the names of people who later denied filing them. The application cited one person filing objections against 32 electors in Hata, Kushinagar, and a UP Congress claim of 700 to 800 objections in four Khalilabad booths.

items.headline: Uttarakhand Congress alleges Form-7 misuse to delete voters during SIR, approaches EC
items.claim: The Pioneer reported that an Uttarakhand Congress delegation told the Chief Electoral Officer that one person had filed objections against about 6,400 voters and about 1,200 people had filed more than ten each. These are the Congress's figures.
items.quote: "Our data analysis revealed that a single individual has filed objections against the names of approximately 6,400 people. There are about 1,200 individuals who have submitted more than 10 objections each. An objection has even been filed against the name of a sitting Congress MLA," Rawat said.
items.response: The Pioneer reported that CEO V. V. R. C. Purushottam said the revision followed the rules and that observers had been sent to districts with many objections, and that Additional CEO Vijay Kumar Jogdande said an ERO must scrutinise cases where one person seeks the deletion of more than five names.

items.headline: Uttarakhand SIR: The unsolved mystery of BJP agents’ ‘forged’ objections against Muslim voters
items.claim: Newslaundry reported that 35 people named as objectors on 1,657 Form 7s in Jhabrera, 31 of them BJP booth agents, said in affidavits that their names, EPIC numbers and signatures had been misused.
items.quote: In affidavits submitted to the Haridwar district administration on August 18 and 19, each of the 35 said an “unknown person” used their name, EPIC number and a forged signature to file Form 7 applications – which are requests seeking the deletion of voters.
items.response: Newslaundry quoted the Jhabrera ERO saying the objections were cancelled after those named sought to withdraw them and the voters would not be deleted, and that the Election Commission would not order any investigation and those whose names were misused should file an FIR.

items.headline: 50,000 Forms Filed Seeking Deletion of Votes
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported, in a story datelined Hyderabad that does not say whether the figure covers the state or the district, that the Commission had received close to 50,000 Form 7 applications against entries in the draft roll, and that parties at a meeting chaired by Hyderabad's District Election Officer asked for the Form 10 lists by Assembly constituency.
items.quote: Amid nearly 93 lakh voters listed with logical discrepancies or placed in the absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) list, the Election Commission of India (ECI) has received close to 50,000 Form-7 applications seeking deletion of names or raising objections to entries in the draft electoral rolls. Political parties have asked election officials to provide details of the Form-7 applications through Form 10, which is the consolidated list of objections and deletion requests received through Form 7.
items.response: Deccan Chronicle reported that officials gave parties the total number of applications at a meeting at the GHMC office but did not share figures by Assembly constituency.

items.headline: Uttarakhand SIR: Who is targeting Muslim voters?
items.claim: Newslaundry reported from its investigation in Uttarakhand that numerous applications were filed to delete Muslim voters' names from the rolls, many in the names of people it said were associated with the BJP. It reported that some people named as objectors later filed affidavits saying they had never filed the objections and that their names, EPIC numbers and signatures had been used fraudulently.

items.place: Delhi (Karol Bagh, Patel Nagar, Sangam Vihar)
items.headline: Delhi SIR: BJP Agent Files 35 Removal Requests in Two Days, ECINet Allows BLAs to Go Over 10-Claims Limit
items.claim: The Hindu reported that Form 10 lists published for 21 to 27 September showed four people in Delhi filing more than ten applications a day through the Commission's ECINET portal, which does not enforce the limit of ten a day for booth agents.
items.quote: Fresh lapses have come to light in the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) exercise in Delhi, with official data showing that booth-level agents (BLAs) bypassed the Election Commission’s (EC) cap on submitting only 10 applications a day during the claims and objections phase by filing through the panel’s ECINET portal, which has no such restriction in place. ... The software has no mechanism to impose the prescribed limit, effectively allowing the guidelines to be bypassed.
items.response: The Hindu reported that the office of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer did not respond to a request for comment.

items.headline: Civil society groups, Congress demand FIRs over bulk Form 7s seeking deletion of names
items.claim: The Hindu reported that as of September 28, 4,000 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names had been filed in Karnataka, which it said mostly targeted Muslim voters. It reported that ten people filed Form 7s seeking deletion of 1,363 names in Babaleshwar in one day, often on forms with the voters' details already printed and only the objector's name handwritten. In Bhalki, it reported, 30 people filed Form 7s seeking deletion of 1,700 names. Civil society groups and the Karnataka Congress demanded that the Commission lodge criminal complaints.
items.response: V. Anbukumar, CEO, Karnataka, was not available for comment.

items.headline: Nearly 29,000 Form-7 applications filed during Telangana SIR
items.claim: Telangana Today reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, said 28,753 Form 7 applications had been filed in Telangana, about 5,000 of them in Hyderabad, and that forms received in bulk would be examined with special care.
items.quote: Revealing SIR of electoral rolls status in the State on Thursday, Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C Sudharsan Reddy said 28,753 Form-7 applications were filed, so far. ... “Special care is being taken while deciding the Form-7 received in bulk. All claims and objections will be placed on the website of the CEO, so that citizens are able to see the list and lodge objections, if any,” he said.

items.headline: Telangana SIR: Congress alleges vote deletion bid in Musheerabad
items.claim: Siasat reported that the Telangana Congress complained to the Chief Electoral Officer that a BJP booth agent in Musheerabad had filed Form 7 applications against a Congress booth agent and about 30 members of his family, on forms that were printed in advance. This is the Congress's allegation.
items.quote: Kumar said that the applications were pre-printed and prepared in advance, rather than being individually and independently prepared by the concerned applicants. “The circumstances raise serious questions regarding the source from which these forms were obtained, who prepared them, who supplied the information contained in them, and whether the applications were submitted with the knowledge and consent of the persons shown as applicants.” the complaint stated.
items.response: Siasat reported that the Congress asked for an investigation to establish the facts, including a forensic examination of whether the forms came from a common source.

items.headline: Karnataka BJP Leader Withdraws Form-7 Pleas To Delete 243 Voters After SIR Row
items.claim: A BJP leader in Koppa, Chikkamagaluru, wrote on 1 October to withdraw Form 7 objections seeking the deletion of 243 voters filed on 21 and 22 September, saying the voters were found on re-verification to live within the polling stations' areas, Free Press Journal reported.
items.quote: "withdrawing the Form-7 objections submitted on September 21 and 22"
items.response: No response from the election authorities was reported.

items.headline: Karnataka SIR: ECI flags bulk Form 7 claims, orders action against false declarations
items.claim: The New Indian Express reported that the Commission wrote to election officials in Bengaluru that bulk Form 7 applications had come to its notice, with allegations that some were not authentic. It reported that the Commission directed Electoral Registration Officers to act against applicants who knowingly make false declarations, after an inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

items.headline: After Musheerabad, Telangana Congress says it found more pre-printed Form 7s aimed at deleting Muslim voters in Bahadurpura
items.claim: The South First reported that it had seen a Form 7 from a polling station in Aliyabad, in Bahadurpura, with the voter's details printed and the objector's part left blank. The Congress alleged that such forms had been handed to BJP booth agents through the party's constituency in-charges.
items.quote: South First has seen one such pre-printed application seeking the deletion of a Muslim voter from a polling station in Aliyabad. It has the voter’s details and address pre-filled, but the applicant’s details are left blank.
items.response: The South First reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, said at a press briefing that officials would thoroughly verify all Form 7 applications before making any decision.

items.headline: SIR: Single Jharkhand Assembly Constituency Accounts for Over a Third of Voter Deletion Requests
items.claim: Of 13,443 Form 7 applications for deletion in Jharkhand, 4,790 came from the Chatra Assembly seat, about 36% of the state's total, in figures the Chief Electoral Officer released on 1 October, The Wire reported, citing the Hindustan Times. West Singhbhum had 1,906 and Deoghar 1,099.
items.quote: About one in every three requests to remove names from Jharkhand's electoral roll has come from just one assembly constituency, data released on Thursday (October 1) by the state's chief electoral officer (CEO) revealed. ... Of the 13,443 Form 7 submitted for deletion of names, 4,790 pertain to the Chatra assembly seat in Chatra district, roughly 36% of the state's total.
items.response: The Wire reported that the Chief Electoral Officer said the Chatra figures were checked with the district administration and no bulk applications beyond the limit were found, and that address changes on Form 8 generate Form 7 entries automatically.

items.headline: Karnataka: 43.43 lakh SIR notices delivered, 84,900 Form 7 applications received so far
items.claim: Vartha Bharati reported, quoting the Chief Electoral Officer's office, that Karnataka received 8,85,952 Form 6, 4,648 Form 6A, 84,900 Form 7 and 11,78,028 Form 8 applications between 16 June and 1 October, and that 35,60,833 hearings had been held, with 7,82,304 pending.
items.response: The figures are a running count while hearings continue. Karnataka's final roll was published on 27 October 2026, and no count of the hearings' outcome came with it.

items.headline: Five FIRs filed across Karnataka over alleged misuse of Form 7, BJP threatens protest
items.claim: The News Minute reported that five FIRs were registered in Belagavi, Bidar and Mysuru over Form 7s alleged to carry false information or forged signatures, and that in Belagavi the voters' details had been filled in beforehand with the objector's name handwritten or blank. In Bidar the complaint alleged that 3,244 voters were falsely shown as shifted or absent, and an FIR naming 32 people was registered on 1 October.
items.quote: The names and other details of voters had already been filled in, while the names of the persons shown as objectors were either handwritten or left blank. ... None of the five FIRs filed in connection with the Karnataka cases invokes the Representation of the People Act.
items.response: The News Minute reported that Karnataka CEO V. Anbu Kumar said that although 84,900 Form 7s had been received, no one had been taken off the rolls.

items.headline: SIR: 15-Pre-Printed Form 7 Now Appear in Goshamahal Constituency
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported, citing Congress sources, that a BJP booth agent brought 15 pre-printed Form 7s to the booth officer at booth 173 in Goshamahal and that the booth officer refused to accept them.
items.quote: Hyderabad: After Musheerabad and Bahadurpura Assembly constituencies, 15-pre-printed Form 7, seeking deletion of Muslim names from voter lists surfaced in Goshamahal constituency. The issue came to light after the local booth level officer (BLO) refused to accept the forms allegedly submitted by BJP booth level agent (BLA).
items.response: Deccan Chronicle reported that the District Election Officer had reportedly directed the Musheerabad ERO to file criminal cases against the booth agent there.

items.headline: Owaisi says Hyderabad will see massive protests if ECI doesn’t act on Form 7 misuse
items.claim: The News Minute reported that AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that Form 7s were being filed to have Muslim voters deleted and warned of protests, and that Congress leaders said the pre-printed forms found in Goshamahal and Bahadurpura were unsigned and were not accepted by booth officers.
items.quote: Following the Musheerabad incident, Congress leaders said they also found pre-printed forms seeking deletion of Muslim voters in Goshamahal and Bahadurpura constituencies, but these forms were unsigned and not accepted by the Booth Level Officers (BLOs).

items.headline: Karnataka BJP leaders meet DGP, seek review of FIRs over Form 7 filings
items.claim: The News Minute reported that Karnataka BJP leaders asked the state police chief to review the FIRs against party workers, saying filing several Form 7s is not by itself a crime and the rules set no limit on their number.
items.quote: Ashoka said Congress leaders had pressured the police to register criminal cases against BJP workers. “Submitting Form 7 is not a crime. It is the Election Commission, not the police station, that has to determine the truth and validity of a voter,” he said.
items.response: The News Minute reported that Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara said ministers had gone to the CEO's office to submit a memorandum.

items.headline: Contested Form 7s rejected, no bulk filings: Telangana DEO
items.claim: Siasat reported, citing PTI, that Hyderabad's District Election Officer R. V. Karnan said the Form 7s in Goshamahal and Musheerabad were not received in bulk and were rejected, the Goshamahal forms because they were unsigned and the Musheerabad ones because the electors were found living at the address.
items.quote: Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) Commissioner and District Election Officer R. V. Karnan told PTI that the Form 7 applications were not received in bulk but in much smaller numbers. In Goshamahal, the applicant did not sign the submitted forms, making them ineligible for consideration.
items.response: Siasat reported that BJP state president N. Ramchander Rao said no BJP booth agents had submitted any such Form 7 applications, and that the Chief Electoral Officer had said bulk forms from a party had to be properly enquired into and verified.

items.headline: Telangana SIR: Congress seeks SIT probe into alleged Form-7 misuse
items.claim: The News Minute quoted a memo of 5 October in which the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, told District Election Officers that bulk Form 7 applications had been filed and that EROs should act under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act against anyone who knowingly made a false declaration.
items.quote: Meanwhile, the Telangana Chief Election Officer (CEO) C Sudharshan Reddy, on October 5, issued a notice stating, “[I]t has come to the notice of this office that there have been instances of filing of bulk applications in Form-7 before the EROs and it is also alleged that such forms are not genuine.”
items.response: Siasat reported that the CEO said this action would follow an inquiry. The memo itself was not found on the CEO Telangana website.

items.headline: SIR: Telangana CEO orders action over bulk Form 7 filings, Congress seeks SIT probe
items.claim: The South First reported that the Telangana Congress asked the Hyderabad Police Commissioner to register an FIR and set up a Special Investigation Team over pre-filled Form 7s in three constituencies, and to examine the BJP's role. These are the Congress's allegations.
items.quote: One such form seen by South First had the voter’s name and address pre-filled while the applicant’s details were blank. ... The Congress alleged that the forms had been printed in advance and asked the police to establish whether the persons named as applicants had actually signed them or even knew about the applications.
items.response: The South First reported that the Congress said the Police Commissioner had assured it he would study the matter and take action.

items.headline: 91,278 Form 7 applications received in Karnataka, officials says no names deleted so far
items.claim: Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer said 91,278 Form 7 applications were received between 16 June and 4 October, that no name had yet been deleted because of one, and that each would go through a notice and hearing before an officer decided. He said EROs would inquire into bulk applications and that his office had registered no FIR, The News Minute reported.
items.quote: Karnataka has received 91,278 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names from electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR). However, no voter has been deleted through the process so far. ... “Just because objections have been filed, no name has been deleted so far from the electoral roll,” Anbukkumar said at a press conference.

items.headline: Karnataka SIR Row: FIR Against BJP BLAs For 'Fake Voter Deletion' In Jayanagar
items.claim: Jayanagar police in Bengaluru registered an FIR against two BJP booth level agents and others on a complaint by Karnataka Mahila Congress president Sowmya Reddy, The Daily Jagran reported, carrying ANI. The complaint alleged Form 7 applications with forged signatures seeking to delete 5,698 voters by falsely claiming they had shifted.
items.response: No response from the BJP, the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission was reported.

items.headline: Goshamahal Voter Deletion Row: Owaisi Seeks ECI Action
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that pre-printed Form 7s seeking the deletion of 122 electors, all Muslim, were submitted at booth 28 in Goshamahal in the name of a BJP supporter, and that the booth officer refused them. This is AIMIM's allegation.
items.quote: We are placing a specific example before the Election Commission from Booth Number 28 in the Goshamahal assembly segment. As part of a deliberate plan, pre-printed Form 7 applications were submitted to delete the names of 122 electors.
items.response: Siasat reported on 5 October, citing PTI, that BJP state president N. Ramchander Rao said no BJP booth agents had submitted any such Form 7 applications.

items.headline: Police probe fake Form-7 applications seeking deletion of 31 voters in Musheerabad
items.claim: Telangana Today reported that Chikkadpally police were checking the forms, signatures and voter details in the Musheerabad case and whether similar forms were filed elsewhere, and that the forms had reportedly been rejected.
items.quote: Police officials are verifying the forms, signatures, and voter details and are also looking into who prepared and submitted the applications and whether others were involved. Officials are also checking whether similar applications were filed elsewhere. Meanwhile, the disputed applications have reportedly been rejected following scrutiny.

items.headline: 28 मतदाताओं के नाम हटाने के लिए फर्जी Form-7 का मामला, कोर्ट ने FIR के दिए आदेश
items.claim: A Judicial Magistrate First Class in Haldwani ordered the Banbhoolpura police on 6 October to register an FIR and investigate. A booth agent of a party had said that Form 7s seeking to delete 28 voters in part 134 were filed online in his name without his knowledge, and the court held that tracing who filed them needed a police investigation, Haldwani Express News reported.
items.quote: विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) प्रक्रिया के दौरान 28 मतदाताओं के नाम मतदाता सूची से हटाने के लिए कथित तौर पर फर्जी तरीके से Form-7 दाखिल किए जाने के मामले में न्यायिक मजिस्ट्रेट प्रथम, हल्द्वानी ने थाना बनभूलपुरा पुलिस को एफआईआर दर्ज कर विवेचना करने के निर्देश दिए हैं। ... हालांकि, अदालत ने स्पष्ट किया कि मतदाता सूची में संशोधन से संबंधित यह उपचार और कथित अपराध की पुलिस जांच दो अलग-अलग विषय हैं।
items.response: Haldwani Express News reported that the police had told the court the complaint concerned SIR Form 7s and that the complainant could object before the assistant returning officer.

items.headline: NDA leaders seek K'taka Guv intervention over 'govt interference' in SIR
items.claim: A BJP and JD(S) delegation including Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy and R Ashoka asked Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot to direct the state government to stop registering criminal cases against people who filed Form 7 objections, ThePrint reported, carrying PTI. They alleged police were being misused to intimidate BJP workers and that the Chief Electoral Office had given in to the state government.
items.quote: It urged Gehlot to issue appropriate directions to the state government to ensure that "false and unwarranted" FIRs and criminal cases under the BNS are not registered against individuals, including BJP workers, in connection with the SIR exercise.
items.response: No response from the state government, the Chief Electoral Officer or Congress was reported.

items.headline: Congress and BJP-JD(S) trade charges over bulk Form 7 filings during SIR in Karnataka
items.claim: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar alleged on 6 October that BJP and JD(S) workers had filed Form 7 applications in bulk and then collected back and destroyed more than a lakh of them, threatening booth officers, The News Minute reported. This is his allegation.
items.quote: "They have burnt them."
items.response: BJP MLC C T Ravi asked the Commission to register a case against people making baseless allegations and sought legal action against Shivakumar.

items.headline: First FIR Related to Form-7
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Musheerabad ERO filed a police complaint, and Chikkadpally police registered a case, against a BJP booth agent who tried to submit 30 pre-printed Form 7s, the first such case in Telangana.
items.quote: The case was booked under BNS Sections 217 (giving false information to a public servant) and 318 (2) (cheating) and Section 31 of the Representation of People Act (making false declarations). ... “The BLO concerned and BLO supervisor collectively refused to receive the bulk forms in spite of repeated requests from the said BLA of BJP and have not given any acknowledgement in token of receipt…,” the FIR copy read.
items.response: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Congress welcomed the case and asked the police to find who printed and supplied the forms.

items.headline: K'taka: BJP-JDS delegation seeks withdrawal of FIR over Form-7 issue
items.claim: A BJP and JD(S) delegation led by Jayanagar MLA C K Ramamurthy went to Jayanagar police station in Bengaluru and demanded that the FIR against BJP workers over Form 7 applications be withdrawn, IANS reported. They warned of an intensified agitation if it was not, and alleged that applications meant to be confidential had been handed to Congress workers.
items.quote: The delegation demanded that the FIR be withdrawn immediately.
items.response: No police response was reported.

items.headline: K'taka: BJP-JDS delegation seeks withdrawal of FIR over Form-7 issue
items.claim: Police at Shanivarasanthe in Kodagu district registered a case against five BJP booth level workers on a complaint that they sought the deletion of 64 voters in Byadagutta village through Form 7 applications, IANS reported.
items.quote: Police have registered a case against the five persons and are investigating the allegations.

items.headline: For Every Form 6 Disposal, Six Form 7s Cleared in Delhi: Report
items.claim: The Wire reported, citing The Hindu's analysis of Delhi's constituency data, that 569 Form 6 applications and 3,209 Form 7 applications were disposed of between 31 August and 4 October, about six Form 7s for every Form 6. It said 2,352 of the Form 7s were disposed of in the last two weeks, and that 2.12 lakh Form 6 and 51,747 Form 7 applications had been submitted from 16 June, before the claims period began on 31 August.
items.quote: only 569 Form 6 applications were disposed of between August 31 and October 4
items.response: No response from the Chief Electoral Officer was reported. On 22 October the Chief Electoral Officer's office replaced the weekly disposal report on which this analysis rests, and officials said the earlier figures were wrong. The revised figures are entered separately, from The Hindu of 23 October.

items.headline: Over 24,000 Form 7 Applications Received During SIR In Telangana
items.claim: Data released by Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer on 8 October showed 24,323 Form 7 applications received from 15 June to 7 October and 12,204 names deleted, PTI reported. The figure is lower than the 28,753 Form 7s the CEO said on 1 October had been filed, and the reports do not explain the difference.
items.quote: Election authorities in Telangana on Thursday said 24,323 Form-7 applications have been received so far during SIR of electoral rolls, of which 12,204 names were removed.
items.response: State BJP president N Ramchander Rao said the Commission decides deletions only after field inquiries.

items.case: CRL.P 102783/2026 and connected matters, a BJP functionary's petition, Karnataka High Court at Dharwad
items.headline: Karnataka High Court Grants Interim Protection To BJP Leader Booked Over Alleged Attempt To Delete Muslim Voters' Names During SIR
items.claim: The Karnataka High Court at Dharwad told the police on 8 October to take no coercive steps until 13 October against a BJP functionary and two supporters booked over Form 7s against voters in Belagavi, LiveLaw and Bar and Bench reported. A Congress block agent's complaint, as the police record it, alleges they handed about 198 fabricated Form 7s to the booth officer. On 13 October Justice Venkatesh Naik T stayed the investigation until the next hearing, citing a coordinate bench's stay in similar cases on 9 October, Bar and Bench reported. The Court allowed the State to seek to have the order modified or vacated, and posted the matter for 29 October.
items.quote: Till then, the respondent-police/IO shall not take any coercive steps against the petitioners.
items.response: The Government Pleader sought time to file objections and the latest investigation report.

items.headline: Delhi CEO restricts number of Form 7 an individual can file to raise objections
items.claim: Delhi Chief Electoral Officer Ashok Kumar announced on 9 October that the Commission had decided to limit an individual voter to ten Form 7 objections for the whole claims and objections period and five a month during continuous updation, citing bulk objections on unsubstantiated grounds, IANS reported. The statement said registration officers would act against false objections under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
items.quote: A maximum number of 10 Form-7 applications during the entire period of claims and objections

items.case: W.P. No. 31887 of 2026 and W.P. No. 31893 of 2026, two BJP booth agents' petitions, Karnataka High Court
items.headline: SIR: Karnataka High Court grants relief to BJP booth agents booked for attempting to delete voters
items.claim: The Karnataka High Court stayed proceedings in two FIRs against two BJP booth agents accused over bulk Form 7s against voters in Bengaluru's Malleshwaram constituency, Bar and Bench reported. The judge said the FIRs looked premature because the registration officer had not yet decided the Form 7s. One FIR concerns applications against 778 voters in ward 64 and the other objections against 136 voters in ward 45.
items.quote: The concerned officer will decide.
items.response: The State said the allegations of impersonation and forgery needed investigation and that the agents filed more applications than allowed. The complainant's counsel said the bulk filing was a conspiracy aimed at OBC and SC/ST voters.

items.headline: In UP SIR, ECI Software Auto-generated 87,127* Forms to Delete Voters Without a Reason
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that in the Tarabganj and Pilibhit Assembly constituencies 90 per cent of Form 7 deletion requests were against Muslim voters, and that in Tarabganj 188 objections were filed under one name on the same date against voters of one booth. It said the published data give no identity of an objector beyond a name, so the objectors cannot be checked.
items.quote: Out of 4.3 lakh Form 7 applications, in two assembly constituencies in UP, people with the same name filed hundreds of requests almost exclusively against Muslim voters. In Tarabganj and Pilibhit assembly constituencies, 90 percent of the deletion requests filed were against Muslims.
items.response: The Collective said it sent questions to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission and had no reply by publication. The report does not say how it determined the voters' religion.

items.headline: Thousands of votes marked for deletion in Andhra Pradesh without reasons on record
items.claim: The News Minute found that 40,006 electors were named for deletion in Form 7 applications in Andhra Pradesh between 29 September and 10 October, the last 12 days of claims and objections, and that 20,959 of them had an Electoral Registration Officer or an Assistant Electoral Registration Officer named as the objector in the Commission's consolidated Form 10 statements. Where an ordinary elector is the objector the statements give a reason, and where an officer is named they give none. In the 20 constituencies with the most names sought for deletion, officers were the objectors for 16,241 of 21,115. In Chandragiri the assistant officer is named 1,991 times and the officer 6 times among 2,452 names, in Palacole the officer 311 times and the assistant officer 1,701 times among 2,220, in Ongole the officer 1,277 times among 1,712, and in Narsapuram 1,369 times among 1,450. TNM could not read the statements from before 29 September, because each stays online for a week. The report sets out that rule 13(2) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 lets only an elector on the roll object to an entry, and that section 22 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and rule 21A let the officer delete a name of his own motion after giving the elector a chance to be heard. Two registration officers told TNM that the ERO-NET software is built so that the reason does not show, and one of them said that it allows deletions to be uploaded in bulk.
