An assistant registration officer said the only option in his login is to mark an elector ineligible, which generates the Form 7, and that the reason is then not listed.
items.quote: We noticed that when Form 7s are filed by normal citizens, the consolidated statement carries the reason for objection. But the reason for objection is not listed when an ERO or AERO is the objector.
items.response: TNM sent questions to Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Vivek Yadav, and had no reply when it published. The Chief Electoral Officer answered on 28 October that the forms were generated through the software on the Commission's instructions for electors found ineligible after notices (form7-65). One registration officer told TNM that the officer is never in fact the objector, that the request comes from a family member or a booth level agent, and that his office holds documents to show it.

items.headline: As thousands were deleted from electoral rolls using auto-generated Form-7s, ECI gave no SOPs to State Electoral Officers
items.claim: Several State election officials told The Hindu that the Commission's software, ERONet, generated Form 7s automatically when officials deleted electors at the hearings of the revision, and that the forms carried the officers' digital signatures, the paper reported on 15 October. It named Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal as states where officials had used this route to delete electors with unresolved logical discrepancies or with no mapping, and it said other reports had put the names deleted this way at more than 87,000 in Uttar Pradesh and more than 95,000 in Uttarakhand. The paper reported, from sources, that no written communication or standard operating procedure on these forms was shared with the election authorities in the states. It set out that the electoral rules make no provision for a registration officer or an assistant registration officer to file a Form 7, and that the Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2024 makes none for the registration officer to file one, though the officer, who decides objections, can delete a name found ineligible. The paper reports that the manual mentions auto-generated Form 7s only in the verification of Photo Similar Entries, where the forms ERONet generates are not filed by the registration officer and must be signed by the booth level officer after a field verification, or the system cannot accept or process them.
items.quote: According to several State electoral officials The Hindu spoke with, the ECI’s software, ERONet, automatically generated these Form 7s when officials deleted voters during the SIR hearings. The auto-generated forms came with the officers’ digital signatures.
items.response: The paper reported that the Commission had yet to answer an official query on the matter. Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer said on 28 October that the forms in that state were generated through ECINET in the officers' names as the Commission instructs, for electors found ineligible after a notice and a speaking order (form7-65). Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer's office called the account of such forms in that state misleading on 13 October, and said notices, hearings, scrutiny and recorded orders came before any action (up-02).

items.headline: Tracking ECI’s U-Turns on Form 7: In West Bengal, After Allowing Unlimited Objections, ECI Caps Them at 10
items.claim: The Wire reported that on 16 January 2026, during West Bengal's extended claims period, the Commission told the state's Chief Electoral Officer in writing that the law set no limit on the number of Form 7 objections one voter could file, and that on 9 October it capped them at ten per voter for a whole claims period, in an instruction to every state. The October instruction cites a paragraph of the Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2023 against entertaining objections presented in bulk by an individual, which the January letter did not mention. Reading the Chief Electoral Officer's daily bulletins, the report counts 3,143 objections from party agents by 20 January, 2,926 from BJP agents and 217 from Trinamool agents, and finds that 2,539 of them first appear in the bulletin dated the day after the extended window closed on 19 January.
items.quote: Currently, there are no such restrictions on number of Form 7 to be filled/submitted by an elector of that constituency to ERO/AERO as per law,
items.response: The report says the Commission has not said whether objections filed in January will be looked at again.

items.headline: Nearly One-Third of Form 7 Objections in Delhi SIR Seeking Voter Deletions Not Disclosed Publicly: Report
items.claim: The Wire reported, citing The Hindu, that 4,263 of the 13,462 Form 7 applications Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer received between 31 August and 16 October, or 31.67%, had not been published in the Form 10 lists. The Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2023 requires each objection to be listed publicly for seven days before an Electoral Registration Officer can act on it.
items.quote: Essentially, if any objection has not been publicly listed, then it is invalid and cannot be acted upon. Processing such an application will be a violation of rules,
items.response: The Hindu reported that it sent questions to the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office and had no response by the time of publication.

items.headline: Delhi SIR: revised data show sharp increase in Form 6 disposal rate
items.claim: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer replaced the weekly report of applications disposed of on 22 October, and officials told The Hindu that the figures published until then were wrong. The revised report shows 1,07,451 of 4,59,796 Form 6 applications for inclusion and 47,105 of 67,709 Form 7 applications disposed of from 31 August to 18 October, about 23% and 70%. The earlier report had shown 1,238 Form 6 disposals to 11 October. Tri Nagar is the only constituency with no Form 6 disposal recorded in any of the seven weeks.
items.quote: The weekly data being uploaded till now was wrong and it was not reflecting the disposals that happened since August 31, we noticed after the newspaper report,
items.response: The Hindu attributes the quoted explanation to an unnamed official and does not say which office the official works in. More than 3.5 lakh Form 6 applications were still to be disposed of. Claims close on 30 October, every application is to be disposed of by 30 November, and the final roll is due on 4 December.

items.headline: Karnataka SIR: Form 7 submissions surged from 58,475 to 2.28 lakh in 1 month, shows data
items.claim: Karnataka received 2,28,917 Form 7 applications between 16 June and 22 October, 1,70,442 of them after 23 September, when the count stood at 58,475, The Indian Express reported from official data. The Chief Electoral Officer's office said every Form 7 received up to 23 September had been cleared on priority and that hearings for all 43.82 lakh voters sent notices were over. Bangalore Urban had the most submissions in the paper's table, 24,268. The ruling Congress has alleged that the BJP is misusing Form 7 to file objections in bulk.
items.quote: All Form-7 applications received up to September 23 have been cleared on priority, the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer office said in a statement issued on Friday.
items.response: After a Congress protest at the Chief Electoral Officer's office earlier this month, the Chief Electoral Officer directed Electoral Registration Officers to look into the allegations. The state BJP has rejected them. The final roll is due on 27 October.

items.headline: Uttarakhand ERO refused BJP worker’s bulk Form 7 objections. After ECI complaint, 5,359 were accepted
items.claim: Newslaundry found 4,390 names on Kichha's draft roll that are missing from the final roll published on 3 October. About 670 of them had Form 7 objections filed against them in August, 509 by a single BJP booth level agent, and the other 3,720 had no objection against them and were deleted on the ground of logical discrepancies. Of the 6,884 Form 7 objections accepted in Kichha, 5,359 were that agent's, and he filed more Form 7 objections than anyone else in Uttarakhand. He told Newslaundry that the Electoral Registration Officer at first refused his bulk objections and took them after he complained to the Election Commission by email, and Newslaundry could not verify what the email said. Form 10 data from the Chief Electoral Officer's office show 504 of his accepted objections with an acceptance date of 14 August, a day after claims and objections closed. Newslaundry reported that every name in his objections was Muslim. He said the party had received information that about 6,000 electors enrolled in Kichha were also enrolled in five nearby constituencies of Uttar Pradesh.
items.quote: Of the 4,390 names missing from Kichha’s final electoral roll, 3,720 had no objections filed against them. The ERO deleted these voters on the basis of logical discrepancies, a mismatch in voter data that the ECI believes requires additional verification before the electoral roll is finalised.
items.response: The Kichha Electoral Registration Officer, Gaurav Pandey, neither confirmed nor denied the agent's account, would not say whether the Commission had directed him, and said the deletions followed the Commission's rules. Newslaundry said the Commission acknowledged its questions and did not answer them, and that it had asked the Chief Electoral Officer why objections were accepted after the deadline. The Congress MLA for Kichha, Tilak Raj Behar, said the objections rested on false information. The report does not say how it established the electors' religion.

items.headline: Dharavi man booked for filing 24 voter roll objections in a single day, exceeding ECI limit
items.claim: The Dharavi police registered a case under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 against a resident who had submitted 24 Form 7 applications in one day in the 178-Dharavi constituency, above the Election Commission's limit of ten a day, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation said on 24 October, The Hindu reported. The corporation alleged that the applications carried false and incorrect information. Mumbai's draft rolls were published on 31 August and claims and objections ran to 26 October.
items.quote: Under the ECI’s guidelines, an individual can submit a maximum of 10 Form 7 applications per day.
items.response: The report gives no account from the accused. Section 31 covers anyone who knowingly makes a false statement or declaration in connection with the roll.

items.headline: FIR in UP Eight Months After Man Who Cannot Sign Says Forged Signature Was Used to Delete 26 Voters
items.claim: A first information report was registered on 24 October against unknown persons, under sections 318(4), 336(3) and 340(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for cheating and forgery, over Form 7 applications that sought the deletion of 26 electors at booth 96 in the Sultanpur Sadar constituency, The Wire reported. The forms were presented as signed by an elector who has said publicly that he cannot read or write and uses his thumbprint. The complaint was made by the lekhpal who supervises the booth, and it does not say who submitted the forms. The Samajwadi Party raised the case in February (up-10), and its president Akhilesh Yadav presented the elector to the media in Lucknow on 8 February.
items.quote: Nevertheless, the BLO’s acceptance of incomplete Form-7 applications without verification was deemed an act of negligence in election-related duties, Rinwa noted.
items.response: Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa said on 26 October that the report of the District Election Officer of Sultanpur found the forms had been given to the booth level officer, and that no action was taken on them because they did not carry the applicant's full name, EPIC number or mobile number. He said the booth level officer had been relieved of all election work and that disciplinary action had been recommended.

items.headline: Over 61,000 Form-7 applications filed by election officials in Karnataka, none cites reason
items.claim: At least 61,059 Form 7 applications seeking deletions from Karnataka's rolls were filed by Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers themselves, and none gives a reason for the deletion, which the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 require, The Hindu reported. Officers listed as the objectors said the system generated the forms with their digital signatures when electors sent notices for no mapping or logical discrepancies could not be reached at hearings and were marked ineligible. Only 192 such applications were filed between 24 August and 23 September, and more than 60,800 between 24 September and 22 October, including 10,105 on 22 October, the last day for disposal. The paper's chart puts more than 53,000 of the officers' applications in the week from 16 to 22 October, with the most on one day, 11,760, on 19 October. In every case the paper checked on the Commission's portal the elector had already been deleted, including electors against whom the application came after 23 September. In the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike South district officers filed 10,374 of 17,491 applications, and in at least 26 constituencies officers filed more than voters or third parties did.
items.quote: Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs), listed as the objectors in these applications, said the system “auto-generated” the forms with their digital signatures when voters could not be reached during hearings on notices issued for no mapping or logical discrepancies, and the voters were therefore marked as “ineligible”.
items.response: The officers said they had been told to file Form 7 for electors who had shifted, had a duplicate entry, were underage, had died or were not citizens. The report gives no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer. Rule 17 of the 1960 Rules says a claim or objection not lodged within the period or in the prescribed form and manner shall be rejected by the registration officer. The paper also found 13,808 fewer Form 7 applications for 24 September to 22 October in the Commission's Form 10 records than the Chief Electoral Officer's statements give.

items.headline: Andhra CEO says no independent deletions. TNM’s questions about transparency remain
items.claim: Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer answered TNM's report on Form 7s naming officers as objectors (form7-64) on 28 October, in a thread on the office's X account that says no registration officer or assistant registration officer deleted any name of his own motion. The thread says booth level officers found 44,89,512 electors not at their addresses between 15 June and 24 July 2026, and the draft roll of 31 July held 3,71,38,182 electors. Officers then sent notices to electors with no mapping or with data anomalies, and by 23 October another 1,73,701 electors had been found ineligible for the final roll. For each of them, the thread says, the officer passed a speaking order giving the reasons and uploaded it to ECINET, the booth level officer delivered the order to the elector with notice of an appeal to the District Collector, and a Form 7 was generated through ECINET in the officer's name as the Commission instructs, because a deletion takes effect in the system only after a Form 7 is generated. It calls the report's insinuations of procedural violations baseless and misleading and condemns them. The News Minute replied the same day that the statement does not say why officers appear as objectors in the published records or why no reason is shown in those cases.
items.quote: For deletion of all such electors, Form-7 have been auto-generated by the ERO / AERO through ECI-Net technically as per the ECI instructions.
items.response: The thread is the Chief Electoral Officer's own reply. TNM says its report did not allege that officers deleted names without due process, and that its question was why the public records give no reason for the deletions officers are named in. The thread does not say how many of the 20,959 electors in TNM's count are among the 1,73,701.

items.headline: Telangana SIR: Form-6 rejections and Form-7 deletions unusually high during pre-SIR period
items.claim: From 1 January to 14 June 2026, before the revision began in Telangana, 5,13,375 Form 7 applications were filed and 4,54,340 accepted, The Hindu reported from information shared by the Chief Electoral Officer's office. In all since 1 January, 5,81,273 Form 7 applications were filed, 5,08,057 accepted, 54,681 rejected and 18,535 were under process, a count that includes electors found ineligible for the final roll at the notice stage. Of 10,77,450 Form 6 applications received from 1 January to 28 October, 2,43,643 were rejected, about 23%, and 1,61,214 were pending, and 1,92,574 of the 5,20,331 received before the revision were rejected, 37%. Only 1,70,374 Form 6 applications came in during claims and objections, which ended on 7 October. The paper puts 73,39,235 electors left off the draft at enumeration and says the exclusions from the roll could be well over 80 lakh.
items.quote: Over 4.54 lakh voters were deleted through filing of Form-7 even before the SIR exercise began.
items.response: Officials said the Form 7 deletions before the revision were entries sifted by an application on the ECINET software as Demographically Similar Entries and Photo Similar Entries. The paper says no explanation was given for the 47,303 Form 7 applications rejected in the same period.

items.headline: After voters found at Delhi addresses, DEO orders field verification of deletion claims
items.claim: The office of the North East Delhi District Election Officer, Ajay Kumar, said on 31 October that election officers would visit every elector against whom a Form 7 objection had been filed in the Mustafabad constituency to check the claim before any name is deleted, and that it would act under the rules against objectors whose claims were found false or mischievous, The Hindu reported. The office was replying to a post on X that shared the paper's report of 30 October, which found all 28 electors at polling booth 129 against whom a booth level agent appointed by the BJP had filed objections, citing absence, a permanent shift or death, living at their registered addresses. The paper reported 843 Form 7 applications in the constituency by 28 October, and 572 of them filed by 19 of the BJP's booth level agents, all against Muslim electors, in 24 parts of the constituency. With 118 more filed on 29 and 30 October the total reached 961, and 684 of them, 71%, were filed by the BJP's agents, the paper reported from the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's list of applications. Officials told the paper the agents' applications carried no undertaking from the agent and were not in the prescribed format. Nine more applications naming the agent at booth 129 as objector appeared on the list of 30 October.
items.quote: election officers would visit every elector against whom a Form 7 application had been filed “to ascertain the genuineness” of the claim before deleting any name from the electoral roll
items.response: The District Election Officer's office said no bulk applications beyond the prescribed limits had been received in Mustafabad, online or on paper, and gave a figure of 832 Forms 7 and 8, 102 of them Form 8, filed in the constituency up to 30 October, which differs from the public list. Senior officials of the Commission told the paper that agents who file as objectors without the undertaking for bulk filing are held to the limit of ten applications set on 9 October. The agent named at booth 129 had told the paper he did not file the forms and was neither a booth level agent nor associated with any party. Neither report says how the paper established that the electors were Muslim. Ali Mehdi, the Congress candidate for Mustafabad in the 2025 Assembly election, said in a post on X that he had complained to the North East Delhi Deputy Commissioner of Police and sought an FIR against the BJP's agents.

items.headline: Telangana SIR: Over 50,000 Form 7 applications seeking deletions of voters filed
items.claim: Figures generated by the Telangana Chief Electoral Officer's office show 50,908 Form 7 applications filed from 8 to 31 October, after claims and objections closed on 7 October, with 48,623 accepted and 435 rejected, Telangana Today reported. State election officials told the paper that a glitch in generating the data had brought some earlier applications into these figures. The Hindu had reported on 29 October, from official records, 5,81,273 Form 7 applications filed in the state since 1 January, which is 7,386 fewer than this report's total of 5,88,659 to 31 October. By the same figures Rangareddy district had 11,935 applications, of which 11,378 were accepted. Hyderabad had 9,858, of which 9,616 were accepted and four rejected, and Medchal Malkajgiri 4,018, of which 3,783 were accepted and four rejected. During claims and objections, from 17 August to 7 October, 15,442 Form 7 applications were filed, 12,930 accepted and 1,637 rejected. From 1 January to 31 October, 5,88,659 Form 7 applications were recorded, 5,16,052 accepted, 57,980 rejected and 14,627 pending.
items.quote: Information generated by the Telangana Chief Electoral Officer's office has revealed that a staggering 50,908 applications filed between October 8 and October 31 even as the claims and objections phase ended on October 7.
items.response: State election officials told the paper that a registration officer must give a speaking order with reasons before a name is deleted, and that they were trying to include as many electors as possible in the final roll. The paper says senior officials of the Chief Electoral Officer's office could not explain the number filed after the claims period.

items.headline: Uttarakhand SIR: 2,700+ names deleted in Gadarpur on objections filed by poll officers after the deadline
items.claim: Form 10 records published by Uttarakhand's Chief Electoral Officer show that Gadarpur's Electoral Registration Officer and ten Assistant Electoral Registration Officers filed 2,742 Form 7 objections on two dates, 763 on 18 September and 1,979 on 28 September, Newslaundry reported on 2 November. Claims and objections had closed on 13 August, and the final roll was published on 3 October. Rule 17 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 requires an objection lodged after the period to be rejected. By the same records, objections against 4,785 names were filed by 13 August and against 2,825 after it, and the other 83 late objections were filed by individuals, 27 of them dated 14 August by a BJP leader. Of the 5,505 names deleted in Gadarpur after the draft, 2,496 followed objections by the assistant registration officers, 240 objections by the registration officer and 240 objections by private persons, and 2,529 were deleted with no objection recorded against them. Newslaundry met at least 15 deleted electors who said they learnt of it only after the final roll was published. Some said they had received a notice and others that they had received none, and all said officials told them to file Form 6 again. The registration officer, Amrita Sharma, told Newslaundry that officers had not known a Form 7 also had to be generated for electors marked absent, and that by the time this was noticed the hearings were over.
items.quote: Both dates fell more than a month after the claims and objections period ended on August 13, with the second batch just logged five days before the final electoral roll was published.
items.response: The registration officer said the late filings were a delay in generating the forms on the system, that hearings had already been held, and that these were Form 7 deletions on anomaly notices, which she distinguished from an officer's own proceedings under rule 21A. She said about 52,000 notices were issued in Gadarpur and about 45,000 electors heard and kept on the roll, that not a single name was deleted without a notice, and that the same ten assistant officers who filed the objections held the hearings. She said only forms submitted by 13 August were accepted and that the entries dated 14 August were uploads made late that night. On two electors who say they gave the documents asked for or had no notice, she said she would have to examine the records. She said more than 1,800 Form 6 applications had been received since the revision, over 900 of them from electors deleted for absence or other reasons. The report gives no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission.

items.headline: Who filed 77% of Form 7s in Delhi’s Mustafabad? BJP BLAs named as ‘objectors’ deny them
items.claim: Twenty people registered with the Election Commission as the BJP's booth level agents are named as objectors in 787 Form 7 applications in Delhi's Mustafabad constituency, at least 77% of the 1,021 deletion applications filed there so far, The Hindu reported on 4 November from the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's public list. The paper reports that all 787 are against Muslim electors and that they are 94% of the 837 deletion applications filed by third parties. It contacted all 20 agents, and 16 of them denied filing or signing any of the forms. One agent named in 32 applications told the paper he had complained to the party and resigned as its agent, and the paper reports that it checked with the area's booth level officer that the electors in those applications live at their registered addresses. One agent named in 57 applications said he had filed them and put his own total at 500 forms. Two agents could not be reached, and the number listed for another was a wrong number. The forms naming the 20 agents were filed without the undertaking or the format prescribed for an agent's bulk filing, the paper has learnt, and all of them were received after the Commission set a limit of ten Form 7 applications for each elector on 9 October. An agent named in 56 applications said the Electoral Registration Officer's office called him on 3 November about the objections and that he told it he had not filed them.
items.quote: In all, 16 of the 20 denied having filed or signed any forms since the claims and objections phase began on August 31, 2026.
items.response: The District Election Officer, the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission did not answer the paper's questions. The District Election Officer had said earlier that every deletion claim would be verified in person by the booth level officer and the registration officer or an assistant, and that action would be taken against claims found false or mischievous (form7-58). The Commission's directive of 9 October, as the paper quotes it, says a registration officer who finds a Form 7 complaint false or fabricated shall act against the applicant under the Representation of the People Act. The report does not say how the paper established that the electors were Muslim.

items.outlet: Anjali Bhardwaj on X, posting the petitioners' letter of 5 November 2026 to the Chief Election Commissioner, the two Election Commissioners and Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer
items.headline: The petitioners in the Delhi case ask the Commission for FIRs, an audit of every Form 7 and a stay on deletions from third-party Form 7s, after The Hindu's report on Mustafabad
items.claim: Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, the petitioners in the Supreme Court case on Delhi's revision (W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, court-54), wrote on 5 November 2026 to the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, the Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, and Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer, Ashok Kumar, about The Hindu's report on Form 7 applications in Mustafabad (form7-60). Their letter gives the report's figures, that at least 787 of the 1,021 deletion applications filed there were in the names of 20 booth level agents appointed by the BJP, all against Muslim electors, and that 16 of the 20 denied filling, signing or knowing of the forms. The letter says this indicates that their identities appear to have been forged and used fraudulently without their consent. It asks the Commission and the Chief Electoral Officer to direct the registration of FIRs under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including for forgery, criminal impersonation, identity fraud and false declarations, and to audit every Form 7 submitted in every Delhi constituency during the revision to check whether the objectors named authorised and signed them. After investigation, it asks for action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 against everyone who knowingly made a false or fabricated declaration in a Form 7. It asks for an immediate stay on every deletion arising from a third-party Form 7 until the electors concerned and the objectors named have been independently verified. It also asks for a public report of how many Form 7 applications were received, how many were confirmed on verification and how many were found to be fraudulent, and for every Form 7 received during the revision to be published on the Chief Electoral Officer's website so that people can check whether one was filed in their name.
items.quote: Immediately stay all deletion proceedings originating from third-party Form 7 applications until independent verification with the affected electors and listed objectors is completed.
items.response: No reply from the Commission or the Chief Electoral Officer had been reported by 5 November. The Commission's directive of 9 October, as The Hindu quotes it, says a registration officer who finds a Form 7 complaint false or fabricated shall act against the applicant under the Representation of the People Act (form7-60). The North East Delhi District Election Officer had said on 31 October that every Form 7 in Mustafabad would be verified in the field before any name is deleted (form7-58).

items.headline: Delhi’s Mustafabad election official lodges police complaint seeking FIR over false Form 7s filing
items.claim: The Electoral Registration Officer of Delhi's Mustafabad constituency lodged a police complaint on Friday 6 November seeking an FIR under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, against a booth level agent named as objector on 37 Form 7 applications, The Hindu reported. The North East Delhi District Election Officer, Ajay Kumar, told the paper that officials had verified its report of 30 October on polling part 129 (form7-58) and found 36 of the 37 forms false or fabricated. A press release from his office said that the booth level officer and the assistant registration officer had checked all 37, that three electors the forms gave as dead were found alive, and that the others were found living at their addresses. It said that verification of the other Form 7 applications was continuing. The paper's earlier report had found the agent registered with the BJP by the Commission's records. A senior police officer told Daijiworld that the complaint had been received and that an investigation was under way. The Delhi Congress leader Ali Mehdi told Daijiworld that he had complained on 31 October, naming 14 booth level agents, and handed a copy to the Chief Electoral Officer, and that the matter was formally registered only a week later.
items.quote: Only one case is found to be true whereas 36 cases are found to be false/fabricated.
items.response: The Delhi BJP spokesperson, Praveen Shankar Kapoor, told Daijiworld that the party had not submitted any such forms, and that the booth level officer is responsible for checking every Form 7 before a name is deleted. The agent had told The Hindu earlier that he did not file the forms and was neither a booth level agent nor associated with any party (form7-58). The reports give no FIR number and do not say whether an FIR has been registered.

items.headline: Delhi SIR: Why BJP BLAs’ voter deletion applications in Mustafabad focused on three neighbourhoods
items.claim: The 796 Form 7 applications that name 20 booth level agents appointed by the BJP as objectors in Delhi's Mustafabad constituency are mostly concentrated in 25 of its 294 polling booths, in the neighbourhoods of Nehru Vihar, Dayalpur and Chandu Nagar, The Hindu reported on 10 November. The paper reports that all of them are against Muslim electors and that they are over 76% of the 1,044 deletion applications received in the constituency up to 4 November, from the published data. The applications give absence, a permanent shift or death as the reason, and the paper found at least 87 of the electors named living at their registered addresses. The paper reports, from an analysis of records and interviews with local BJP workers, that the 25 booths appeared to have been selected because they had a sizeable Muslim population and, by the workers' claims, few names left off the draft roll. BJP leaders who spoke to it on condition of anonymity said that after the draft of 31 August party workers compared the number of names placed on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors in booths with a majority of Muslim electors and in booths with a majority of Hindu electors, prepared lists of Muslim electors, which the paper says it saw, and then concentrated on the 25 booths, where the agents began filing from the first week of October. The paper says it found copies of these booths' rolls, with the names of Muslim electors marked on them, with BJP workers in the area. It reports that the Commission's booth-wise figures do not bear out the workers' claim. By its count, names left off the draft averaged 274 a booth in Mustafabad and reached 538 at the most, and in most of the 25 booths they were close to the average. Parts 108 and 129, which it counts among the five booths with the fewest names left off the draft, carry 35 and 37 of the agents' applications. No application names a BJP agent in the other three, which BJP workers said were mostly Hindu. Nehru Vihar has the most applications, 496. The paper reports that none of the Form 7s received in Mustafabad came with the undertaking an agent must give.
items.quote: The Form 7 applications were all against Muslim electors, and the 25 booths, spread across three neighbourhoods, appeared to have been selected because they had a sizeable Muslim population with claims of few deletions when the draft electoral roll was published as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, an analysis of records and interviews with local BJP workers showed.
items.response: The Delhi BJP spokesperson, Praveen Shankar Kapoor, told the paper that the party's agents had not filed any Form 7s in Mustafabad, that the party had not directed any forms to be filed, and that booth level officers and the Commission would act on any objections under the rules. The BJP councillor for Nehru Vihar, Arun Bhati, said he was not authorised to speak about the applications, and said that some booths in Mustafabad had 300 to 500 votes deleted, which he said were coincidentally of Hindu voters, while others had fewer than 100, and that the two could not both be correct. The paper reports that officials maintain religious identity has no role in verification. The agent named in 57 applications told the paper he had filed them himself because the electors had shifted, and the councillor's brother, an agent named in 37, denied filing his. The report does not say how the paper established the religion of the electors or of each booth's population.

items.headline: Form 7 withdrawals, rejections follow Maharashtra scrutiny on false objections
items.claim: Amit Sanap, the electoral registration officer for Bhiwandi East, told the Hindustan Times that his office had received 540 Form 7 applications seeking deletions in the constituency and had rejected over 450 of them, because the electors the forms said were not living at their addresses were found living there. The paper reports that political parties' booth level agents filed 480 of the 540 and that some applicants could face criminal action for false information. Sanap said some applicants had withdrawn their applications and that action would begin once the formal orders were prepared. The paper reports that Form 7s filed by agents and private complainants have been withdrawn or rejected in large numbers on scrutiny in Mumbai and the constituencies around it, after Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer told registration officers to place the burden of proof on the objector, to summon objectors and verify their claims before acting, and to begin criminal action against false filings. A senior state election official told the paper that objectors are allowed to withdraw, and that withdrawals began once action started and the first FIR was registered in Dharavi three weeks earlier (form7-55). With claims and objections due to close on Friday, 13 November, the Commission had received over 23 lakh forms for additions, deletions and corrections in Maharashtra, more than 95,000 of them Form 7s, the paper reports.
items.quote: We received 540 applications seeking deletions through Form 7, of which over 450 have been rejected. We will initiate action once the formal orders are prepared. We found that the people against whom Form 7 applications were filed, alleging that they did not live at the given addresses, were actually residing there,
items.response: Rais Shaikh, the Samajwadi Party MLA for Bhiwandi East, alleged that agents of the BJP had filed objections in bulk against his party's supporters and withdrew them only when faced with police action. The BJP's Atul Deulgaonkar, who oversees the revision for the party, rejected the allegations of the Samajwadi Party and the Congress and said electors of opposition parties were not being targeted. He said anyone with credible information about an incorrect registration has the right to file a Form 7 and that the authorised officer decides whether it is correct. The report does not say which parties' agents filed the 480 applications in Bhiwandi East.

items.headline: Delhi CEO's office to review SIR timeline as outreach to excluded voters awaits start
items.claim: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer's office received 3,04,352 Form 6 applications for inclusion, 549 Form 6A applications, 30,954 Form 7 objections seeking deletion and 1,11,516 Form 8 applications for correction or shifting between the draft of 31 August and 11 November, according to the bulletin it issued on 12 November, Hindustan Times reported. The paper gives the totals with the applications received before the draft as 5,16,752 Form 6, 1,900 Form 6A, 82,425 Form 7 and 3,72,284 Form 8. Claims and objections close on 25 November, the applications are to be disposed of by 15 December and the final roll is due on 22 December. Hindustan Times reported that the enumeration forms for electors left off the draft had not yet begun to be handed out, and an official told the paper that this would begin the next week because the ECINet software was being updated. The paper reports that each booth level officer will have to reach about 300 such electors. PTI reported officials as saying that the Commission was changing the portal so that booth level officers could generate forms only for the electors left off, and an official of the Commission as saying that at present forms are generated for all 1.45 crore electors in Delhi and the officers have to pick out those left off by hand. The official told Hindustan Times that the office would review whether the schedule needs a further extension, next week or closer to 25 November. The Tribune reported, from officials, that the Commission is considering an extension of about two weeks, which is yet to be approved and is to be discussed at the next meeting, and that nearly 15,000 booth level officers are expected to visit the registered addresses of the electors left off and hand them fresh forms.
items.quote: The process of distributing enumeration forms will begin next week as the ECINet software is being updated.
items.response: None of the officials is named in the three reports, and none of the reports says that an extension has been ordered. Officials told The Tribune that electors who have already filed Form 6 during the revision need not file an enumeration form and that their applications will be decided by the registration officers. The Commission's letter of 6 November says that such an elector need not submit the enumeration form and that the application is to be decided under its letter of 3 November. The letter sets no last date for the enumeration forms.

items.headline: Over 23.6 lakh voter forms filled in SIR claims period in Maharashtra; no word on deadline extension from ECI
items.claim: Maharashtra received 23,60,021 applications for inclusion, deletion and correction on its electoral roll in its 36 districts from the draft of 31 August to 12 November, the day before claims and objections closed, The Times of India reported on 14 November from the district figures released by the state election office. The paper reports that 15.18 lakh of them were Form 6 applications for inclusion, 1.25 lakh were Form 7 applications seeking deletion and 7,15,729 were Form 8 applications for correction. Hindustan Times, reporting the same figures on 14 November, gives 1,25,693 Form 7 applications. Mumbai Suburban received the most applications, 1,91,308, followed by Pune with 1,65,446 and Thane with 1,64,834, and Sindhudurg received the fewest, 16,098. Election officials told The Times of India that the count includes only the applications made online and that the forms submitted on paper had not yet been digitised. The paper reports that the district figures also leave out the applications received on 13 November, the last day, and officials told it that the final count will therefore be higher. The paper reports that the applications are to be disposed of by 25 November and that the final roll is to be published on 30 November.
items.quote: Of the 23,60,021 forms received across 36 districts till Nov 12, as many as 15.18 lakh were Form 6 applications for inclusion of names in the electoral roll.
items.response: The Times of India reports that the Commission had not announced any further extension of the period for claims and objections when the paper went to press, although opposition parties and activists had asked for one. They argued that the period was too short because it took in the Diwali week, and that electors whose names were left off the draft would need time to submit documents. The report names no official.

items.headline: EC relief to 99.4% electors served notices during SIR in Maharashtra
items.claim: Of the 12.24 million electors on Maharashtra's draft roll who were served notices, 6.25 million for discrepancies in their names, ages, addresses and other details and 5.98 million because they could not be mapped to the 2002 roll, 99.41 per cent have cleared and 72,601 have not, because they have yet to submit documents or their documents are still being checked, Hindustan Times reported on 14 November. The Times of India reported the same day, from the latest data released by election officials, that 99.4 per cent of the 1.2 crore electors served notices had cleared scrutiny and would stay on the roll. It gives 99.6 per cent of the 62.5 lakh served notices for discrepancies and 99.2 per cent of the 59.7 lakh served notices as unmapped. An official of the Chief Electoral Officer's office told Hindustan Times that documents can be submitted and verified until 23 November and that a few more of these electors are expected to clear. Both papers report that Nandurbar has the highest share cleared, 99.99 per cent, and Nanded the lowest, 96.18 per cent, followed by Jalna at 96.83 per cent. Both give Mumbai City at 99.61 per cent, Mumbai Suburban at 99.73 per cent and Thane at 99.88 per cent, and The Times of India gives Pune at 98.91 per cent. Hindustan Times reports that so many cleared after the Commission relaxed its guidelines for the revision in Maharashtra and other states. By its account, personal hearings with booth level officers were dropped, documents could be sent on WhatsApp and PAN and Aadhaar details were accepted. Election officers at the assembly constituency level told the paper that after the protests across the country booth level officers were told to be lenient and could decide for themselves whether to ask an elector for more details.
items.quote: The last day for submission of documents and their verification is November 23. We expect a few more voters to be added back to the rolls from this lot,
items.response: None of the officials is named in either report. A senior official of the Chief Electoral Officer's office told The Times of India that the figure showed that in 99.4 per cent of cases the documents and information supplied by the electors served notices were found satisfactory. Neither report gives a response from a political party, and neither says what will happen to the 72,601 electors whose cases are not settled by 23 November.

items.headline: Their addresses changed without consent. Then their voter names vanished
items.claim: The Pune District Election Officer, Suhas Diwase, wrote to Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer, S Chockalingam, on 17 October 2024 that a large number of electors in the district were being shifted to other constituencies through Form 8 applications for a change of address, that many of the applications gave the same electricity bill as proof of the new address in a name that did not match the elector's, and that many came from a single IP address, The Indian Express reported on 14 November from documents it reviewed. The paper reports that one of two later letters suggested the applications were being submitted in bulk by persons other than the electors. In the first of them, on 20 March 2025, his successor, Jitendra Dudi, wrote that the electors had been found living where they were and had not shifted. In the second, on 4 April 2025, he wrote that when a Form 8 is approved in the new constituency the ERONET software generates a Form 7 for deletion in the old one, which the registration officer there can only accept, and he asked for an option to reject it. On 19 November 2025 Ajit Gavhane, who contested Bhosari for the NCP (Sharad Pawar) in the 2024 Assembly election, gave the Chief Electoral Officer's office a list of 58 electors of Bhosari who, he said, had never applied to be moved or deleted, and the office ordered an inquiry the next day. The Bhosari registration officer reported that one of the 58 had been moved within the constituency and that the other 57 were among 5,603 electors for whom a Form 7 had been generated automatically after an address change was accepted in another constituency. The reports of the Pimpri and Khadakvasla registration officers and of the Thane District Election Officer, which the Pune District Election Officer sent on with his reply of 27 January 2026, said the address changes had been accepted on the documents submitted without a field check by a booth level officer, and the other five reports said the check had been done. After the paper's queries, the District Election Officer directed on 31 October 2026 that action be taken against those responsible and issued a show-cause notice to the Pimpri registration officer. On 1 November the Pimpri assistant registration officer filed a non-cognizable offence report at Nigdi police station under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, against the persons who used four mobile numbers to file 40 Form 8 applications. The paper reports that the District Election Officer found that three of the 58 had died and 11 were living where they were registered, and that Form 6 applications had been filed online to bring the other 43 back onto Bhosari's roll. Dudi told Hindustan Times, in its report of 15 November, that 60 electors of Bhosari had been moved without their knowledge before the 2024 Lok Sabha election, that two of them had since died, and that the other 58 had been added back to the roll after filing Form 6.
items.quote: The remaining 57 figured among the 5,603 voters, for whom Form 7 (the form for deleting a voter) had been automatically generated after address change applications were submitted and accepted at some other constituency.
items.response: Chockalingam told The Indian Express that an option to reject the generated Form 7 was not feasible because it would leave an elector registered in two constituencies at once, and that bulk filing had been addressed by the Aadhaar-based digital signature the Commission made mandatory in September 2025. The Pune District Election Officer's reply of 27 January 2026 said that a very large number of applications had been received during the 2024 election period and had to be decided within the time set so that the roll could be printed for the Assembly election. The paper reports that the Chief Electoral Officer's office wrote to the Pune District Election Officer asking for an explanation and the action taken on 2 November, the day the paper sent its query. Gavhane claimed more than 15,000 such cases, and the paper reports that the person who prepared his list called it a representative list. Dudi told Hindustan Times that the case at Nigdi was against one person who had submitted all the Form 8 applications, and that his office was gathering details of that person's background. Neither report names the person.

items.headline: ECI yet to generate forms for 20.6 million deleted Maharashtra voters, likely to miss final roll revision deadline
items.claim: Ten days after the Commission's letter of 6 November, fresh enumeration forms had not yet been generated on ECINET for the 20.60 million electors left off Maharashtra's draft roll of 31 August, Hindustan Times reported on 16 November. The paper gives 7.54 million of them as absent, 7.67 million as permanently shifted, 3.48 million as dead, 1.76 million as registered at more than one polling station and 2,22,390 as other. It reports that the Commission said the forms would be sent by WhatsApp, SMS or calls or delivered in person by booth level officers, and that without the forms the booth level officers and registration officers have been unable to reach these electors. The paper reports that the Commission asked an elector who has not moved to fill Annexure B and one who has moved to give the new address in Annexure C, and that no last date has been set for either. Officials told the paper that the revision was likely to be delayed further. One of them said that the final roll would not be published on 30 November as scheduled. Another said that there was no last date for bringing these electors back, and that distributing, collecting and digitising the forms would take a few weeks and the revision would be extended again. The paper reports that the letter of 6 November is understood to have been issued to meet the Commission's assurance to the Supreme Court, which is hearing petitions against the deletions in Maharashtra, that these electors would be given another opportunity.
items.quote: It is expected to take much longer, as even the pre-filled enumeration forms have not yet been generated.
items.response: The report gives no response from the Commission or from the office of Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer, and none of the officials is named. One official told the paper that the Commission could have asked the electors marked absent to file Form 6 and those marked shifted to file Form 8. Sandesh Kondvilkar, a general secretary of the Congress in Maharashtra, told the paper that the process so far had been an "eyewash". He alleged that in many cases booth level officers had marked electors absent without visiting their addresses, and said that the enumeration forms and Annexures B and C were not yet being accepted on the ground and that the final roll would now be postponed.

items.headline: Delhi SIR: 31,000 Form 6 applications received since deadline extension on Oct 29
items.claim: Officials in Delhi received 31,027 Form 6 applications for inclusion between 29 October, when the Commission extended claims and objections to 25 November, and 15 November, PTI reported from official figures. The Tribune gives the same figures and says the 31,027 were received from 30 October. Both give 2.79 lakh Form 6 applications from the draft of 31 August to 30 October, which takes the count since the draft to about 3.10 lakh. Officials said that the schedule may be extended again, because few applications were coming in and another round of enumeration forms had to be handed out. They said the fresh distribution of enumeration forms was expected to begin later in the week. The final roll is due on 22 December.
items.quote: The poll officials said that amid low submissions and the task of distributing enumeration forms to the people, the SIR exercise may see another extension.
items.response: None of the officials is named, and the report does not say that a further extension has been ordered. PTI says the Commission's revision of 29 October was caused by a Supreme Court direction asking it to consider extending the time for claims and objections and to distribute enumeration forms.

items.case: Three petitions by BJP booth level agents against FIRs over Form 7 applications, Crl.P. No. 15507 of 2026 (Mysuru), W.P. No. 32308 of 2026 (Jayanagar) and W.P. No. 32215 of 2026 (Kodagu), with the State's applications to vacate the stays in the two Malleshwaram petitions of 9 October, W.P. No. 31887 of 2026 and W.P. No. 31893 of 2026, Karnataka High Court (form7-48)
items.headline: Karnataka High Court stays probe against 10 more persons accused of attempting to delete Muslim voters through Form 7
items.claim: Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde of the Karnataka High Court on 17 November 2026 stayed further investigation in three more FIRs against BJP booth level agents over bulk Form 7 applications, Bar and Bench, LiveLaw and Hindustan Times reported. LiveLaw gives the three FIRs as one at the Narasimharaja police station in Mysuru against three agents, one at the Jayanagar police station in Bengaluru against two and one at the Shanivarasante police station in Kodagu against five, ten petitioners in all. With them the Court has stayed the investigation in five cases. In the two Malleshwaram cases (form7-48) the orders defer the State's applications to vacate the stays of 9 October and stay further investigation until further orders. Each order says that the inquiry by the registration officer under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 has to run its course first, and that the officer's finding may give the material to decide whether an FIR should be quashed or investigated. In the Malleshwaram and Jayanagar orders the Court said that the agents had not disowned their signatures on the forms and that the allegation of forgery could not be accepted at that stage. In those three cases and in Kodagu the Court directed the Election Commission, a respondent in each, to place on record the materials on its decisions on the Form 7 applications the agents filed. In the Mysuru case it directed the petitioners to add the State Election Commission as a respondent and directed that respondent to place the same materials on record. The complaints, as Bar and Bench and Hindustan Times report them, allege that the applications carried false information, forged signatures or impersonation, and some of them allege that the applications were aimed at Muslim electors. Bar and Bench gives the complaints' counts as 778 applications across eight polling stations in Malleshwaram, 5,698 applications in Jayanagar, 4,327 of them in Gurrappanapalya ward, 136 electors in Yeshwanthpur and 64 in Kodagu.
items.quote: The Court is of the view inquiry under the Rules, 1960, has to run its course to ascertain whether the petitioners have furnished correct information.
items.response: The Advocate General, K Shashi Kiran Shetty, opposed the petitions for the State and argued that fake or forged applications could not be permitted during the revision, because the right to vote is a valuable right. The petitioners argued that booth level agents were entitled to file Form 7 objections for political parties and that the registration officer had to examine whether the objections were correct. The Court allowed the complainants to seek modification or vacation of the interim orders, and the State to seek modification once it receives the Commission's records, Bar and Bench reported. No next date was reported.

items.headline: Maharashtra SIR: On BJP seat, 14,567 voter deletion requests were filed; only 74 found valid
items.claim: In the Bhusawal Assembly constituency of Jalgaon district, 14,567 Form 7 objections seeking deletions were received by post, and after an inquiry by booth level officers only 74 electors were found eligible for deletion, The Indian Express reported on 21 November from the factual report prepared after the inquiry. The report says 21 objectors withdrew 2,532 objections in writing. For the rest, notices were issued to the objectors and a public notice published in the newspaper on 5 November asked them to submit evidence, and booth level officers inspected and inquired into each application on the spot. By the order of 17 November of the Sub-Divisional Officer, who is the Electoral Registration Officer, all 14,567 objections were disposed of. Action has begun on the 74 as the rules require, and the paper reports that the district administration has begun legal action against those who filed objections with malicious intent. The paper's opening says 186 people had sought the deletion of 14,562 voters. The seat is held by the BJP's Sanjay Savkare, Maharashtra's Minister for Textiles. A Congress booth level agent who first raised the bulk filing told the paper that many of the people named as objectors denied having signed the forms, and asked for a detailed inquiry. A senior official in the state Chief Electoral Officer's office said the forms came by post, so all were accepted because there was no way of knowing who the objector was, and that after hearings and the disposal of malicious objections only 74 were accepted.
items.quote: A total of 14,567 objections were received by post in Form No. 7 in the 12-Bhusawal Assembly Constituency. Out of the above, 21 objectors have voluntarily withdrawn 2,532 objections through written applications.
items.response: The figures are the factual report's and the registration officer's order's, as the paper quotes them. The report does not say who the objectors were, against whom the objections were filed, or when they were sent. No reply from the minister or the BJP was reported.

items.headline: BLOs hard to reach? Dist admin may turn to agents of netas
items.claim: Nagpur district received 65,829 Form 6 applications for inclusion until 13 November, the last date for them, 38,533 of them online and 27,296 on paper, and 31,560 had been digitised, The Times of India reported on 18 November from figures it obtained from the district administration. The paper reports that nearly 14.43 lakh electors were left off Nagpur's draft roll, and that the administration is likely to ask the booth level agents of political parties to help trace eligible electors whose enumeration forms could not be collected, after complaints that booth level officers are hard to reach. A senior district official told the paper that the agents could help contact such electors and share information, and that verifying them and deciding on their inclusion would stay with the election authorities. The paper says that under the Commission's recent guidelines eligible electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate can still submit fresh enumeration forms after 13 November, and should contact their booth level officers or registration officers for help with them.
items.quote: Of these, 38,533 were submitted online and 27,296 offline, while 31,560 applications have been digitised so far.
items.response: The official is not named, and the report records no decision to involve the agents. It gives no response from the Commission or from the office of Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer.

items.headline: Uttarakhand SSR: वोटर लिस्ट सुधारने के लिए कल से स्पेशल अभियान, घर बैठे भी जांच सकेंगे नाम
items.claim: Booth level officers in Uttarakhand are to check the roll of their own booths in a special campaign from 20 to 27 November 2026, during the special summary revision, to find names entered more than once, ineligible entries and errors in electors' details, Live Hindustan and Dainik Jagran reported on 19 November from the Chief Electoral Officer, B.V.R.C. Purushottam. Live Hindustan reports that the officers will check in particular whether an elector's name is entered twice at the same booth, and will mark the extra entries of anyone whose name is on the roll of more than one Assembly constituency. It reports the election department as saying that duplicate entries found in the check will be deleted under the rules, with the necessary action taken through Form 7. The revision takes 1 January 2027 as its qualifying date. The draft roll was published on 12 November, and claims and objections on Form 6, Form 7 and Form 8 can be filed until 11 December.
items.quote: निर्वाचन विभाग के अनुसार, जांच में सामने आने वाली दोहरी प्रविष्टियों को नियमों के तहत हटाने की प्रक्रिया अपनाई जाएगी। इसके लिए फॉर्म-7 के माध्यम से जरूरी कार्रवाई की जाएगी।
items.response: The reports give no estimate of how many duplicate entries the campaign may find and do not say who will sign the Form 7s. The Chief Electoral Officer asked electors to check their own entries and those of their families, and Dainik Jagran reports that he asked them to rely only on official sources.

items.headline: SIR: Telangana Gets Only 9 Enumeration Forms
items.claim: Only nine enumeration forms had been received across Telangana from electors left off the draft roll of 17 August as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, nearly a fortnight after the Commission directed officials to accept them, Deccan Chronicle reported on 19 November. All nine came from Rangareddy district and none from Hyderabad district. The paper gives official figures of 73,39,234 electors in the category, 9,22,230 of them dead, 11,25,546 absent or untraceable, 45,18,961 permanently shifted, 6,70,203 already enrolled elsewhere and 1,02,294 other. Sources told the paper that about 11 lakh Form 6 applications had been received in the state, from electors in the category seeking to return and from people who had turned 18, and that 7 lakh had been cleared, 2 lakh rejected and the rest were in process. A senior official said most of those who said they had not received an enumeration form and found themselves left off the draft had already applied on Form 6. The paper reports that the Chief Electoral Officer directed officials, the day after the Commission's direction, to display the booth-wise lists of these electors afresh on the notice boards of the polling stations, to give the arrangement wide publicity and to involve the political parties. ETV Bharat reported the same day, from figures cited by Hyderabad's district election authorities, that 15 electors had been reinstated in Hyderabad district, where 19,41,444 were left off the draft. They were three in Secunderabad Cantonment, five in Amberpet, four in Musheerabad and three in Secunderabad, and the report says none had been reinstated in the other constituencies it lists.
items.quote: All nine applications were received from Rangareddy district, while Hyderabad district has not received a single application.
items.response: The Form 6 figures come from sources the paper does not name, and none of the officials in either report is named. Asked about the low number reinstated, Hyderabad's district election department told ETV Bharat that about 1,300 electors in the category had applied on Form 6 to be registered afresh. Neither report says how many of the state's Form 6 applications came from electors left off the draft, and ETV Bharat does not say whether the 15 were reinstated through enumeration forms or Form 6.

items.place: Lohardaga; West Singhbhum; Sahibganj; Pakur; Jamtara; Palamu
items.headline: झारखंड में मतदाता सूची पुनरीक्षण: 41 लाख मामलों का निष्पादन, 8 लाख लंबित
items.claim: Of 45,49,961 logical discrepancy cases in Jharkhand, 41,03,251, or 90.18 per cent, had been disposed of by 19 November and 4,46,710 were pending, and of 14,03,981 no-mapping cases 10,42,976, or 74.29 per cent, had been disposed of and 3,61,005 were pending, Amar Ujala reported from official figures. Dainik Jagran gives the same figures from the office of the Chief Electoral Officer. Lohardaga and West Singhbhum had disposed of every case in both categories and updated them on the ECINET app. Sahibganj had disposed of the smallest share, 76.36 per cent of its discrepancy cases and 55.69 per cent of its no-mapping cases, against 77.89 and 57.96 per cent in Pakur and 85.09 and 58.67 per cent in Jamtara, and Palamu had disposed of 56.65 per cent of its no-mapping cases. Dainik Jagran reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, told district and registration officers in a video conference on Thursday, 19 November, that electors on the draft roll who had been sent notices and had not yet given documents were to be visited at home to collect them, and that electors on the absent, shifted, dead or duplicate list were to be contacted again to fill enumeration forms. Dainik Jagran credits the progress to camps it calls 'one more chance' camps, held at all polling stations on Tuesday. Live Hindustan reported on 19 November that 9,46,954 Form 6 applications, 128 Form 6A, 1,50,007 Form 7 and 5,86,762 Form 8 had been digitised in the state so far.
items.quote: राज्य में लॉजिकल डिस्क्रेपेंसी श्रेणी के अंतर्गत कुल 45,49,961 मामले दर्ज किए गए थे। इनमें से अधिकारियों ने 41,03,251 मामलों का निष्पादन कर दिया है, जो कुल संख्या का 90.18 प्रतिशत है।
items.response: The figures are those of the Chief Electoral Officer's office as the papers report them. Neither report says how many of the disposed cases ended with the elector kept on the roll and how many with the name to be deleted. Live Hindustan does not say from what date its counts of digitised forms run or name its source.

items.place: Ranchi; Palamu; Giridih; Daltonganj; Hatia; Seraikela; Bokaro; Jharia
items.headline: SIR: Hatia, Daltonganj face rising voter verification pressure
items.claim: The Times of India reported from the bulletin the Chief Electoral Officer's office issued on Friday that 5,585 Form 7 objections were digitised across Jharkhand on Thursday, 19 November, taking the total to 1,75,398. Ranchi district accounted for 1,666 of the day's objections, Palamu for 1,049 and Giridih for 906, together nearly 65% of the day's total. Among constituencies Daltonganj had the most that day, 991, followed by Hatia with 869, Bagodar 579, Kodarma 496, Tamar 479, Simdega 353 and Kanke 300. The Commission's scrutiny data for Thursday showed 28,047 cases unresolved in Hatia across the no-mapping, logical discrepancy and other categories, and 27,773 in Daltonganj. The paper reports the largest backlogs in Seraikela, 39,589, and Bokaro, 31,238, which recorded one and five fresh Form 7 objections that day. Across the state 10,587 applications on Forms 6, 6A, 7 and 8 were digitised on Thursday, taking the total to 17.21 lakh. The Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, said the daily Form 7 figures include both objections and forms generated automatically when electors are shifted between polling stations. The paper reports that on an inspection in Jharia on Friday he found lapses in verification, among them eligible voters left out although they had documents, and ordered officials to complete the hearings, to issue Form 6 to those turning 18 by 1 October 2026 and to include all eligible voters.
items.quote: Kumar clarified that the daily Form 7 figures include both objections and auto-generated forms created when electors are shifted between polling stations.
items.response: The figures are the Chief Electoral Officer's office's as the paper reports them, and the bulletin itself was not read. The report does not say how many of the 1,75,398 are objections filed by people and how many were generated when electors were shifted, or how many have been decided.

items.headline: Delhi SIR: ECI Bends Its Own Rules to Bring Back Deleted Voters
items.claim: Delhi's Deputy Chief Electoral Officer wrote to the Commission's headquarters asking how to carry out its order that electors left off Delhi's draft roll as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate may return through a fresh enumeration form with an annexure, The Reporters' Collective reported on 20 November. Under the order an elector who has moved within Delhi adds the new address in an annexure to the enumeration form and does not file Form 8. The Collective reported that the office of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer told the Commission that printing and sorting the regenerated forms would take at least a month, and that many electors were asking whether they could download their forms with their old EPIC numbers when no such provision existed in ECINET. The part of the letter the Collective shows says the enquiries were reaching the office's 1950 call centre, that "as on date no such provision exists in ECINET", and asks the Commission, whose IT team maintains ECINET, to provide for electors to download or fill their forms on ECINET or the website. It reported that the office asked for changes to ECINET so that the EPIC numbers of these electors could be brought back into the database and the forms downloaded online, to the BLO app so that booth level officers could hand out the forms, verify the details and process the cases, and to the portal of the registration officers so that they could take final decisions on these electors. The Collective says the route was needed because the EPIC numbers of electors in the absent, shifted, dead or duplicate list had been deleted from the database, and an elector needs one to file Form 8. It gives 47.6 lakh electors left off the draft, 43 lakh of them marked shifted or absent, and the Commission's timeline as enumeration forms decided by 10 December and the final roll published by 22 December. It also reports informal WhatsApp instructions sent to booth level officers in the last week of October, which it saw, asking them to obtain the lists for their booths, revisit the addresses of the electors they had marked missing and bring back those they found through Form 6. The Commission wrote on 3 November that no action was to be started against an elector only because the elector was on an earlier roll and had filed Form 6, and the Collective reports that the order for regenerated enumeration forms came three days later.
items.quote: The Delhi CEO office wrote to the ECI, pointing out that printing and sorting through these forms “will take at least a month.”
items.response: The Collective reports that its questions to the Commission and to the office of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer on how the changes would be made had not been answered. The report does not date the letter, name the Deputy Chief Electoral Officer or say whether the Commission has replied. Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer said in a press note of 17 November that an elector can fill the form on the Commission's website or the ECINET app with the EPIC number held before the name was left off, and the report does not say whether the letter came before or after that note.

items.headline: ASDD voter review moves at snail’s pace in Hyderabad
items.claim: Of the 19,41,444 electors in Hyderabad district's 15 Assembly constituencies who were left off the draft roll as absent, shifted, dead, duplicate or other, verification had been completed for 7,69,112, or 39.62 percent, by 20 November, leaving 11,72,332, The New Indian Express reported on 22 November from figures presented at a meeting with representatives of political parties. Of the 13,45,333 electors in the shifted category 4,22,994 had been verified, and of the 2,99,850 absent electors around 1,66,813. Of the 1,56,392 in the dead category 95,198 had been verified and 61,194 were pending, and of the 99,264 duplicates 66,122 had been verified and 33,142 were pending. In the other category around 17,985 of 40,605 electors, or 44.29 percent, had been verified. By 20 November officials had distributed 10 enumeration forms and collected 10, all of them in the shifted category, and the figures for the other categories were zero. In all 1,528 electors on the list had applied afresh on Form 6, 1,077 of them in the shifted category and 420 in the absent category.
items.quote: As of November 20, officials had distributed just 10 forms and collected the same number. All 10 cases belonged to the ‘Shifted’ category, while the corresponding figures in the remaining categories were recorded as ‘zero’.
items.response: The figures are those presented to the parties as the paper reports them, and the paper does not say who presented them or what the verification involves. It does not say how many of the electors verified were found at their addresses, or how many are to return to the roll.

items.case: Writ petition by four petitioners to quash the Suddaguntepalya police FIR of 7 October over Form 7 applications, W.P. No. 32768 of 2026, Karnataka High Court (form7-42, form7-75)
items.headline: Karnataka High Court Refuses To Stay Form 7 Voter Deletion Probe, Bars Arrest Of Petitioners
items.claim: Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde of the Karnataka High Court declined on 20 November 2026 to stay the police investigation into an FIR over Form 7 applications filed to delete six electors from the roll in Bengaluru, and directed that the petitioners not be arrested and that no chargesheet be filed without the Court's leave, LawChakra and Bar and Bench reported. The Suddaguntepalya police registered the FIR on 7 October against the Jayanagar MLA of the BJP, C K Ramamurthy, and three others, under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and sections 217(b), 3(5), 336(2), 340(2) and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. The complainant alleges that Form 7 applications were filed to delete his name and those of five members of his family, who have lived at Old Gurappanapalya in Bengaluru for about 50 years, and that the MLA acknowledged in a conference call that an application had been submitted and said it would be withdrawn and corrected. LawChakra says these are allegations in the complaint and have not been tested. The petition, filed by four petitioners to quash the FIR, argued that they were already accused in the FIR the Jayanagar police registered on 5 October on a complaint by the former MLA Sowmya Reddy (form7-42), that a second FIR over the same exercise was not maintainable, and that the ingredients of forgery and of using forged documents were not made out. The Court issued notice to the complainant, asked the petitioners to serve the petition on the Election Commission's standing counsel and listed the case on 8 January 2027. On 17 November the same judge had stayed the investigation in three other FIRs over Form 7 applications (form7-75).
items.quote: Under these circumstances, prayer for stay of the proceeding is not granted at this juncture. The petitioners shall co-operate for investigation. The respondent-State shall not arrest the petitioners and charge sheet shall not be filed without the leave of the Court.
items.response: The Additional State Public Prosecutor, Anoop Kumar, said the complaint required investigation, and that in earlier cases raising almost the same questions the State had said it would not arrest the petitioners, which would apply here as long as they cooperated with the probe, LawChakra reported. No report carries a statement by the MLA.

items.headline: Over 6 Lakh Voter Names Deleted in Telangana Since Jan. 1 via Form-7; Opacity Over 79 Lakh Pleas Sparks Row
items.claim: More than 6 lakh names had been deleted from Telangana's rolls through Form 7 since 1 January by Saturday, 21 November, Deccan Chronicle reported on 22 November. The paper reports that about 5 lakh names had been deleted from 1 January before the intensive revision began, and that more than one lakh were deleted through Form 7 in the past month. Official sources the paper does not name told it that officials had received 79 lakh Form 7 applications seeking deletion through the year, had rejected 64 lakh of them and kept 8.8 lakh pending. That count is more than 13 times the 5,88,659 Form 7 applications that Telangana Today reported the Chief Electoral Officer's office had recorded from 1 January to 31 October (form7-59), and the paper does not reconcile the two. A senior official told the paper that most of the applications came in the claims and objections period, and would not give a break-up by applicant, the dates of the applications or who was deleted. P. Rajesh Kumar, chairman of the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee's Election Commission Coordination Committee, said the party had tried to stop booth level agents from filing false Form 7s, and that the applications outnumbered the electors on the absent, shifted, dead or duplicate list, which he put at 73 lakh. The paper reports that the authorities did not provide the forms filed by booth level agents in the Karimnagar Assembly constituency in answer to an application under the Right to Information Act, and gave instead the details of applications by voters seeking to delete the names of members of their families. The applicant told the paper that after the application was escalated to the collector the authorities gave details of only six members from the entire constituency.
items.quote: According to official sources, poll officials throughout the year had received 79 lakh applications via Form-7 seeking deletion of names. Of these, poll officials rejected 64 lakh applications and kept 8.8 lakh pending.
items.response: The figures come from official sources the paper does not name, and the senior official is not named. The report gives no count for any district, and does not say how the 79 lakh applications were counted.

items.headline: SIR: Over 18k names likely to be struck out from electoral roll so far; Kodarma, Deoghar account for 27%
items.claim: In Jharkhand 18,425 cases had been marked ineligible for inclusion in the final roll by 21 November, The Times of India reported from the latest data of the Chief Electoral Officer's office. Kodarma had the most, 2,781, and Deoghar 2,293, together 5,074, or around 27.5% of the state's total. Of the 18,425, 9,153 were in the logical discrepancy category, 7,766 in the no-mapping category and 1,506 in the category the data calls other. Of 2,21,19,847 cases in the three categories, 2,13,65,467 had been disposed of as of 21 November, a disposal rate of 96.59%, and 7,54,380 were pending, 3,71,970 of them logical discrepancy cases, 3,11,757 no-mapping cases and 70,653 other. The Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, said cases marked Park for Final would be included in the final roll and cases marked Found Ineligible for Final would not, and told the paper that the number of deletions could increase as officials completed scrutiny of the remaining cases.
