On an inspection in Deoghar on Saturday, 21 November, he found deficiencies in the verification of documents at hearings at polling stations in Sonaraitharhi block of the Jarmundi constituency, and directed the registration officer and assistant registration officers to correct them and report by 30 November.
items.quote: As per the latest data from Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office, 18,425 cases have so far been marked ineligible for inclusion in the final voter list.
items.response: The figures are the Chief Electoral Officer's office's as the paper reports them, and the data itself was not read. The report gives no total of cases for each category, and does not say what the other category holds.

items.headline: NCP(SP) alleges BJP targeting voters via SIR objections
items.claim: More than 6,300 objections to entries in the draft roll were filed in the Indapur Assembly constituency of Pune district during the intensive revision, The Indian Express reported on 21 November. The Naib Tehsildar at Indapur, Vijay Ghughe, told the paper that 2,120 of them had been withdrawn by the people who filed them. A list of withdrawals he shared showed that 100 sets of applications, filed by 98 people against 2,120 voters, had been withdrawn. He said hearings on the objections were being held at the Tehsildar's office. The paper checked the lists of booth level agents by party against the names of those who withdrew, and found that at least 55 of the 100 sets, accounting for 1,172 objections, had been withdrawn by BJP booth level agents. One of them was listed as an agent of both the BJP and the NCP(SP), and none of the others who withdrew was listed as an agent of any party. At least two people had filed and withdrawn more than 100 objections each, and at least four more than 70 each. A BJP booth level agent who had filed objections against 136 voters in part 176 and withdrawn all of them told the paper that the party had engaged an agency which gave them the names, and that he withdrew after pressure was put on him. Rahul Makhare of the NCP(SP) alleged that the BJP's booth level agents had filed objections in 140 villages of Indapur taluka, giving death or shifting as the reasons, and that the objections were incorrect. Aakash Kamble, general secretary of the BJP in Pune rural, denied the allegations, said people from all parties had filed objections, and said a name would not be deleted if documents were submitted at the hearing.
items.quote: A list of withdrawn objections shared by Ghughe showed that 100 sets of applications filed by 98 separate people objecting to 2120 voters had been withdrawn.
items.response: The BJP's Pune rural general secretary denied the allegations. A man listed as a BJP booth level agent for part 115, in whose name 70 objections were filed and withdrawn, denied to the paper being a BJP agent. The report does not say how many of the objections that were not withdrawn have been decided, or how.

items.headline: No voter-deletion forms for BJP workers in UP in this round of electoral roll preparation
items.claim: The BJP has decided not to give Form 7 to its booth level agents in Uttar Pradesh during the special summary revision and is giving them only Form 6 and Form 8, The Indian Express reported on 22 November from sources in the party. The paper reports the decision after complaints from several constituencies of Form 7s filed in bulk during the intensive revision, some of which led to FIRs. Party sources told the paper that the BJP has sent its workers the list of names deleted during the intensive revision as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, and that its booth level agents and workers are checking it in door-to-door visits. A senior BJP leader said the party had given its workers in every Assembly seat around 5,000 copies of Form 6 and 1,000 copies of Form 8, with a copy of the roll and the list of deleted names, and that no Form 7 was being provided. On the allegations that its booth level agents had filed Form 7s in bulk, the leader said the forms its workers had submitted were largely not processed. Another leader said that on 22, 23 and 24 November ministers, MPs, MLAs and office-bearers would be at their assigned polling booths for door-to-door contact, as part of the party's month-long Matdata Jodo Abhiyan, whose progress is to be reviewed on 13 December. The paper reports that the draft roll of the summary revision put Uttar Pradesh's electors at 13.58 crore as of 17 November, 18.84 lakh more than the final roll of 10 April, and that claims and objections run till 16 December and the final roll is due on 4 January.
items.quote: No Form 7 is being provided as the party wants to use its energy and human resources towards the inclusion of new and left-out voters.
items.response: The account is the party's, from sources and leaders the paper does not name. The report gives no official count of Form 7s filed in the summary revision, and does not say how many of the forms BJP workers filed during the intensive revision were decided, or how.

items.headline: BJP launches voter enrolment drive in UP, warns cadres against ‘intruders’
items.claim: The BJP's president in Uttar Pradesh, Pankaj Chaudhary, told PTI on Sunday, 22 November, that the party's workers had been briefed to use Form 6 to add eligible electors left off the roll during the summary revision and Form 8 to correct entries or record a change of residence. PTI reports that the workers have also been asked to keep watch against 'ghuspaithiyas', a word PTI glosses as intruders, and it quotes Chaudhary as saying that the party's stand on 'ghuspaithiyas' is clear and that, if required, Form 7 will be used towards that objective. Chaudhary took part the same day in the party's three-day voter enrolment drive, which began on Sunday, at Faizullahganj in Lucknow, where PTI quotes him telling people to use Form 6 to add names and Form 7 to object to suspect entries. The Times of India reported on 23 November that the party has given its district chiefs the task of adding 10,000 to 15,000 names 'in each of the state's 402 assembly constituencies' through house visits, and that the party's block head at Behrampur in Ghaziabad said its workers were handing out Forms 6, 7 and 8 and working with the booth level officers of their areas. The paper reports that 18.8 lakh names have been added to the roll through the summary revision so far, around 61,000 of them in Ghaziabad. The draft roll of 17 November held 18,84,113 more electors than the final roll of 10 April, which is a net rise.
items.quote: But surely the party’s stand on ‘ghuspaithiyas’ is clear and towards this objective, if required, Form 7 will be used,
items.response: The Indian Express reported on 22 November, from party sources, that the BJP had decided to give its booth level agents no Form 7 in this revision and only Form 6 and Form 8 (form7-88). PTI's report quotes the state president as saying Form 7 will be used if required, and The Times of India reports a block head as saying workers hand out Form 7 with Forms 6 and 8. Neither report gives a count of Form 7s filed by the party's workers, and neither carries a reply from the Chief Electoral Officer.

items.headline: Pakur’s SIR docu checks under lens over birth cert discrepancy
items.claim: The Times of India reported on 23 November that a letter of 22 November from the medical officer in charge of the community health centre at Barharwa in Sahibganj district to the civil surgeon says 'the Union govt did not issue' a birth certificate dated 17 May 2026 in the name of a woman whose parents are reported to live in Pakur district. The paper gives the letter as saying that the civil registration system portal 'was not open at the Union govt on that date', that no certificate was issued through it and that a search of the portal for the date returned no records. The certificate gives 17 May as both its date of registration and its date of issue and names the Barharwa health centre as the registering institution. The paper says it remains to be established whether the certificate was submitted at a hearing of the revision and who produced it. The discrepancy came to light on Sunday, 22 November, as the Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, reviewed the revision in the Rajmahal and Pakur constituencies. The Times of India quotes him as saying that no elector would be deleted without due procedure, including two notices, a hearing, physical verification and a reasoned final order. In Pakur he found electors on the draft roll who had not given the documents asked for, and he asked applicants who had moved from West Bengal and whose documents were pending there to give their present registration officers the acknowledgements of their applications so that officials in Jharkhand could take it up with those in West Bengal. Dainik Jagran reports that registration officers in Pakur had sent notices to many such people while their documents were being prepared in West Bengal, that officials in Rajmahal told him many people in the Diyara area have no khatiyan and so cannot get residence or caste certificates, and that the Commission is concerned at the slow progress of the revision in Rajmahal. The Times of India reports that as of 19 November Sahibganj had disposed of 55.69% of its no-mapping cases and Pakur 57.96%, and that the two districts together had 99,025 no-mapping and logical discrepancy cases pending.
items.quote: No elector would be deleted without due procedure, including two notices, a hearing, physical verification and a reasoned final order.
items.response: The letter was not read, and the paper does not say who gave it the letter or what step the civil surgeon or the registration officer has taken on it. Neither report says how many electors in Pakur were sent notices while their documents were pending in West Bengal.

items.headline: Most of the 12.22 lakh electors removed during SIR yet to apply for inclusion in the rolls
items.claim: Most of the 12.22 lakh electors in Chennai district whose names, The Hindu says, were removed during the intensive revision after they were classified as permanently shifted have yet to apply to be included again, the paper reported on 22 November. The paper's standfirst says only 83,972 voters have been included in the rolls after the revision, that many residents of rented homes say they need help to be included, and that officials point to a lack of awareness of the revision among residents.
items.quote: Most of the 12.22 lakh electors, whose names were removed during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Chennai district after they were classified as “permanently shifted”, are yet to apply for inclusion of their names in the electoral rolls.
items.response: The report is for subscribers, and only the headline, the standfirst and the first paragraph that The Hindu shows free are used. They carry no reply from the District Election Officer or the Chief Electoral Officer, and the rest of the report is not used.

items.headline: Post SIR, Jharkhand final electoral roll likely to list 2.33 crore voters: CEO
items.claim: Jharkhand's Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, told The Times of India on Monday, 23 November, that he expected the final roll, due on 22 December, to hold around 2.33 crore electors, including the 9 to 10 lakh names likely to be added during the revision, and that deletions after the revision could be around 33 lakh. The paper gives around 2.64 crore electors on the roll before the revision began on 30 June and around 2.21 crore on the draft of 5 August. It reports from the bulletin of 23 November that 17,56,325 applications had been digitised in the state, 9,64,306 on Form 6, 136 on Form 6A, 1,96,853 on Form 7 and 5,95,030 on Form 8, and that 13,114 were digitised on 22 November alone, 8,837 of them on Form 7. At a review by video conference the same day he told district election officers and registration officers that super checks had found fake birth certificates attached in cases in Garhwa, Ranchi and Palamu, and that one more was found in Pakur during his inspection of 22 November. He directed them to verify the eligibility of applicants, to take legal action against those who submit fake birth certificates and those who help to provide them, to record the names and EPIC numbers of applicants' parents where these are on the rolls, and to complete super checks and send compliance reports by 30 November. He said that no elector on the draft roll should be deleted without a proper inquiry, a reasoned order and due process. He added that no further special camps are planned.
items.quote: The total number of name deletions after the SIR could be around 33 lakh, state chief electoral officer (CEO) K Ravi Kumar said on Monday.
items.response: The 2.33 crore and the 33 lakh are the Chief Electoral Officer's expectations, and the paper says the precise calculation behind the projected additions, deletions and final electorate awaits the final roll. Neither report says how the 2.33 crore is reached from the draft, the names to be added and the deletions. Dainik Jagran says the fake certificates are being found in the notices and hearings. Neither report says how many were found or whether any case has been registered.

items.headline: Delhi Congress alleges 75 living voters shown as dead on Form 7 in Mustafabad
items.claim: The Delhi Congress alleged on Monday, 23 November, that 75 living electors in Mustafabad had been classified as dead in Form 7 applications during the revision, and demanded an impartial inquiry, PTI reported. The party's Delhi president, Devender Yadav, told a press conference at Rajiv Bhawan that the party's booth level agent had identified 65 of the 75 as alive during door-to-door verification in the Nehru Vihar ward of the constituency. The party said 16 of the electors attended the press conference with their voter identity cards. Yadav alleged that booth level agents appointed by the BJP had misused Form 7 to show living electors as dead, asked the Commission to make clear who had given the authority to do so, and demanded special hearings for the electors and action against those found responsible. He also questioned the transfer of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer, Ashok Kumar, during the revision.
items.quote: According to the complaints received by the Delhi Congress, Form 7 has been misused to declare living persons as dead.
items.response: PTI reports no immediate response from Delhi's election office or the BJP. The figures are the party's. The report does not say when the applications were filed, whether they are among those The Hindu counted (form7-67), or whether any of the 75 names has been deleted.

items.headline: Delegation of political parties, civil society groups meets Delhi CEO over SIR deletions
items.claim: A delegation of political parties and civil society groups met Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer on Monday, 23 November, and said afterwards that he had accepted their suggestions, Hindustan Times reported on 25 November. The delegation included members of the Aam Aadmi Party, the Communist Party of India, the Communist Party of India (Marxist) and the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist), the activists Anjali Bharadwaj and Amrita Johri, and members of the Voter Adhikar Manch. It said the Chief Electoral Officer accepted that electors whose names were deleted and placed on the absent, shifted, dead and duplicate list of 31 August can be restored by filling an enumeration form and will keep their original serial and EPIC numbers, that he issued directions, and that a standard operating procedure would be released shortly. It asked that electors deleted who had applied afresh on Form 6 after 31 August be given their original EPIC numbers, and said the Chief Electoral Officer assured it this would be considered. On Form 7 it asked that verification be sought from the booth level agent who filed the form, that all Form 7 applications be made public, that notices go to the electors concerned and that decisions follow a fair hearing. It raised incorrect Form 7 filings in Mustafabad, and said it was agreed that cases where a registration officer or assistant registration officer had filed Form 7 to remove a name would be examined again. The talks were about carrying out the Commission's letter of 6 November on another chance for these electors.
items.quote: For voters whose names were deleted and later placed in the ASDD list released on August 31, the CEO accepted a proposal that their voting rights can be restored by filling an enumeration form. They will retain their original voter serial number and EPIC number.
items.response: An official told the paper the meeting went well and that the office would work on the suggestion, and said several suggestions were already in the pipeline and all demands that make the process easier for ordinary voters would be considered. The paper's opening gives the account of what the Chief Electoral Officer accepted as the delegation's, and a later paragraph states the acceptance on the enumeration form in the paper's own words. No statement or standard operating procedure from his office giving it was found.

items.outlet: The Wire; The Indian Express; The Times of India
items.headline: Bengal Police Are Demanding Documents From Voters Awaiting SIR Tribunal Orders. The CEO Office Doesn't Know Why
items.claim: An order of the West Bengal Police headquarters, No. 1754/DGP(L&O)/26 dated 23 November 2026 and signed by the Director General and Inspector General of Police (Law and Order), asks every police commissioner in the state except Kolkata's and the superintendent of police of every district and police district to examine the data for their jurisdictions on the website of the Civic Research Group, which compiles public data on the adjudication and appeals of the revision by constituency, to analyse it as instructed in a video conference that day and to send a comprehensive report by 30 November, The Wire reported on 27 November from the order, which it has seen. The order's subject is the SIR adjudication and tribunal appeals against exclusion and inclusion across all 294 Assembly constituencies of West Bengal. The Wire reports that the order says nothing about visiting electors, calling them to police stations or collecting their documents, and that police visits to electors whose appeals are pending before the tribunals began in most places on 24 and 25 November, in the districts of Malda, Jalpaiguri, Dakshin Dinajpur, Purba Bardhaman, Bankura, South 24 Parganas, Hooghly, Howrah, Paschim Medinipur, North 24 Parganas and Murshidabad. A checklist of the Kotwali police station in Paschim Medinipur that The Wire has seen asks for each elector's EPIC number, constituency, booth and contact number and whether the elector holds each of six documents, tells the officer to collect a self-attested copy of any the elector has, asks for reports to the District Intelligence Branch by 6 pm every day and sets 28 November for finishing the verification. A second document, in Bengali and headed 'Simplified Check List for Deleted Voters', lists six kinds of proof, among them a land deed from before 1987 in an ancestor's name, a Class X certificate from before 1987 in the elector's or an ancestor's name and an ancestor's name on the rolls of 1971, and The Wire reports that its first line says a deleted voter 'can be considered an Indian citizen' if they can give any one of them. The Indian Express reports that a senior police official, speaking without being named, said a drive began on Tuesday, 24 November, in Jalpaiguri, Uttar Dinajpur, Howrah and East Midnapore and was extended to Murshidabad on Thursday, 26 November. The Times of India reports that sub-inspectors and civic volunteers checked the EPIC cards and family records of appellants at verification points in Murshidabad, Malda, East Burdwan, Jalpaiguri, West Midnapore and other districts on 26 November, with seven verification camps in each block of Jalpaiguri. The Wire reports that on the morning of 27 November booth level officers in at least two constituencies of South 24 Parganas were told by forwarded messages to bring electors under adjudication to the block office with copies of six documents, among them their tribunal application. The Times of India reported on 28 November that the police went on collecting and checking the documents of deleted electors who had appealed to the tribunals on Friday, 27 November, on a directive of Monday, 23 November, from the Additional Director General (Law and Order), sent to every superintendent of police and police commissioner with a deadline of 30 November for all 294 constituencies. It reports camps in Gopalpur, Manikchak and other places in Malda to collect tribunal applications and Aadhaar cards, home visits to check birth certificates and Aadhaar cards in Niyamatpur in West Burdwan, checks at the Burdwan police station covering four gram panchayats and 35 municipal wards, and checks of birth certificates and the 2002 roll in West Midnapore since Wednesday, 25 November, where it says 56,518 appeals were filed. In Jhargram, where the paper says 1,200 names were deleted and about 450 appealed, the superintendent of police, Manav Singla, confirmed that the physical verification ended on 27 November. The All Bengal Joint Forum to Safeguard the Right to Vote, which The Times of India describes as a platform of political parties including the CPI(M), Mamata Trinamool, the Congress and the CPI(ML) Liberation and of civil society, said it would file a petition in the Calcutta High Court the next week, after the Supreme Court asked the petitioners on 27 November to raise the police action there (court-101), and the advocate Jhuma Sen told the paper that the police action was illegal.
items.quote: The data available on the website shall be downloaded, carefully analysed as per instructions given today in Video Conference (VC) and a comprehensive report in respect of the respective jurisdiction shall be submitted to this office positively by 30/11/2026.
items.response: The Additional Chief Electoral Officer, Arindam Niyogi, told The Wire that there was no directive from the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, and told The Indian Express that the office had no knowledge of any such drive and did not know whether the Election Commission had asked the police to verify the documents of excluded electors. The Director General of Police, Siddhinath Gupta, told The Indian Express that he could not share the directives and orders his office issues and that he did not know about any forms being filled up, and The Wire reports that he had not answered its questions by the time of publication. The Superintendent of Police of Barasat, J Marcy, told The Times of India that police stations had been tasked with identifying those who had applied to the tribunals and examining how they applied and what documents they submitted, and the Superintendent of Police of Malda, Anupam Singh, said his officers were collecting birth dates on a direction from the Director General and that it had nothing to do with the revision. A senior official of the state administration, speaking without being named, told The Indian Express that the police may verify whether a person is an Indian citizen. The Wire reports that a notice issued in the name of the BJP MLA for Naihati, Sumitro Chatterjee, asked electors whose cases are before a tribunal and who had been called by their police station to go there on 26 or 27 November with their documents, and that his representative said the Election Commission had sent the order through the block and subdivision offices. The CPI(M)'s state secretary, Mohammed Salim, asked under what law the police were asking for the documents, and the Association for Protection of Civil Rights wrote to the Director General of Police and the Chief Secretary asking under what authority the police were acting. The Times of India reported on 28 November that the Additional Director General (Law and Order) did not answer its questions and that an official of the Commission said it had issued no instruction to the state police to collect documents from tribunal appellants. The paper reports that Prasenjit Bose, who heads the Bengal Congress's panel on the revision, said he had written to the Chief Minister, Suvendu Adhikari, against the deployment of police to verify documents and called it a contempt of the Supreme Court's order. The Trinamool Congress's Rajya Sabha member Samirul Islam wrote to the Chief Election Commissioner that the police were asking for Aadhaar, birth and school certificates, parents' educational records and land records while working from a plain form with no seal or letterhead, the paper reports. The Week reports that the Commission has said the exercise is not being carried out at its behest, and that the forum is asking electors not to give in to pressure to hand over their documents.

items.headline: Andhra Pradesh: 17.1% of ASDD electors get enumeration forms for re-enrolment
items.claim: In Andhra Pradesh 769,000 enumeration forms had been handed out to electors left off the draft roll as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate since the process for their return began on 18 November, Hindustan Times reported on 24 November. The paper puts them at about 17.1% of the 4.4 million electors left off in those categories, or roughly one in six. The Chief Electoral Officer, Vivek Yadav, said, as the paper quotes him, that all the forms had been generated by Wednesday, 18 November, under the Commission's guidelines, that booth level officers had been distributing them since, and that 769,000 electors had collected them. The paper reports that each form must be returned to the booth level officer for review before a name is restored, that the forms are to be submitted by 30 November and that the final roll is due on 22 December. It gives nearly 41.6 million electors on the roll before the revision and about 37.1 million on the draft.
items.quote: So far, 769,000 electors have collected them. These forms will now be submitted and reviewed,
items.response: The count is of forms handed out. The report gives no count of forms returned, accepted or rejected, and no count for any district.

items.headline: Fate of 13.25 lakh ASDD voters in limbo
items.claim: Of the 14,43,511 electors The Hitavada counts as left off Nagpur district's draft roll as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, the district election machinery has identified 1,18,099, or 8.18 per cent, as already enrolled on the draft roll in some constituency, the paper reported on 24 November. The paper says the status of the other 13,25,412 is yet to be established from the data available, and that the lack of clear word on whether submitted enumeration forms have been accepted or rejected has added to the uncertainty. It gives the district's list as 2,40,327 dead, 5,45,647 untraceable or absent, 5,29,954 permanently shifted and 9,484 other, besides the 1,18,099 enrolled elsewhere. Hingna has the most electors found already enrolled, 19,940, followed by Kamptee with 17,689. Katol has the highest share, 16 per cent of its 49,851 electors on the list, and Nagpur West the lowest, 6,402 of 1,60,571, or 4 per cent. The paper reports that these electors can submit enumeration forms until 30 November, that claims and objections will be disposed of by 15 December and that the final roll will be published on 22 December.
items.quote: The status of the remaining 13,25,412 voters is yet to be established through the available data.
items.response: The paper names no official and gives no count of enumeration forms handed out, returned or decided in the district. The 1,18,099 it calls already enrolled equals the number of electors left off Nagpur's draft as duplicates, and the paper does not say whether the other 13,25,412 were checked for enrolment elsewhere.

items.headline: Mustafabad: no new deletion requests naming BJP agents after reports on fake Form 7s
items.claim: No fresh Form 7 naming a BJP booth level agent as objector has been listed in Delhi's Mustafabad constituency since 5 November, The Hindu reported on 24 November from the data. The standfirst The Hindu shows with the report says 31 fresh applications were filed in the area between 5 and 21 November, none of them naming an agent of the ruling party, and that a non-cognisable offence report was filed against two BJP agents on 7 November on a poll official's complaint. The paper says the change follows allegations that the agents' names were used without their knowledge to seek the deletion of Muslim electors, during the period of claims and objections.
items.quote: No fresh Form 7s (deletion applications) naming Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Booth Level Agents-2 (BLA-2) as objectors have been listed in Delhi’s Mustafabad Assembly constituency since November 5, data shows.
items.response: The report is for subscribers, and only the headline, the standfirst and the first paragraph that The Hindu shows free are used. They carry no reply from the BJP, the registration officer or the District Election Officer, and do not say how many of the earlier applications have been decided.

items.headline: Deletion of father’s name from voter list poses hurdle to infant’s birth certificate
items.claim: A two and a half month old infant in Cooch Behar district has been denied a birth certificate as a result of the deletion of her father's name from the roll during the revision, The Hindu reported on 24 November. The girl was born on 9 September at the sub-divisional hospital in Dinhata. The paper reports that when her parents approached the hospital and the panchayat office for the certificate, they were asked to arrange residential verification from the panchayat pradhan or the MLA, that the office of the MLA for Dinhata, Ajoy Roy, refused the father's request for the verification, and that the father was told the certificate could not be issued because his name had been deleted from the roll. The father told the paper that an official from the MLA's office said he was a Bangladeshi national and would first have to register through the National Register of Citizens. He said he has lived in India since his birth, that his house was built by his grandfather, and that he had shown all his documents and was still refused. He said the block development officer of Sahebganj refused a similar request on the same grounds. The paper reports that the names of three of his sisters were also deleted, that the Commission had called them for a hearing citing a logical discrepancy that six other persons had given the name of his father, and that his parents, his wife and an elder sister are on the roll. He has appealed to a tribunal to have his name included. The Association for Protection of Civil Rights said in a statement that birth registration is a statutory obligation, that every child has the right to immediate registration and legal identity under Article 7 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, and that a child's right to legal identity must not be linked to the electoral status of her parents, and demanded that the government provide the certificate at once. The Wire carried the same account on 25 November. On 23 November the Supreme Court issued notice on an application asking it to direct the state to withdraw notifications that restrict the welfare benefits of electors deleted in the revision (court-96).
items.quote: An official from the MLA office said that I am a Bangladeshi national and therefore, I would need to get myself first registered through the National Register of Citizens. Why would I do that? I have been living in India since my birth.
items.response: The report carries no statement from the MLA, his office, the panchayat, the block development officer, the hospital or the Chief Electoral Officer. The paper states the refusal by the MLA's office in its own words. The official's remark on nationality and the refusal by the block development officer are the father's account.

items.outlet: The Times of India; Dainik Jagran
items.headline: Delhi SIR: Last day to file claims, objections on Wednesday; final roll on December 22
items.claim: The office of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer said on Tuesday, 24 November, that 3.3 lakh Form 6 applications, 35,155 Form 7 objections, 1.2 lakh Form 8 applications and 610 Form 6A applications had been received from the draft of 31 August to 23 November, The Times of India reported on 25 November. Dainik Jagran reported on 24 November that 5,41,270 Form 6 applications, 86,626 Form 7 objections and 3,84,142 Form 8 applications had been received in all, up to 30 August and from 31 August to 23 November. Claims and objections close on Wednesday, 25 November, and an official told The Times of India that no further extension was likely. The final roll is due on 22 December.
items.quote: The office also received 35,155 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names and 1.2 lakh Form 8 applications for corrections in voter details, shifting of residence or replacement of EPIC cards.
items.response: Neither report says how many of the applications were accepted or rejected, and neither gives a new count of applications disposed of.

items.headline: पात्र युवाओं को भी मतदाता सूची में शामिल नहीं किया जा रहा, CEO ने रांची के तमाड़ में होम टू रोल सत्यापन में पकड़ी गड़बड़ी
items.claim: Jharkhand's Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, reviewed home to roll verification of the roll at three polling stations of the Tamar Assembly constituency on Tuesday, 24 November, with the registration officer and assistant registration officers, Dainik Jagran reported on 25 November. In a sample survey of 30 houses in two villages and the urban area of Bundu, officials found seven eligible citizens whose names were not yet on the roll, and the paper reports that all seven are young and meet the conditions for registration. He then directed all district election officers and registration officers to run an intensive home to roll verification drive in their constituencies, and to identify and register every eligible citizen who had turned 18 by 1 October 2026. He said it must be ensured that no eligible citizen is left without a name on the roll.
items.quote: सर्वेक्षण के दौरान सात ऐसे पात्र भारतीय नागरिकों की पहचान की गई, जिनका नाम अभी तक मतदाता सूची में दर्ज नहीं है।
items.response: The report does not say whether the seven were ever on a roll, whether they applied on Form 6 or whether they were left off the draft. The Jharkhand Mukti Morcha's central general secretary and spokesperson, Vinod Pandey, told the paper that the revision was troubling the poor, asked the Commission to stop harassing Adivasis, Moolvasis, migrant workers, women and the elderly, said documents that are hard to provide were being demanded, and called it a matter of concern that only 2.21 crore of Jharkhand's 2.64 crore electors were on the draft.

items.headline: 73.3 lakh left off draft roll, barely 1,000 file fresh forms in Telangana
items.claim: Barely 1,000 of the 73.3 lakh electors left off Telangana's draft roll of 17 August had submitted fresh enumeration forms, The Times of India reported on 25 November. The office of the Chief Electoral Officer told the paper that reports from the districts showed only around 50 to 100 people in each district had come forward. The paper gives 45.1 lakh of those left off as permanently shifted, 11.2 lakh as absent or untraceable, 9.2 lakh as dead and 6.7 lakh as already enrolled elsewhere. The office said the electors in these categories were identified only after house to house visits and due enquiry by booth level officers. Officials told the paper that many electors who found their names missing had applied on Form 6 before the Commission gave them the further opportunity. Booth level officers collect the fresh forms until 30 November, and the final roll is due on 22 December. District reports as of 20 November showed that nearly 99 per cent, or 92 lakh, of the 92.8 lakh electors on the draft who were sent notices had been cleared for the final roll, 60.1 lakh of them with logical discrepancies and 31.8 lakh who could not be matched with earlier rolls. Of the 2,64,87,213 electors on the draft, officials had marked 2,63,96,341 for inclusion in the final roll and 58,772 as ineligible, and decisions were pending in 32,100 cases, 22,958 of them in Hyderabad, against 29 in Rangareddy and 22 in Medchal-Malkajgiri. Across the state 35,934 unmapped electors and 21,885 electors with logical discrepancies were marked ineligible. Rangareddy had the most marked ineligible, 13,493, 11,471 of them unmapped, and Mulugu the highest share, 1.39 per cent of its draft electorate, against 0.22 per cent for the state.
items.quote: The Telangana chief electoral officer’s (CEO) office said reports from districts showed that only around 50 to 100 people in each district has so far come forward to submit fresh enumeration forms.
items.response: The count of fresh forms is rounded, and the paper gives no count for any named district. It does not say how many of the forms were accepted, or how many electors left off the draft applied on Form 6.

items.place: Pune; Kasba Peth; Jalgaon; Sangli; Kolhapur; Satara
items.headline: Missing links: Voter revision leaves Maharashtra sex workers in limbo
items.claim: Sex workers in Maharashtra are at risk of being left off the roll because they cannot link a parent's name to the 2002 roll or produce other documents, The Times of India reported on 25 November. The National Network of Sex Workers wrote to the state's Chief Electoral Officer in July asking for special provisions. In one polling booth of Budhwar Peth in Pune, in the Kasba Peth constituency, 200 of 800 residents were flagged during the revision, and the registration officer for Kasba Peth, Vitthal Joshi, told the paper that officials were now looking into the last 49. The sex workers' collective Sangram found only 46 of roughly 660 women in one part of Sangli on the draft roll, and a worker of Aadhar Bahuudeshiya Sanstha in Jalgaon said 85 of roughly 500 members of the community and their relatives in her area had received notices. A peer educator in Jalgaon said many booth level officers had also asked for caste certificates, which are issued in the father's name. The paper reports that officials require a gap of at least 15 years between the ages of a mother and her child, and the peer educator asked how women who gave birth as minors could meet it. The paper reports that in Sangli, Kolhapur and Satara sex workers had gone missing from the rolls or appeared both on the draft and on the absent, shifted, dead and duplicate list. Joshi said special camps had been held at polling stations and civic offices, that where mapping to a parent failed officials placed women in a no linkage category and accepted letters from organisations, statements from landlords on 15 to 30 years of residence and booth level officers' field reports, and that those left off can still apply on Form 6. The final roll is due on 22 December.
items.quote: Where progeny mapping failed, officials placed women under a “no linkage” category, accepting NGO letters, landlord statements confirming 15 to 30 years of residency, and BLO field reports.
items.response: The counts for Sangli and Jalgaon are the organisations' and the paper gives no official count for any of the places. Akshay Jain, chairman of media and communication of the Maharashtra Youth Congress, said he knew several women sex workers and transgender people in the area who had been left off the rolls despite living there for 25 to 35 years, and that the Commission must ensure no vulnerable citizen is disenfranchised in the name of verification.

items.headline: BJP-led Bengal govt links Bharosa scheme benefits to post-SIR voter roll, CAA applications
items.claim: The Government of West Bengal has made inclusion in the final roll published after the 2026 revision a key condition of eligibility for its Bharosa scheme, which is to pay educated unemployed people aged 21 to 45 up to Rs 2,000 a month from 1 January 2027, The New Indian Express reported on 25 November with inputs from PTI. The paper reports the guidelines issued by the state government as saying that people whose cases are pending before the SIR appellate tribunal, or whose applications under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act are under consideration, will also be eligible. The state Cabinet approved the scheme on 23 November. Graduates and people taking or holding vocational certificates from government industrial training institutes are to receive Rs 2,000 a month, and non-graduates and undergraduates Rs 1,500. Applicants must be permanent residents of the state, and the guidelines leave out the self-employed, people in government or private employment, beneficiaries of the Annapurna Yojana and other state social security schemes, and more than two applicants from one family. Persons with disabilities receiving pensions such as the Manabik pension remain eligible. Assistance may be withheld or stopped, after the person concerned is heard, if it was sanctioned on incorrect information or the beneficiary ceases to meet the conditions.
items.quote: Those whose cases are pending before the SIR Appellate Tribunal or whose applications under the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) are under consideration will also be eligible, according to guidelines issued by the state government.
items.response: The report gives no statement from the state government beyond the guidelines, no response from any party and no estimate of how many applicants the condition would affect. The guidelines and any notification of them were not found.

items.headline: Howrah Police collect documents from people excluded during SIR; Election office unaware!
items.claim: Police in the Jagacha area of Howrah were collecting personal details and copies of identity documents on Wednesday, 25 November, from residents of Unsani whose names the report says were omitted from the final roll of the revision, Taaza TV reported. Residents told it they were asked for voter identity cards, Aadhaar cards, PAN cards and bank passbooks, and that several declined to hand over copies because no receipt or acknowledgement was given. A sub-inspector said instructions had been sent to all police stations by the state police about two days earlier to collect and forward data on residents left out in the revision, and an official of the district's election office, speaking without being named, said the election administration had no knowledge of any collection of data led by the police. Dainik Jagran reported on 26 November that police stations of the Howrah City Police and the Howrah Rural Police had begun collecting the documents of electors whose cases are pending before the tribunal, asking for copies of Aadhaar and voter identity cards, and that the police said the state police had directed the police stations of every district to verify the documents of electors whose cases are pending before the tribunals. A former CPI(M) councillor, whose own case has been before the tribunal since April, told the paper that collecting documents is the work of the election officials and booth level officers, and that they do not even know of the process. The convener of the Howrah district Left Front, Paresh Pal, wrote to the District Magistrate asking for a meeting on it, and the Left Front asked why the police had been given the work without notice to the public and without a meeting of all parties.
items.quote: Meanwhile, an acting official at the district’s chief electoral office stated anonymously that the election administration had no knowledge of any such police-led data collection exercise.
items.response: Neither report gives the written order or its legal basis, and Taaza TV reports that the officers did not cite either. Neither gives a statement from the state police, the District Magistrate or the Chief Electoral Officer.

items.headline: Pune: Special Camps On November 28, 29 To Help ASDD Voters Submit SIR Forms
items.claim: The Pune district election administration will hold special camps at every polling station in the district on Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November for electors left off the draft roll as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate to submit their enumeration forms, The Free Press Journal reported on 25 November. The paper gives the schedule of the Commission's letter of 17 November as forms prepared and printed by 18 November, handed out and collected from 18 to 30 November and processed by 10 December, claims and objections decided by 15 December and the final roll published on 22 December. Loksatta reported on 24 November that Thane's District Election Officer, Shrikrishna Panchal, told a press conference on Monday, 23 November, that the enumeration forms of 28,60,266 electors in the district's 18 Assembly constituencies are in the category of electors left off the draft. Of them 2,22,706 are recorded as dead, 17,08,045 as not found at their address or absent, 7,35,144 as permanently shifted and 41,033 for other reasons, and 1,53,338 are recorded as already enrolled. The forms are being sent through booth level officers and by WhatsApp, email and SMS, and the paper gives 30 November as the last date. Electors who had not filed an enumeration form before are to submit Annexure B with it, and electors who moved within the state Annexure C. The district received 1,67,152 applications from 31 August to 13 November, 1,06,149 on Form 6, 360 on Form 6A, 11,093 on Form 7 and 49,550 on Form 8, and the paper reports that inclusion had been completed on 1,30,739 of them and 10,887 were pending.
items.quote: The Pune district election administration will organise special registration camps at all polling stations across the district on Nov 28 and 29 to facilitate the submission of enumeration forms by such voters.
items.response: Neither report gives a count of enumeration forms received so far from these electors, and The Free Press Journal gives no count of them for Pune district.

items.outlet: The Times of India; Dainik Jagran
items.headline: Jharkhand achieves 93% completion of SIR electoral roll hearings in 41 assembly constituencies
items.claim: Jharkhand's Chief Electoral Officer, K. Ravi Kumar, reviewed on Thursday, 26 November, the 40 of the state's 81 Assembly constituencies where hearings on the notices for no mapping and logical discrepancies had progressed least, and directed the registration officers to dispose of every logical discrepancy, no mapping and other case by 30 November, The Times of India and Dainik Jagran reported. The Times of India reports that more than 93% of the hearings had been completed in the other 41 constituencies, and Dainik Jagran gives 93%. He asked officials to identify the reasons for slow progress and to dispose of each case under the rules, and to speed up home to roll verification. For cases still pending he asked the officers concerned to survey and verify them in person and review their status. He directed that during super checking and home to roll verification special efforts be made to enrol every eligible citizen who had turned 18 by 1 October 2026.
items.quote: Reviewing the progress of hearings in 40 assembly constituencies, where the disposal rate has been low, Jharkhand chief electoral officer (CEO) K Ravi Kumar on Thursday directed electoral registration officers (EROs) to achieve 100% disposal of ‘Logical discrepancy’, ‘No mapping’ and ‘Others’ cases by Nov 30.
items.response: Neither report gives a count of hearings held or pending, names the constituencies on either side of the line or gives a count of electors found ineligible. The Times of India reported from the office's data that 18,425 cases had been marked ineligible by 21 November (form7-87).

items.headline: NPCC urges comprehensive SIR
items.claim: The president of the Nagaland Pradesh Congress Committee and Lok Sabha member, Supongmeren Jamir, and its working president, Khrieti, met Nagaland's Chief Electoral Officer, Bhagyashree Banayat, on 26 November to discuss the revision, The Morung Express reported from the party's press statement of that day. The statement as the paper reports it says that during the meeting it was learnt that about 1.57 lakh electors had been deleted from the rolls and that about 25% of them had so far been covered by the revision, and that the exercise was expected to continue until 22 December. The Nagaland Tribune reports that the delegation was told this. The party asked the Election Department for a more detailed and comprehensive revision so that every elector whose name had been deleted, or who remained uncovered, had an adequate chance to be included, The Morung Express reports. The meeting followed a march by the party and its Kohima District Congress Committee.
items.quote: During the meeting, it was learnt that approximately 1.57 lakh voters had been deleted from the electoral rolls, of which around 25% had been covered by the revision process so far.
items.response: The account of what the delegation was told is the party's, and neither report gives a statement from the Chief Electoral Officer. Neither says what being covered by the revision means, whether an enumeration form handed out or returned or a name added back.

items.headline: गुरुग्राम में SIR में गायब मिले 4.53 लाख वोटर्स, नाम जुड़वाने के लिए पहुंचे महज 200
items.claim: In Gurugram district's four Assembly constituencies, Gurgaon, Badshahpur, Pataudi and Sohna, 4,53,079 of the 15,55,034 electors on the roll before the revision were not found at their addresses during it, Dainik Jagran reported on 27 November. Of them 30,000 had been verified so far, and only 200 had come forward to apply to have their names added again. The district has 1,504 booth level officers going from house to house to verify them, and the paper gives 30 November as the last date for the verification and for applying to be added again. The paper reports that under the Commission's revised schedule for Haryana claims and objections are to be decided by 15 December and the final roll published on 22 December. The election tahsildar of Gurugram, Rajendra Hooda, told the paper that electors still not found after 30 November were likely to have moved, to have been enrolled at more than one place, so that one entry is deleted, or to have died, and that each elector's status is being verified so that no eligible elector's name is deleted.
items.quote: इनमें से अब तक 30 हजार मतदाताओं का सत्यापन किया जा चुका है। लेकिन, नाम दोबारा जुड़वाने के लिए केवल 200 मतदाता ही आगे आए हैं।
items.response: The report does not say what the verification of the 30,000 found, how many of them were found at their addresses, or how the 200 applied. It gives no statement from the District Election Officer.

items.headline: Nearly one in three Form 7s not disclosed on Delhi CEO website
items.claim: At least 11,816 of the 37,078 Form 7 objections seeking deletion that Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer received in the 87 days for claims and objections of the revision, 31.87%, are missing from the mandated public lists of such objections on the office's own website, The Hindu reported on 27 November. The paper gives the 37,078 as the count in the Chief Electoral Officer's own data, and reports that the period for claims and objections ended on 25 November after nearly three months. The office's press note of 26 November gives 37,038 Form 7 objections received from 31 August to 25 November (form7-113), 40 fewer than the paper's count.
items.quote: At least 11,816 (31.87%) deletion applications from the 37,078 received as per Delhi CEO’s data source in the 87-day claims and objections window of Delhi SIR remain missing from the mandated public lists of such applications on its own website
items.response: The headline, standfirst and opening paragraph give no response from the Chief Electoral Officer's office and do not say how many of the objections missing from the lists were acted on.

items.headline: ECI to soon launch a single-point App for stakeholders; to subsume over existing 40 IT Apps with enhanced UI/UX
items.claim: The Commission announced in May 2025 that it was building ECINET, one platform to bring together more than 40 of its apps and websites for voters, election officials and other users.
items.quote: The new one-stop platform, ECINET, will integrate and reorient over 40 of ECI’s existing mobile and web applications. ... To ensure that data is as accurate as possible, the data on ECINET will be entered solely by the authorized ECI official.

items.headline: Order of 19.01.2026, W.P.(C) 1089/2025
items.claim: The Supreme Court recorded, from the documents before it, what the logical discrepancy category in West Bengal covered and that about 1.36 crore voters fell in it.
items.quote: The documents brought on record by the parties indicate that, within the category of logical discrepancies include, inter alia, a mismatch of the father’s name, a mismatch of parents’ ages, a difference in parents’ ages of more than 50 years, a difference in grandparents’ ages of less than 40 years, and those having more than six progeny.

items.headline: ECINET Digital Platform launched at IICDEM-2026
items.claim: The Commission launched ECINET formally on 22 January 2026 and said its trial version had already been used during the Bihar election and the SIR.
items.quote: The beta version was successfully piloted during the 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), enabling the Election Commission to deliver enhanced citizen-centric electoral services and make available all election-related information at the click of a button.

items.headline: Press note No.EL.63/2026/50: CEO Meghalaya Reviews Notice and Hearing Phase of SIR 2026
items.claim: Meghalaya's Chief Electoral Officer listed six checks that ECINET used to flag mapping discrepancies in the third phase, among them a sibling age gap under nine months.
items.quote: The discrepancies identified through ECINET are: mismatch between the elector's name and the name available in the SIR 2005 records; mismatch between the elector's parent's name and the corresponding name recorded in SIR 2005; age difference between the elector and parent being less than 15 years or more than 50 years; age gap of less than nine months between siblings linked to the same parent; more than six children being linked to the same parent; and age difference of less than 40 years between an elector and grandparent.

items.headline: The meeting of the Commission was held today i.e. 26.09.2026 at 3:00 PM
items.claim: After its full meeting on 26 September 2026 the Commission said field officers have access to ECINET by role, set up a committee with an independent expert to check ECINET against the law, and said new IT modules would first go to a committee of officers.
items.quote: Field officers have role-based access to the ECINET system as per their statutory powers. A Committee headed by Sr. Deputy Election Commissioner (DEC) and including an independent expert from IIT/IIIT will review the ECINET to double-check that it complies with the provisions of the Acts and Rules and submit report to the Commission. ... Henceforth, all the new initiatives about IT modules and portals will be discussed in the Committee of Officers (COO) before approval by the Commission.

items.headline: MP Special Intensive Revision: 100 Forms A Day, BLOs Complain Of Impossible Targets; Voters Can’t Find Old Records
items.claim: Booth officers in Bhopal told the Free Press Journal they were asked to upload 100 forms a day and could not, because the booth officers' app server was down or very slow.
items.quote: They are being asked to collect and upload 100 forms a day. It is an impossible target to achieve, they say, adding that they are unable to feed the data of voters as the server of BLO App is either down or very slow.

items.headline: How ECI’s dubious software branded 3.66 crore voters in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh as suspects
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported, from internal Commission records it acquired, that the Commission's software initially flagged 1.31 crore voters in West Bengal and 2.35 crore in Madhya Pradesh for logical discrepancies, and that officials had no written instructions on how to resolve them. It reported that no criteria for deciding which flagged voters to summon had been made public.
items.response: The Collective said the Commission did not answer its question on how flagged voters were chosen, and that questions sent to the Commission and three state offices on testing and procedure went unanswered.

items.headline: Verified: ECI’s top West Bengal officer sent orders to state officials for SIR on WhatsApp
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that on 29 December 2025 the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer's office told state officials in writing that the logical discrepancy software was faulty because the 2002 roll had not been digitised accurately.
items.quote: On December 29, after the enumeration phase was complete, the CEO West Bengal’s office admitted on record to state officials that the software finding ‘logical discrepancies’ was malfunctioning. This was because the base data, the 2002 voter list, had not been digitised accurately, the CEO admitted.
items.response: The Collective said the Commission and the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer did not reply to its questions on the WhatsApp instructions.

items.outlet: Siasat (IANS, citing officials of the Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal)
items.headline: West Bengal SIR: ECI explains why ‘logical discrepancy’ cases are high
items.claim: Officials of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer told IANS that the logical discrepancy check caught people who had falsely linked themselves to unrelated voters, and gave examples they said were found at hearings.
items.quote: “There have been cases where eight to ten voters were shown as sons or daughters of a single senior citizen voter during progeny mapping. However, during hearings, it was found that the senior citizen had only two children and had no blood relationship with most of those listed as his sons or daughters,” said an official from the CEO’s office.

items.headline: BLO App underwent 30 changes in two months in Tamil Nadu
items.claim: The New Indian Express reported that the Android version of the booth officers' app was updated 31 times between 13 November 2025 and 20 January 2026, with no user manual for the updates, and that officials relied on the app to learn what the revision allowed.
items.quote: TNIE’s analysis of iOS and Android version logs showed that the Android version underwent 31 updates between November 13 (version 8.65) and January 20 (9.10), which is at an average of a new version released every second day. ... “The options available on the BLO App informed us what is permitted and what is not rather than detailed instructions or training material regarding the process or the use of the app,” a district-level official said.

items.headline: BLO App underwent 30 changes in two months in Tamil Nadu
items.claim: The same report quoted a Chennai booth officer who said the app often froze on her phone, so that data was lost or finished work had to be done again.
items.quote: A BLO from Chennai told TNIE that her phone couldn’t handle the application and frequently froze, leading to loss of data or redoing of completed work.

items.headline: ECI misled the Supreme Court on SIR in West Bengal
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that hearing notices in West Bengal were generated in bulk by the Commission's software for logical discrepancies, and that two EROs it spoke to, with a few deputies, were signing 4,000 to 5,000 printed notices each day. It reported that the software transliterated names from Bengali into English before matching, so that spellings such as Xalxo and Khalkho triggered a discrepancy. The Collective said this showed the Commission had misled the Supreme Court, where it said there was no automated generation of notices.
items.response: The Collective said the Commission had not responded by publication. It set its finding against the Commission's submission to the Court that "There is no automated generation of notices" and that officers were "signing them off after application of mind".

items.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that in West Bengal the logical discrepancy check flagged five kinds of mismatch, from spelling differences between the Bengali 2002 roll and the English draft to age gaps with parents and grandparents.
items.quote: The discrepancies were of five kinds, as per ECI’s new algorithm: Differences in spelling between the names in the 2002 in Bengali script and in the 2025 draft voter rolls in English More than six voters had linked themselves to a single ancestor from the 2003 list; The age gap between a voter and their parent fell outside the 15-to-45-year range; A cited grandparent was less than 40 years older than the voter; The gender of the voter did not align with the name provided.
items.response: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

items.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that a registration officer showed its reporter that the button to clear voters with a name mismatch had disappeared from ERONET since that morning, so such cases now needed the district officer's approval.
items.quote: “These options keep changing every other day,” the ERO told me. “Till this morning, for logical discrepancies with name mismatch, ERONET was allowing me to verify the elector by myself. Now, when I open ERONET, that button has disappeared. Now, these have to be approved by the DEO.”
items.response: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

items.headline: Express Special | EC changes Form 6 for new voters without amendment to rules; seeks SIR details of parents
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that the online Form 6 on the Commission's ECINET portal carried a new declaration asking whether the applicant or their parents or grandparents were in the electoral roll of the last SIR, although the statutory form had not been amended. It reported that although the section was not marked mandatory, applicants could not submit the form without completing it, and that the downloadable Form 6 on the same portal did not include it.
items.response: The EC did not respond to a request for comment and Legislative Department Secretary Rajiv Mani could not be reached despite repeated attempts.

items.headline: SIR: Not even 0.5% submit enumeration forms online amid website glitches
items.claim: The Hindu reported that 13 days into the Karnataka SIR only 0.41% of enumeration forms had been submitted online, and that voters complained of captcha failures, server errors and an ECINet search that failed to find records appearing in the published rolls. It reported that online submission required a current mobile number linked to the voter's EPIC.
items.response: Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar said the process was still under way. However, the CEO did not comment on the technical glitches reported by voters.

items.headline: SIR: ECINET Portal Faces Peak-Hour Glitches
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that people filling in enumeration forms on ECINET in Telangana kept being sent back to the home page, and an official put it down to the load from voters in more than a dozen states at once.
items.quote: Officials admitted the portal was hit by server overload as voters from over a dozen states under Phase 3 of SIR accessed it simultaneously. “It is a fact that people are facing issues. In Telangana, there is no need to panic as the ECI has extended the deadline till August 3,” a senior official told Deccan Chronicle.

items.headline: ‘Illegal, unauthorised’: Election Commissioners objected to Form 6 change
items.claim: The Indian Express reported, from internal records it investigated, that on May 16 Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi recorded that Form 6 is prescribed by statute and cannot be altered without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and that Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu concurred on May 19. It reported that the declaration was added to the online form anyway, and that on August 13 Sandhu wrote that the changes were unauthorised and illegal and must be removed immediately.

items.headline: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary’s door over voter software integrity
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi warned on file, from November 2025 to August 2026, that control of the electoral roll software was being centralised in the Commission's IT division. It reported that on August 14 Sandhu wrote that many Chief Electoral Officers, District Election Officers and Electoral Registration Officers had told him they lacked proper and complete access to ERONet, and that on July 29 both Commissioners wrote separately to the Cabinet Secretary about a change in work allocation.
items.response: The Election Commission and the two ECs, Sandhu and Joshi, did not respond to calls and questionnaires emailed by The Indian Express seeking comment.

items.headline: The many categories of SIR’s logical discrepancy list keep voters on toes
items.claim: The Hindu reported that up to 11 categories of logical discrepancy were being applied in the third phase of the SIR, up from four when the concept was introduced in West Bengal. They include a sibling age gap of nine months or less, which flagged a Delhi resident's twin children, and a marital mapping mismatch where a woman is linked to her father in the old roll and her husband in the new. It reported that the term has never been clearly defined in any official communication.

items.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out: EC’s flawed system
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that Goa's Electoral Registration Officers heard electors flagged for logical discrepancies and found 97 of them eligible, but could not reverse the earlier decisions on ECINET because the permission was controlled from Delhi. It reported that the Goa Chief Electoral Officer's office wrote eight times in seven days asking for a rollback option, and that all 97 were missing from the final roll published on February 21 and were still missing on September 20.
items.response: Goa's Chief Electoral Officer, Sanjay Goel, told the paper the decision not to include them was the Commission's. The Indian Express later reported that the Commission said, after its meeting of 26 September, that 81 of the 97 had filled Form 6 and that the Chief Electoral Officer had been told to help include them.

items.headline: ECINet is decentralised, only designated officials have access, says ECI
items.claim: Commission officials said ECINET is decentralised, that each field officer acts through their own login, and that nobody at headquarters can perform those officers' statutory functions. ERONET is now part of ECINET.
items.quote: “No one else can perform their statutory function on ECINet, including any other officer of the ECI,” an official said. Cybersecurity for the platform is, however, provided centrally by the ECI. ... Official documents refer to it as the “Electoral Roll module of ECINET Portal (previously ERONET)”.

items.headline: Delhi SIR: Over 350 names already marked ineligible; CEO warns against deletion on flimsy grounds
items.claim: The Hindu reported that more than 350 Delhi electors had been marked ineligible within a month of hearings, about 200 of them in Vikaspuri, and officials said the marking could not be rolled back by the registration officer or the state's Chief Electoral Officer.
items.quote: Of the 350 electors already marked ineligible less than a month into the hearings process, about 200 are from the Vikaspuri constituency; once a voter is marked ineligible, this cannot be rolled back at the level of ERO or State CEO, officials said
items.response: The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer wrote to officers on 25 September 2026 setting a 10-point checklist before marking anyone ineligible and telling them not to delete names on flimsy or frivolous grounds.

items.headline: Maharashtra Poll Chief Seeks More ERO Powers As ECINet Faces Scrutiny Over SIR
items.claim: Outlook, citing NDTV, reported that Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer S Chockalingam asked for four changes to the ECINET software and more discretion for registration officers in logical discrepancy cases.
items.quote: Chockalingam has also sought four changes in the ECINet software, including for cases marked as “logical discrepancies”.
items.response: The Commission said on 26 September that several portal upgrades had already been made on inputs from state Chief Electoral Officers and that further flexibility needed by field officers would be made operational.

items.headline: EC removes Form 6 change two Commissioners had called ‘illegal’
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that on the night of 29 to 30 September 2026 the Commission removed the SIR declaration from the online Form 6 on ECINET for states where the final SIR rolls have been published. It reported that the declaration remained for states where the SIR is still ongoing.
items.response: The article cites the Commission's September 26 announcement that ‘for non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used’.

items.headline: Cong accuses EC of 'lying' about ECINet, calls for accountability
items.claim: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh alleged that by restricting registration officers' access to the ECINet roll system and overruling them in Goa, West Bengal and other states, the Commission broke the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
items.quote: “By restricting access of Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to the ECINet voter roll system and by overruling EROs in states like Goa, West Bengal and others, the ECI controlled by the CEC has violated The Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960,” Ramesh said.
items.response: PTI recalled that the Commission, under fire over objections from two of its Commissioners, had said differing views are a normal part of deliberation and that all its orders carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.

items.headline: After 13 crore names dropped from draft rolls, EC orders ‘left out’ voter drive
items.claim: The Indian Express reported a letter of 29 September from the Commission’s Secretary ordering a special drive to enrol "left out and young/first time eligible electors" in the 20 states and union territories where the revision is complete, using the statutory Form 6, with the added declaration kept for the revision phase only. It reported that at a video conference with all Chief Electoral Officers, the states were told to compare the roll from before the revision with the one after, list those left off or deleted, visit them at home and help those left out fill in Form 6, with help from the parties’ booth agents.
items.response: The letter of 29 September itself was not found. The Commission's letter of 1 October, which continues it, is in the timeline above. The Commission’s press note of 26 September, in the timeline above, had already ordered the drive, and Uttarakhand’s Chief Electoral Officer set out its steps in a press note of 3 October.

items.headline: EC explains new ERONET options for SIR notice disposal to EROs through demo video; no written instructions yet
items.claim: The Hindu reported that the options reached Delhi officers on 30 September and only the ten states and union territories where the third phase was still under way, and that a case marked ineligible still could not be reversed.
items.quote: EROs in Delhi could access the options from September 30, while the eight-minute video explaining the changes was shown to them at a meeting on Saturday (October 3, 2026). ... While the new options let EROs clear notice cases faster, including those where documents are unavailable, based on their satisfaction, they still cannot reverse a case once an elector has been marked ineligible, officials said.
items.response: The Delhi CEO’s office and the EC did not respond to queries on why the options were introduced at this stage.

items.headline: 'Misleading': ECI fact-checks Rahul Gandhi's Form 6 claim, cites SC ruling on Bihar SIR order
items.claim: Rahul Gandhi of the Congress, the Leader of the Opposition, said the Chief Election Commissioner had changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. The Commission replied on X that the statement was misleading, that its Bihar order of 24 June 2025 had the Commission's unanimous approval and was upheld by the Supreme Court on 27 May 2026, and that its press note of 26 September said the declaration attached to Form 6 had been upheld, Business Today reported.
items.quote: "It is now established beyond doubt that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally," Gandhi said. ... Fact Check ❌The statement made in this post is misleading ✅1) The order for SIR in Bihar issued on 24 June 2025 was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. This order has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its judgment dated 27 May 2026 ✅2) In its Press Note No. 120 dated 26 September 2026, in Point 1(iii), ECI has stated that, "The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court." #ECIFactCheck

items.headline: Dozen Bengal tribunal judges flag EC portal: ‘Can’t restore deleted voters’
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that at a meeting on 11 August 2026 more than a dozen West Bengal appeal tribunal judges recorded that the Commission's portal did not let them serve notices, hold virtual hearings, restore a deleted voter or give appellants a copy of the order.
items.quote: “There is no mechanism to hold virtual hearings in case the Tribunal intends to hear the parties…Once the appeal is disposed of either by way of deletion or inclusion of the voter, it cannot be restored on the portal if the restoration is needed on account of direction of the judicial order or otherwise.”
items.response: The paper said it emailed the Commission and the Registrar General of the Calcutta High Court on 1 October and received no response.

items.headline: ECINET flaws were flagged to poll body, cyber-security agency CERT-In in July: Researcher
items.claim: Hindustan Times reported that a security researcher emailed CERT-In on 8 July 2026, copied to the Commission's complaints address, about flaws in the voter-services website and the ECINET app. The worst, in the researcher's account, let anyone obtain election officials' names and mobile numbers without logging in.
items.quote: The issue [the researcher] rated as critical concerns a server behind the voter portal. He says it returned the names and mobile numbers of election officials to requests that carried no login, CAPTCHA or visible limit on the number of requests.
items.response: HT said neither CERT-In nor the Commission answered its questions of 5 October. On 6 October CERT-In told the researcher that one flaw, the hardcoded encryption key he rated least serious, had been fixed and that work on the rest was under progress. HT said none of the flaws related directly to registration officers' access to the roll, and that the email alleged no theft or misuse of data.

items.headline: ECINET designed to centralise voter deletions from BJP headquarters, Congress alleges
items.claim: Congress alleged after the Hindustan Times report that ECINET was designed to centralise deletions and additions from the BJP's headquarters. This is a party's allegation. Hindustan Times had said none of the flaws it reported related directly to registration officers' access to the roll.
items.quote: The Congress on Thursday alleged that the Election Commission’s online portal for voter registration and related services was designed to “centralise all deletions and additions from the Bharatiya Janata Party headquarters”.
items.response: Scroll did not report a response from the Commission to this allegation.

items.headline: 'Was Ghosted': Why [the researcher] Wrote to Election Commission and CERT-in in July
items.claim: The security researcher who reported the ECINET flaws told The Wire that CERT-In and the Commission did not reply to him until a Hindustan Times reporter contacted them. CERT-In then said one issue had been resolved, which he said was the most minor. He said the flaws affected at least eight parts of the Commission's systems, including the Suvidha portal and ECORE.
items.quote: According to him, it was the most minor of the lot.
items.response: No statement from the Commission was reported.

items.headline: In UP SIR, ECI Software Auto-generated 87,127* Forms to Delete Voters Without a Reason
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported, from more than 4.3 lakh Form 7 disclosures on the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's website, that 87,127 deletion requests were filed by registration officers and assistant registration officers between 15 March and 2 April 2026 and that none of them gave a reason. Registration officers it spoke to said ERONET generated a Form 7 carrying their digital signature whenever they did not approve a voter at a hearing. It also reported that 1,10,476 deletion requests from individuals were accepted after the deadline.
items.quote: The Election Commission of India (ECI) forced officers in Uttar Pradesh to sign deletion forms for 87,127* voters without giving any reason during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in the state.
items.response: The Collective said the Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission had not replied by publication. On 13 October 2026 IANS reported the Chief Electoral Officer's office calling the claims misleading and saying "Notices, hearings, scrutiny and recorded orders preceded action. Pending cases were decided after 6 March as per procedure."

items.headline: The ECI Software Deleted 5.38 Lakh Bengal Voters With Auto-Generated Rejections Without Citing a Reason
items.claim: The Wire reported that 5,38,320 names were deleted from West Bengal's roll between the draft of December 2025 and the final roll of 28 February 2026 through Form 7s that the Commission's software generated in the officer's name when an officer did not approve an elector at a hearing, and that 7,733 more were deleted on Form 7s that people had filed. In the Form 10 registers it read for 284 of the 294 constituencies, 5,23,998 of 5,24,420 Form 7 deletions give the Electoral Registration Officer as the objector and leave the reason blank, and 422 give an individual objector. The Chief Electoral Officer's statement of 6 March 2026 said the state's Form 7 figure included these auto-generated forms, and that the Commission had sent the figure of 5,38,320 by email on 28 February.
items.quote: The figure of deletion due to Form 7 as mentioned, includes the auto generated Form 7 generated due to rejection of Enumeration Forms (EFs) as electors not found eligible for Final Roll.
