This Figure which was received from ECI (Election Commission of India) by mail on 28.02.26 in 5,38,320 (sic).
items.response: The Wire reported that the Additional Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal told it Form 10 gives no option to record details, and that those deleted can apply again through Form 6.

items.headline: Audit finds Bengal-specific access curbs in ECINET code
items.claim: The Hindustan Times reported a review of ECINET's publicly served code by Saurav Rajput, a data scientist at the civic-tech initiative Charchagram, which found an exception written into the code that can bar Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers in West Bengal from the View Enumeration Form Details tile on the SIR Phase II landing page and from the notice-and-hearing dashboard. The review found no such exclusion for these officers in any other state. The enumeration form page lists each form with its documents and the booth level officer's recommendation, and holds documents labelled as hearing orders. The review read only the code a browser receives before login, on 2, 6, 7 and 9 October and in code fetched on 19 October, so it cannot say whether the rule was ever used, whether the server enforces it, or when it was added. The paper could not verify the review independently.
items.quote: West Bengal is separately hard-coded in the codebase and excluded from it (for ERO and AERO).
items.response: The Hindustan Times reported that the Election Commission did not answer a questionnaire it sent.

items.headline: On ECINet platform, access for States can be switched off and on centrally: report
items.claim: The Hindu reported another finding from Saurav Rajput's review of ECINET's code for the civic-tech initiative Charchagram. Behind the official login the portal has an area for managing State Nodal Officers, and each officer's row has a disable button whose confirmation says the user will no longer be able to access the application. Separately, the code carries the message that viewing enumeration form details is not enabled for the selected State, which the review reads as a feature switched on or off State by State. The review read only code the site serves before login. The paper says it was not clear since when the feature has been on the portal, which was launched in January 2026, and the reviewer said he had seen it since 28 September.
items.quote: On disabling this State Nodal Officer, the user will no longer be able to access the application.
items.response: The Hindu carried a statement by the Congress general secretary (communications), Jairam Ramesh, that the ECINET system and the Commission's IT division had overruled the statutory authority of Electoral Registration Officers. It reported no response from the Commission.

items.headline: TMC seeks EC explanation on Bengal specific feature in voter’s enumeration forms in ECINET
items.claim: Millennium Post reported that the Trinamool Congress, reacting to the Hindustan Times report of the same day on the West Bengal rule in ECINET's code, asked the Election Commission who had authorised the Bengal-specific changes, why West Bengal was treated differently from other states, who is accountable and what safeguards protect every eligible voter's rights. The party also asked when the Chief Election Commissioner would take responsibility and resign.
items.quote: Who authorised these Bengal-specific changes, and Why?
items.response: The report carries no response from the Commission.

items.headline: ECINET Audit Finds State-Level Access Could be Restricted by Election Commission, VIP Tags for Voters
items.claim: The Wire reported three findings from Saurav Rajput's review of ECINET's code for the civic-tech initiative Charchagram, made on 2, 6, 7 and 9 October from code the site serves publicly, with no passwords and no use of ECINET's programming interfaces. Besides the State Nodal Officer controls and the West Bengal rule in the two reports before it, the review found code showing that the officials' portal marks some voters with a gold VIP symbol on the screen that shows the documents in an enumeration form, and a button that downloads a list of these VIP electors by Assembly constituency, which can be narrowed by state, district, constituency and polling part. The criteria for marking a voter are not known. The review cannot say whether any of these features were used, by whom or how often. The Reporters' Collective earlier reported a Mark VIP module in the booth level officers' app, and Charchagram says its review examined the other end of that chain.
items.quote: At present, we cannot say whether these features have been used, or prove how they have been used
items.response: The report carries no response from the Commission.

items.headline: Details of software used in SIR exempt from RTI, Election Commission cites 'trade secrets'
items.claim: In a reply dated 16 October to an RTI application from a social activist in Karimnagar, the Commission declined to give the name and version of the software it used to find errors and anomalies in the rolls during the revision, citing commercial confidence, trade secrets and intellectual property under Section 8(1)(d), the Hindustan Times reported. It called the questions on automatic flagging, artificial intelligence and safeguards against wrongful flagging a clarification outside the definition of information, and cited Section 8(1)(g) on who reviews flagged records.
items.quote: no new software has been developed or procured for the SIR exercise
items.response: The Commission said Electoral Registration Officers decide on including or excluding an elector on the basis of facts and records, and that under Sections 13B(1) and 13B(2) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 the officer of each constituency prepares and revises its roll.

items.headline: Pending SIR notice lists published for only 39 assembly constituencies out of 288 so far
items.claim: Lists of electors whose notices were still pending had been published for 39 of Maharashtra's 288 Assembly constituencies, in 14 districts, on the election authorities' websites by Saturday 24 October, The Times of India reported. Officials said the lists hold only unresolved cases and do not cover all 1.22 crore notices generated in the revision. In Pune district only the Shivajinagar list was up, with one elector on it, and in Mumbai the lists for Malabar Hill, Byculla, Dharavi, Dahisar and Vandre West. A circular of 23 October from the Chief Electoral Officer's office told electoral registration officers to download the data from the Commission's ECINET platform, compile one PDF for each constituency, publish it on the district election officer's website by 26 October and share part-wise lists with parties' booth level agents. Officials said documents some electors had given booth level officers during enumeration were not uploaded because the system did not support it then. Notices are to be disposed of by 10 November and the final roll is due on 16 November.
items.quote: The lists cover voters whose names could not be matched with previous electoral rolls, categorised as ‘No Mapping’, and those whose records showed logical discrepancies despite successful mapping. A name appearing on the list does not mean the voter has been finally deleted from the electoral roll,
items.response: An electoral official said a name on the list does not mean the elector has been finally deleted from the roll, and the report says the Chief Electoral Officer's office will review whether district election authorities have complied with the circular.

items.headline: Judges of Bengal tribunals ask Election Commission to fix portal, drop Aadhaar authentication
items.claim: The appellate tribunals of retired High Court judges that hear appeals in West Bengal's revision have asked the Election Commission at least twice in four weeks to remove an Aadhaar authentication step from its portal, because without it they cannot upload final orders, The Indian Express reported from official records. The screen was added on 21 September, the judges asked in writing on 24 September for it to be removed, and on 13 October the tribunals told the Chief Electoral Officer's office again that the system did not let them upload final orders. Orders are being disposed of on paper and not uploaded. The portal also limits the documents the judges can accept to the 13 the Commission listed for the revision. On 1 October ten of the judges wrote about their working conditions at Joka, about 30 km from Kolkata and New Town, and asked for the tribunals to be moved to a more central place and for an honorarium befitting the judges. They noted that a request to raise it from Rs 25,000 a week to Rs 50,000 had been pending with the Chief Justice since June. The report says the Commission told the Supreme Court that 38.31 lakh appeals had been filed as of 18 September, 22.21 lakh by deleted electors and 16.10 lakh against inclusions, and that 1.26 lakh had been disposed of by 10 September.
items.quote: The Honourable Judges at the Appellate Tribunal require the Aadhaar authentication screen removed from the AT portal for the purpose of disposal of appeals.
items.response: The Election Commission did not respond to the paper's queries mailed to its spokesperson on 21 October.

items.headline: Did 27 Lakhs Lose the Right to Vote Because the EC Software Switched Bengal Voters Already Decided by EROs Over to Judges Overnight?
items.claim: Electoral registration officers in Murshidabad had decided almost every hearing case before them by the deadline of 21 February, and a week later far more electors were marked under adjudication and sent to judicial officers than the officers had left pending, The Wire reported from the Commission's ERONET status reports. At 10 pm on 21 February, of 18,84,772 electors called for hearings in the district's 22 constituencies, the officers had parked 18,30,045 for the final roll, found 41,214 ineligible and left 13,513 pending. On 28 February 11,01,145 Murshidabad electors were under adjudication, and judicial officers deleted 4,55,137 of them. In Samserganj 2,391 cases were pending on deadline night, 1,08,400 electors went to adjudication and 74,775 were deleted. Nadia's report of 4:04 am on 22 February shows 57,525 pending, and The Wire puts 2,67,940 of the district's electors under adjudication. An assistant electoral registration officer told The Wire that after hearings closed on 14 February the portal stopped taking document uploads and gained a category, Documents to be reviewed, into which micro-observers and roll observers moved electors the officers had parked for the final roll, and that those the officers then approved again went to adjudication. On 20 February Congress MP Isha Khan Choudhury wrote to the Chief Electoral Officer that the Malda District Magistrate had told an all-party meeting that 5.91 lakh cases had been returned for review that day. Subrata Gupta, the Commission's special roll observer, told The Wire that the observers had recommended a review of lakhs of cases the officers had cleared and that the decisions had to be taken by the registration officers.
items.quote: Of 18,84,772 voters called for hearings across the district’s 22 constituencies, they had approved 18,30,045 for the final rolls and found 41,214 ineligible. Only 13,513 cases were still pending.
items.response: On 1 March the Chief Electoral Officer's office posted on X that names were marked under adjudication because the registration officers had not decided them after hearing. On 2 March it posted that it had nowhere said all such cases were due to indecision by the officers, and that a certain number had remained pending and were referred for adjudication. Gupta said the Commission had told the observers that about 60 lakh of about 1.5 crore cases heard were pending and were referred to judicial officers, and that he could not say whether these were the cases marked for review. The Wire says it has written to the Commission and to the current and previous Chief Electoral Officers, and no reply is reported.

items.headline: Did 27 Lakhs Lose the Right to Vote Because the EC Software Switched Bengal Voters Already Decided by EROs Over to Judges Overnight?
items.claim: A screen recording of the Commission's officer portal seen by The Wire shows how the logical discrepancy check flagged a woman in Deganga, North 24 Parganas, born in 1977, The Wire reported. She had named her father and the portal had found him in the 2002 roll. Under the heading 'Logical Discrepancies' the portal gave a single reason, that six other electors had also named the same man as their father, and the only option on the screen was to schedule a hearing. A leader of a booth level officers' association in West Bengal told The Wire that the BLO app changed about 16 times during the revision and that the logical discrepancy system 'was done from Delhi'. The Wire reported that booth level officers were told to verify the flagged electors in person and did so, and the leader said their reports were submitted through the software and no action was taken on them. He said the then Chief Electoral Officer, Manoj Kumar Agarwal, had told the association that his office was forwarding its letters to Delhi and that 'Whatever is being done is being done from Delhi'.
items.quote: You have been linked as son/daughter with someone who is also claimed by six others as father, giving suspicion of a likely incorrect match.
items.response: The Wire says it asked Agarwal to confirm the remark the association leader attributes to him and that it will update the report when he replies. No reply is reported.

items.headline: Delhi BLOs to record reasons for removing names of eligible voters
items.claim: Booth level officers in Delhi have been told to record why eligible electors were marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate at enumeration, and why those traced in the re-verification of the 47.56 lakh names left off the draft of 31 August are unwilling to apply on Form 6 as new voters, The Hindu reported. A Remarks column has been added to the BLO mobile app for the purpose. It is to record why the elector was placed in those categories, whether the person was found at the registered address, and whether an elector found there is already enrolled in another constituency. Officers are to keep count of their visits, the electors found eligible, the Form 6 applications filed and the reasons for not filing. The paper says the instructions follow the Commission's order of 2 October for a special drive to include eligible electors left off the draft, and that the Chief Electoral Officer's directions came nearly a week after the drive was announced. On 30 October officials said they were planning to step up the door-to-door re-verification with all 14,947 booth level officers, and that special camps for students, homeless people, transgender persons and sex workers were being considered for 15 and 22 November, PTI reported.
items.quote: This field will be used to record why an elector was placed in the ASDD categories during the enumeration phase, whether the person was found residing at the registered address and, if eligible, why the person was reluctant to submit Form 6.
items.response: The instructions are the Chief Electoral Officer's. The report does not say what the recorded reasons will be used for.

items.headline: ECI’s Software and Rules Allow the Pilibhit Fake-Voter Playbook to Run Anywhere in India
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that the Commission's manual for processing Form 8 corrections in its software lets an Electoral Registration Officer start a correction on his or her own motion and approve it without field verification or a hearing, so that one officer can start a change, pass over the check and approve it without the voter knowing. It examined the code of the ECINET app and reported that the software let voters' details be changed without booth level officers or other officials having to upload supporting documents. It decompiled ECINET and ERONET and reported that a registration officer could skip the booth level officer's verification and approve a correction request. It also reported that the software does not require officers to keep a record of the changes they make, and that computer operators used ECINET through the officer's login. It reported that the Commission's disclosures of correction forms give only the voter's name and Assembly constituency and no EPIC number, which it said makes it nearly impossible for the public to tell whose entry was changed. The Collective downloaded 12,082 correction forms submitted across Uttar Pradesh between April and September 2026 from the Commission's portal, while the Chief Electoral Officer's own figures put the forms accepted in those months at 33.8 lakh. It said the same manual and software are used for the regular updating of the roll in every state after the SIR.
items.quote: We found that the constituency-level EROs can initiate changes in voter data on their own without informing the voter or uploading any documentary evidence. They can also approve these changes without field verification of the voter.
items.response: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer and that neither had replied by publication.

items.headline: Judges deciding Bengal voters’ appeals asked to prove their own identity by EC
items.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer's office in West Bengal asked the judges of the SIR appellate tribunals in the last week of October to set up digital signature certificates through a private agency, The Indian Express reported from official records. The judges have not logged in to the Commission's portal since they asked on 24 September for its Aadhaar authentication screen to be removed. The agency's email of 28 October to the Chief Electoral Officer lists what each judge must give, which is colour scans of the PAN card and a government identity card, a colour photograph, a mobile number and an email address, the authorising person's government identity card and an authorisation letter. The process also needs one-time passwords sent to the judge's phone and email and a video verification in which the judge shows the original PAN card and identity card. The paper puts the cost of each certificate at Rs 2,300 at the government-notified rate. It reports that the Aadhaar screen was added on 21 September, after the Commission's Director General (IT), Seema Khanna, made a presentation to the judges on changes to the portal, and that the judges have been working offline, according to sources. It says 1.26 lakh of the 38.31 lakh appeals had been disposed of, by the Commission's figures given to the Supreme Court in September.
items.quote: The Honourable Judges at the Appellate Tribunal require the Aadhaar authentication screen removed from the AT portal for the purpose of disposal of appeals.
items.response: The report carries no reply from the Election Commission or the Chief Electoral Officer's office.

items.headline: Election Commission completes Form 6 U-turn, drops SIR para a Commissioner called ‘illegal’
items.claim: The Election Commission has taken the SIR declaration out of the online Form 6 on its ECINet portal in the states where the revision is still running, and the declaration is now on the portal as a separate form, The Indian Express reported on 4 November. The declaration sat between Sections J and K of the online form and asked an applicant to say whether their own name, or a parent's or grandparent's, was on the roll of the last intensive revision, and an applicant could not go on without answering it. The paper reports that the Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October (court-52) records a decision of its ER Division of 21 October that the online application would be in two parts, Form 6 and the SIR declaration, as the paper forms are, and that this is what the portal now shows. After the Commission's note of 26 September the declaration had been taken off the online form only in the states where the revision had ended. The paper also reports that four changes to ECINet that Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer, S. Chockalingam, sought in a letter of 24 September have been made. Personal hearings for electors sent notices over mapping or logical discrepancies are now held only in exceptional cases, with booth level officers collecting documents at home. Electors may give documents outside the listed categories. Registration officers can decide logical-discrepancy cases themselves without sending them to the District Election Officer. The upload of an extract from the previous SIR roll is no longer mandatory. The paper reports that applicants filing Form 6 in the special summary revision ordered for 17 states and union territories will not have to fill the SIR declaration. The paper reports that a committee to check whether ECINet complies with the applicable Acts and Rules was constituted by a circular of 14 October. It is headed by a Senior Deputy Election Commissioner and includes a second Senior Deputy Election Commissioner, a Deputy Election Commissioner, a director, four Chief Electoral Officers and two independent experts, from IIT Bombay and IISc Bengaluru. On Goa, the paper reports that the Chief Electoral Officer has been directed to see that the 97 electors left off the final roll are included. It reports that the affidavit says 88 of them have filled in Form 6 and had their applications accepted, that six are out of the country and that three hold Portuguese passports. On West Bengal, the paper reports that the affidavit does not give the number of appeals filed against the inclusion of electors, that the appeals have not been withdrawn, and that the affidavit says the electors concerned are on the rolls and voted in the recent Assembly elections.
items.quote: What this means is that the declaration inserted between Sections J and K of the online enrolment application for new voters is no longer part of Form 6.
items.response: The Commission's counter affidavit, as the paper quotes it, maintains that Form 6 was never amended: "There is no substance in the contention that Form 6 has been amended by the Commission vide the SIR Orders." It says the declaration was placed inside the online Form 6 so that an applicant would need a single OTP and a single e-signature.

items.headline: UP’s 18-19 age group voters drop by 5.8L, 72.63L below population estimate
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, announced on 17 November a change to the Election Commission's software to stop the same person being registered more than once, The Times of India reported. He said the earlier system detected a duplicate only when an applicant was already registered, and could not identify several applications made by the same person while an earlier one was pending. Under the changed system booth level officers will receive an alert if an applicant is already registered or has made another application, and the system will show the existing elector's photo identity card number or the reference of the pending application. He said nearly two lakh duplicate entries had been removed in an earlier exercise, and that the duplicates found after the intensive revision came mostly from several applications made after its draft roll of 6 January 2026. He said the aim was that not a single duplicate elector should remain on the final roll of the summary revision, due on 4 January 2027.
items.quote: Under the upgraded system, booth-level officers (BLOs) will receive alerts if an applicant is already registered or has submitted another application.
items.response: The report does not say when the change took effect, whether it applies outside Uttar Pradesh, or which earlier exercise removed the two lakh duplicates and over what period. It carries no statement from the Commission.

items.headline: UP gets searchable, copyable PDF electoral rolls
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, has introduced PDF versions of the draft rolls of the summary revision in which users can search for names and select and copy text, The Times of India reported on 19 November. The paper says the rolls had earlier been available as scanned or image-based PDFs in which text could not be searched, selected or copied, which made checking and analysis more cumbersome. It says the change follows demands for machine-readable rolls during the intensive revision, and that the facility has been introduced by the Chief Electoral Officer's office as part of the summary revision. Rinwa told the paper that the new format was expected to make it easier to scrutinise entries during the claims and objections period, before the final roll is published on 4 January 2027. The draft roll published on 17 November holds over 13.58 crore electors.
items.quote: Previously, electoral rolls available in scanned or image-based PDF formats did not allow users to directly search, select or copy text, making verification and analysis more cumbersome.
items.response: The change is the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report does not say from what date the files have been available, where they are published, whether they carry electors' photographs or whether the final roll will be issued in the same format. It carries no statement from the Commission or from a political party.

items.headline: SIR tribunals resume order uploads after EC removes 13-document cap
items.claim: The Election Commission has changed its portal for West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals as the judges demanded, and the tribunals have begun uploading their orders again after a gap of nearly 45 days, sources told The Times of India, which reported it on 21 November. The dispute over the portal is recorded in soft-41 and soft-50. A source told the paper that orders have been uploaded again since 6 November. The paper reports that the changes let the judges decide which documents they consider in an appeal, and that the portal had let them consider or record only the 13 documents the Commission specified. A source in the tribunals said the use of the judges' Aadhaar numbers to upload orders has been replaced by their digital signatures, and the paper reports that the judges can now review their orders and add observations. The paper reports that the judges stopped logging in to the new portal on 21 September, and that their letter to the Commission in September said the tribunals had been practically rendered functionless and that the limit of 13 documents interfered with the functioning of quasi-judicial authorities. It says that the Supreme Court, when it ordered the tribunals set up in March, noted the 13 documents and said the list was indicative. On the strike by the tribunals' housekeeping staff of 19 November (court-90), a senior official in the Chief Electoral Officer's office told the paper on Friday, 20 November, that the 'matter has been solved', and a source in the tribunals said the strike did not continue that day.
items.quote: Orders are being uploaded again from Nov 6. The EC has made the changes demanded by the judges, following which the tribunals have begun uploading the orders,
items.response: The account of the changes is from sources in the tribunals. The report carries no statement from the Commission and does not say on what date the portal was changed or how many orders have been uploaded since 6 November.

items.headline: Voters’ personal data submitted though Form 6 was exposed on ECI citizen service portal, claims report
items.claim: The Hindu reported on 23 November a report by the civic-tech initiative Charchagram which claims that for at least three years the personal data voters submitted to the Election Commission through Form 6, the application for registration as an elector, was exposed on the Commission's Citizen Service Portal to anyone with a login. The paper's standfirst says that records going back to 2023 were verified for the report and that there was nothing to suggest earlier records were protected, so the exposure may be longer. In a thread on X on 24 November, Charchagram said its audit found that the data voters submit in Form 6 was not secured on the ECInet portal and that anyone could access anyone's details through a simple web address, and it listed the voter's name, phone number, address, Aadhaar details and photograph among the data. In a second post the same day it said the data was accessible on the Commission's Citizen Service Portal to anyone with a login, that its verification found records going back to 2023, and that the scale of the exposure was estimated at at least 7 crore voter enrolments. It said it reported its findings to CERT-In and to the Commission, after which the Commission took steps to restrict access and address the exposure, and it asked how the data came to be left exposed for years, what safeguards were in place, whether this was a data breach and who is accountable.
items.quote: We reported our findings to CERT-In and the Election Commission of India, following which ECI took steps to restrict access and address the exposure.
items.response: The part of The Hindu's report shown free carries no reply from the Commission or CERT-In, and none was found. The account of the Commission's steps is Charchagram's, and it does not say when they were taken.

items.headline: ECI’s Bengal SIR Dashboard Used Hard-Coded Numbers Instead of Live Data, Code Analysis Finds
items.claim: Some of West Bengal's figures on ECINet, the Election Commission's online system for managing the electoral rolls, are written into the code of its pages, so that they stay the same whatever the Commission's database holds, according to an analysis The Wire reported on 24 November. The Wire says it began looking into the code after a tip-off, asked three senior computer scientists and a cybersecurity expert, none of whom wishes to be named, to examine the findings, and read the code as it stood on 18 November, which the server records as last changed on 16 October. By The Wire's account, the dashboard of electors flagged for logical discrepancies shows the database's figure for every state except West Bengal, where the code shows 94,49,132, which The Wire says is the official count of the state's electors flagged in the verification. On a second dashboard the code sets West Bengal's notices at 1,51,92,735 and works out the number of hearings from that figure, and The Wire says the only other figure the code replaces on that dashboard is Tamil Nadu's count of cases found not OK. The Wire reports that the rules used to flag electors are written into the West Bengal dashboard. They are a parent linked to six or more children on the roll, a father's name that does not match, a parent and child less than 15 or more than 50 years apart in age, and a grandparent and grandchild less than 40 years apart. The analysis also found a backup screen for turnout that shows 2,84,19,840 votes from 3,60,77,304 electors, 78.77%, marked as last updated on 11 April 2026, which The Wire matches to the turnout at 3 pm on 23 April, the first day of polling. The Wire says it sent its questions to the Commission on 21 November and that on 23 November the portal was redeployed and visitors to its code files were sent to a login page.
items.quote: When West Bengal is chosen, the code shows 94,49,132, whatever the database says.
items.response: The Wire says the Commission had not answered its questions when the report was published, and that the Commission has not said whether the restriction on the code was connected to them. The Wire says the analysis rests only on the files the portal sends to browsers, that it cannot show what the Commission's servers hold or why the fixed figures are there, and that it found no field for religion, caste or community and no feature that deletes electors automatically at this stage.

items.headline: In Bengal, voters await their fate as judicial tribunals’ functioning comes under scrutiny
items.claim: Electors in West Bengal who face an appeal against their inclusion in the roll before the SIR appellate tribunals have not been able to see the appeal on the Commission's portal since 18 September, Hindustan Times reported on 27 November. Before that date an elector with an appeal against them could enter their EPIC number on the adjudication dashboard on ECINET and see the appeal's ID and status. On 18 September the portal brought in an OTP step for checking the status of appeals against exclusion. From then until 18 November, the paper reports from screen recordings made by electors that it has seen, the 'Track Appeal for Individuals (Under Adjudication)' page on voters.eci.gov.in answered electors facing an appeal against inclusion with the error 'Something went wrong'. Since Thursday, 19 November, the page answers them that the mobile number was not provided while filing the appeal. The paper reports from an analysis by the Civic Research Group, which it describes as a research collective based in Kolkata, that appeals against inclusion mostly carry 17-digit IDs, and appeals against exclusion carry 20-digit IDs. The 17-digit appeals return the error. The 20-digit ones need a second OTP, sent to the mobile number the appellant gave when filing, which is separate from the OTP for logging in to the account. The paper spoke to at least 10 electors across the state who described the same problem. All had been included in the adjudication supplementary lists, and all say the appeals against them could not be traced on the portal after 18 September. It reviewed a screen recording made after 18 September in which a known appeal against an elector's inclusion could not be retrieved, and a screenshot from before that date which showed the same appeal, filed on 5 April, as pending. The paper reports from the Commission's affidavit to the Supreme Court that the 16 lakh appeals against inclusion were filed by officers of the Chief Electoral Officer's office, and the electors the paper spoke to are among them.
items.quote: From then until November 18, the “Track Appeal for Individuals (Under Adjudication)” page on voters.eci.gov.in returned a “Something went wrong” error for voters facing an appeal against their inclusion, according to screen recordings by electors seen by HT.
items.response: The paper reports that there was no response from the Commission or the Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal. It does not say why the page changed on 18 September or on 19 November, or whether an elector facing an appeal against inclusion can see it any other way.

items.headline: Election Commission fixes website flaw exposing voters’ personal data after report flags security lapse
items.claim: A flaw in the Election Commission's website that gave access to the personal details and documents of some electors has been fixed after Reuters found it and told the Commission, Reuters reported on 27 November. By Reuters's account of a review it made over more than a month, when an elector logged in to their account and asked for a telephone call with their local electoral officer, the network tab of an ordinary browser's developer tools showed the reference number of the form the elector had submitted online to enrol or to change their details. Using those reference numbers to book the call made the same network details show the elector's name, phone number, email, date of birth and address, and the file paths of identity documents they had uploaded, such as passports. Two security researchers, Karan Saini and Ehraz Ahmed, reviewed the findings step by step on the website, and Reuters reports them saying that the reference numbers followed a predictable pattern that would let someone guess them and download data in bulk, and Saini saying that the server appeared to check only whether a user was logged in. Reuters says it shared its findings with the Commission and its three commissioners on 26 October and had no reply, that a Commission spokesman said on Thursday, 26 November, that its information technology division had been asked to look into them, and that hours later the personal details and file paths were hidden, which the two researchers confirmed. Reuters says it could not find out whether the flaw had been used, how long it had existed or how many electors could have been affected, and that the call booking feature was introduced in June 2025.
items.quote: The server only appeared to check whether a user is logged in, not whether they’re authorised to see a particular document,
items.response: A Commission spokesman told Reuters that the information technology division had been asked to look into the findings, and the Commission gave no other reply, by Reuters's account. Reuters reports that the BJP did not respond, that Pawan Khera, a spokesperson for the Congress, criticised the Commission over the findings, and that the former election commissioner Ashok Lavasa said the flaw appeared to be inadvertent. Reuters quotes the website's privacy policy as saying that no system can be guaranteed to be completely secure.

sections.title: Instructions given without a written order

items.headline: Verified: ECI’s top West Bengal officer sent orders to state officials for SIR on WhatsApp
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer sent instructions on a WhatsApp group of district magistrates that brought forward the enumeration deadline and asked officers to mark voters absent before the written deadline. The Trinamool Congress had first made the allegation before the Supreme Court.
items.quote: However, instructions issued solely on WhatsApp, advanced this date and asked officials to mark voters absent even before this deadline elapsed. ... We verified the informal instructions. Two officials showed the messages
items.response: The Collective said the Commission and the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer did not reply to its questions on the WhatsApp instructions.

items.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that district magistrates of at least three West Bengal districts wrote to the state election office asking for a written procedure for logical discrepancy cases, and that the portal accepted only the 12 listed documents.
items.quote: “Regarding logical discrepancies for mapped cases: An SOP may kindly be provided of logical discrepancy cases…and the role of BLO, ERO/AERO and DEO. Also, instruction may be provided about requisite documents to be taken at the time of hearing by ERO/AERO for such cases. It may be kindly noted that there is no provision for uploading other than 12 categories at the portal at the moment,” said the letter to the CEO.
items.response: The Collective reported that the officers received no response and carried on with their own methods.

items.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
items.claim: A registration officer told The Reporters' Collective that officers were told orally to ask unmapped electors for a second document besides Aadhaar, and that the software for a time would not accept Aadhaar alone. The Collective said it could not check this claim.
items.quote: “While this contradicts the original SIR instructions, we received no written orders. Just the software stopped allowing us (EROs) to only upload Aadhar. We were required by design to upload additional documents. The feature seemed to have disappeared now,” he said while showing us the interface. The Collective could not independently verify this claim.

items.headline: SIR: EC state poll machinery to share details of 'suspected foreigners' with authorities
items.claim: PTI reported that the Commission's written instructions of 14 May 2026 for the third phase told registration officers to refer suspected foreign nationals to the authority under the Citizenship Act.
items.quote: In a detailed set of instructions circulated on May 14 to state chief electoral officers on procedure to be followed while holding SIR, the poll authority said "... Also, electoral registration officers (EROs) will refer cases of suspected foreign nationals to the competent authority under the Citizenship Act, 1955. For these purposes, assistant EROs shall exercise ERO's powers independently..."

items.headline: EC explains new ERONET options for SIR notice disposal to EROs through demo video; no written instructions yet
items.claim: A Delhi registration officer told The Hindu that officers were first told to identify suspected foreigners during enumeration and later told in the middle of it to stop, and that many oral instructions had been taken back.
items.quote: “Since SIR was announced, we have received a lot of instructions, some written and some oral. Many have since been taken back. For instance, we were told to identify ‘suspected foreigners’ along with Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate, and then, in the middle of the enumeration phase in Delhi, we were told not to identify or report such cases.”
items.response: The Delhi CEO's office and the EC did not respond to The Hindu's queries on why the new ERONET options were introduced at that stage.

items.headline: EC explains new ERONET options for SIR notice disposal to EROs through demo video; no written instructions yet
items.claim: The Hindu reported that new ERONET options letting registration officers clear notice cases without a hearing or documents were explained only through an eight-minute video from the Commission's IT department, with no written instruction.
items.quote: Days after adding new options to its ERONET portal that allow Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to dispose of notice cases without hearings or documents, the Election Commission (EC) is now explaining the changes to officials through a demonstration video prepared by the Election Commission’s Information Technology (IT) Department, with no written documents circulated so far, sources told The Hindu.
items.response: The Delhi CEO’s office and the EC did not respond to queries on why the options were introduced at this stage.

items.headline: Maharashtra CEO Seeks Changes to Form 6
items.claim: Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer wrote to the Commission asking it to change Form 6 so that electors left off the draft in the revision can register again without declaring themselves first-time voters, Deccan Chronicle reported. The letter says officers find it hard to persuade such electors to sign a form that carries a penalty for a false declaration. It asks for the words "new voters" to be taken out of the form's title, for a separate declaration for people who were enrolled before and are no longer on any roll, and for a place to give the earlier EPIC number.
items.quote: Election officials have reported difficulties in persuading such voters to submit Form 6, as many fear that declaring themselves first-time applicants despite having been registered previously could expose them to legal action.
items.response: Officials said that any change to the statutory Form 6 would need the Central government to amend the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. No decision by the Commission was reported.

items.headline: 37% of pre-SIR Form-6 applications rejected in Telangana due to absence of declaration form
items.claim: Electoral officials in Telangana attributed the rejection of 1,92,574 of the 5,20,331 Form 6 applications for new enrolment made from 1 January to 14 June 2026, before the revision began, to the absence of the declaration form, The Hindu reported. The paper says the declaration, which asked for details of the applicant or a relative from the 2002 roll or one of 12 listed documents, was made mandatory only for the revision, and that the applications were not decided within a week as the Registration of Electors Rules require. By the figures of the Chief Electoral Officer's office, 3,22,785 of them had been accepted by 28 October and 4,972 were still to be processed. A registration officer told the paper that declaration forms are now being sent door to door through booth level officers so that the pending applications can be processed. Officials said rejected applicants will not be on the final roll unless they apply again.
items.quote: Electoral officials attributed the rejections to non-submission of declaration form along with Form-6.
items.response: The paper says the Election Commission announced recently that the declaration is not required with Form 6 in states where the revision is not on, and that this came too late for Telangana. The report carries no other reply.

items.headline: Voter ID cards, not Aadhaar, to access Panchayati Raj benefits now
items.claim: The New Indian Express reported that Rajiv Ranjan Singh, the Union Minister of Panchayati Raj, said on 30 October 2026 that a new panchayat scheme will make Aadhaar-based payments and benefits outdated, and that biometric authentication with the voter identity card number, the EPIC number, will be the only valid way to receive payments and benefits. The paper reported that he said this at a national workshop on the People's Plan Campaign 2026-27 in New Delhi. It reported that a Cabinet committee led by the Prime Minister had approved the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana, which replaces the Rashtriya Gram Swarajya Abhiyan and is to run from 2026-27 to 2030-31.
items.quote: “Going forward, the Aadhaar card will no longer serve as the basis for identifying beneficiaries. Instead, beneficiaries will need to provide biometric authentication along with their EPIC (Voter ID Number). These will serve as their identification credentials, and payments will be made based on that information.”
items.response: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj's release on the same workshop, issued through the Press Information Bureau on 31 October 2026 (Release ID 2330751), does not mention the EPIC number, Aadhaar or biometric authentication.

items.headline: Delhi SIR: Aadhaar alone not enough, BLOs asked to seek ‘citizenship proof’ from voters
items.claim: Booth level officers in several Delhi constituencies told The Hindu that registration officers were sending them back to electors who had answered a notice for no mapping with only an Aadhaar card, to collect further documents as proof of citizenship, after the officers had filed field verification reports and undertakings that the electors were eligible and had lived at their addresses for years. One officer said his registration officer called him on 2 November, after he had finished verifying all his cases, and asked him to gather proof of citizenship. Another said the instructions on documents had changed repeatedly. Officers said they had been told at a meeting on 1 October that their undertakings could be accepted where electors had none of the prescribed documents. The Hindu says it saw electors who gave only Aadhaar flagged on the system used by registration officers and their assistants, and an officer said an elector who had given a passport was also asked for documents again. Of nearly 97 lakh electors on Delhi's draft, 33.1 lakh were sent notices, 13.9 lakh for no mapping and the rest for logical discrepancies, and data the Chief Electoral Officer's office shared the week before showed more than 94% of the 33.1 lakh marked for the final roll. The time to decide notices runs to 15 December and the final roll is due on 22 December.
items.quote: I was asked to gather citizenship proof. The voters have been living there for many years, and there are many in my area who never went to school
items.response: Officials denied that any such instruction had been issued and said no identification or record of 'illegal immigrants' on the roll is being kept. A senior official said that Aadhaar alone was not sufficient, that a registration officer could still mark an elector eligible on a satisfactory field report, and that neither mapping nor logical discrepancies affect an elector's eligibility. Officials said a registration officer not satisfied with the documents could mark an elector ineligible through a speaking order recording the reasons. A registration officer said officials were first told during enumeration to identify foreign nationals on the rolls, that the direction was changed soon after, and that no such list is being prepared.

sections.title: Wrong entries reported on the rolls

items.outlet: Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, on X
items.headline: This is Revision not Treason.
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, answered on X on 21 November a post by Prashant Kanojia, who describes himself on X as a former journalist, which said that nearly 2.89 crore names, almost one in every five electors, had been left off the state's draft roll in the revision, that in 359 of 403 Assembly seats the names left off other than the dead exceeded the winning margin of 2022, and that the revision should be viewed as no less than treason. The Chief Electoral Officer wrote that the revision was the sanitation of the roll and the most important work ever done in cleaning electoral rolls, that errors may still be left in the roll after it but far fewer than before, and that his office is committed to correcting them during the summary revision now under way in the state. The image attached to Kanojia's post shows pages headed as a preliminary report of the Sabar Institute, which give the names left off as 18.7 per cent of the roll before the revision, say that only 16 in every 100 of them were left off because the electors had died, and give the count of 359 of 403 seats. The Sabar Institute posted the same figures on X on 20 November. IANS, which reported the reply the same day, gives the 18.7 per cent and the 16 per cent as the claims of the viral post. The roll held 15,44,30,092 electors before the revision and the draft roll of 6 January 2026 held 12,55,56,025, a difference of 2,88,74,067, or 18.70 for every 100 electors, and 46,23,796 of them, 16.0 per cent, were left off as dead.
items.quote: There may be errors still left in the electoral roll even after SIR but they are much less than what was the situation before SIR. We are committed to rectify even those also during current SSR in UP.
items.response: The post is the Chief Electoral Officer's own reply. It does not take up any of the figures, and no answer to it was found.

items.headline: New voters list in Indian state includes wrong photos and dead people
items.claim: The BBC reported that voters in villages near Patna told it the Bihar draft roll carried wrong photographs, duplicate entries and the name of a person who died more than five years earlier. It reported that in Danara village many residents were not sure officials had visited their homes.
items.response: In response to the BBC's questions, the Election Commission shared its 24 June order on conducting the SIR and a 27 July press note outlining efforts to ensure no eligible voter was "left behind". "Further, [the commission] does not take any responsibility of any other misinformation or unsubstantiated allegations being floated around by some vested interests," it added. The BBC also noted the commission has said BLOs worked "very responsibly".

items.headline: Declared Dead in Draft Electoral Roll, Bihar Voter Appears in Supreme Court
items.claim: The Wire reported that a voter from Ara, Bhojpur, who had been declared dead in the Bihar draft roll, appeared alive in the Supreme Court on 12 August 2025, produced by petitioner Yogendra Yadav. The voter told The Wire he had filled the enumeration form and that the BLO came to his house only after he complained.
items.response: Senior advocate Rakesh Dwivedi, for the Commission, called the production of the voter "drama". The bench of Justices Surya Kant and Joymalya Bagchi said there may have been an "inadvertent error", which could be rectified.

items.headline: How booth-level officers in Bihar are deleting voters arbitrarily
items.claim: Scroll reported that its analysis found 200 booths across 58 constituencies in 26 Bihar districts where between 324 and 641 names were left off the draft roll, 77,454 in all. It reported that most of the voters left off whom its team met in 10 of those booths had been marked absent or shifted though they had lived at their addresses for years, and that interviews with 17 BLOs showed no consistent procedure for deciding who was left off.
items.response: Parth Gupta, electoral registration officer for Purnia, acknowledged that one deleted voter should not have been asked for her parents' documents, and said, “Please provide her details and I will look into it.” Scroll also reported that Election Commission spokespersons and Bihar Chief Electoral Officer Vinod Singh Gunjiyal did not respond to requests for comment.

items.headline: ECI Skipped its Fraud-Busting Software, Flooding Bihar Voter Roll with Lakhs of Suspect Duplicates
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that a top Commission official and four Bihar EROs confirmed to it that the Commission did not run its de-duplication software during the Bihar SIR and did not give state officials access to it. It quoted the official saying the focus was on document collection. It reported that its own earlier analysis of the final roll found 14.35 lakh suspect duplicate entries.
items.response: The Collective said the Commission and Bihar's Chief Electoral Officer did not answer its emailed questions. In person, the Chief Electoral Officer told its reporter "We cannot share this information with you" and said the Supreme Court was hearing the matter.

items.headline: Ctrl+Alive+Delete: 3 living voters in Lucknow marked 'dead' in SIR draft roll, struck off list
items.claim: Three living residents of one address in the Lucknow North constituency were listed as dead in the draft roll of 6 January 2026, The Times of India reported. All three had voted on 27 October 2025 and held acknowledgements for the enumeration forms they handed to the booth officer. At their booth 41 of 1,241 voters were marked dead.
items.quote: At this particular booth, the Booth Level Officer (BLO) declared 41 out of 1,241 voters as dead.
items.response: The Times of India reported that the Chief Electoral Officer advised everyone missing from the draft to apply on Form 6 as new voters.

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: A BJP minister in the Uttar Pradesh government alleged that 9,200 bogus voters were enrolled in Varanasi South and asked for them to be checked again, BBC News Hindi reported.
items.quote: वाराणसी से यूपी सरकार में मंत्री रवींद्र जायसवाल ने आरोप लगाया है कि वाराणसी दक्षिण में 9200 फर्ज़ी मतदाता दर्ज हैं
items.response: The Varanasi District Magistrate told the media "इस मामले में बीजेपी की तरफ से शिकायत मिली है.अलग-अलग बूथों की शिकायत है. जांच के बाद उचित कार्रवाई की जाएगी."

items.headline: ‘I didn’t know my name was deleted’: Voters in Okhla on the pre-SIR ‘clean-up’
items.claim: Newslaundry reported that several voters in Delhi's Okhla constituency whose names were deleted before the SIR began said they got no notice or hearing and learnt of the deletion only when they tried to take part in the SIR. It reported that 34,644 names were deleted in Okhla during the 2026 mapping phase, against 9,170 in all of 2025.
items.response: Delhi Chief Electoral Officer Ashok Kumar said that no voter had been deleted without an inquiry and an opportunity for a hearing.

items.headline: Goa CEO says 88 of 97 voters left out after SIR have filed Form 6, applications accepted
items.claim: Goa's Chief Electoral Officer said on X that 88 of the 97 voters missing from the final roll of February 2026 had filed Form 6 and been accepted, The Pioneer reported. The cases came to light after The Indian Express reported that the Commission's software did not let verified electors be added.
items.quote: The Goa CEO's office on Thursday released the status of all 97 cases, saying 88 voters had submitted Form 6 and their applications had been accepted.

items.headline: 'Dead' on voter list, but alive: 3 Vijayapura women demand action over SIR controversy
items.claim: The Week reported that Vijayapura City MLA Basanagouda R Patil Yatnal wrote to officials on 31 August seeking the deletion of 1,054 voters, eight of whom were shown as dead on death certificates, and that three living women among them came forward on 7 October. District Electoral Officer Anandh K said no Form 7 had been filed and the certificates were found to belong to namesakes, so the inquiry was opened under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act.
items.quote: Instead, the inquiry into Yatnal's complaint was opened under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, Anandh said.
items.response: Deputy Commissioner and District Electoral Officer Anandh K said officials were still seeking legal opinion on how to proceed. No response from the MLA was reported.

items.headline: UP Chief Electoral Officer rejects media report alleging 'mysterious' 16.18 lakh voter additions
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that 16.18 lakh Form 6 applications were collected in Uttar Pradesh before the draft roll of 6 January 2026 and that their details were not published. The Chief Electoral Officer rejected the report on X, The New Indian Express reported, saying the forms were collected by booth officers during enumeration under the Commission's instructions.
items.quote: The clarification came in response to a report titled “The Mysterious 16.18 Lakh Voters Added to Uttar Pradesh’s Roll”, which questioned the collection and subsequent processing of 16.18 lakh Form-6 applications during the SIR.
items.response: The Chief Electoral Officer said "The allegations levelled in the report are not correct as these are based on faulty assumptions and are therefore categorically denied", that only Form 6s received after the draft had to go in the published list of claims, and that "There is no formula or logic for the acceptance of forms to adhere to a particular percentage."

items.headline: Final verification for 46.63L flagged voters launched
items.claim: The Hans India reported that Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer announced a door-to-door re-check of 46,62,583 names before the final roll of 16 October. They are the 44,89,512 left off the draft and the 1,73,071 found ineligible after notices, and booth officers are to help anyone left off in error file Form 6.
items.response: The paper quoted the Chief Electoral Officer, Vivek Yadav, as saying the drive will recheck the flagged cases, and that a name found deleted by mistake is to be restored through Form 6 after verification.

items.headline: "Fraud across the 403 seats": Akhilesh Yadav threatens to release proof of SIR fraud
items.claim: The Samajwadi Party president said on 12 October 2026 that Uttar Pradesh's voter list holds lakhs of fake votes, with one person registered as many as ten times, and that the party had found such entries in several Assembly constituencies and would release the list, ANI reported.
items.quote: There are lakhs of fake votes in Uttar Pradesh. A single person has as many as ten votes registered. We have identified such fake votes in several assembly constituencies... we will release the list.

items.headline: Delhi SIR 2026: Over 2.3 lakh new voter registration applications received between August 31 and October 15
items.claim: ANI reported figures from Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer. Between the draft of 31 August and 15 October the office received 2,30,165 Form 6 applications to be added to the roll and 12,568 Form 7 objections, beside 2,12,400 Form 6 recorded up to 30 August and 51,471 Form 7 recorded earlier. Special camps were set at polling stations across Delhi on 18 and 25 October. Claims and objections close on 30 October, are to be decided by 30 November, and the final roll is due on 4 December 2026.

items.headline: Door-to-door BLO visits expected to include ‘left-out’ voters in Delhi SIR
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer ordered on 14 October a special drive to find eligible electors left off the draft roll. Booth officers visiting homes to collect documents from those sent notices are also to look for electors left off in their part and help those found eligible fill in Form 6. Booth officers told the paper the instruction reached them orally or on WhatsApp and that they had seen no formal order. One registration officer's message asked them to visit every elector marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate within seven days and take Form 6 from any found living at the address. The paper reported that the office also directed that Form 6 handed in on paper must not be refused and must be entered within two days.
items.response: The paper reported a statement from the Chief Electoral Officer's office that 26 lakh of the 33.1 lakh notices had been resolved.

items.headline: Congress alleges voter roll manipulation in UP's Pilibhit, seeks probe into SIR process
items.claim: The Uttar Pradesh Congress alleged at a press conference in Lucknow that in Pilibhit Sadar the names of 13,150 voters were changed between July and September, after the final roll of 10 April 2026, while their EPIC and serial numbers stayed the same, PTI reported. The party said 884 names of people still living there were deleted and 2,600 names of people who did not live there were added, and that the changes appeared to have been made in batches. It asked for an inquiry and said it would go to court. These are the Congress's allegations.
items.quote: If the same EPIC number is assigned to another person, the original voter may face an identity mismatch at the time of voting and be denied the right to vote,
items.response: The report carries no response. The next day The Wire reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, after an inquiry found that searching some EPIC numbers online showed other voters' details, had ordered the constituency's Electoral Registration Officer and Voter Registration Centre operator off roll duties and legal action against them.

items.headline: UP MLC Voter List: 'राम ने शर्मा को मारा', पिता का नाम- 'टक्कर मारना'; वोटर लिस्ट में अजीबोगरीब नाम
items.claim: Voter slips for the Legislative Council election in the Allahabad-Jhansi graduates' constituency, where polling was set for 23 October, carried Hindi phrases in place of electors' and fathers' names, and pictures of them spread on social media before the polling parties left, Dainik Jagran reported. On the instructions of the Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, the Returning Officer, Bimal Kumar Dubey, who is Divisional Commissioner of Jhansi, had the roll checked and reported clerical errors and more than 100 duplicate names. The Bharatiya Janata Party separately complained to the Chief Electoral Officer that the roll held 4,397 duplicate electors, and that electors born between 2001 and 2005 were on it whom the party called too young to qualify. The party's Prayagraj city president put 3,163 of the duplicates in Prayagraj.
items.quote: जांच में मतदाता सूची में लिपकीय त्रुटियों के साथ ही 100 से अधिक डुप्लीकेट मतदाताओं के नाम भी सामने आए हैं।
items.response: The Returning Officer said in a press note of 17 October that no elector would be denied the vote because of a clerical error, and that an elector whose identity satisfied the presiding officer or polling officer would be allowed to vote. The report says the clerical errors found in the check were marked and corrected, and that a separate list of the duplicate names was being given to the presiding officers of the polling stations concerned, with instructions to keep a special watch on those names during the poll. The Indian Express reported on 26 October that the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, replied on X to the Aam Aadmi Party's Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh, who had asked the Chief Election Commissioner why a voter slip read “Ram ne Yadav ko Maara” and whether the Commission's computer was casteist. The reply said the roll of the recent Legislative Council election also carried the entry “Ram ne Sharma ko Maara”, and the office shared a slip from the graduates' constituency election with that phrase in place of an elector's father's name. The paper quotes Rinwa as saying “Computers/software are not casteist” and “We accept that an error was made, but fortunately, even while making the error, no caste discrimination took place. Thank God that Ram did not hit a minority. Otherwise, besides being accused of casteism, we would have also faced allegations of communalism.”

items.headline: Pilibhit Voter Roll Irregularities: FIR Against Two SDMs, Computer Operator Over 10,470 Entries
items.claim: An FIR was lodged on 22 October against the two Sub-Divisional Magistrates who had served as Pilibhit's Electoral Registration Officers and a computer operator at the constituency's Voter Registration Centre, under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, The Wire reported. The Chief Electoral Officer's inquiry found that the operator had entered 13,779 Form 8 applications to change voters' details between 31 May and 29 August 2026, of which 10,470 were approved and 3,309 rejected, and that the office held no forms or records for any of them. The two officers were moved to district headquarters and the operator's services were ended. The District Election Officer was told to examine every Form 6 and Form 7 entry made by the same operator from 10 April to 21 October.
items.quote: No forms or records related to any of these entries were found available in the office,
items.response: The finding is the Chief Electoral Officer's own. Officials said the entries found irregular were being corrected, and the District Magistrate said the rolls of every constituency in the district would be cleaned up in a day or two.

items.headline: Six election officials removed in U.P. after SP flags voter list errors
items.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, took five booth level officers and a computer assistant off all roll work on 24 October and began ending their services, after an inquiry into the roll of the Azamgarh Assembly constituency (347), The Hindu reported. The Samajwadi Party had said at a press conference that one elector's name appeared ten times on that roll. The District Election Officer's report found the name 13 times in Hindi. Two of the entries had been taken up for deletion, and the other 11 belonged to 11 different people living in Azamgarh, ten of whose names and details were being corrected through Form 8. The Chief Electoral Officer ordered charge sheets and departmental proceedings against the Electoral Registration Officer of the time and two Assistant Electoral Registration Officers, with action under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and asked for a report on the rolls of every constituency in the district within a week.
items.quote: In response to the clerical lapses, the CEO directed the immediate removal of the responsible computer assistant and five BLOs from voter registration work.
items.response: The finding is the Chief Electoral Officer's own. His office said a further entry with the same name, in the Chauri Chaura constituency of Gorakhpur district, belonged to a different elector. The Indian Express quoted him saying the three officers would face action for negligence and laxity in supervision while the roll was prepared.

items.headline: SIR exercise: After Pilibhit, Azamgarh roll ‘errors’, UP CEO orders scrutiny of all Forms 6, 7, 8 filled by computer assistants
items.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, ordered on 25 October that every Form 6, Form 7 and Form 8 entered by computer assistants between the final roll of 10 April and 24 October be checked again, after the errors found in the rolls of Pilibhit and Azamgarh, The Indian Express reported. Computer assistants may no longer enter forms received on paper, which booth level officers are to digitise through the BLO App. Electoral Registration Officers are to review pending forms every day, and officials were told not to share their ERONET login IDs and passwords, were directed to study Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, which deals with breaches of official duty in preparing the roll, and were warned of strict action. The office pulled up the District Election Officers of Bulandshahr, Sitapur, Ghaziabad and Aligarh for late reports on complaints of duplicate voters circulated on social media, and directed that the draft rolls of the coming Special Summary Revision carry no duplicate entries.
items.quote: “All such forms must be digitised by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) through the BLO App,” the directive stated.
items.response: The directions are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. They followed a virtual meeting with Divisional Commissioners, District Election Officers, registration officers and computer assistants, held to prepare for the Special Summary Revision, which The Hindu dates 24 October. The Hindu reports the same directions from an official statement, says officials were warned of action under Section 32, and adds that the section provides for imprisonment of at least three months and up to two years, with a fine.

items.headline: DMs to be held accountable for voter list glitches, says UP chief electoral officer
items.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, said on 30 October that each District Election Officer would be held accountable for unnecessary pending cases, inactive users, incomplete profiles, errors in the roll or lax supervision in the district, Hindustan Times and The Hindu reported. In the official statement The Hindu prints, District Election Officers are to log in to ECINET every day, and no officer is to share a user ID, password or OTP. Both reports say the receipt and disposal of Forms 6, 6A, 7 and 8 is to be reviewed daily and that no form is to stay pending at any level. Hindustan Times reports that a call request made through the Book a Call with BLO facility is not to stay pending for more than 48 hours, and that a booth level officer who marks a request Contacted or Unavailable without contacting the elector is to face strict action. It also reports that Rinwa sought an explanation from the present District Election Officer of Pilibhit and his predecessor over a complaint that one elector's EPIC number was shown with another elector's details in the roll of Pilibhit Sadar. An inquiry there found that 13,779 erroneous forms had been entered between 31 May and 29 August 2026 and that 10,470 of them were accepted.
items.quote: If any district finds unnecessarily pending cases, inactive users, incomplete profiles, inaccurate voter lists, or lax supervision, the DEO will be held accountable, and appropriate action will be considered based on the merits of the case,
items.response: The directions and the request for an explanation are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report gives no reply from the two District Election Officers.

items.headline: Telangana SIR: Social audit tracks down 23% deleted voters in Secunderabad Cantonment constituency
items.claim: Volunteers of the Telangana Voter Rights Forum checked 174 of 721 electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate and found 40 of them, 23%, living at the same addresses, The Hindu reported from a public hearing the forum held for the electors of two polling stations in the Secunderabad Cantonment constituency. Several electors at the hearing said they had returned their enumeration forms to the booth level officer, and held copies signed by the officer, and said they were now being asked to apply on Form 6 as new voters. A soldier who had voted in 2024 was listed as absent or untraceable, and his wife said nobody had brought them the forms. A man said his and his wife's enumeration forms had gone to two different addresses while their EPIC cards carry the right one, and that he was marked permanently shifted and she untraceable. A woman was sent a notice as the sixth sibling mapped to the same parent, and her husband said she had four siblings. Most of the electors learnt that their names were left off the draft of 17 August from the forum's volunteers, who traced them house to house with an open source app the forum developed. The forum has set up a help desk to help them file Form 6 under protest.
items.quote: The volunteers checked 174 voters from the 721 marked as ASDD, and found 40 of them existing at the same addresses.
items.response: The report carries no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the registration officer. The panel at the hearing, among them the activist Shanta Sinha and the commentator Parakala Prabhakar, demanded that the revision be scrapped and the deletions rolled back.

items.headline: ECI’s Software and Rules Allow the Pilibhit Fake-Voter Playbook to Run Anywhere in India
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that it compared the Commission's data for 55 of Pilibhit's 419 booths with the final roll of 10 April 2026, matching entries by EPIC number, and found 2,691 entries in which the elector's name and the relative's name had been replaced by different names, 5.7 per cent of the electors at those booths. It said 2,372 of the changes were made in August, 656 of them on 19 August within 7.4 minutes between 6.26 pm and 6.34 pm, and that 523 were made on 31 August within 19.4 minutes. It said the Urdu roll still carried the original details where the English and Hindi rolls had been changed. It checked 15 of the cases on the ground against two government photo identity documents for each and found that the documents matched the original entries in the final roll. When it checked again eight days after the Chief Electoral Officer's finding of 22 October, 2,638 of the 2,691 changed entries were still on the roll. Two booth level officers told it that the tehsil office asked them to verify a set of Form 8 applications and then told them, before they began, that the applications had already been resolved.
items.quote: Before his admission, we had independently verified the injection of 2,691 fake voters in just 55 booths of Pilibhit. Eight days after the Uttar Pradesh (UP) CEO acknowledged the fraud, we rechecked and found that 2,638 of these fake voters were still on the Pilibhit voter roll.
items.response: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer and that neither had replied by publication. The Chief Electoral Officer's press note of 22 October, which the report links, said the computer assistant at the constituency's voter registration centre had entered 13,779 Form 8 applications between 31 May and 29 August 2026, 4,717 of them up to 16 July and 9,062 from 17 July, that no form or record of any of them was found in the office, and that 10,470 were approved and 3,309 rejected. It ordered legal action against the operator and the two registration officers who served in those periods, departmental proceedings against both officers and the end of the operator's services, and said the wrong entries were being corrected under the rules. The report says a computer operator and two registration officers were suspended, which the press note does not say.

items.headline: Computer assistants in U.P. ERO offices to lose ECINET login IDs after Pilibhit misuse claims
items.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, directed on 31 October that the login IDs of all computer assistants working on the ECINET portal in the offices of Electoral Registration Officers across the state be deactivated at once, after complaints and information from Pilibhit district about the misuse of those IDs, The Hindu reported from an official statement. The computer assistants work as operators of the voter registration centres. The report puts their number at about 806, two in each Assembly constituency. Registration officers were asked to report compliance at the earliest, and the firm concerned was directed to end at once the services of the outsourced computer assistant involved in the case of the Pilibhit constituency (127).
items.quote: “The concerned firm has been directed to immediately terminate the service of the involved outsourced computer assistant in the case of Assembly Constituency 127-Pilibhit,” the statement said.
items.response: The directions are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. His office's press note of 31 October, posted on X, addresses them to the District Election Officers. They are to have the login ID of every voter registration centre operator in every constituency disabled, so that no operator can do any work on the ECINET portal through it, obtain confirmation from each registration officer, check the action themselves and send a compliance report at once. The report gives no response from the firm or from the operator.

items.headline: EC Orders Suspension of Two Election Officers in UP Following Pilibhit Revelations
items.claim: The Election Commission directed in a letter of 31 October to the Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh that two Electoral Registration Officers of the Pilibhit constituency, Mayank Goswami and Hemant Chaudhary, be placed under suspension at once, The Wire reported. Their chargesheets are to be sent to the Commission for vetting, and they cannot be reinstated without its prior approval. The Commission directed that Section 198 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which the report describes as a public servant disobeying the law with intent to cause injury, be added to the existing FIR against the two officers and a voter registration centre computer operator, and that the cases be pursued in court. It asked for the Pilibhit District Election Officer's report on the rolls of all four constituencies in the district within a week, and for a report within three days on the action taken against the computer operator and five Assistant Electoral Registration Officers of the Pilibhit seat. The FIR of 22 October followed an inquiry that found 13,779 Form 8 applications entered between 31 May and 29 August, 10,470 of them approved, with no application forms or documents for them in the office.
items.quote: The EC on Saturday (October 31) directed in a letter to the chief electoral officer (CEO) of Uttar Pradesh that EROs Mayank Goswami and Hemant Chaudhary be placed under immediate suspension.
items.response: The directions are the Commission's own. The report gives no reply from the two officers. PTI, in a report carried by ThePrint, gives the same suspension, the vetting of the chargesheets, the bar on reinstatement and the addition of Section 198.

items.headline: Gems of Karnataka SIR! BUY 2, GET 5 OFFER VOTER IDs!
items.claim: Mohammed Zubair, co-founder of Alt News, posted on X on 1 November that an elector in the Mahadevapura constituency (174), whose name was missing from the draft roll and who submitted Form 6 twice, now has five different EPIC numbers. The graphic with his post shows five records styled as Voter Helpline cards with the same name, age, gender, parent's name, Assembly constituency and Lok Sabha constituency, Bangalore Central, each with a different EPIC number, part of which is blacked out.
