He wrote that he suspected a closer look across Karnataka could find thousands of similar cases. In a reply to the same post he said that an elector in the Bangalore South constituency, in the Bangalore Rural Lok Sabha seat, submitted Form 6 four times on one day and now has four EPIC numbers, and the graphic with that post shows four such records and a Form 9 list of four applications in one name received on 5 September 2026. Both cases rest on the posts alone. No news outlet had reported either of them, and no official had answered them, by 2 November. On 4 November The Hindu reported an elector of the same first name and age with five EPIC numbers in Mahadevapura (soft-55). On 7 November the Chief Electoral Officer's office said, answering The Hindu's report, that more than one EPIC number had been generated for one person where an applicant filed more than one Form 6 through the Citizen Service Portal (soft-58).
items.quote: One person applied twice. The EC issued him five voter IDs.
items.response: No reply from the Chief Electoral Officer of Karnataka or the Election Commission was found by 2 November. In a similar case Zubair posted from Uttar Pradesh on 17 October, the Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh replied on X that the elector had submitted four applications and that the post's count of two was false, called the issue of several EPIC numbers from several forms a long-standing one, and said deduplication was done through ECINET from time to time, The Wire reported on 20 October.

items.case: Reference of electors to judicial officers in West Bengal's revision under the Supreme Court's orders (court-57, soft-42)
items.headline: How Over 50 Lakh Cleared West Bengal Voters Ended Up Under Judicial Review In SIR
items.claim: The Election Commission's statewide Notice and Hearing Report dated 22 February, seen by The Wire, records that when the deadline for deciding hearing cases passed on 21 February, West Bengal's Electoral Registration Officers and their assistants had cleared 1,31,45,109 of 1,51,92,634 cases for the final roll, 86.5%, found 11,58,636 ineligible, 7.6%, and left 8,88,889 undecided, 5.9%, The Wire reported. The final roll of 28 February placed 60,06,675 electors under adjudication, and The Wire says at least 51 lakh of them had already been decided by a registration officer. In the report the Electoral Roll Micro Observers marked 31,43,868 cases 'documents need to be reviewed' and the roll observers marked 40,28,055, some of them the same cases. Where the registration officers acted on these flags they disagreed with the observers in 35,92,292 cases and agreed in 2,02,926. Across the 24 districts The Wire finds that the number placed under adjudication rises and falls with the observers' flags, with a correlation of 0.95, and that the observers' flags bear little relation to the number of cases the registration officers left undecided, with a correlation of 0.26. In Malda 8,730 cases were left undecided and 8,28,127 electors were placed under adjudication, and in Murshidabad the figures were 12,194 and 11,01,145. In Uttar Dinajpur 4,80,341 were placed under adjudication against 2,75,074 observer flags.
items.quote: The commission’s own deadline report shows that EROs had left only about 8.9 lakh cases undecided, against 60 lakh sent to judges.
items.response: The Wire quotes the Chief Electoral Officer's office as saying on 1 March that names were marked under adjudication 'since the concerned EROs/AEROs did not decide them after hearing'. Subrata Gupta, the Commission's special roll observer, told it that the Commission had told observers that about 90 lakh of about 1.5 crore cases heard had been disposed of and 60 lakh were pending. The Wire says it has sent the Chief Electoral Officer queries on who decided to send cases the registration officers had already decided to the judges, and that it will update the report on a reply.

items.headline: Bengaluru's electoral rolls: 'Husband Husband' to '????' and 'XXX'
items.claim: The Hindu found errors in at least 1,000 entries of Bengaluru's final electoral rolls. In part 324 of the Dasarahalli constituency, which has 425 electors, the names of electors and their relatives at seven runs of consecutive serial numbers, 4 to 7, 143 to 150, 152 to 157, 300 to 302, 306 to 313, 327 to 330 and 336 to 340, appear as strings of unfamiliar characters. Elsewhere the relative's name is blank, a single letter, 'NA' or 'None', or the relationship itself, such as 'Husband Husband' in part 7 of Dasarahalli and 'Wife' in Chamarajpet. Some relatives' names in Mahadevapura are a single letter. In part 332 of Yelahanka a relative's name is an email address, in BBMP South district a relative's name runs into a string of letters and numbers, one elector's name runs into a date, and another elector's name appears as '??????K'. Most of the electors the paper spoke to whose entries were wrong said they had given correct details, and some said they saw that their details were wrong only when they traced their entries by house number.
items.quote: The Hindu found discrepancies in at least 1,000 entries here alone.
items.response: Assistant Electoral Registration Officers and BLO supervisors the paper contacted said they were unaware of the cases and would look into them. A polling official put the problem down to an error in transliteration when a file was converted from a font the computer did not recognise. At least three booth level officers said the software had kept showing such glitches, that they had told their supervisors and had been told the system would fix them after the final upload, and that they had asked the few electors who approached them after the final rolls to file Form 8.

items.headline: Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer directs DEOs to re-examine all rejected Form 6 applications
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, directed all District Election Officers on 2 November to re-examine every rejected Form 6 application so that eligible people are included in the roll, and said electors missing from the roll should be added by matching the rolls of panchayats with those of Assembly constituencies, Hindustan Times reported. He spoke at a meeting in Meerut at which he and the Commission's Senior Deputy Election Commissioner, Maneesh Garg, reviewed preparations for the 2027 Assembly election in 18 districts of the Meerut, Saharanpur, Moradabad and Aligarh divisions. He repeated the direction to re-examine every Form 6, 7 and 8 entered by computer assistants since the revision ended on 10 April (up-24), asked officers to see that applicants enter their mobile number and full address correctly on Form 6, and asked that operators of public convenience centres be trained in the online Form 6 and prevent multiple entries. Garg asked officers to verify the electors on the lists of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors and to pay attention to enrolling young voters and women.
items.quote: Missing voters should be included in the voter list by matching the electoral rolls of panchayat and assembly constituencies, he said at a meeting in Meerut on Monday.
items.response: The directions are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report gives no count of rejected Form 6 applications in the state and does not say how the panchayat rolls are to be matched.

items.headline: Telangana SIR: Address change applications at odds with enumeration forms ending up in deletion of voters
items.claim: Electors in Hyderabad who had applied on Form 8 to change their address, some of them before the revision began in Telangana, and who did not return enumeration forms because they expected the Form 8 to be processed, were left off the draft roll as absent, untraceable or permanently shifted, and their Form 8 applications are now being rejected as claims and objections are decided, The Hindu reported. An elector from the Secunderabad Cantonment constituency told a public hearing of the Voter Rights Forum at Lalbazar that his family's names were left off with the remark 'untraceable'. An elector in Khairatabad said the booth level officer told her to file Form 8 before her enumeration form, that she filed it online on 12 July, and that it was rejected recently with no reason given. The paper reports that these electors were not given notice before their names were left off, and that in other cases names were left off even after a Form 8 had been processed, because officials had not removed the elector's entry at the old address. By 2 November Telangana had received 11,63,294 Form 8 applications, for address changes and other corrections, and had accepted 9,19,275 and rejected 1,64,865. Of the 6,09,466 received from 1 January to 14 June, before the revision, 5,19,317 were accepted, 86,550 rejected and about 3,559 are pending.
items.quote: Electors who did not submit enumeration forms thinking that it did not apply to them due to their address change applications, have all been summarily deleted from the draft electoral rolls under Absent/Untraceable/Permanently Shifted categories.
items.response: The report carries no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or a registration officer. It says Form 8 claims are to be processed within two weeks and that many were not, because booth level officers were taken up with enumeration.

items.headline: Voters marked absent despite signed forms: Forum; seeks SIR rollback
items.claim: The Telangana Voter Rights Forum told a press conference in Hyderabad on 3 November that electors who said they had returned enumeration forms signed by the booth level officer were left off the draft roll as absent or untraceable, The Times of India reported. A. Suneetha, who presented the forum's findings, said its volunteers surveyed 757 electors, about 42% of those in polling stations 150 and 151 of the Secunderabad Cantonment constituency. Of these, 232 were on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors, and the forum counts 43 of them as wrongly left off. Another 383 had been sent notices. The forum gave the official figures for the two polling stations as 1,829 electors on the 2025 roll, 721 left off the draft and 960 sent notices. In Musheerabad the forum counts 42 of the 95 electors it surveyed on that list as wrongly left off. Electors at the press conference said they had been left off though they held enumeration forms signed by the booth level officer or had lived at the same address for years, and refused to file Form 6 as new voters. Maria Tabassum, a member of the jury at the forum's public hearings, spoke of the difficulty married women have in linking themselves to their parents. Kiran Vissa of the forum said the faults it found lay in the design of the process, asked the Chief Electoral Officer to address them, and asked that the rolls for Hyderabad's coming municipal elections be prepared from the 2025 rolls. The forum asked for the revision to be withdrawn.
items.quote: Voters holding enumeration forms signed by booth-level officers were marked absent or untraceable during the special intensive revision (SIR), Telangana Voter Rights Forum alleged on Tuesday, citing surveys that identified 43 wrongful deletions in two booths in Secunderabad Cantonment and 42 in Musheerabad assembly constituencies.
items.response: The report says the forum's release contained no response from the election authorities. It carries no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or a registration officer.

items.headline: Telangana SIR: ‘Not one illegal immigrant found on Hyderabad district’s electoral rolls’
items.claim: Hyderabad's District Election Officer, R.V. Karnan, who is also Commissioner of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation, said the revision had found no illegal immigrant on the rolls of the district's 15 Assembly constituencies, The Hindu reported. He said only a few Nepali citizens had been found on the rolls and that their names had been deleted. He put them at 10 to 12 in the Sanathnagar constituency, and the paper says the exact number was not yet available. He said they could not be called illegal immigrants because they had entered the country by a legal route, and that their names were deleted because they are not citizens and hold their vote in Nepal. The paper reports that he denied that Bangladeshi nationals or Rohingya were on the district's rolls.
items.quote: District Election Officer and Commissioner of Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) R.V. Karnan has confirmed this, and said only a few Nepali citizens were found on the rolls, and they stand deleted.
items.response: The New Indian Express reported the same day, from unnamed sources, that twelve electors in Sanathnagar were found to be Nepali nationals and deleted, and that officials were examining suspected registrations of Rohingya in the neighbouring Rangareddy district. It reported Karnan as warning that officials would face action for wrongly deleting the names of eligible electors through negligence.

items.headline: Jharkhand government employee suspended for ‘taking bribe’ to correct errors in voters’ SIR documents
items.claim: An assistant administrative officer in Hazaribag district was suspended after a video shared on social media appeared to show him accepting Rs 100 for verifying a voter identity card and correcting errors in an affidavit during the revision, PTI reported on 4 November. The suspension order of Hazaribag's Deputy Commissioner and District Election Officer says the Barhi Sub-Divisional Officer reported the video and that the allegation is prima facie established and contrary to the Government Servants' Conduct Rules, 1976. The officer's headquarters while he is suspended is the Chalkusha block office.
items.quote: The administrative officer has been suspended, and the Chalkusha Block Office in Hazaribag is fixed as his headquarters,
items.response: The report gives no statement from the officer and does not say who made the video or when.

items.place: Bengaluru, Mahadevapura, Dasarahalli, Sarvagnanagar and Hebbal
items.headline: In Karnataka seat where ‘vote chori’ claims first surfaced, over 800 voter IDs linked to 397 names after SIR
items.claim: The Hindu found in the final roll of the Mahadevapura constituency in Bengaluru, published after the revision, 803 EPIC numbers linked to 397 people. It counted more than 500 cases in which one person held two or more EPIC numbers within a polling station and 300 more in which one person held several across polling stations of the constituency. It found seven people with more than three EPIC numbers each, among them an elector of 63 entered five times, three times in one part and once each in two others, with the same age, address and relatives' names in every entry. The graphic Mohammed Zubair posted on X on 1 November (soft-49) shows the same first name, age and five EPIC numbers in Mahadevapura. The Hindu found at least seven EPIC numbers that each appear against two entries in different constituencies, 14 entries in all, three between Mahadevapura and Dasarahalli, three between Mahadevapura and Sarvagnanagar and one between Mahadevapura and Hebbal. In another case an elector left off the draft as permanently shifted applied on Form 6 on 14 August and again on 18 September, according to the Form 9 report, and now appears twice in the final roll, both times at the address from which she had been marked as shifted. The paper notes that Mahadevapura is the constituency over which Rahul Gandhi alleged that more than one lakh votes were fake or stolen in the 2024 Lok Sabha election in Bengaluru Central.
items.quote: The Hindu found that after the SIR exercise, Karnataka’s Mahadevapura Assembly constituency alone had 803 voter IDs linked to just 397 people.
items.response: The office of the Chief Electoral Officer said it had received no formal complaints about duplicate entries, that it was watching complaints raised on social media and by political parties, and that the cases would be verified. On 7 November the office explained the cases in a press note and referred them to the district and registration officers for verification (soft-58).

items.headline: U.P. to match Assembly voter lists with Panchayat and Urban local body rolls to find missing voters
items.claim: The office of Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer said in a statement on 4 November that the roll of every Assembly constituency in the state is to be matched with the electoral rolls of the panchayats and urban local bodies to find eligible people missing from the roll in the special summary revision, The Hindu reported. Guidelines were sent to every District Election Officer. Electoral Registration Officers are to have Form 6 filled for each eligible person found who is on no Assembly constituency's roll anywhere in India. District Election Officers are also to use the fair price shops run by the Food and Civil Supplies Department, and people aged 18 or more who are registered at a fair price shop in the district and are not on the roll are to be added if found eligible. Electoral Literacy Clubs in schools and colleges are to be activated for young voters, and the NSS, the NCC, Nehru Yuva Kendra, Yuvak Mangal Dal and the Bharat Scouts and Guides are to be brought in. Aaj Tak reported the Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, as saying that the roll holds unusually few women against men, and that ASHA, ANM and anganwadi workers and the women's self-help groups would help find eligible women missing from it and have them fill Form 6.
items.quote: Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh has directed that voter lists of all Assembly constituencies of the State be matched with Panchayat and Urban Body electoral rolls in order to find eligible citizens missing from the rolls during the Special Summary Revision of Voter Lists 2027.
items.response: The directions are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report does not say how the rolls are to be matched or how many electors the matching has found.

items.headline: UP has 1.21cr fewer women voters than men, CEO orders special enrolment drive
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, directed District Election Officers on 4 November to hold a special drive to find and enrol eligible women before the 2027 Assembly election, because the state's rolls hold 1.21 crore fewer women than men, The Times of India reported. By the Commission's data for 7 October 2026 as the paper gives it, the rolls held 13.47 crore electors, of whom 7.34 crore were men, 6.13 crore women and 4,082 third gender electors. The paper puts the gap among women at about 1.71 crore against a projected adult female population of 7.84 crore, and the gap among men at about 99 lakh against a projected adult male population of 8.33 crore. It puts the projected adult population at 16.17 crore, a gap of nearly 2.70 crore from the roll, and says the difference does not necessarily represent eligible people who are not registered. Against a projected 84.47 lakh people aged 18 or 19, 19.62 lakh were registered on 7 October. ASHA workers, auxiliary nurse midwives, anganwadi workers and women of self-help groups are to find eligible women who are not on the roll and help them apply on Form 6 in the special summary revision.
items.quote: According to Election Commission data as of Oct 7, 2026, UP had 13.47 crore registered voters, comprising 7.34 crore men, 6.13 crore women and 4,082 third-gender electors.
items.response: The direction is the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report does not say where the projected adult population comes from or how many women the drive is expected to enrol.

items.headline: UP sees 3,786 fewer polling stations after ECI approval
items.claim: The number of polling stations in Uttar Pradesh fell by 3,786, from 1,77,516 to 1,73,730, after the Election Commission approved the District Election Officers' proposals for all 403 Assembly constituencies in an exercise carried out on 4 November at the norm of 1,200 electors to a polling station, Hindustan Times reported. The summary revision's draft roll is to be published at the 1,73,730 polling stations. The Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, said the allocation began on 16 October. He directed District Election Officers to place booth level officers at the approved polling stations and to tell every elector whose polling station has changed in writing through the booth level officer. He also directed that all members of a family be entered in the same section of the roll, and that an elector found at a different polling station from the rest of the family after the draft be corrected on Form 8. The list of approved polling stations is to be given to the representatives of recognised political parties.
items.quote: Uttar Pradesh has witnessed a reduction of 3,786 polling stations, from 1,77,516 to 1,73,730, after the Election Commission of India (ECI) approved proposals submitted by district election officers (DEOs) for the allocation of polling stations in 403 Assembly constituencies across all 75 districts.
items.response: The figures are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report does not say how many electors were moved to a different polling station.

items.headline: UP could add over 1 crore voters through electoral roll revision
items.claim: The Times of India reported on 5 November that the rural panchayat rolls in Uttar Pradesh, finalised on 10 June 2026, hold 12.58 crore electors and the urban local body rolls, published on 2 April 2023, hold 4.33 crore, 16.91 crore in all, against 13.46 crore electors on the Assembly rolls on 7 October 2026, a difference of nearly 3.45 crore. The Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, told the paper that the Assembly rolls hold about 10.20 crore rural electors, about 2.38 crore fewer than the 12.58 crore on the panchayat rolls. The paper puts the urban electors on the Assembly rolls at about 3.36 crore, nearly 97 lakh fewer than the urban local body rolls hold. Rinwa said the panchayat rolls were revised with 1 January 2026 as the qualifying date, while the Assembly rolls also take in people who turn 18 on 1 April, 1 July and 1 October. He said the special summary revision could add more than one crore electors to the roll. He cited a district-level verification carried out after court proceedings involving the two election authorities, which found 144 eligible people missing from the Assembly roll once dead, duplicate, shifted and untraceable electors were excluded, about 7% of the entries examined. The paper says those findings led to the order to compare the Assembly rolls with the panchayat and urban local body rolls across the state (up-32). By the paper's figures the Assembly rolls held 15.4 crore electors before the Special Intensive Revision and 13.39 crore when it ended on 10 April 2026.
items.quote: There is a clear difference between the two lists. This is despite the fact that assembly electoral rolls have four qualifying dates, whereas panchayat rolls have only one.
items.response: Rinwa told the paper that the comparison is not exact, because the municipal rolls were last revised in 2023 and the Assembly rolls are current, and that the differences cannot be taken as eligible people who are not registered, because the rolls may hold dead electors, people who have moved, duplicate entries and other ineligible names. The rural and urban figures as reported, 10.20 and 3.36 crore, make 13.56 crore, 10 lakh more than the 13.46 crore total, and the paper does not explain the difference. The Free Press Journal reports that the State Election Commission prepares the panchayat rolls and the Election Commission of India the Assembly and Lok Sabha rolls, and puts the difference between the panchayat rolls and the rural electors on the Assembly rolls at nearly 2.4 crore.

items.headline: 4.5 lakh names off draft roll, Gurgaon electorate shrunk by 30%
items.claim: Nearly 4.5 lakh names were left off Gurgaon's draft roll, which fell from 15.6 lakh electors before the revision to 11 lakh in the draft of 31 July, a fall of 29%, while the city received 40,563 Form 6 applications between 1 June and 30 September, The Times of India reported. The paper says the figures suggest fewer than one application for every 11 names left off, and says the two are not directly comparable, because Form 6 applications include first-time voters. Haryana's Chief Electoral Officer, A. Sreenivas, asked District Election Officers to publicise widely the Commission's clarification of 3 November that an elector missing from the draft roll can apply on Form 6 whatever the earlier enrolment. The paper also reports that hearings had found 12,754 electors ineligible by 28 October and that their names are likely to be deleted from the final roll, due on 30 November, and it does not say whether that figure is the city's or the state's.
items.quote: The city received just 40,563 Form 6 applications seeking inclusion between June 1 and Sept 30.
items.response: The figures for the city are the paper's and are not attributed to an official. The report does not give the 4.5 lakh by reason.

items.headline: Karnataka chief electoral office admits multiple voter IDs generated for same person during SIR
items.claim: The office of Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer said in a press note of 7 November that The Hindu's report of 803 voter ID numbers linked to 397 people in Mahadevapura after the revision (soft-55) reflected two situations that arose in processing applications. Some applicants filed more than one Form 6 through the Citizen Service Portal during the revision, and because each application was processed separately, more than one EPIC number was generated for the same person. In other cases a Form 8 to shift residence was approved and the elector was added to the roll of the new constituency, while the Form 7 to delete the entry in the old constituency stayed pending, because roll operations were frozen by law for the final publication. The office said the cases had been referred to the District Election Officers, Additional District Election Officers and Electoral Registration Officers for verification and remedial action under the law. Mohammed Zubair's post of 1 November described an elector in Mahadevapura who submitted Form 6 twice and now has five EPIC numbers (soft-49). The press note does not mention the post.
items.quote: The Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer on Saturday admitted that multiple Elector Photo Identity Card numbers were inadvertently generated for the same person during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls due to “procedural circumstances during data processing”.
items.response: The note is the Chief Electoral Officer's own reply. Vartha Bharati reports that it gives no count of the electors affected or of the entries marked for deletion, no date for the corrections, and does not say whether the final rolls are affected. Karnataka's final roll was published on 27 October.

items.headline: Nearly 2 lakh Voters Declared Dead by ECI are Confirmed Alive for Panchayat Elections
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported on 7 November that 1,82,440 electors whom the Election Commission marked dead and left off the draft roll in Rajasthan's Special Intensive Revision are on the State Election Commission's panchayat roll as living electors. The Collective compared the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors, on which about 8.75 lakh people were marked dead, with the panchayat roll by each elector's voter ID and EPIC number, and checked a sample against the State Election Commission's own search portal. The two rolls were revised in parallel. The Commission finished its revision on 21 February 2026 and the State Election Commission finished its own four days later, and the panchayat draft roll was published after the Commission had published its list. By the Collective's chart of ten constituencies, the most such electors were in Garhi (4,889), Sirohi (4,624), Banswara (4,549) and Ghatol (4,429). The Collective says it did not verify on the ground which of the two commissions is right. It downloaded both rolls in October, when polling for the panchayats had begun in four phases. It says it could not check the Commission's monthly updates to the roll since the revision, because the Commission does not say whether an elector once marked dead and later restored keeps the same voter ID. Two booth level officers it spoke to denied the discrepancy, and the Collective says its analysis shows they were wrong.
items.quote: We found 1,82,440 citizens who were marked dead after the ECI’s SIR were alive on the Panchayat's electoral roll.
items.response: The Collective says it sent detailed questions to the Commission and to Rajasthan's State Election Commission and had no answer. The report does not say how many of the 1,82,440 are eligible electors, or whether any of them have been added back to the Commission's roll since the final roll. Amar Ujala reported on 8 November that the State Election Commission used the Commission's roll from before the revision as the base roll for the local body and panchayat elections (soft-57).

items.headline: राजस्थान में वोटर लिस्ट का बड़ा अंतर: एसआईआर के बाद 30 लाख नाम कम, निकाय चुनाव में पुरानी सूची से हुआ मतदान
items.claim: Amar Ujala reported on 8 November that the roll Rajasthan's State Election Commission used for the local body elections holds about 5.45 crore electors, against about 5.15 crore on the Election Commission's final roll after the Special Intensive Revision, a difference of about 30 lakh. The social activist Nikhil Dey told the paper that the Commission's roll held about 5.47 crore electors in Rajasthan before the revision and about 5.15 crore after it, about 32 lakh fewer. He said the State Election Commission has the right to prepare its own roll for its elections and had always taken the latest roll from the election department, but took the roll from before the revision for the urban local body and panchayat elections, a roll on which the revision found about 1.80 lakh electors dead. He said the State Election Commission told his group that its election process had begun well before, and did not agree to an audit his group asked for, and that the group is seeking the information under the RTI Act. He asked how one booth level officer could mark an elector dead on one roll while the name stayed on the other, and asked for the difference to be looked into. The Reporters' Collective reported a day earlier that 1,82,440 electors the Commission marked dead are on the State Election Commission's panchayat roll as living electors, on a roll it describes as revised in parallel with the Commission's (soft-59).
items.quote: राज्य निर्वाचन आयोग की रिपोर्ट में बताया कि स्थानीय निकाय चुनाव की तैयारियां काफी पहले शुरू हो गई थीं। इसी वजह से निर्वाचन आयोग की SIR से पहले वाली मतदाता सूची को आधार सूची के रूप में इस्तेमाल किया गया।
items.response: The State Election Commission's report, as the paper gives it, says the preparations for the local body elections began well before, and the Commission's roll from before the revision was used as the base roll for that reason. The Chief Electoral Officer, Naveen Mahajan, said the State Election Commission relied on the roll from before the revision, and that no objection had been raised about the final roll of the revision in Rajasthan. The report does not say how many of the 30 lakh are on the local body roll and not on the final roll, or how many of them are eligible.

items.headline: 1.27 crore Hindu voters missing from UP rolls … have appealed to EC: Yogi Adityanath
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Minister, Yogi Adityanath, said at the Aaj Tak Panchayat programme in Ayodhya on 8 November that about 1.27 crore Hindu voters whose names are on the electoral rolls of the state's panchayat elections are missing from the Election Commission's rolls after the revision, and that the number of Muslim voters in the state rose by 1.65% after it, The Indian Express reported. In his words as the paper gives them, 66 lakh such voters are on the panchayat rolls, 55 lakh are Hindu voters who receive the benefits of government welfare schemes and are missing from the rolls, and 4.5 lakh are aged 18 or 19 and are missing from the rolls. He said a memorandum had been given to the Commission asking why this happened, and he appealed for these names to be included. Asked in the interview where the figure came from, he said that the rolls from before and after the revision are with everyone, in Aaj Tak's video of the interview. ThePrint reports him saying that about 46 lakh dead electors were on the rolls before the revision, and India Today and Aaj Tak report him saying that the names of about 46 lakh dead electors should be removed and the names of eligible voters should also be included.
items.quote: I am speaking about those 1.27 crore Hindu voters who have their names in the electoral list of UP panchayat polls, but their names do not exist in the electoral rolls of the Election Commission of India.
items.response: The Samajwadi Party president, Akhilesh Yadav, asked reporters how the Chief Minister had figures of electors by religion when the Commission had released none, ThePrint reported. In a post on X on 9 November he asked that Aadhaar be linked with voting, that metal cards be issued in place of paper or plastic voter cards, and that fingerprints or iris scans be used to identify voters, and he said the BJP would then be unable to have bogus votes cast. The party's spokesperson, Udaiveer Singh, asked the Chief Minister to explain how he got the data and to demand action against the Chief Election Commissioner and the state's Chief Electoral Officer, The Indian Express reported. The Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, said he would answer all questions on the revision on 17 November, after the draft roll of the special summary revision is published. No reply from the Commission was reported.

items.headline: Ghaziabad to use Census to spot deleted SIR voters, bring them back on roll
items.claim: The Ghaziabad district administration will use the Census 2027 enumeration to find residents aged 18 or more who are not on the electoral roll and put them in touch with booth level officers to enrol, The Times of India reported. The decision was taken on 9 November at a meeting chaired by the District Magistrate and District Election Officer, Ravindra Kumar Mandar, to review preparations for the Census and the special summary revision. The paper reports that 5.7 lakh names (20.2%) went off Ghaziabad's roll in the revision, and 3.16 lakh in the Sahibabad constituency, which it says is the highest of any constituency in the state. It gives the Census self-enumeration as running from 16 to 30 November and the house-to-house enumeration from 1 December to 4 January. The meeting also reviewed the polling stations, and by the list the Commission approved the district, with the part of the Dhaulana constituency that falls in it, will have 865 polling centres and 3,073 polling stations.
items.quote: A decision to link the Census exercise with identifying eligible voters for inclusion in the electoral rolls was taken at a meeting chaired by district magistrate Ravindra Kumar Mandar, who is also the district election officer, on Monday to review preparations for Census 2027 and the SSR exercise.
items.response: The decision is the District Election Officer's own. The report does not say how the names found in the Census are to reach the booth level officers.

items.headline: BJD questions SIR credibility over alleged dual voter IDs in villages bordering Odisha, Andhra Pradesh
items.claim: The Biju Janata Dal alleged at a press conference on 11 November that residents of villages on the border of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh still held voter identity cards issued by both states after Odisha's revision, and asked how residents of Kotia in Koraput district and Jumdang village in Malkangiri district could remain registered in two states, Hindustan Times reported. The party's senior leader Devi Prasad Mishra said the law does not allow a person to be registered in two places, and asked that Odisha's Chief Electoral Officer seek from the Andhra Pradesh government the number of Odisha residents who had voted in that state's elections. He also asked why Andhra Pradesh had not removed from its rolls duplicate electors and electors the party alleges are ineligible. The Koraput Collector, Manoj Satyawan Mahajan, said some residents of Kotia had crossed into Andhra Pradesh to vote in its panchayat elections the week before, and that about 10% of Kotia's voters had voted there. He said the 40% turnout that Andhra Pradesh officials gave was the combined turnout at a polling booth serving several villages, some of them in Andhra Pradesh, and that the district administration had prevented Andhra Pradesh from setting up a polling booth inside Kotia. Odisha's Law Minister, Prithiviraj Harichandan, said the state government would look into the matter and that the Revenue Department needs to identify people holding voter identity cards from both states and take legal action against them.
items.quote: Raising the issue at a press conference, senior BJD leaders Devi Prasad Mishra and Bijay Nayak questioned how residents of Kotia in Koraput district and Jumdang village in Malkangiri district could remain registered as voters in two states despite the completion of the SIR exercise.
items.response: The report gives no reply from Odisha's Chief Electoral Officer, from Andhra Pradesh's or from the Commission, and no count of electors registered in both states. The Collector's 10% is the share of Kotia's voters he says voted in Andhra Pradesh, and the report does not say how many of them are on Odisha's roll.

items.headline: यूपी: वोटर लिस्ट से 3.38 करोड़ नाम गायब, पंचायत-निकाय की लिस्ट से खुलासा; हिंदू नाम ज्यादा कटे
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's panchayat rolls hold 12.58 crore electors against 10.20 crore rural electors on the Assembly rolls, 2.38 crore fewer, and the urban local body rolls hold 4.32 crore against 3.31 crore urban electors on the Assembly rolls, more than one crore fewer, Live Hindustan reported on 11 November. Together the panchayat and local body rolls hold 16.90 crore electors and the Assembly rolls 13.52 crore, and the paper reports the difference as 3.38 crore electors missing from the Assembly rolls. It reports that the Election Commission has ordered the three sets of rolls to be matched, and that the matching follows an inquiry ordered by the High Court in Makdoompur village in Rae Bareli. Makdoompur's panchayat roll held 1,987 electors, of whom 1,549 were on the Assembly roll. After the matter was taken to the High Court, 448 electors missing from the Assembly roll were examined on the Court's direction. By the paper's account the Commission found that 44 of them had been moved to a neighbouring polling station and 290 were ineligible, shifted or duplicate, and 114 were eligible electors living in the village who were on the panchayat roll and off the Assembly roll, and their names were added. The paper says Form 6 is now being filled to enrol such electors. By its figures the Assembly rolls hold 7.37 crore men and 6.15 crore women, 834 women to every 1,000 men, and 2.04 crore names of dead, shifted and absent electors were cut in the revision.
items.quote: रायबरेली के मकदूमपुर गांव में पंचायत की मतदाता सूची में कुल 1987 मतदाताओं के नाम थे और उसमें से 1549 वोटरों के नाम ही विधानसभा मतदाता सूची में थे।
items.response: The report does not name the case in the High Court or date its order, and it does not date the Commission's order to match the rolls or say how the matching is to be done. It gives no date for its count of the Assembly rolls. No reply from the Commission or the Chief Electoral Officer is reported. The Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, has said he will answer questions on the revision on 17 November (up-34).

items.headline: यूपी: पीलीभीत मतदाता सूची में गड़बड़ी का मामला, निलंबित दोनों एसडीएम की जांच करेंगी मुरादाबाद आयुक्त
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Appointment Department has named the Moradabad Divisional Commissioner, Sangeeta Singh, on the Election Commission's direction, as the officer to hold an administrative inquiry against Mayank Goswami and Hemant Kumar Chaudhary, who were Sub-Divisional Magistrates of Pilibhit at the time and were suspended on allegations of malpractice in the revision of the roll of the Pilibhit Sadar constituency, Amar Ujala reported on 12 November. She is to go to Pilibhit soon, take the records and an account of events from the officials concerned, and then examine the allegations. The department's letter on the inquiry has been sent to the Pilibhit and Moradabad administrations. The paper recalls that after complaints about the constituency's roll in October the District Election Officer, Alok Kumar, sent the Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, an inquiry report that found irregularities in the disposal of 13,779 offline forms received between 31 May and 28 August, of which 10,470 were accepted and 3,309 rejected. On that report and the Chief Electoral Officer's letter, the Commission decided on 31 October to suspend the two officers, said they could not be reinstated without its prior permission, and wrote to the Chief Secretary for action.
items.quote: भारत निर्वाचन आयोग के निर्देश पर नियुक्ति विभाग ने मुरादाबाद कमिश्नर संगीता सिंह को जांच अधिकारी नामित किया है।
items.response: The inquiry is the state government's, on the Commission's direction. The report does not date the Appointment Department's letter or set a time for the inquiry, and it carries no reply from the two officers.

items.case: Letters of the Chief Electoral Officer's office, West Bengal, to the Registrar General of the Calcutta High Court on adjudication cases that judicial officers had not decided or not e-signed (court-59)
items.headline: Election Commission Says Around 6,000 Voters in Bengal Are Still ‘Under Adjudication’. In Just 22 Seats, the Real Number is Almost 30,000
items.claim: The office of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer told the Registrar General of the Calcutta High Court in memos dated 12 October and 29 October 2026 that judicial officers had not decided 815 adjudication cases and had decided 5,004 more without e-signing them, The Wire reported on 13 November. The two figures add to 5,819, which is the 'around 6,000' of The Wire's headline. The Wire publishes the memo of 12 October, No. 9806-Home (Elec) from the Additional Chief Electoral Officer. It says the Commission's IT team wrote on 6 August that the logins of the judicial officers of the constituencies concerned had been reactivated, and it asks the Registrar General to have those officers e-sign the decided cases and decide the rest at the earliest. It refers to an earlier memo of 7 August. The Wire reports that the memo of 29 October gives the same two figures, and that the office asked district election officers the same day to report on these cases by 3 November, before the integrated draft roll of the special summary revision due on 23 November. The Wire says the Commission's ECINET report 'Individuals Under Adjudication' of 9 April, which it has seen, records 22,163 cases that judges had not decided when the judicial review ended and 83,504 that they had decided and not signed, 44,027 of them found eligible. It reports that 12,337 of the undecided cases were in Murshidabad, 5,194 in Purba Bardhaman and 3,374 in South 24 Parganas, across 67 constituencies, with 3,183 in Farakka. The Wire's own count, from the rolls of 304 polling stations in 11 of Murshidabad's 22 constituencies, is 29,347 electors still marked under adjudication, which it says is five times the number the Chief Electoral Officer's office gives for the whole state. In three polling stations of Mahadebnagar gram panchayat in Farakka, whose roll as revised up to 6 April it has seen, it counts 1,914, and booth level officers told it that the judicial review there never took place. The Wire says an elector whose case was never decided has no order to take to the appellate tribunals and was not able to vote in April.
items.quote: In memos dated October 12 and 29, the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), West Bengal, told the Calcutta high court that across the entire state of Bengal, 815 cases had still not been decided by judicial officers.
items.response: The Wire says it asked the Chief Electoral Officer on 5 November why 22,163 cases had not been decided by the time the roll was frozen, when and by whom they were decided while the judicial officers' logins were inactive, and how many of those electors were found eligible, and that it will update the report on a reply. It gives no response from the Chief Electoral Officer's office, the Election Commission or the High Court.

items.headline: Voter roll errors may cost BLOs, officials their honorarium
items.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, directed District Election Officers on Saturday, 14 November, to fix responsibility for serious errors in the roll during the special summary revision for 2027, The Times of India reported on 15 November. Booth level officers found responsible between 17 November and 16 December for errors in names, ages, gender or addresses, or for duplicate entries, may lose up to one month's honorarium, according to the number and seriousness of the errors. Their supervisors may lose up to a month's honorarium where poor supervision leaves members of one household at different polling stations or in different sections of the roll. Electoral registration officers and assistant electoral registration officers are to be assessed from 7 November, when the roll was frozen, to 4 January 2027, when the final roll is due, and serious lapses in scrutiny, supervision or the disposal of applications may bring deductions from their honorarium in proportion, for that period of nearly two months. Dainik Jagran puts the deduction for them at up to about two months' honorarium, for lapses that include the acceptance or rejection of claims and objections. Booth level officers are to scrutinise the roll of their polling stations at their desks from 17 to 20 November and correct errors in names, photographs, ages, gender and addresses through Form 8 applications from the electors concerned. The draft roll is to be published on 17 November and claims and objections taken until 16 December, with special camps at all 1,73,730 polling stations on 21, 22, 28 and 29 November, when booth level officers are to be present from 10 am to 4 pm. The Times of India reports that Rinwa also directed officials to upload the details of claims and objections to the district election websites every day and to give the roll to the recognised political parties, and that District Election Officers will recognise the people who report the most errors that are confirmed on checking. Dainik Jagran and Live Hindustan reported the same directions.
items.quote: According to the directions, BLOs found responsible for errors in names, age, gender, addresses or duplicate entries between Nov 17 and Dec 16 may face deductions of up to one month’s honorarium, depending on the number and seriousness of mistakes.
items.response: The directions are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. None of the three reports carries a reply from booth level officers, their associations or a political party, and none says who hears an officer's objection to a deduction.

items.headline: SIR: No application records for over 1.13 lakh new enrolments in Bengaluru’s final voter rolls
items.claim: An analysis by The Hindu found that at least 1,13,059 new enrolments added to the final rolls of Bengaluru's 28 Assembly constituencies after the revision could not be traced, the paper reported on 17 November. The paper's summary of the analysis says that 44% of the new enrolments in the final rolls could not be matched to Form 6 or Form 8 records, which it calls the two ways through which a voter is enrolled.
items.quote: Across Bengaluru’s 28 Assembly constituencies, at least 1,13,059 new enrolments added to the final electoral rolls after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) could not be traced, an analysis by The Hindu has found.
items.response: The report is for subscribers, and only the headline and the standfirst that The Hindu shows free are used. They carry no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer's office or the Commission, and the rest of the report is not used.

items.headline: यूपी में अब भी ढाई करोड़ से ज्यादा वोटरों का नाम गायब, एसएसआर की ड्राफ्ट मतदाता सूची जारी
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, set the draft roll of the summary revision against the state's projected adult population when he released its figures on 17 November, Live Hindustan reported. The Indian Express gives the same comparison from the Report of the Technical Group on Population Projections for India and States (2011-2036). By the population projections he cited, 16.16 crore people in the state are aged 18 or more, and the draft roll holds 13.58 crore electors, 2.58 crore fewer. Live Hindustan gives the projected adult population as 7.84 crore women and 8.32 crore men, against 6.20 crore women and 7.38 crore men on the draft, and puts the gaps at 1.64 crore women and 94.17 lakh men. Against a projected 84.47 lakh people aged 18 or 19, the draft holds 11.83 lakh, a gap of 72.63 lakh. The Chief Electoral Officer said the number aged 18 or 19 looked low because electors who were 18 or 19 at the intensive revision had since grown older, and that people who turn 18 by 1 January 2027 would be added before the final roll of 4 January 2027. The Indian Express reports him saying that the revision would give special emphasis to enrolling women and young people. Asked about the Chief Minister's claim, in The Indian Express's words, that 1.27 crore Hindu voters were excluded from the state's electoral rolls after the intensive revision (up-34), he said the Commission's database holds no details of religion or caste and so it cannot release any such data, and that the roll records only an elector's name, the type of relation named, age, date of birth, house number and gender, The Indian Express reported. The paper reports the Commission saying that no names had been deleted on the basis of religion, caste, community, village or locality, and Rinwa saying that software on the market could be used to analyse the rolls for the religion of electors and that those making the claims might have used it. Live Hindustan reports him saying that citizens of India who live in another country should apply on Form 6A in place of Form 6, because electors living abroad are not issued an elector's photo identity card and vote by showing their passport, and that whoever files Form 6 for an elector living abroad will face strict action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act.
items.quote: “Our database does not have any other details such as religion or caste. Since we don’t have any such data, how can we release that?” UP Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa said when asked about the CM’s claim.
items.response: The figures and statements are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. Neither report carries a reply from the Chief Minister or the BJP. Neither report says how many of the people the projection counts are eligible to be on the roll, or how many are on a roll elsewhere.

items.headline: UP adds 590 overseas voters since SIR, tally reaches 4,215
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, said on Wednesday, 18 November, that the number of overseas electors in the state rose from 3,625 on the final roll of 10 April to 4,215 on the draft roll of the summary revision published on 17 November, The Times of India and Hindustan Times reported. The 3,625 were 3,035 men and 590 women, and the 4,215 are 3,492 men and 723 women. The Times of India gives the rise as 590, made up of 457 men and 133 women. The Chief Electoral Officer said that during the intensive revision some family members had filled in and submitted enumeration forms on behalf of Indians living abroad, so that these people were registered as ordinary electors. The Times of India reports that they have been advised to surrender their elector's photo identity cards and apply as overseas electors on Form 6A during the claims and objections period from 17 November to 16 December, and that Rinwa warned that false declarations could bring action under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act. Dainik Jagran gives the same advice and says that registering as an ordinary elector with wrong information or a false declaration can bring legal action. He said an applicant must be an Indian citizen who has not acquired the citizenship of another country and is at least 18 years old, and is registered in the constituency of the Indian address in the passport. Applications can be made online at voters.eci.gov.in or on the ECINET app, in person or by post. Overseas electors are not issued an elector's photo identity card and vote in person at their polling station on their original Indian passport. Hindustan Times reports him saying that an applicant who already holds an elector's photo identity card as a general elector must surrender it when applying, and that an overseas elector who returns to live in India must inform the registration officer and may then apply on Form 6 as a general elector.
items.quote: The CEO said instances were detected during SIR where family members submitted enumeration forms on behalf of overseas Indians, resulting in their registration as ordinary electors.
items.response: The figures and the advice are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. None of the three reports says how many overseas Indians were registered as ordinary electors during the intensive revision, how many have since moved to Form 6A, or whether the overseas electors are counted in the draft roll's total of 13.58 crore.

items.headline: SIR: Names in ASDD list make it to final rolls with same EPIC numbers
items.claim: At least 1,635 people across Bengaluru who were listed for deletion during the revision as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate are in the final roll with the same EPIC numbers they held before it, The Hindu reported on 20 November. The paper says many of them are now listed in constituencies other than those in which they were enrolled before. The Wire, reporting The Hindu's findings, says the paper found such entries across 28 Assembly constituencies and in each of the four categories, and that the Commission's manual says an elector deleted from the roll who returns to it through Form 6 cannot keep the earlier EPIC number. The Wire says that the Commission's letter of 6 November, under which electors wrongly placed in the ASDD list in seven states are to be restored with the same EPIC numbers, does not cover Karnataka, and that the clarification of 3 November, which let electors left off the draft apply on Form 6, applied there.
items.quote: Many of them are now listed as voters in constituencies different from those in which they were originally enrolled.
items.response: The parts of The Hindu's report it shows free carry no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission, and The Wire reports none. The Wire says the Commission would have to explain whether these names were kept after election staff verified them or whether the revision failed to remove entries it had marked for deletion.

items.headline: SIR: Deleted EPIC numbers ‘reissued’ to different names in Bengaluru
items.claim: In at least 290 cases across Bengaluru, the EPIC numbers of people marked for deletion during the revision as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate have been transferred or reissued to different people in the final roll, The Hindu found, the paper reported on 20 November. It says this means that an EPIC number that identified one person before the revision now identifies someone else, and that the Commission's manual requires every elector to have a unique EPIC number.
items.quote: In hundreds of cases across Bengaluru, EPIC numbers of people marked for deletion during the SIR have been reissued to other individuals, violating the ECI manual’s requirement that every elector have a unique EPIC number
items.response: The parts of the report The Hindu shows free carry no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission.

items.headline: Panel seeks data from Yogi Adityanath on claim of 1.27 crore Hindu voters' exclusion in Uttar Pradesh
items.claim: The Independent Commission on the SIR, chaired by the former Supreme Court judge Justice Madan B. Lokur, wrote to Uttar Pradesh's Chief Minister, Yogi Adityanath, on 21 November asking him for material supporting his reported statement that about 1.27 crore Hindus from the state had been excluded from the voters' list (up-34), Deccan Herald and The Hindu reported. It asked for any supporting material, substantive data or information that may point to gaps in the methodology of the revision which could have led to the deletions. The Commission said the statement was directly relevant to its mandate of examining whether eligible electors were unfairly removed from the rolls during the revision, and that it would examine any material with complete autonomy and impartiality. Citing the elections ahead and the risk that millions of electors would be denied their votes, it asked for the material at the earliest, Deccan Herald reports. The Commission was set up as a civil society initiative by the Lawyers' Association for Constitution, and its mandate covers the constitutional and legal validity of the revision, its methodology and its impact on eligible voters and the final rolls. Its other members are the former Supreme Court judge Justice A.K. Patnaik, the former Chief Justice of the Jammu and Kashmir High Court Badar Durrez Ahmad, and the former judges Rekha Sharma of the Delhi High Court and Anjana Prakash of the Patna High Court.
items.quote: In its letter, the commission asked the chief minister to furnish any supporting material, substantive data or information that may point to gaps in the methodology which could have led to such deletions.
items.response: No reply from the Chief Minister or his office has been found. The Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, said on 17 November that the Election Commission's database holds no details of religion or caste, The Indian Express reported (up-43).

items.place: Khair; Sikandrabad; Sahibabad; Husainganj; Kairana; Sidhauli; Gorakhpur Rural
items.headline: What did UP SIR achieve? Final voter roll riddled with anomalies
items.claim: Alt News compared the draft roll of 6 January 2026 with the final roll of 10 April 2026 for 69 polling stations in 20 districts of Uttar Pradesh, covering 60,558 electors, and checked the names added against the published lists of Form 6 applications (the Form 9 lists) of 13 Assembly constituencies, in a report by Mohammed Zubair and Shinjinee Majumder published on 21 November. Alt News chose the 69 polling stations itself, and it counted two entries as the same person only where the name, the name of the father or husband, the age and the house number all matched. It reports 230 people listed at least twice in the final rolls of those polling stations, some three or four times, each entry with a separate EPIC number, and cases in which one Form 6 became two or three entries. Across the Form 9 lists of the 13 constituencies it found 3,369 people who filed Form 6 between two and 10 times. The largest cluster it found is in polling station 449 at Chachoi in Sikandrabad, Bulandshahr district, where the final roll adds 69 names and 34 of them are entries for 17 people, each listed twice with a new EPIC number. It also reports 62 new electors entered with house number 0 or with none across 37 urban polling stations, and 15 cases across 20 rural polling stations in which the name on an entry changed between the draft and the final roll while the EPIC number, the husband's name, the house number and the age stayed the same. In polling station 943 of Sahibabad it describes 298 entries of one part of the 2025 roll as deleted, 280 of them marked absent, in consecutive runs of 23, 17, 14 and 10 names. Alt News says a shared or missing house number is in itself no evidence of irregularity, since most villages have no house numbering, that the name changes could be legitimate corrections that only the Form 8 applications can explain, and that runs of deletions could mean a building or group of homes was vacated, which a house visit would establish. It says some of the errors it documented were corrected by the Commission before the report was published, and it asks how one Form 6 became several EPIC numbers and how often this happened across the state.
items.quote: We treated two entries as the same person only if the name, father’s or husband’s name, age and house number all matched.
items.response: Alt News reproduces the reply the Chief Electoral Officer's office posted on X on 17 October to Zubair's post about one of the electors in its sample, which soft-49 records. The reply said the elector had submitted four applications and that the post's count of two was false, called the issue of several EPIC numbers generated from several forms of one person a long-standing problem, said deduplication is done through ECINET periodically, and said the office was working towards catching repeated forms at the stage of submission and would do so very soon. Alt News says the Chief Electoral Officer directed officials on 19 October to speed up the removal of duplicate entries. No reply to the report of 21 November was found.

items.headline: Gems of UP SSR: 1.1 lakh voters whose parent is younger to them or of same age
items.claim: Alt News counted 1,10,875 electors on Uttar Pradesh's draft roll of the summary revision, published on 17 November, whose entry names a father or a mother who is listed in the same polling station and the same house with the same age as the elector or a younger one, in a report by Ankit Jain published on 23 November. Alt News says it took every elector whose entry names a father or a mother and looked in the same polling station for an elector of that name living in the same house. In 35,523 of the cases the parent and the child are listed with the same age, and in the other 75,352 the parent is younger, in 6,860 of them by 20 years or more. Alt News says the cases are spread across all 75 districts and all 403 Assembly constituencies, that Kushinagar district has the most, 3,646, and that Fazilnagar has the most of any constituency, 711. It recalls that in the intensive revision a parent less than 15 years older than the elector was one of what the Commission called logical discrepancies, which Alt News says its software looked for, that about 2.22 crore electors in Uttar Pradesh were sent notices for such discrepancies, and that the Commission says hearings were completed on all of them. Alt News says all 1,10,875 are on the draft, which it puts at 13.58 crore electors, and that claims and objections can be filed till 16 December, with the final roll due on 4 January 2027.
items.quote: We found 1,10,875 such cases spread across all 75 districts and 403 constituencies.
items.response: The report carries no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission, and none was found. Every count is Alt News's own, from the draft roll. The report matches a parent to an elector by name within one house and polling station, and it does not say how it treated two electors of the same name in one house.

items.headline: Samajwadi Party claims to have identified 1 lakh duplicate voters in UP, demands cash reward
items.claim: The Samajwadi Party claimed on 23 November that it had found around one lakh duplicate entries in Uttar Pradesh's draft roll of the summary revision, published on 17 November, and asked that the cash reward which it says the Chief Electoral Officer announced for finding such entries be given to it in full, PTI and Hindustan Times reported. In a memorandum to the Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, the party's state president, Shyamlal Pal, said the party had examined the names of all 13,58,68,905 electors in 1,73,730 polling booths of the state's 403 Assembly constituencies. The party says it found entries in which the elector's name, the relative's name, the address, the age and other details are the same and the EPIC numbers differ, and that it has emailed the details of the entries, with their serial numbers, polling booth numbers and constituency-wise and district-wise details, to the Chief Election Commissioner and the Chief Electoral Officer. It cites an announcement it says the Chief Electoral Officer made on 11 November that political parties or individuals who identify duplicate electors would be given cash rewards, and claims the whole reward because it was the first to identify the entries and submit the list. It urged the election authorities to verify and correct the roll thoroughly on a war footing, which it said was needed for Uttar Pradesh's Assembly election of 2027 to be transparent, fair and free.
items.quote: The party claimed its verification exercise had uncovered around one lakh duplicate entries in the draft electoral rolls (mother roll) published on November 17, 2026.
items.response: Neither report carries a reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission, and none was found. Neither says how much the reward is or on what terms it was announced. Every count of duplicates is the party's own.

items.headline: From 2000 on Nov 1 to 4.16 lakh on Nov 22: UP sees massive surge in Form 6 applications after SSR draft roll
items.claim: Alt News counted the Form 6 applications for inclusion in Uttar Pradesh's roll day by day and found that they rose from around 2,000 on 1 November to 4,16,380 on 22 November, in a report by Anindya Hazra published on 24 November and carried the same day by Newslaundry. Alt News says that from 1 to 16 November the state received about 10,000 applications on an average day, that the count began to rise on 17 November, when the draft roll of the summary revision was published, with around 31,000 that day, and that it reached around 2.31 lakh on 21 November. By its count 10,56,778 Form 6 applications were submitted between 29 October and 22 November, 1,65,289 of them between 1 and 16 November and 4,37,235 between 17 and 21 November. Matching the applicants against the 2.89 crore names left off the intensive revision's draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, it found around 45,000 whose names had been deleted and who had applied again in the same Assembly constituency, about 4.3% of the 10.4 lakh applications it examined. Matching by the applicant's name and the father's or husband's name within each constituency, it found 10,773 people whose names appeared more than once, accounting for 11,684 additional applications, and 427 people who had applied in two constituencies. It counts 6,969 repeat applications between 20 and 22 November and 4,325 on 22 November alone, and it reports 44 applications from one address in Siwalkhas constituency of Meerut district, all filed on 5 and 6 November. On 22 November, it says, 191 of the 403 constituencies received more than 1,000 applications, which none had before 17 November, while by the compiled Form 9 lists eight constituencies in Bijnor district received none on 20 and 21 November.
items.quote: On November 22 alone, the number stood at 4,16,380.
items.response: The report carries no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission, and none was found. Every count is Alt News's own, from the Form 6 and Form 9 data it compiled. The Chief Electoral Officer's statement of 24 November puts the applications received on 22 November at 3,99,218 (up-52), 17,162 fewer than Alt News's 4,16,380, and neither says how its count was made. Alt News matches applicants by name, and a match by name can join two different people of one name.

items.place: Ghaziabad; Kheri; Barabanki; Sahibabad; Gautam Buddh Nagar; Noida
items.headline: 10.39 lakh Form 6 applications during 7 days of SSR in UP
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, said on 24 November that 10,39,836 Form 6 applications for inclusion in the roll were received from 17 to 23 November in the summary revision, Hindustan Times, PTI and Dainik Jagran reported from his statement. Of these, 6,40,239 came on the special campaign days of 21 and 22 November, held at all 1,73,730 polling stations, with a record 3,99,218 on 22 November. Hindustan Times and Jagran report 1,84,379 on 23 November, and both say that the campaign days brought 61.6% of the total and that 22 November brought 65.6% more than 21 November. Jagran reports that the state received 5.99 applications per polling station on average, with 47 districts below that average. By the statement as PTI gives it, Ghaziabad received the most applications, 57,981, followed by Kheri with 50,078, Agra with 38,191, Lucknow with 32,091 and Barabanki with 30,666, and Sahibabad, with 16,834, received the most of any constituency. Ghaziabad, Kheri and Barabanki led the districts and Badaun, Jaunpur and Jhansi lagged behind. Among constituencies Ghaziabad led with 24.28 applications per polling station, 37 constituencies received more than 10 per polling station and 56 fewer than three. The Chief Electoral Officer told district election officers to give special attention to the districts and constituencies with few applications on the next campaign days, 28 and 29 November, when booth level officers are to be at every polling station from 10 am to 4 pm. At a meeting with election officials in Noida, which The Indian Express places on Monday, 23 November, and Hindustan Times late on Tuesday, 24 November, he directed that Form 6 applications in Gautam Buddh Nagar district stay pending with assistant electoral registration officers for no more than 24 hours and that online applications be assigned to the booth level officer on the day they are received, Hindustan Times reported. An officer told The Indian Express that in the seven days the district averaged six applications at each of its 1,926 polling stations, 32nd of the 75 districts, against about 20 at each of Ghaziabad's polling stations. Hindustan Times reports that the district administration plans to involve ASHA and anganwadi workers, auxiliary nurse midwives and Sakhi groups to find eligible women and help them apply on Form 6. Amar Ujala reported on 28 November, before the next campaign days, the same 6.40 lakh applications on 21 and 22 November and 3.99 lakh on 22 November, and wrote that the 16.16 crore people aged 18 or over in the state against the 13.58 crore on the draft left 2.58 crore names to be added, and that the names of 1.67 crore women and 73 lakh first-time electors were to be added.
items.quote: During these special campaign days, 6,40,239 ‘Form-6’ applications were received, with a record 3,99,218 ‘Form-6’ applications received on November 22 alone.
items.response: The figures are the Chief Electoral Officer's. None of the reports says how many of the applications have been decided or how many repeat an earlier application. The account of the Noida meeting comes from his statement as Hindustan Times gives it and from officers who spoke to The Indian Express without being named.

items.headline: UP to verify flagged voter details during 2027 electoral roll revision; no changes without consent
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, said on 25 November that the details collected in the intensive revision would be matched against the entries on the present roll to find probable errors in electors' names, relatives' names, the type of relationship, dates of birth, mobile numbers and photographs, and that no elector's particulars would be changed without the elector's consent and a signed application, PTI and The Times of India reported from his statement. Every entry flagged is to be checked on the ground. Booth level officers are to contact the electors concerned and verify the details against the facts and the documents available, and wherever a correction is needed they are to obtain a filled in and signed Form 8 from the elector. Assistant electoral registration officers and electoral registration officers are to scrutinise the applications and decide after examining the documents. He said the exercise follows the Election Commission's instructions for the summary revision of 2027, with 1 January 2027 as the qualifying date, and that all district election officers had been directed to see that the instructions are followed.
items.quote: No changes shall be made suo motu in the elector's name, relative's name, type of relationship, date of birth, mobile number, photograph or any other particulars.
items.response: The statement is the Chief Electoral Officer's own. Neither report says how many entries the matching has flagged, when it began or when it is to end, and neither cites the Commission's instructions by date or number. Those instructions were not found.

items.headline: Do not have data to agree or disagree: UP poll officer on Yogi’s ‘Hindu voters deleted’ claim
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, told The Indian Express in an interview published on 25 November that his office has no data on electors by religion and has given none to the Chief Minister, and that he does not have the data to agree or disagree with the Chief Minister's claim that 1.27 crore Hindu voters are missing from the roll (up-34). He said that about 2.5 crore people in the state are eligible to be on the roll and are not on it, and that he cannot say how many of them belong to any religion or caste, because the database can be analysed by gender and age and Form 6, the application for inclusion, has no column for religion or caste. He said a name can be added only when the person fills in the form and signs it or puts a thumb impression on it. He said some political party's overactive agents may have had names deleted, that his office first received such a complaint on 31 January and gave figures at a press conference on 8 February, and that a news portal which analysed the figures on his office's website found no more than 114 to 115 names deleted through these attempts. Those electors have been put back on the roll on Form 6, and the officials concerned have been issued show-cause notices. He said that the Commission's order of 9 October allows no one to submit more than ten Form 7 objections during the summary revision and no more than five a month after it, and that Uttar Pradesh had applied this cap in February. The same day, at an event held by a media house in Lucknow, the Chief Minister said that he had arrived at the 1.27 crore figure using artificial intelligence, and that the information had been extracted with an AI tool and not obtained from government officials, The New Indian Express reported.
items.quote: I am saying I do not have the data to agree or disagree with the Chief Minister.
items.response: The answers are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The Indian Express does not name the news portal, and he does not say over what period its count of 114 to 115 runs. The Chief Minister does not say what the AI tool was, what records it was given or how it assigned a religion to an elector, in The New Indian Express's report, and no figure by religion has been published by the Commission.

items.headline: SIR: In Karnataka’s electoral rolls, thousands of parents are younger than their children
items.claim: More than 17,000 entries in Karnataka's final roll after the revision list a parent as younger than or the same age as their child, and thousands of others show a gap of less than 15 years between parent and child, The Hindu reported on 27 November from its analysis of the final rolls. Its opening paragraph gives a 70-year-old man listed as the son of a 59-year-old, and a 40-year-old man listed as the father of another 40-year-old man at the same address. Scroll, reporting The Hindu's findings the same day, says Raichur district has the most such entries, 1,960, followed by Kalaburagi and Yadgir, and that in at least 2,200 entries across the state the father is listed as one to five years younger than the child. By Scroll's account of the analysis, the gap was between six and 10 years in more than 5,000 entries and between one and five years in another 3,000. Scroll says a gap of less than 15 years between a parent and child is one of the nine categories of logical discrepancy the Commission set for the revision, and that in Karnataka more than 43 lakh people were served notices over logical discrepancies at the end of the draft stage. The Congress said in a post on X on 27 November that thousands of these errors had survived into the final roll although more than 43 lakh electors were issued notices and hearings were held, and asked the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, to explain it, Moneycontrol and National Herald reported. The post puts the fathers in the 2,200 cases at one to five years older than their children.
items.quote: More than 17,000 entries in the final SIR rolls show parents listed as younger than or the same age as their children, while thousands of others have an age gap of less than 15 years
items.response: Scroll reports that the Chief Electoral Officer's office said it would verify the entries after The Hindu sent it a few sample cases. No other reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission was found. The counts are The Hindu's own and are not checked.

items.headline: Two suicides, BLO protests threaten to disrupt SIR in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Rajasthan
items.claim: The Indian Express reported the deaths of two BLOs. The family of a BLO in Kannur, Kerala, alleged he was under pressure to finish by December 4, and police said a note found on a BLO in Jaipur said he faced extreme pressure from his supervisor and was told he would be suspended if he did not meet his SIR target. It also reported that revenue employees in Tamil Nadu announced a statewide boycott of SIR work over workload.
items.response: Kannur District Collector Arun K Vijayan's report indicated that the BLO was not under any work pressure. The Indian Express said its multiple calls and messages to Rajasthan CEO Naveen got no response.
actors: Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu

items.headline: 4 deaths in a week: 2 woman assistant BLOs die of ‘heart attack’ in Gujarat amid concerns on ‘SIR work pressure’
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that two women assistant BLOs died of heart attacks in Tapi and Vadodara districts, bringing BLO deaths in Gujarat that week to four. The husband of one said she was a heart patient who had asked to be excused from BLO duty, which the Vadodara Collector disputed.
items.response: Vadodara District Collector Anil Dhameliya said, “We checked with the institute as well as with the local officials.
